Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program to recognize public high school students for their civic readiness and engagement. The State Board of Education is required to set criteria for awarding a 'Seal of Civic Excellence' to students who meet specific requirements, including the completion of a capstone project focused on civic service within state or local government. Local school systems may choose whether or not to participate in the program, but if a system does participate, its high schools must implement the program and award qualifying students with the seal and a corresponding cord, medal, or other insignia for their diploma.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the State Board of Education
stakeholders: Public high school students and local school systems in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education can implement the program using existing resources. Local school systems that choose to participate may experience increased expenditures related to staffing for extracurricular supervision and the cost of award materials (cords, medals, or insignia). However, because participation is voluntary for local school systems, these fiscal impacts are considered discretionary. No state or local revenue impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies like MSDE and coordinates policy initiatives related to the Governor's priorities for Maryland's youth and public education system.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the State Board of Education, and would likely review the regulations required to be adopted under this bill.

DBM oversees fiscal planning and personnel policies; the bill's provision for new extracurricular activities supervised by paid staff could have marginal personnel or budgetary implications for state-run educational programs.

MSDE is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Civic Excellence Program, receiving reports from local school systems, and supporting the State Board in developing the necessary regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's mission to promote service and civic engagement is directly aligned with the bill's goal of recognizing students for civic readiness and requiring a civic service capstone project.
GOCI oversees community affairs and volunteerism, providing a framework for the types of civic service and community partnerships encouraged by the bill's capstone requirement.
The bill explicitly authorizes participating local school systems to collaborate with institutions of higher education to support the implementation of the program.
As the coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency oversees the institutions that may collaborate with local school systems on civic excellence initiatives.
As a state agency providing tuition-free public education to Maryland students, the school may implement the program to recognize the civic engagement of its high school students.
The agency's mission to promote fair and transparent elections aligns with the bill's focus on civic literacy and engagement, which often includes education on the electoral process.
As a public university, Morgan State may serve as a partner for local school systems seeking to implement civic service capstone projects or other civic excellence criteria.
As Maryland's public honors college, it is a potential institutional partner for school systems implementing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program.
The University System of Maryland institutions are potential collaborators for local school systems in developing and supporting the civic readiness goals established by the bill.
Volunteer Maryland coordinates service opportunities and volunteer management systems, which directly correlates with the bill's requirement for a civic service-focused capstone project.

Synopsis: Requiring a county that submits an application to the Secretary of Transportation for funding for certain transportation services for elderly and disabled persons to identify interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers in the application; requiring the Secretary to adopt procedures to ensure counties cooperate in establishing interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers; etc.
Title: Transportation - Paratransit Services - Interjurisdictional Routes
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires counties that apply for State funding for elderly and handicapped transportation services to identify and establish interjurisdictional paratransit routes connecting to facilities within specific healthcare networks, including Adventist Healthcare, Johns Hopkins Medicine, LifeBridge Health, Luminis Health Maryland, MedStar Health, and the University of Maryland Medical System.
stakeholders: Elderly and handicapped residents, Maryland county governments, Baltimore City, and major healthcare provider networks.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be managed within existing budgeted resources. Total State funding for the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (at least 4305908 adjusted for inflation) remains unchanged, but the bill may shift the distribution of these funds among local jurisdictions. Local governments are expected to see an indeterminate increase in expenditures to provide the mandated interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The Secretary of Transportation manages the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (SSTAP), identifies funding for elderly and handicapped transportation in the budget, and is tasked with adopting procedures to ensure counties cooperate on interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Transportation to consult with the Department of Aging in distributing funds and developing enforcement procedures. Furthermore, local area agencies on aging, which fall under this department's network, must certify approval of the projects for which counties seek funding.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Transportation consult with the Department of Disabilities regarding the distribution of funds and the creation of enforcement procedures for the paratransit program, which specifically serves handicapped individuals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and would be responsible for advising on the development of new procedures and enforcement mechanisms related to interjurisdictional paratransit requirements and county cooperation.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term planning. The bill requires MDOT to identify specific amounts within its budget for these services, which DBM monitors to ensure efficiency and alignment with state resources.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and appoints the Secretary of Transportation. The bill modifies the administrative responsibilities and budget execution of a cabinet-level agency reporting to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring certain expedited proceedings in a wrongful detainer action if the property that is the subject of the action is, at the time of the complaint, advertised or listed for sale or lease by the complainant and requiring that notice of a hearing or appeal be served in person or, under certain circumstances, posted conspicuously on the property; requiring the District Court or the circuit court to issue a warrant within 24 hours if the court rules in favor of the complainant in an expedited wrongful detainer action; etc.
Title: Real Property - Expedited Wrongful Detainer Proceedings - Property for Sale or Lease
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m. (Economic Matters)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill establishes an expedited legal process for wrongful detainer actions when the real property in question is advertised or listed for sale or lease. It mandates specific shortened timelines for court summons, hearings, and judicial rulings, requiring the District Court to hold a hearing within five days of a complaint and issue a ruling within two business days. Additionally, it requires that warrants for possession be issued within 24 hours of a favorable ruling and executed immediately by the sheriff.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts) and local Sheriffs' Offices
stakeholders: Property owners listing real estate for sale or lease, individuals in actual possession of property without a legal right, the Maryland court system, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While the Maryland Judiciary and local sheriffs' offices may experience operational impacts to meet the expedited schedules for hearings, appeals, and warrant executions, the fiscal note states that no significant expenditure or revenue changes are expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates specific, expedited timelines for processing wrongful detainer cases in both District and Circuit Courts, including requirements for immediate summons, hearings within five days, rulings within two business days, and warrant issuance within 24 hours. The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for providing the operational, legal, and technological support needed to implement these procedural changes within the Maryland Judicial Branch.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State, providing legal counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies. The agency would be responsible for interpreting the new legal requirements for expedited proceedings and representing the state's interests or advising the courts on the implementation of these procedural changes to the Real Property Article.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is tasked with ensuring safe and secure housing and overseeing community vitality. While the bill is procedural, it modifies the process for recovering possession of real property that is listed for sale or lease, which has implications for property owners and the broader real estate market within the department's policy scope.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an institution of higher education from denying access or services to a student based on the student's diagnosis of sickle cell disease; requiring an institution of higher education to provide reasonable accommodations for students with sickle cell disease; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop an education and awareness campaign, designed to enhance understanding of sickle cell disease and reduce stigmas, for institutions of higher education in the State regarding students with sickle cell disease; etc.
Title: Sickle Cell Disease - Institutions of Higher Education - Policies, Procedures, and Educational Campaigns (Kaitlyn's Law)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment and Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Kaitlyn's Law prohibits Maryland institutions of higher education from denying services or access to facilities based on a student's sickle cell disease diagnosis and requires the provision of reasonable accommodations. The Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with other state entities, must develop a sickle cell disease education and awareness campaign, a framework for assessing and treating students, and comprehensive training materials for institutional faculty and staff.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students with sickle cell disease enrolled in higher education, institutional health personnel, faculty, and administrative staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $139,400 in FY 2027 and $157,900 in FY 2028 to hire contractual personnel at the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop educational materials, clinical procedures, and monitoring frameworks. Public four-year institutions and local community colleges are expected to meet the bill's requirements using existing resources, assuming accommodations like flexible attendance and hydration access remain low-cost.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Maryland Department of Health is responsible for developing the sickle cell disease education campaign, creating the framework and procedures for institutions of higher education, providing technical assistance, and monitoring implementation.

MHEC is a key implementing partner tasked with consulting on the framework and procedures, jointly providing technical assistance to institutions, and helping to monitor the implementation of the bill's requirements across Maryland's postsecondary schools.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Statewide Steering Committee on Sickle Cell Disease to collaborate with MDH and MHEC in developing the framework, providing technical assistance, and creating educational materials for faculty and staff.

As a major public institution of higher education, the University System of Maryland is directly required to implement the bill's mandates, including providing reasonable accommodations for students with sickle cell disease and establishing reporting procedures for potential violations.

As an independent state institution of higher education, Morgan State University must comply with the bill's requirements to provide reasonable accommodations and access for students with sickle cell disease and establish a process for reporting and publicizing these policies.

As a state-operated institution of higher education, Saint Mary's College is directly impacted by the mandates to provide accommodations, ensure non-discriminatory access, and follow the framework developed by MDH and MHEC.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact, requiring over $139,000 in general fund expenditures for new contractual personnel at MDH and MHEC, which falls under DBM's responsibility for state budget supervision and execution.
The OAG will likely provide legal guidance to MDH, MHEC, and the state's public universities regarding the implementation of the bill's anti-discrimination and reasonable accommodation requirements.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive departments (MDH and MHEC) tasked with implementing the law and coordinates the statewide policy initiatives that this legislation addresses, particularly in public health and education.

The bill's focus on 'reasonable accommodations' for a chronic health condition aligns with the Department of Disabilities' mission to ensure inclusive and accessible services across state programs, although they are not specifically named as an implementer.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student financing company" to exclude an institution of postsecondary education for purposes of certain registration and reporting requirements.
Title: Financial Institutions – Definition of Student Financing Companies – Alteration
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' to exclude institutions of postsecondary education. This change exempts these institutions from specific registration and annual reporting requirements mandated for entities providing student financing in Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Institutions of postsecondary education, student financing companies, and students who utilize student financing products
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. Specific revenue or expenditure estimates are unavailable because the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' within the Financial Institutions Article, which falls under the regulatory oversight of the Department's Office of Financial Regulation. This office is responsible for the registration and reporting requirements that institutions of postsecondary education will be exempt from under this legislation.

MHEC is the state's central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education. Since the bill exempts institutions of postsecondary education from certain financial registration and reporting requirements, it directly affects the operational and regulatory environment of the institutions under MHEC's purview.

As the state's public higher education system comprising 12 institutions, USM is an 'institution of postsecondary education' that would be exempted by this bill from the registration and reporting requirements typically applied to student financing companies.

As a public, state-governed postsecondary institution, Morgan State University is directly impacted by the bill's alteration of the definition of student financing companies, which removes the university from certain regulatory requirements if it provides student financing products.

As an independent public honors college and an institution of postsecondary education, Saint Mary's is directly impacted by this legislation, which exempts it from registering as a student financing company with the Department of Labor.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor and the Maryland Higher Education Commission. It would likely be responsible for advising on the implementation of these definition changes and interpreting the extent of the exemption.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions for various state agencies, including the Department of Labor. Changes to registration and reporting mandates for student financing entities could affect the scope or volume of administrative cases brought by or against the Office of Financial Regulation.

Synopsis: Requiring the District Court for Anne Arundel County to issue its summons for a trial to repossess for failure to pay rent to any constable or sheriff's designee; providing that a sheriff's designee in Anne Arundel County has the same authority and responsibility as a constable or sheriff in an action to repossess for a failure to pay rent; requiring a sheriff's designee to post a notice of a trial at a certain property or address; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Summons for Actions to Repossess for Failure to Pay Rent - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal procedures for summonses and trials in failure to pay rent cases specifically in Anne Arundel County. It requires the District Court to issue summonses to constables or sheriff's designees, changes the trial date from the 5th day to the 30th day after a complaint is filed, requires trial notices to be posted at the property at least 7 days before the trial, and limits the court to 100 such cases on any given day.
responsible_party: District Court for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Landlords and tenants in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State finances, although the Judiciary anticipates operational impacts regarding case scheduling and high volumes in Anne Arundel County. Local expenditures may decrease if the bill leads to operational efficiencies and reduced overtime within the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's office. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations of the District Court in Anne Arundel County, which is supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts. It alters procedural requirements for issuing summonses, increases the timeline for trial from 5 to 30 days, and imposes a cap on the number of cases scheduled per day. The fiscal note explicitly identifies a moderate operational impact on the Judiciary.

Synopsis: Requiring certain interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports sponsored by certain schools and certain locker rooms to be expressly designated based on biological sex; prohibiting certain entities from taking certain adverse actions against a school for maintaining separate interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports or locker rooms for students of the female sex; etc.
Title: Education - Interscholastic and Intramural Junior Varsity and Varsity Teams and Locker Rooms - Designation Based on Sex (Fairness in Girls' Sports Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: The Fairness in Girls' Sports Act requires that interscholastic and intramural athletic teams and locker rooms in Maryland public high schools and certain nonpublic high schools be expressly designated based on biological sex. The bill prohibits students of the male sex from participating on teams or using locker rooms designated for females, protects schools from adverse actions for maintaining these sex-based designations, and establishes a right for students or schools to bring civil actions for damages and legal fees in the event of violations or retaliation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems
stakeholders: Public and nonpublic high school students, local school systems, and athletic associations or organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local school systems may incur additional costs related to potential civil litigation and locker room modifications; however, a reliable estimate of these costs is not feasible at this time according to the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates high-profile policy initiatives. This bill involves significant social and educational policy that aligns with executive oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

While the fiscal note indicates no direct State fiscal impact, DBM is the principal fiscal agency and supervises budget execution and personnel policies that may be tangentially affected by changes in school system administrative requirements.

MSDE is the primary agency for the bill's implementation. It oversees public education policies and regulations, specifically those governing the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA) which manages the athletic programs mentioned in the bill.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to MSDE regarding the bill's compliance with federal laws like Title IX and constitutional Equal Protection clauses, and would represent the State in any resulting litigation.
The bill creates a new cause of action allowing students and schools to bring civil suits for damages, which will be adjudicated within the State's judicial system managed by the AOC.

The MCCR enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws. The bill's requirements for sex-based designation and its protections against 'adverse actions' may conflict with or impact the Commission's enforcement scope regarding sex and gender identity discrimination.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze the challenges related to the delay in student enrollment counts and its effect on school funding and the connection between growing student populations and the provision of school funding; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2026.
Title: Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze challenges related to student enrollment counts and population growth as they relate to school funding. The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local boards of education, the Maryland State Department of Education, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) assumes that the task force can be staffed using existing resources, resulting in no net fiscal impact. However, the Office of the Governor estimates a fiscal 2027 requirement of $254,000 for contractual support and an executive assistant. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Office of the Governor to provide staffing for the Task Force and mandates that the Governor appoint nine members and the chair. The Governor's Office also noted a potential fiscal impact of $254,000 for contractual staff to fulfill this mandate.

As the agency overseeing public education funding and enrollment, MSDE is a primary stakeholder. A representative from the department is a named member of the Task Force, and the study directly concerns MSDE's core operations and funding formulas.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary task force to address specific government issues (education funding and student population growth), falling under the regulatory and administrative scope of this entity.
The Office of the Comptroller is a named member of the Task Force, reflecting its role as the state's chief financial officer in analyzing fiscal data related to education funding.

The fiscal note identifies the Maryland Department of Planning as the agency responsible for school enrollment projections, which are a central component of the Task Force's required analysis of student population growth.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting the nine members and chair to be appointed to the newly created Task Force.

As the agency responsible for state budget development and long-term fiscal planning, DBM would be impacted by Task Force recommendations regarding changes to education funding formulas and state expenditures.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a communication between an attorney and a client that acts as a fiduciary is subject to the attorney-client privilege even if fiduciary funds are used to compensate the attorney for services rendered to the client.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Fiduciaries - Attorney-Client Privilege
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 501
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that attorney-client privilege applies to communications between an attorney and a client who is acting as a fiduciary, such as an executor or trustee, even if the attorney is compensated using fiduciary funds. It further establishes that the fiduciary relationship between the client and a beneficiary does not waive this privilege.
stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, executors, personal representatives, and agents under power of attorney), beneficiaries of estates and trusts, and attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judicial Branch by codifying rules regarding the attorney-client privilege, an evidentiary standard applied in judicial proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides legal and operational support to the state's courts, including the Orphans' Courts where fiduciary matters are frequently adjudicated.

The Register of Wills is the primary state agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and overseeing personal representatives and executors, who are explicitly defined as fiduciaries under the Estates and Trusts Article. This bill clarifies legal protections for communications between these fiduciaries and their counsel.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies that may act in fiduciary capacities (such as guardians or trustees). The bill clarifies the application of attorney-client privilege in these scenarios, particularly when fiduciary funds are used for compensation.

The Department of Human Services frequently interacts with the legal system in fiduciary roles, such as serving as guardians for vulnerable children and adults. This bill clarifies the legal protections afforded to communications between the agency's representatives and their legal counsel in those capacities.

The Department of Aging oversees programs for older adults and individuals with disabilities, including long-term care advocacy and support for guardians. The bill's clarification of fiduciary attorney-client privilege is relevant to the legal environment surrounding the populations and advocates the department serves.

The Department of Disabilities is concerned with the legal rights and services provided to individuals with disabilities, many of whom have fiduciaries such as guardians or agents with power of attorney. This bill clarifies the privacy of legal communications for those managing the affairs of disabled residents.

Title: Environment - Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative - Withdrawal (Restoring Energy Freedom Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to withdraw Maryland from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI), a multi-state program to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. It repeals statutory provisions regarding the sale of carbon dioxide allowances and the distribution of auction proceeds to the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund. The bill also mandates that the Governor report on the reasons for withdrawal and propose an alternative plan for reducing emissions from power plants, specifically considering the use of native, warm season grasses.
responsible_party: The Governor and the Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Electricity customers, low-income residents receiving energy assistance, power plant operators, local governments, and small businesses in the clean energy and energy efficiency sectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund revenues and expenditures are estimated to decrease by $138,300,000 in fiscal 2027 and by $276,600,000 annually thereafter due to the loss of RGGI auction proceeds. General fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount if the State opts to maintain programs, such as energy assistance for low-income households, that were previously funded by RGGI revenues. Local government and small business finances will also be negatively impacted by the loss of grant funding for clean energy and efficiency projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor withdraw the State from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and requires the Governor to report to the General Assembly regarding the withdrawal and future plans for carbon reduction.

The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is the primary recipient of RGGI auction proceeds. The bill would result in a significant loss of special fund revenue ($276.6 million annually) that MEA uses to fund various energy efficiency and renewable energy programs.

The Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for carbon reduction strategies and enforcing environmental laws. The bill amends the Environment Article, repeals MDE's authority regarding RGGI allowances, and removes funding for MDE's Air and Radiation Administration.

The Department of Human Services (DHS) receives at least 50% of RGGI proceeds to fund the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) and other energy assistance for low-income residents. The bill's withdrawal from RGGI would eliminate this dedicated funding source.

The bill removes statutory language requiring the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund to help achieve RGGI offset opportunities. Additionally, DNR's Power Plant Research Program currently receives funding from RGGI proceeds.
DHCD is a significant recipient of RGGI funding from the SEIF, which it uses to administer low- and moderate-income energy efficiency and conservation programs.

The bill specifically identifies and modifies funding allocations for the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which will be significantly reduced following the withdrawal from RGGI.
The PSC regulates the utilities and energy markets impacted by RGGI. The bill involves PSC oversight of ratepayer refunds and transfers related to the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
Member institutions, including the University of Maryland, College Park, receive RGGI funding for energy innovation and climate-related research, such as the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute.
MDOT receives RGGI funding from the SEIF for initiatives related to clean energy and climate change mitigation in the transportation sector.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved in the oversight of the SEIF and the fiscal note indicates a potential need for General Fund increases to replace lost RGGI revenues for essential programs.
DGS utilizes RGGI funding from the SEIF to implement energy efficiency and renewable energy projects in state-owned facilities.
The OPC advocates for residential utility consumers. Withdrawing from RGGI impacts energy costs, assistance program availability (EUSP), and energy conservation efforts that affect residential bills.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Strategic Energy Investment Fund separately and manage its investments, which are directly impacted by the bill.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and managing the distribution of certain funds mentioned in the bill's amendments to the State Government Article.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the legal process of withdrawing from an interstate memorandum of understanding such as RGGI.
The bill impacts the manufacturing sector and energy-related businesses by altering the regulatory framework and funding available for clean energy transitions and emissions monitoring.
MHEC oversees policies for higher education institutions that may see shifts in funding for energy-related programs and institutional efficiency projects funded by RGGI.
As a public higher education institution, Morgan State is eligible for and may be impacted by changes in state funding for energy efficiency and climate initiatives derived from SEIF.
As a public college, St. Mary's may be impacted by changes in state funding for energy efficiency and climate initiatives derived from SEIF.
The Department of Labor is involved in workforce development; RGGI-funded programs often include components for job training in the green energy and energy efficiency sectors.
The bill impacts environmental regulations and energy assistance programs that have indirect consequences for public health outcomes and environmental justice.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain Ten Commandments Monument to be placed on the grounds of the Maryland State House; requiring the Commission on Artistic Property to oversee the care and maintenance of the monument; and establishing the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument.
Title: State Government - State House Trust - Ten Commandments Monument Display Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: The Ten Commandments Monument Display Act requires the placement of a monument of the Ten Commandments on the grounds of the Maryland State House. It establishes a temporary Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument to oversee the design, site selection, and placement of the monument, which must be executed by a private entity at no cost to the State. The Commission on Artistic Property is assigned responsibility for the ongoing care and maintenance of the monument.
responsible_party: Commission on Artistic Property, Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument, and the Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Citizens and visitors of the State of Maryland, and private entities or small businesses involved in the monument's design and construction.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no fiscal impact in FY 2027. General fund expenditures will increase by at least $4,000 in FY 2028 and biennially thereafter for the care and maintenance of the monument by the Maryland State Archives. The monument itself is required to be designed, constructed, and placed by a private entity at no cost to the State. The bill has no effect on State revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives oversees the Commission on Artistic Property, which the bill designates as the official custodian responsible for the care and maintenance of the Ten Commandments monument.

The bill mandates that the Division of Historical and Cultural Programs within the Department of Planning provides primary staffing and administrative support for the newly established Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument.
The monument is to be placed on the grounds of the State House, which is under the jurisdiction of the State House Trust. The Trust is also named as a consulting agency for the commission's staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent body, the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument, to oversee the design, construction, and site selection of the monument.
The Governor is responsible for appointing three members to the commission and designating its chair. The office also oversees the implementation of policy initiatives related to state grounds.
The bill specifically authorizes the Attorney General to prepare and present a legal defense of the monument in the event of a constitutional or legal challenge.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance of state facilities and grounds, DGS is named as a consulting entity for the commission and would likely be involved in the physical placement of the monument.
The Office of Appointments would be responsible for recruiting and vetting the individuals the Governor must appoint to the newly created commission.
The Maryland State Arts Council, which falls under the Department of Commerce, is explicitly named as a consulting agency to assist in staffing the commission.

DBM would oversee any fiscal impacts related to the reimbursement of travel expenses for commission members and the ongoing general fund expenditures for monument maintenance identified in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to develop and make available an Old Line Plate with a certain numeric-only registration number for certain motor vehicles.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Special Registration Plates - Old Line Plates (Old Line Plate Program Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Old Line Plate Program Act of 2026 requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to develop and auction numeric-only registration plates that resemble Maryland's 1911 license plates, featuring white characters on a black background. The bill establishes a program for the auction, issuance, and transfer of 'registration number rights' for numeric-only sequences of one to five digits, with collected fees used to recover administrative costs and the remainder credited to the Transportation Trust Fund.
stakeholders: Owners of passenger vehicles, light trucks, and multipurpose vehicles in Maryland; vehicle registration number collectors; and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues will increase from auction proceeds and transfer fees, with the first auction required by December 1, 2026. TTF expenditures will also increase for plate production and auction administration. While the exact impact depends on participation, an illustrative estimate from the Fiscal Note suggests $275,000 in annual revenue based on the auction of 1,000 plates at an average price of $275, with production costs estimated at $10 per set and auction costs at $27,500 per event.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including developing the Old Line Plate, managing the inventory of numeric-only registration numbers, operating the public auction program, and adopting regulations.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a modal administration under the Department of Transportation, and the bill directs that all fees collected from the program be credited to the Transportation Trust Fund, which the Department manages.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services oversees Maryland Correctional Enterprises, which is the entity responsible for the actual manufacturing and production of Maryland state vehicle registration plates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Motor Vehicle Administration and will be involved in drafting the necessary regulations and reviewing the legal framework for the auction and transfer of registration number rights.

The Maryland State Police enforce motor vehicle laws and traffic safety; the introduction of a new registration plate design (numeric-only with a unique color scheme) impacts law enforcement identification and automated reader systems.

The Office of Administrative Hearings will adjudicate any contested cases resulting from the Motor Vehicle Administration's authority to deny, suspend, or revoke registration number rights or transfers.

The Office of Legislative Audits will be responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of the Motor Vehicle Administration's management of the auction program and the collection of associated revenues.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state's budget and personnel; the bill creates a new revenue stream and requires state expenditures for the administration of the auction and plate production.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state procurement and contracts, which may include approving any major service contracts required for the plate production or the operation of the public auction program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals may be called upon to adjudicate bid protests or contract disputes if the state procures external services for the auction platform or plate manufacturing.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the fiscal integrity and revenue collection processes established by the bill.
The State Treasurer manages state funds, including the Transportation Trust Fund, and sits on the Board of Public Works to approve procurements related to the implementation of this new program.

Synopsis: Altering the exemption from overtime pay for individuals who are employed to work in an administrative, executive, or professional capacity.
Title: Labor and Employment - Exemptions From Overtime Pay - Administrative, Executive, or Professional Capacity
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the exemption from overtime pay for employees working in administrative, executive, or professional (EAP) capacities under the Maryland Wage and Hour Law. It establishes a schedule to increase the minimum salary threshold for these exemptions annually from $769.23 per week (approximately $40,000 per year) starting July 1, 2027, to $961.54 per week (approximately $50,000 per year) by July 1, 2031, and codifies the job duties required to qualify for the exemption.
stakeholders: Employees in administrative, executive, and professional roles earning between the current federal threshold and the proposed state thresholds, and private sector employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local government expenditures as employers because they are exempt from the Maryland Wage and Hour Law's overtime provisions. The Maryland Department of Labor expects to handle enforcement and outreach with existing budgeted resources. Small businesses will experience increased personnel costs as the salary thresholds for overtime eligibility rise annually between 2027 and 2031.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for enforcing the Maryland Wage and Hour Law, the Department of Labor is tasked with investigating complaints, conducting outreach, and developing guidance for employers and workers regarding the new overtime salary thresholds and duties tests.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Department of Labor regarding the enforcement of wage laws, regulation updates, and representation in any civil or criminal appeals related to labor disputes.

The judicial branch may experience an increase in civil litigation as employees seek to recover unpaid overtime wages and liquidated damages through the court system under the updated salary thresholds.

The OAH may be required to adjudicate administrative disputes or contested cases involving enforcement actions and regulatory decisions made by the Maryland Department of Labor regarding overtime exemptions.

Because the bill has a 'meaningful' fiscal impact on small businesses by increasing their personnel costs for administrative and professional staff, the Department of Commerce is relevant as the state's primary economic development and business support agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is relevant due to the bill's significant impact on small businesses, which may need guidance or advocacy as they adapt to higher payroll costs and reporting requirements for formerly exempt employees.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Highway Administration to study and make recommendations on the implementation of a consistent statewide policy for the use of traffic calming devices on highways in the State; and requiring the Administration to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
Title: State Highway Administration - Traffic Calming Devices - Study
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Environment and Transportation; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Highway Administration (SHA) to study and make recommendations for a consistent statewide policy on the use of traffic calming devices, such as speed bumps and traffic circles. The study must research best practices, develop implementation guidelines, recommend technical support for local governments, and identify potential partner organizations, with a final report due to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Bicyclists, motorists, pedestrians, counties, and municipalities
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures are estimated to increase by $75,000 total, with $12,500 in fiscal 2026 and $62,500 in fiscal 2027, to hire a consultant to conduct the required study. There is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Highway Administration to report its findings and recommendations regarding a statewide traffic calming policy directly to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

The bill has a fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund, requiring additional expenditures in FY 2026 and FY 2027. As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term fiscal planning.

Traffic calming devices, such as raised crosswalks and narrowed roads, directly impact pedestrian safety and accessibility for residents with disabilities, which is a core focus of this department's advocacy and policy coordination.

The bill requires recommendations on providing technical support to counties and municipalities. The Department of Planning is responsible for promoting sustainable growth and providing technical assistance to local governments regarding land use and infrastructure.
As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT oversees the state's multi-modal transportation network and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which will fund the required study.

The bill requires a consistent statewide policy for traffic calming on highways in the State. As the agency responsible for operating and maintaining Maryland's toll highways, the MDTA would be affected by the implementation of such a policy.

The State Highway Administration is the primary agency tasked with conducting the study, researching best practices, developing guidelines, and reporting recommendations for a statewide traffic calming policy.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to reimburse a psychiatric rehabilitation program for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 30 psychiatric rehabilitation community psychiatric support services delivered to certain individuals each month.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Psychiatric Rehabilitation Program Services - Reimbursement (Youth Psychiatric Rehabilitation Parity Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to reimburse psychiatric rehabilitation programs for a minimum of six and a maximum of thirty services per month provided to individuals with serious emotional disturbances or persistent mental disorders who are severely impaired and living with a legally responsible relative.
stakeholders: Medicaid participants with serious emotional disturbances or persistent mental disorders, psychiatric rehabilitation program (PRP) providers, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures are estimated to increase by $74,700,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, with 60% ($44,820,000) coming from federal funds and 40% ($29,880,000) from state general funds. Federal fund revenues are expected to increase by $44,800,000 accordingly. Local governments providing PRP services may experience increased expenditures to adjust delivery processes and increased revenues from Medicaid billing. Small business PRP providers will receive higher reimbursement but are required to provide more services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and oversee the reimbursement of psychiatric rehabilitation program (PRP) services.
The bill has a significant fiscal impact, increasing state Medicaid expenditures by an estimated $74.7 million annually starting in FY 2027, requiring budget planning and oversight by DBM.
The bill focuses on youth psychiatric rehabilitation services, directly aligning with this office's mission to improve access to health services and well-being for Maryland's children.
Psychiatric Rehabilitation Programs serve individuals with serious emotional disturbances or mental disorders, which are categories of disability coordinated by this department.
The bill targets youth with severe functional impairments living with guardians; this population often receives preventative services and aid through DHS and local departments of social services.

Youth involved in the juvenile justice system frequently require psychiatric rehabilitation services; the bill's changes to reimbursement and service frequency directly impact treatment options for DJS youth.
The Commission is responsible for planning the state's health system needs and improving access to care, which includes community-based psychiatric support services.

The OAG will likely provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of regulations, especially concerning potential conflicts with federal laws like EPSDT and the Mental Health Parity Act mentioned in the fiscal note.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Health, and proposes the annual budget which must account for the substantial increase in Medicaid spending.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the distribution of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which oversees significant state expenditures like Medicaid provider contracts.
The Treasurer manages state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which would be involved in approving large-scale fiscal commitments related to Medicaid expansions.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state procurements and contracts; the bill's large fiscal impact on Medicaid may require administrative review of provider payment structures.
OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; changes to Medicaid reimbursement rules and service caps may lead to hearings regarding medical necessity or benefit denials.
The target population for these psychiatric services includes school-aged youth, and PRPs often coordinate with educational systems to support students with serious emotional disturbances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a meaningful impact on small businesses, as many Psychiatric Rehabilitation Program providers operate as small businesses in the healthcare sector.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on youth programs and public safety strategies, where psychiatric rehabilitation is a key component of reducing juvenile delinquency and recidivism.

The team is tasked with identifying initiatives to address child poverty and economic mobility; expanding mental health support for youth is a central pillar of improving outcomes for vulnerable families.

GOPI oversees the implementation of the State Comprehensive Plan and coordinates across agencies to ensure measurable results, which is relevant given the bill's mandate for new regulations and substantial funding.

Synopsis: Establishing an Edible Forests and Foraging Program within the Department of Natural Resources; requiring individuals who forage in designated foraging areas to obtain a foraging permit; requiring the Department to charge a permit application fee and establish a fee waiver process for individuals who demonstrate financial need; requiring the Department to establish and maintain edible forests on State land, subject to available funding; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Edible Forests and Foraging Program - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Edible Forests and Foraging Program within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to manage and regulate the harvesting of mushrooms and plant materials on State-owned land. It requires the department to designate foraging areas where individuals must obtain a permit to forage and allows for the establishment of 'edible forests' where no permit is required for noncommercial personal consumption. A special fund is created to collect permit fees and support the program's administrative and maintenance costs.
stakeholders: Individuals who forage for mushrooms or plant materials for personal consumption and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures increase starting in fiscal 2027. The Department of Natural Resources estimates that establishing an edible forest plot costs approximately $10,000 per acre for site preparation and planting. Additional staff costs, such as a technician, may be required at approximately $75,223 annually. Special fund revenues will increase from foraging permit application fees, though the total amount is indeterminate. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Natural Resources as the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and regulating the Edible Forests and Foraging Program, including designating foraging areas and issuing permits.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Edible Forests and Foraging Fund separately and to invest the money within the fund.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund, which is a special, nonlapsing fund created to support the program.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the budget for the new program and fund. The fiscal note also suggests that additional personnel may eventually be needed to manage the program.

The bill mandates the establishment of edible forests on 'State-owned land,' not just land owned by DNR. As the agency responsible for the maintenance and management of state facilities and real estate, DGS may be impacted by these land-use designations.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources as it develops the regulations, permit requirements, and fee waiver processes mandated by the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Natural Resources and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must include appropriations for the new Edible Forests and Foraging Fund.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and the use or transfer of state property, which may be relevant as areas of state-owned land are designated for the program.
The program's focus on cultivating noninvasive plants for consumption aligns with the Department of Agriculture's mission regarding plant resource protection and environmental stewardship.
The establishment of edible forests and foraging areas impacts land use and quality of life in rural counties, areas of primary focus for the Rural Maryland Council.
The Department of Planning provides policy guidance on sustainable growth and resource management, which overlaps with the creation of new land-use categories like edible forests.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Education to develop, by July 1, 2027, curriculum content for an elective course in water safety and swimming for public school students in kindergarten through grade 8; requiring, beginning in the 2027-2028 school year, county boards of education to implement the water safety and swimming curriculum content for students in kindergarten through grade 8 in public schools in the county; etc.
Title: Public Schools - Water Safety and Swimming Course - Established

Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Education to develop curriculum content standards for a water safety and swimming course for public school students in kindergarten through grade 8 by July 1, 2027. Local boards of education must implement the course starting in the 2027-2028 school year and are required to provide reasonable accommodations for students with disabilities to ensure equal participation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Public school students (kindergarten through grade 8), students with disabilities, local school systems, and local parks and recreation agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2027 for a consultant to develop the required curriculum standards. Beginning in FY 2028, local school systems will face significant expenditure increases to implement the course, with estimates for individual counties ranging from $300,000 to over $16,000,000 annually. These costs are primarily driven by transportation, staffing (instructors and lifeguards), equipment, and pool facility rental fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works must approve the $250,000 contract for a consultant to develop the curriculum content standards, as it oversees significant state procurements and expenditures.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the state's budget and will need to account for the $250,000 general fund expenditure required for the curriculum development consultant.
The bill explicitly requires county boards to provide reasonable accommodations to ensure students with disabilities have an equal opportunity to participate in the water safety and swimming course.

The State Board of Education (overseen by MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for developing the curriculum content standards and overseeing the implementation of the course by local school boards.

As the agency responsible for managing Maryland's waterways and providing expertise on water-related activities, the DNR was consulted in the fiscal analysis and serves as a technical resource for water safety standards.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MSDE, DBM) and proposes the state budget, which must include the funding for the mandated curriculum development.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for equal access to state programs and services; it would be involved in ensuring the mandated swimming course and its accommodations are accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing students.
As a unit within MSDE focused on safety standards and training in schools, the Center may be involved in developing or reviewing the safety protocols and resource materials for the new curriculum.
As a state agency providing public education, the Maryland School for the Deaf would likely be required to align with new statewide curriculum standards for its students.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the State Board of Education during the development of curriculum standards, regulations, and policies related to disability accommodations.

The bill's implementation requires significant new staffing (instructors, lifeguards, coordinators) at the local school level, which falls under PERB's jurisdiction regarding labor relations and collective bargaining for public school personnel.

Synopsis: Requiring a procurement contract for 3 years or more in duration and valued at greater than $2,000,000 for security services to include a clause requiring contract modification for the equitable adjustment of the contract for increased costs for compensation and benefits as a result of statutory changes increasing required compensation or benefits or collective bargaining; and requiring a certain contract that is modified to be contingent on approval by the chief procurement officer of the appropriate primary procurement unit.
Title: State Procurement - Security Services - Contract Modification
Status: In the Senate - Rereferred to Budget and Taxation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: The bill requires Maryland State procurement contracts for security services that are valued at over $2,000,000 and have a duration of three years or more to include a clause for contract modification. This clause mandates an equitable adjustment of the contract to cover increased costs for compensation and benefits that result from statutory changes or collective bargaining agreements. Any such contract modification is contingent upon the approval of the chief procurement officer of the appropriate primary procurement unit.
responsible_party: Chief procurement officer of the appropriate primary procurement unit (such as the Department of General Services or the Maryland Department of Transportation)
stakeholders: Private security service contractors, employees of security contractors, and State procurement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a potentially significant increase in State procurement expenditures across all funds starting in fiscal 2027. This impact arises from the requirement that the State compensate contractors for higher labor costs caused by future legislative changes or collective bargaining agreements. A specific total dollar estimate is unavailable because the number of future contract modifications depends on unpredictable statutory changes and labor negotiations. Additionally, state procurement units may require additional staff or resources to process an increased volume of contract modifications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the highest administrative body overseeing state expenditures and procurement contracts. The bill requires contract modifications to be approved by the chief procurement officer of the appropriate unit, and existing regulations require BPW approval for modifications over $50,000, which most contracts covered by this bill ($2M+) would trigger.

DGS is a primary procurement unit and the central authority for state construction and service contracts. The fiscal note explicitly identifies DGS as one of the agencies likely to require additional staff to process the increased volume of contract modifications mandated by this bill.

MDOT is a primary procurement unit that manages significant construction and security contracts for its various administrations. The bill requires its Chief Procurement Officer to approve modifications, and the fiscal note highlights MDOT as an agency that may face increased administrative and project costs.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency and a primary procurement unit for various services. It is responsible for budget supervision and would be impacted by the potential increase in procurement costs across state agencies.

USM is identified in the fiscal note as a primary procurement unit impacted by the bill. It has independent procurement authority and its Chief Procurement Officer would be responsible for approving the mandated contract modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a major user of security services and facilities construction. The bill's requirements for contract modifications for security services and construction projects directly impact its operational budget and contract management.

As an independent state agency with its own Board of Regents and independent procurement authority, Morgan State University would be responsible for implementing these contract clauses and its Chief Procurement Officer would need to approve relevant modifications.
As an independent unit of state government with its own procurement oversight, the college would be required to include the mandated clauses in its large construction or security contracts.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees significant state contracts and expenditures. The agency's role in the BPW makes it relevant to the approval process for the high-value contract modifications discussed in the bill.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which reviews and approves major state contracts and modifications. The office also oversees certain procurement activities.

The Maryland Stadium Authority plans, builds, and manages major sports and entertainment facilities. It frequently enters into large construction and security service contracts that would likely meet the bill's $2 million and 3-year thresholds.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards. It would likely be involved in drafting and reviewing the mandatory contract clauses to ensure compliance with the new statutory requirements.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on applicants for and holders of video lottery operation licenses and persons who own an interest in video lottery facility operations in the State from directly or indirectly making contributions to certain campaign finance entities.
Title: Video Lottery Operations - Prohibitions on Campaign Contributions - Parity Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals the existing state prohibition that prevents applicants for video lottery operation licenses, current license holders, and individuals or entities with at least a 5% ownership interest in video lottery facilities from making campaign contributions to candidates for nonfederal public office in Maryland.
stakeholders: Applicants for video lottery operation licenses, video lottery operation license holders, owners of interests in video lottery facilities, and candidates for nonfederal public office in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 13-237 of the Election Law Article, which is the primary body of law overseen and administered by the State Board of Elections. The agency is responsible for regulating campaign finance reporting and ensuring compliance with election laws affected by this repeal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts applicants and holders of video lottery operation licenses, which are regulated by this agency. The bill specifically references the State Government Article sections governing the agency's oversight of video lottery facilities and operations.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes criminal offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and campaign finance laws. Repealing a prohibition on specific types of campaign contributions directly affects the scope of their investigative and prosecutorial oversight.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies, including the State Board of Elections and the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of repealing these contribution restrictions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the agencies impacted by this legislation. The Governor also has the authority to sign or veto the legislation, which represents a policy shift regarding the interaction between gaming interests and political campaigns.

The State Ethics Commission is charged with maintaining public confidence in the integrity of state government. Changes to campaign finance laws involving highly regulated industries like gaming have implications for government transparency and public ethics standards.

Synopsis: Authorizing the reallocation of certain school safety grants to local school systems that have fully expended their grant allocation and demonstrate unmet need within the same fiscal year.
Title: Local School Systems - School Safety - Grant Allocations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill allows for the reallocation of unspent funds from the state's annual $10 million school safety grant program to local school systems and law enforcement agencies that have already used their full allocation and can demonstrate additional financial need for providing school resource officers or law enforcement coverage in public schools within the same fiscal year.
responsible_party: School Safety Subcabinet and the Maryland Center for School Safety
stakeholders: Local school systems, local law enforcement agencies, and Maryland public schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no net effect on State general fund expenditures as it only authorizes the reallocation of existing mandated funding. However, it may reduce the amount of unspent grant money that reverts to the General Fund; for example, $6.2 million remained unspent in fiscal 2023 and $3.7 million in fiscal 2024. Local school systems and law enforcement agencies may see increased revenues if they qualify for reallocated funds, though these increases are contingent on the availability of unspent funds and the discretion of the School Safety Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) provides staff support to the School Safety Subcabinet and is identified in the fiscal note as the primary entity responsible for implementing the grant reallocation authorized by the bill.

The State Superintendent of Schools chairs the School Safety Subcabinet, which is responsible for the grants. Additionally, the department oversees the local school systems that are the primary recipients and potential beneficiaries of the reallocated funds.

The Secretary of State Police is a mandated member of the School Safety Subcabinet, which is authorized to reallocate these funds. The grants are intended to assist in providing law enforcement coverage for public schools.
The Attorney General is a mandated member of the School Safety Subcabinet, the body responsible for making decisions regarding the reallocation of unspent school safety grant funds.
The Secretary of Health is a mandated member of the School Safety Subcabinet, which oversees the allocation and reallocation of the $10 million in annual school safety grants.

The Secretary of the Department of Disabilities is a mandated member of the School Safety Subcabinet, the entity that will exercise discretion in reallocating unspent school safety funds to systems with unmet needs.

The Executive Director of the Interagency Commission on School Construction serves on the School Safety Subcabinet, which is the governing body for the grant reallocation process established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The School Safety Subcabinet, which is the specific multi-agency body authorized to manage the reallocation of these grants, falls under this category of executive entities.
DBM is responsible for the annual budget bill which contains the $10 million mandated appropriation for these grants and monitors the fiscal impact of reversions back to the General Fund.

The Governor is required to include the $10 million mandated appropriation for school safety grants in the annual budget bill and oversees the executive departments that comprise the School Safety Subcabinet.

Synopsis: Requiring certain ticket resellers to register annually with the Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General to resell an event ticket in the State; regulating the sale and resale of event tickets in the State; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to enforcement and penalty provisions under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Sale and Resale of Event Tickets - Registration and Regulation
