General fund revenues are estimated to decrease by 13253000000, while special fund revenues will decrease by 843200000. Local government revenues are projected to decrease by 96900000 in fiscal 2027 due to reduced distributions from corporate income taxes and cannabis sales taxes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the administrative support for the Governor, who proposes the annual state budget and coordinates policy initiatives, this office is highly relevant as the bill proposes a massive overhaul of the state's tax structure resulting in an estimated $13.3 billion general fund revenue decrease, fundamentally altering the state's fiscal landscape.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for implementing and enforcing the proposed changes to the individual income tax, corporate income tax, and sales and use tax rates, including the repeal of specific IT-related sales taxes.

As the chief financial agency managing state funds and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer's Office is relevant due to the bill's significant impact on state revenue and fund distributions, which impacts the state's fiscal protection and bond sale revenue oversight.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies. The implementation of a flat tax and major rate alterations will likely require legal review, advisory opinions, and potential litigation support during implementation.

The bill includes a specific income tax exemption for the first $10,000 of net capital gains for individuals who are at least 65 years old, which directly concerns the Department's mission to advocate for the rights and quality of life for older adults.

As the principal fiscal agency responsible for developing the state's budget and long-term fiscal planning, DBM is critically impacted by the bill's multi-billion dollar impact on general fund revenues and the subsequent need for budget execution adjustments.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the bill's significant reduction in corporate and individual income tax rates and the repeal of sales taxes on IT services are highly relevant to the Department's mission of attracting and retaining businesses.
The bill's reduction in sales tax revenues significantly impacts the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund, which is a key funding source for the public education system overseen by MSDE.

MDH oversees public health services and local health departments. The bill's reduction of cannabis sales tax rates will decrease funding for the Cannabis Public Health Fund, which is managed under the department's regulatory purview.

The bill's reduction of the cannabis sales tax rate decreases revenue for the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, which supports community revitalization investments and municipal infrastructure projects managed by DHCD.

The bill repeals the sales and use tax on data or information technology services and software publishing. As the agency responsible for the state's IT strategy and digital services, these changes directly impact the economic environment of the technology sector.

MDOT is highly relevant because the bill alters distributions to the Transportation Trust Fund and affects the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, leading to a significant decrease in revenues for building and maintaining the state's transportation network.

The reduction in the corporate income tax rate reduces revenues distributed to the Higher Education Investment Fund, which MHEC uses to support statewide policies and financial aid programs for postsecondary education.

The Board (Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer) oversees significant state expenditures and fiscal integrity. The massive revenue loss proposed by this bill creates a significant fiscal challenge that the Board must monitor as the state's highest administrative body.

As the independent agency responsible for regulating the cannabis industry, MCA is directly impacted by the reduction of the cannabis sales and use tax rate from 12% to 3%, which reduces the revenue stream used to fund its operations and equity programs.

MEA manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which receives a portion of corporate income tax revenue. The bill's reduction of the corporate tax rate will impact SEIF funding for renewable energy and efficiency programs.

As a state-funded research university, Morgan State is impacted by the bill's changes to the corporate income tax, which funds the Higher Education Investment Fund, and the broader reduction in general fund revenue.

OLA is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits. The massive changes to tax collection and distribution proposed in this bill will require significant oversight and auditing to ensure financial accountability and legal compliance.
As a public college and independent unit of state government, the college is relevant due to the bill's significant impact on state general fund revenues, which support higher education institutions.

The USM is impacted by the bill's reduction of the corporate income tax rate, which directly decreases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund used to support the system's institutions and research.

Synopsis: Establishing a rebuttable presumption relating to the best interest of an alleged incapacitated or protected person in an action under the Act; authorizing a certain person to petition a certain court for reasonable visitation with a certain alleged incapacitated or protected person; authorizing the court to impose certain restrictions on a certain visitation; establishing a certain immunity from civil liability under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Family Law - Incapacitated or Protected Persons - Petition for Visitation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: This bill establishes a legal process allowing family members and other interested parties to petition the court for reasonable visitation with an adult who is alleged to be incapacitated or a protected person. It creates a rebuttable presumption that visitation with specific relatives is in the person's best interest, outlines court procedures for evaluating these petitions, and requires authorized decision makers to provide information regarding the person's location or funeral arrangements upon written request.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and authorized decision makers
stakeholders: Alleged incapacitated or protected adults, their spouses, adult children, adult grandchildren, parents, adult siblings, legal guardians, and health care facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. While the court may assess costs or sanctions related to visitation petitions, these are directed at the petitioners or parties interfering with visitation rather than the State, and no costs may be assessed against the incapacitated person.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new legal cause of action (a petition for visitation with an incapacitated adult) and establishes specific evidentiary standards and rebuttable presumptions that the court must apply. The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for supporting the judicial functions and policy implementations required by this legislation.

The bill impacts health care facilities (hospitals, nursing homes, hospices, and assisted living) regulated by the Department of Health. It also involves 'authorized decision makers' such as health care surrogates and agents under advance directives, which are governed by Health-General statutes overseen by this department.

The Department of Aging advocates for the rights and quality of life of older adults and individuals with disabilities. This bill directly addresses the social rights and visitation access for incapacitated adults, a population frequently served by the department and its network of Area Agencies on Aging.

Since incapacitated or protected persons often include individuals with disabilities, this bill is relevant to the department's mission of ensuring that state policies are inclusive and support community living and social engagement for people with disabilities.

DHS oversees Adult Protective Services and is involved in guardianship matters for vulnerable adults. While the bill excludes petitions where a public guardian is the authorized decision maker, the department is still a stakeholder in the legal framework surrounding the protection and rights of incapacitated adults.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Department of Aging regarding the new requirements, immunity provisions, and notification duties established by the bill for health facilities and authorized decision-makers.

The Register of Wills maintains records and provides administrative support for the courts regarding estates and guardianships. This bill relates to visitation for individuals who may already be under court-ordered guardianships managed in part by the Register's offices.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies (MDH, DHS, Aging) impacted by this bill and coordinates broad policy initiatives regarding the safety and rights of vulnerable Marylanders.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors legislation for any personnel or fiscal impacts on state agencies, even if the fiscal note indicates the impact is not material.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of a political subdivision to designate certain noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts.
Title: Economic Development - Tax Increment Financing - Noncontiguous Areas
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 536

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows local political subdivisions, including Baltimore City, to designate noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts for Tax Increment Financing (TIF). It defines a blighted area as one where a majority of buildings have declined in productivity because of obsolescence or depreciation to the point that repairs are no longer justified.
responsible_party: Local governing bodies of Maryland political subdivisions and Baltimore City
stakeholders: Local governments, property owners in blighted areas, and small businesses in the construction and development sectors
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local revenues and expenditures are expected to increase starting in fiscal 2027 as local governments utilize TIF bonds for noncontiguous blighted areas. Increased revenues will come from bond proceeds and eventually increased property tax revenues from redevelopment, while expenditures will cover project costs and debt service. Baltimore City is expected to have no impact as its charter already allows for noncontiguous TIF districts; however, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) is a quasi-governmental entity that provides financing and real estate development services. The fiscal note specifically mentions that local revenues from Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts may be pledged to debt issued by MEDCO, making them a primary vehicle for implementing the financing enabled by this bill.

The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is responsible for community revitalization and municipal infrastructure projects. TIF is a key tool for financing the infrastructure and revitalization of the 'blighted areas' defined and addressed in this legislation.

The Maryland Stadium Authority's mission includes economic development initiatives such as the removal of blight, specifically in Baltimore City. As this bill defines 'blighted areas' and expands TIF authority for such areas in political subdivisions including Baltimore City, it directly aligns with the Authority's revitalization work.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce oversees programs to attract and retain businesses. TIF is a major economic development tool, and the agency is listed as an information source for the fiscal analysis of this bill.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and land use planning. The authorization of noncontiguous development districts is a significant land-use planning change that affects how local jurisdictions manage growth and resource allocation.

TIF districts operate by 'freezing' a property tax base and collecting revenue on the 'incremental valuation.' Disputes regarding property assessments within these new noncontiguous blighted districts would be heard by the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from the final decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board. Cases involving property tax assessments and credits within these specialized development districts would ultimately fall under its jurisdiction.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies (such as Commerce and DHCD) that coordinate economic development policy and may be required to interpret the new statutory definitions of 'blighted area' and 'noncontiguous development districts.'

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a 'potential meaningful' impact on small businesses located in or adjacent to blighted areas that receive TIF-funded improvements. This office monitors socioeconomic procurement and business opportunities that may arise from such development projects.

The Rural Maryland Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's 18 rural counties. The expansion of TIF authority to noncontiguous blighted areas provides rural jurisdictions with a more flexible tool for regional economic development and community revitalization.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on community revitalization and sustainable development. The bill's focus on blighting and sustainable growth through TIF districts directly relates to the initiative's coordination of land use and resource conservation.

The Authority advises on the use of impact aid for revitalization in neighborhoods surrounding the Pimlico Race Course in Baltimore City. The expansion of TIF authority for noncontiguous blighted areas provides a potential additional mechanism for the community development projects they oversee.

Synopsis: Altering an exemption that allows an official of the Legislative Branch to accept a gift of food or beverages as part of a meal or reception to which a legislative unit is invited to instead allow an official of the Legislative Branch to accept a gift of food or beverages at a meal or reception to which all members of the General Assembly are invited and that was open to the public; altering the written invitation and registration report requirements a regulated lobbyist must meet under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Maryland Public Ethics Law - Officials of the Legislative Branch - Gifts of Food and Beverages
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland Public Ethics Law regarding gifts of food and beverages to Legislative Branch officials. It requires that for such a gift to be acceptable, all members of the General Assembly must be invited to the event and the event must be open to the public. Additionally, the bill extends the required notice period for lobbyists to register these events from 5 to 14 days and mandates that the Department of Legislative Services post event details on the General Assembly website within one business day of registration.
responsible_party: Maryland State Ethics Commission and the Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Members of the General Assembly, Legislative Branch officials and employees, and regulated lobbyists.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $50,000 in fiscal 2027 only for the State Ethics Commission to update its electronic lobbying reporting and training systems. The cost is split evenly between the general fund ($25,000) and the Lobbyist Registration Fund ($25,000 in special funds). There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Ethics Commission (MSEC) is the primary agency responsible for administering and enforcing the Maryland Public Ethics Law. This bill directly alters regulations concerning gifts to legislative officials and requires MSEC to update its electronic lobbyist reporting and training systems, resulting in a noted fiscal impact of $50,000 for IT services.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes criminal offenses related to the integrity of state officials and the electoral process, including violations of public ethics laws. Changes to the legal exemptions for gifts of food and beverages for legislative officials fall under their investigative and prosecutorial purview.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal representative for the State and provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies. They would be responsible for providing legal interpretations of these changes to the Public Ethics Law and ensuring statutory compliance.

The Office of Legislative Audits (OLA) is responsible for ensuring financial accountability and legal compliance within the state government. New reporting and gift-acceptance requirements for legislative branch officials would be subject to OLA's oversight and auditing processes to ensure compliance with the modified law.

As the principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management oversees state budget development and execution. The fiscal note indicates an expenditure increase for the State Ethics Commission to implement IT changes necessitated by this bill, which requires DBM coordination.

Synopsis: Establishing qualifications for an individual to be appointed by a court as a custody evaluator; and authorizing a court to waive certain requirements for a court employee or an individual under contract with the court under certain circumstances.
Title: Family Law - Child Custody Evaluators - Qualifications
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Physicians -see also- MedExmnrs; Pediatr; Psychiatrists etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes specific qualifications and training requirements for individuals appointed by a court as custody evaluators in contested custody and visitation cases. It requires evaluators to hold specific professional licenses (such as in psychiatry, psychology, or clinical social work), complete a training program approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts, and demonstrate knowledge in topics like domestic violence and child development. Additionally, the bill prohibits courts from requiring a party to pay for an assessment without providing notice and an opportunity to object.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and State Circuit Courts
stakeholders: Children in contested custody cases, parents and guardians involved in custody litigation, and professional custody evaluators including physicians, psychologists, and social workers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) to establish guidelines for training programs for court-appointed custody evaluators and supports the Judiciary in implementing these new qualification standards.

The bill specifies that custody evaluators must be licensed professionals, including psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, and counselors, all of whom are regulated by various boards under the Department of Health.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and state agencies regarding the implementation of new statutory requirements and would be involved in interpreting the legal standards for evaluator qualifications.

DHS is the primary state provider for child welfare services; the bill's focus on child custody, neglect, abuse, and the safety of children in contested cases directly aligns with the agency's mission.
The bill requires that custody evaluators demonstrate knowledge and experience in disability-related issues, which is a core area of focus for this department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that evaluators be trained in domestic violence and child abuse, topics which the GOCPP coordinates as part of its public safety and victim services strategies.
This office coordinates efforts to promote the well-being and safety of children, making the standards for custody evaluations relevant to its broader policy goals.

Synopsis: Establishing that engaging in sexual contact with another without the consent of the other in connection with a first-, second-, or third- degree burglary constitutes sexual offense in the third degree; and altering the definitions of "tier I sex offender", "tier II sex offender", and "tier III sex offender" applicable to provisions relating to sex offender registration to include certain acts constituting sexual offense in the third degree.
Title: Criminal Law - Third-Degree Sexual Offense - Burglary
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill establishes that engaging in non-consensual sexual contact with another person during the commission of a first-, second-, or third-degree burglary is a third-degree sexual offense. It also updates sex offender registration requirements, classifying these offenders into Tier I, Tier II, or Tier III based on the victim's age.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual offenses or burglary, victims of such crimes, Maryland law enforcement agencies, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates a potential minimal increase in State expenditures due to enhanced incarceration penalties and changes in sex offender classifications. Local revenues may see a minimal decrease because third-degree sexual offenses do not carry the fines associated with the fourth-degree offenses they may replace in some cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the enforcement of state laws and the coordination of criminal justice policy, and is responsible for signing the bill into law.
The OAG represents the state in all civil and criminal appeals, which may include cases prosecuted under the newly defined third-degree sexual offense felony.
DBM oversees the state's budget and personnel; the fiscal note indicates a potential minimal increase in state expenditures due to enhanced incarceration penalties.
The bill updates sex offender registry tiers based on whether victims are minors, which impacts safety policies and reporting standards within the state's public education system.
DHS provides protective services for children and may be involved in the care and advocacy of minor victims of the sexual offenses addressed in the bill.
DJS is responsible for youth involved in the justice system; the bill applies to offenses that may involve juvenile offenders or minor victims.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a primary implementing agency as it manages the state's correctional facilities where offenders will serve sentences and oversees the Division of Parole and Probation, which monitors registered sex offenders.
The GOC coordinates statewide efforts to promote the well-being of children and families; the bill's provisions regarding minor victims align with its mission to protect vulnerable youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, including the development of policies for sexual offense and burglary crimes.
The AOC supports the judicial branch where cases involving these new felony classifications and enhanced penalties will be adjudicated in Circuit Court.

MCSS focuses on coordinated approaches to school safety and the safety of minors; the bill's changes to sex offender classifications for crimes involving minor victims are relevant to its safety mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants charged with the felony offenses established or reclassified by this bill.
MSP is the primary law enforcement agency responsible for criminal investigation and the maintenance of the state's Sex Offender Registry, which is directly altered by the bill's tier definitions.
The Secretary of State manages the 'Safe at Home' address confidentiality program for victims of domestic violence and sexual crimes, who may be impacted by the offenses covered in this bill.
The team focuses on enhancing economic mobility and addressing child poverty, and it has a broad interest in the safety and outcomes of children who may be victims of the offenses described.

Synopsis: Establishing November 11 as a tax-free day each year during which an exemption from the sales and use tax is provided for sales to certain veterans if the taxable price of the item for sale is less than $250.00; and requiring an individual, in order to qualify for the exemption, to provide to the vendor evidence of eligibility for the exemption.
Title: Sales and Use Tax - Tax-Free Day - Veterans' Day
Status: In the Senate - Third Reading Passed (43-0)
bill_summary: This bill establishes an annual sales and use tax-free day in Maryland for veterans, occurring on the Saturday preceding Veterans' Day starting in 2026. Under the provided bill text, the exemption applies to items with a taxable price of less than $100, though the fiscal note suggests an amended limit of $250. To qualify, a veteran must provide evidence of eligibility, such as a government-issued identification card with a veteran notation. The Comptroller is authorized to suspend the tax-free day at their sole discretion.
stakeholders: Maryland veterans and retail vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is estimated to reduce state general fund revenues by $30,600 and Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund revenues by $4,200 in FY 2027, for a total state revenue decrease of $34,800. These revenue decreases are projected to grow slightly in subsequent years based on forecasted sales and use tax growth. The bill has no impact on state expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and is responsible for administering the sales and use tax. The bill explicitly grants the Comptroller the sole discretion to suspend the established tax-free day.
As the primary agency for veterans in Maryland, this bill directly impacts their constituent population by providing a targeted tax benefit on Veterans' Day.

The bill specifies that a valid driver's license or government-issued identification card with a veteran notation serves as evidence of eligibility. The MVA is responsible for issuing these licenses and managing those notations.
DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. The bill results in a decrease in general fund revenues, which impacts the state budget that DBM manages.
The fiscal note indicates a decrease in revenue for the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which is the primary funding mechanism for the educational reforms overseen by MSDE.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding the implementation of the new tax law and the exercise of the Comptroller's discretionary authority to suspend the tax-free day.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies implementing the tax changes and must sign the legislation into law.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to hold an election for a vacant elected board member position that occurs 55 days or more before the candidate filing deadline for a certain election; requiring each county board and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to appoint a replacement for a vacant elected board member position that occurs 54 days or less before a certain candidate filing deadline for a certain election; etc.
Title: County Boards of Education and Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners - Vacancy Procedures - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill standardizes the procedures for filling vacancies on local boards of education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners across Maryland, replacing various local methods with a uniform statewide process. It requires vacancies for elected positions occurring early in a term to be filled by election at the next general election, while vacancies occurring later or with no qualified candidates are filled by board appointment following specific public requirements such as advertising the vacancy and conducting livestreamed interviews. Appointed member vacancies must be filled within 60 days using existing appointment methods.
responsible_party: Maryland County Boards of Education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners
stakeholders: Current and future members of Maryland local boards of education, candidates for school board positions, and Maryland voters.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. It establishes a uniform statewide administrative process for filling school board vacancies, replacing various local procedures without significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the governance and vacancy-filling procedures of the 24 local boards of education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, which are under the leadership and oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

The bill mandates that vacancies for elected board members occurring before certain deadlines be filled via special elections conducted in accordance with the Election Law Article, which the State Board of Elections is responsible for supervising and administering.

The bill standardizes and alters the vacancy-filling process for school boards across the state, many of which currently grant the Governor direct appointment power. This represents a significant shift in executive appointment authority.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recommending candidates for state-level positions. Standardizing the vacancy process for local school boards directly impacts this office's workflow for boards where the Governor currently holds appointment authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically repeals or modifies the functions of several existing local school board nominating commissions, such as those in Baltimore County, Washington County, and Wicomico County.

As the chief legal representative for the state, the OAG would be involved in providing legal counsel regarding the implementation of standardized vacancy procedures and ensuring compliance with the new statutory requirements across multiple jurisdictions.

Synopsis: Providing collective bargaining rights to certain graduate assistants  at certain public institutions of higher education; defining "graduate assistant" as a graduate student at the University of Maryland, College Park or the University of Maryland, Baltimore County who is a teaching, administrative, or research assistant or in a comparable position, a fellow, or a postdoctoral intern; and establishing a separate collective bargaining unit for the graduate assistants.
Title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Graduate Assistants
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 774

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants collective bargaining rights to graduate assistants, including teaching, administrative, and research assistants, as well as fellows and postdoctoral interns, at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP) and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). It establishes separate collective bargaining units for these employees and tasks the Public Employee Relations Board with overseeing the bargaining process, including the certification of employee organizations.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board, University of Maryland, College Park, University of Maryland, Baltimore County, and the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Graduate students at UMCP and UMBC serving as teaching, administrative, or research assistants, fellows, or postdoctoral interns.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for UMCP and UMBC will increase minimally beginning in FY 2029 to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) for collective bargaining expenses. Administrative and personnel expenditures at these institutions may also increase if negotiations result in higher salaries or fringe benefits for the approximately 3,600 eligible individuals. Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for PERB will increase minimally as elections and disputes occur.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates PERB as the regulatory body responsible for overseeing the new collective bargaining units, administering elections for exclusive representatives, and adjudicating disputes.
USM is the primary administrative entity for UMCP and UMBC, the specific institutions where graduate assistants are granted collective bargaining rights under the bill.
As the central personnel and fiscal agency, DBM oversees state personnel policies and the budget execution impacted by negotiated salary and benefit increases.
This agency coordinates statewide policies for public universities and ensures institutions adhere to financial and academic standards which may be influenced by collective bargaining.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including PERB and the public universities, regarding the implementation of the new collective bargaining laws.
Morgan State University is explicitly named in the bill's amendments to the statutory structure requiring the creation of separate bargaining units for eligible graduate assistants.
The college is explicitly included in the bill's provisions requiring higher education institutions to establish separate bargaining units for graduate assistants.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies involved and is responsible for the final approval and policy coordination of the legislation.
The Board oversees significant state expenditures and contracts, which may be impacted by the fiscal outcomes of collective bargaining agreements at state institutions.
The department enforces labor laws and manages workforce development, providing the broader regulatory context for the expansion of collective bargaining rights.
As the state's principal tax collector and payroll officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the administration of state employee payments and revenue tracking.
The agency manages retirement benefits for state higher education employees, which may be subject to change through the collective bargaining process.

Synopsis: Specifying that the amount of earnings withholding or a wage withholding order for child support may not exceed 25% of the obligor's disposable earnings under certain circumstances; requiring an earnings withholding order or earnings withholding notice sent to an obligor's employer to include information on certain limits on earnings withholding; and authorizing an employee to contest the amount of an earnings withholding order based on certain limits.
Title: Child Support - Earnings Withholdings Limits
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill limits child support earnings or wage withholding to no more than 25% of an obligor's disposable earnings if the obligor's individual income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines. These limits apply unless the obligor was determined to be voluntarily impoverished in their most recent court order. The bill also requires withholding notices to employers to include these limits and allows employees to contest withholdings that exceed them.
responsible_party: Child Support Administration of the Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Child support obligors with individual incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines, employers processing wage withholdings, child support recipients, and the Maryland Department of Human Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general and federal fund expenditures increase by at least 3,810,749 dollars in FY 2027 for one-time programming costs to update the Child Support Management System and for at least 10 additional staff members to handle manual calculations and notices. Future year expenditures are estimated at approximately 800,000 dollars annually. Federal fund matching revenues will increase accordingly. There is a potential reduction in child support collections, which could affect federal performance incentive payments. Local circuit court operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Small businesses may experience increased administrative workloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department's Child Support Administration (CSA) is the primary agency responsible for managing child support services, issuing earnings withholding notices, and calculating the new 25% cap on disposable earnings based on federal poverty guidelines.

The bill explicitly designates the Office of Administrative Hearings as the venue for employees to appeal the results of an investigation by the Child Support Administration regarding withholding contests.

The bill modifies the requirements for earnings withholding orders issued by the Judiciary, requiring courts to ensure that support and arrearage totals do not exceed the newly established limits for low-income obligors.

As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the budgetary and staffing changes required to implement the bill, including the estimated need for at least 10 to 29 new caseworker positions at the Department of Human Services.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Child Support Administration regarding the interpretation and enforcement of new withholding limits and represents the state in related legal proceedings.

The bill requires significant one-time programming changes to the statewide Child Support Management System to automate the calculation of withholding caps and update notice formats, which falls under DoIT's strategic and infrastructure oversight.
The Department of Labor administers unemployment insurance benefits, which are defined in the bill as 'earnings' subject to child support withholding and the newly established limits.
The agency administers pensions and disability benefits, which are included in the bill's definition of 'earnings' from which child support may be withheld subject to the 25% cap.
The Commission adjudicates worker's compensation payments, which are defined as 'earnings' subject to the bill's withholding limits and administrative contest procedures.

The bill directly impacts child support collections and the disposable income of low-income families, which are central factors in the office's mission to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility.
The team is tasked with identifying and testing strategies to reduce child poverty; the bill's changes to child support withholding for low-income obligors are directly relevant to this policy area.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission and the Maryland Energy Administration jointly, in consultation with neighboring states, to study the benefits and costs of, and make recommendations on, potential options for certain actions with regard to withdrawing from the PJM Interconnection, LLC capacity market model, developing a certain multistate compact, withdrawing from PJM Interconnection, LLC, and establishing or joining an alternative regional transmission organization; etc.
Title: Electric Company Contracts, Capacity Market Models, and Regional Transmission Organizations - Studies
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Public Service Commission (PSC), in consultation with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), to study the benefits and costs of requiring electric companies to contract for at least 80% of their load-serving capacity over a five-year period. It also requires PSC and MEA to jointly study the implications of withdrawing from the PJM Interconnection, LLC capacity market model or the regional transmission organization entirely, including options for forming a multistate compact or joining an alternative organization. A report with findings and recommendations is due to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland electricity ratepayers, electric utility companies, PJM Interconnection, LLC, and neighboring states
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $600,000 in fiscal 2027 only to hire consultants to perform the required studies and report. Special fund revenues increase by an identical amount through assessments imposed on regulated public service companies. The bill does not materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission to lead studies on electric company capacity contracts and the costs and benefits of withdrawing from PJM Interconnection. The fiscal note also identifies a $600,000 special fund impact on the Commission for hiring consultants.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Energy Administration to consult with and jointly conduct studies with the Public Service Commission regarding electric load-serving capacity and regional transmission organization alternatives.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the state's advocate for residential utility consumers. Since the bill's primary justification is PJM’s failure to address electricity affordability and ratepayer impacts, the results of these studies directly involve the agency's core mission.

The bill specifically explores withdrawing from PJM Interconnection (an interstate regional transmission organization) and potentially developing a new multistate compact or joining a different interstate RTO.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the PSC and MEA. Withdrawing from a federally-regulated regional transmission organization and establishing a multistate compact would require extensive legal analysis and representation.

The bill requires the joint report of findings and recommendations to be submitted to the Governor. Additionally, the Governor oversees the agencies responsible for the study and manages intergovernmental relations.

Electricity capacity and regional transmission organization policies significantly impact the state's ability to meet climate commitments and environmental quality standards, which are regulated by the Department of the Environment.

The Secretary of State is involved in the coordination of international and interstate affairs and serves as a custodian for official records, including state laws and potentially interstate compacts mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide additional operating funds for the Antitrust Division of the Office of the Attorney General; requiring that certain civil penalties, damages, attorney's fees, and costs awarded to the State be credited to the Fund; and requiring, for fiscal years 2028 through 2033, that the Governor include in the annual budget bill a certain appropriation to the Fund.
Title: Commercial Law – Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund – Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 144 establishes the Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide additional operating resources for the Antitrust Division of the Office of the Attorney General. The fund is composed of civil penalties, damages, and legal fees recovered from Maryland Antitrust Act violations, which were previously directed to the state's General Fund. Additionally, the bill mandates a budget appropriation from fiscal 2028 through 2033 sufficient to fund one new full-time investigator position.
responsible_party: Antitrust Division of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General; businesses and individuals subject to the Maryland Antitrust Act; the State of Maryland General Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a decrease in General Fund revenues as civil penalties and legal recoveries (estimated at $180,000 for FY 2027) are diverted to the newly created Fair Pricing and Market Competition Special Fund. State special fund expenditures will increase to support the Antitrust Division, specifically for a mandated full-time investigator position costing an estimated $107,588 in FY 2028. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of the Attorney General by establishing the Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund to support its Antitrust Division and mandating the creation of a new full-time investigator position within that division.
The bill contains a mandated appropriation requiring the Governor to include funding for a specific investigator position in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2033.

As the state's principal personnel and budget agency, DBM is responsible for the creation of the new Position Identification Number (PIN) for the investigator and overseeing the execution of the mandated budget appropriation.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund separately and managing the investment of the fund's money.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the new Fair Pricing and Market Competition Fund, including tracking revenue from civil penalties and other sources.

Synopsis: Requiring and authorizing the State Administrator of Elections to take certain actions if the State Administrator receives a credible report that election misinformation or election disinformation, including a deepfake, has been or is being communicated, disseminated, or distributed; requiring the Administrator to communicate accurate information to the public; and prohibiting a person, under certain circumstances, from knowingly or with reckless disregard using or disseminating a deepfake to produce materially false information.
Title: Election Law - Election Misinformation, Election Disinformation, and Deepfakes
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill establishes regulations and prohibitions concerning election misinformation, disinformation, and the use of deepfakes. It requires the Maryland State Administrator of Elections to disseminate accurate information to correct credible reports of election misinformation or disinformation and authorizes the Administrator to seek injunctions to remove such content from online platforms. Additionally, the bill prohibits the use of generative artificial intelligence or digital technology to create deepfakes intended to influence voters or misrepresent election facts, establishing criminal penalties for violations and allowing the State Board of Elections to seek civil damages and cost recovery.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and the State Administrator of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, political candidates, campaigns, political action committees, and online information platforms.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues (Fair Campaign Financing Fund) and general fund revenues may increase starting in FY 2027 due to criminal fines of up to $5,000 per violation and the recovery of costs through civil actions. State expenditures are not expected to be materially affected as the State Board of Elections already monitors and corrects misinformation. Local government finances are not expected to be significantly impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) and its State Administrator are the primary implementing authorities for the bill. They are responsible for maintaining a reporting portal, issuing corrective information, seeking injunctions, and filing civil actions against entities that disseminate election misinformation or disinformation.

The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Elections to refer material from the reporting portal to the State Prosecutor as necessary. Additionally, the agency is responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process, which aligns with the bill's focus on deepfakes and disinformation.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides counsel to the State Board of Elections and would represent the State Administrator in seeking injunctions or filing civil actions for damages authorized under the bill.

The bill creates new civil causes of action and criminal penalties (misdemeanors) that will be adjudicated through the state's judicial system. The Judiciary will handle filings for injunctions, civil damages, and criminal trials related to deepfake violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense for the creation or dissemination of deepfakes with intent to influence an election. The Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for representing indigent individuals charged with this new criminal offense.

As a state agency that functions as a broadcaster (MPT), the Commission is subject to the bill's provisions regarding deceptive deepfakes in broadcasts and the specific exemptions provided for news interviews, newscasts, and required candidate advertisements.

The fiscal note indicates that criminal fines collected under the bill are distributed to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. The State Treasurer's Office is the custodian of state funds and responsible for their management and distribution.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and the State Board of Elections. The bill grants significant new enforcement and communication powers to an executive official (the State Administrator of Elections) within the Governor's purview.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved in monitoring the state's budget and revenues; the bill is expected to generate new fine and civil damage revenues for the state.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord of property that is served by an on-site wastewater system to ensure, on or before July 1, 2028, and before each new tenant occupies the property thereafter, that the system has been inspected and pumped out in a certain manner; requiring a delegated approval authority to approve, to the extent practicable, the repair or replacement of any failed components of a drain field of a failing on-site wastewater system; extending certain dates; etc.
Title: Environment - On-Site Wastewater Systems - Requirements for Inspection and Pumping Services and Implementation Dates
Status: In the Senate - Senate Refuses to Recede

bill_summary: This bill extends the deadlines for the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations regarding on-site wastewater professionals and for those professionals to become licensed. It also mandates that, starting July 1, 2028, landlords of properties with septic systems must ensure the systems are inspected and pumped before a new tenant moves in, and requires similar inspection and pumping provisions in real estate sales contracts.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals
stakeholders: Landlords of properties with septic systems, real estate buyers and sellers, on-site wastewater service professionals, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues may be affected as early as FY 2027 due to delays in licensing fees, but the impact cannot be reliably estimated. Local governments may experience increased administrative costs and fee revenues; for example, Prince George's County estimates annual expenditures of $100,000 and revenue increases of $17,000 resulting from new inspection and permit requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, as it oversees the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals and is tasked with adopting the necessary regulations for the on-site wastewater industry.

The bill defines and tasks 'delegated approval authorities,' which are typically local health departments (LHDs) overseen by the Maryland Department of Health, with receiving failure notifications and approving repairs or replacements of failing septic systems.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment for regulation development and may be involved in consumer protection enforcement related to the bill's new septic system requirements for landlords and real estate contracts.

The bill establishes new mandatory provisions for real estate sales and rental agreements, which could lead to increased litigation and contract disputes that the judicial branch would be responsible for adjudicating.

Synopsis: Repealing a termination provision relating to provisions of law establishing a nonprofit organizations navigator within the Department of Commerce.
Title: Nonprofit Organizations Navigator - Termination Provision - Repeal
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the termination provision for the nonprofit organizations navigator position within the Department of Commerce, effectively making the position and its duties permanent. The navigator provides technical assistance to nonprofit organizations for state grant applications, helps resolve procedural delays in the grant-making process, shares information on grant opportunities, and represents nonprofit interests on the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council.
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $92,200 in FY 2028 to convert the existing contractual nonprofit organizations navigator position to a permanent, regular position. This cost is projected to increase annually, reaching approximately $105,300 by FY 2031. No fiscal impact is expected in FY 2027 because the position is already funded contractually through that fiscal year. There is no impact on local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the nonprofit organizations navigator within the Department of Commerce and repeals the termination provision for this position, making it a permanent role within the agency with specific technical assistance and reporting requirements.

The nonprofit organizations navigator's duties, which include providing technical assistance for grants and resolving grant-making complexities, directly overlap and coordinate with the mission of the Governor's Grants Office to manage federal grant information and assist organizations.

The fiscal note indicates a direct impact on general fund expenditures and the need to convert a contractual position into a regular state position, which falls under DBM's responsibility for budget development and personnel management.
As the primary executive unit for community engagement and nonprofit partnerships, GOCI's mission is highly relevant to the navigator's role in supporting and advocating for nonprofit organizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the navigator to serve as a member of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application (MEGA) Council, which is a body categorized under this entity.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments involved (Commerce and DBM) and coordinates policy initiatives related to state efficiency and support for nonprofits.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from engaging in certain surveillance-based price setting; making a certain violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice that is subject to enforcement and penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; and prohibiting an employer from engaging in certain surveillance-based wage setting.
Title: Consumer Protection and Labor and Employment - Surveillance-Based Price and Wage Setting - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits businesses and employers from using surveillance data and automated decision systems to set customized prices for goods and services or customized wages for employees. It classifies surveillance-based price setting as an unfair or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act and empowers the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to investigate complaints related to surveillance-based wage setting.
responsible_party: The Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry) and the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, employees, job applicants, and businesses or employers utilizing automated pricing or wage systems
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures increase by $349,400 in fiscal 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Labor to hire 3.5 total staff members (technologists, investigators, and assistant Attorneys General) to handle enforcement and technical investigations. Annual costs are projected to rise to $468,800 by fiscal 2031. The bill is not expected to have a material impact on local government finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) is a primary implementing agency for this bill. The bill classifies surveillance-based price setting as an unfair trade practice subject to the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the OAG's Consumer Protection Division enforces. Additionally, the Attorney General is authorized to bring civil actions for violations of the surveillance-based wage setting prohibitions.

The Maryland Department of Labor, specifically the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, is tasked with investigating complaints regarding surveillance-based wage setting and taking enforcement actions, including mediation or referring cases to the Attorney General.

The bill's definitions of 'Artificial Intelligence' and surveillance-based technologies are tied to the state's technical strategy and existing IT policies managed by DoIT. DoIT also supports the Governor's AI Subcabinet, which oversees state AI enablement and study roadmaps mentioned in the fiscal analysis.

The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch, including the Governor's AI Subcabinet which governs the use and assessment of AI systems in the state, directly overlapping with the bill's focus on automated decision systems.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and resources. The bill's prohibition on surveillance-based wage setting applies to the State as an employer, necessitating DBM oversight of state agency pay practices.

As the state's primary economic development and business advocacy agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by new regulations on how Maryland businesses set prices for consumer goods and services and how they manage wage setting.

The bill explicitly states that its protections do not diminish the rights of employees to collectively bargain over terms and conditions of employment. PERB, which centralizes labor relations for state and public sector employees, would oversee disputes or bargaining issues arising from these new wage-setting regulations.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. Enforcement actions taken by the Department of Labor or consumer protection disputes may be referred to OAH for impartial hearings and findings of fact.

The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judiciary. The bill creates new grounds for civil actions and refers to an AI Evidence Clinic Pilot Program in the courts to handle specialized technological evidence.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill and its fiscal note reference the Workgroup on AI Implementation and the Governor's AI Subcabinet, which are advisory bodies composed of public servants and experts tasked with recommending AI policies and monitoring state implementation.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipal corporation to designate assistant fire marshals with the approval of the State Fire Marshal or to request that the State Fire Marshal designate certain fire marshals and requiring the State Fire Marshal to adopt certain regulations governing the qualifications, training, standards, and certification of designees; requiring, by October 1, 2026, the installation of certain automatic fire sprinklers in certain high-rise residential buildings; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the installation of automatic fire sprinklers and other fire safety equipment in residential rental high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovations starting October 1, 2026. It also establishes a licensing and regulatory program for fire alarm system technicians and companies and sets new standards, training, and certification requirements for assistant State fire marshals designated by local governments.
responsible_party: State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission
stakeholders: Owners and tenants of residential rental high-rise buildings, fire alarm system technicians, fire alarm system companies, local governments, and the Office of the State Fire Marshal.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $311,100 in FY 2027 for hiring three administrative staff members, IT system upgrades for licensing, and NFPA certification for Office of the State Fire Marshal employees. Annual expenditures are projected to be between $231,400 and $264,500 in subsequent years. General fund revenues will increase from new licensing fees for fire alarm system technicians. Local government expenditures will increase to cover training and certification for assistant fire marshals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (MSP) houses the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission, which are the primary entities responsible for implementation, regulation, and enforcement of the fire safety standards and technician licensing programs created by the bill.

The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the state budget, requiring the addition of three new administrative positions and funding for information technology upgrades, which falls under DBM’s oversight of personnel and fiscal planning.

The OAG will provide essential legal counsel to the State Fire Prevention Commission and the State Fire Marshal in drafting the new regulations and establishing the licensing and enforcement procedures mandated by the bill.
The bill regulates fire safety in residential rental high-rise properties, which aligns with the department's mission to ensure safe and secure housing for Maryland residents.

The fiscal note indicates that the University System of Maryland may face substantial costs (estimated at $2 million) to upgrade older high-rise residential housing facilities (dormitories) to comply with the new fire safety and sprinkler requirements if they undergo substantial renovation.

As a state-governed university with residential high-rise facilities, Morgan State University may be impacted by the new requirements for automatic fire sprinklers and safety equipment in the event of substantial renovations to its dormitories.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland operates residential facilities that may be subject to the bill's updated high-rise fire safety standards during future renovations.

DGS is responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of state-owned facilities. It would be involved in overseeing the installation of mandated fire safety equipment for any state-owned residential high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovation.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues, including the new licensing fees for fire alarm system technicians and companies established under the bill.

The Commission coordinates policy for Maryland's higher education institutions, many of which own residential high-rise buildings that are specifically identified as being potentially impacted by this legislation.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and the State Fire Marshal. The office is responsible for coordinating the policy initiatives and regulatory changes proposed in this bill.

Synopsis: Proposing amendments to the Maryland Constitution relating to the selection and tenure of circuit court judges; altering the method of filling vacancies in the office of a judge of a circuit court; providing for retention elections following an appointment to fill a vacancy in the office of a judge of a circuit court; providing for a transitional period during which the terms of certain amendments are to become effective; and submitting this amendment to the qualified voters of the State for their adoption or rejection.
