bill_summary: This bill repeals the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP), which is a program jointly administered by the Motor Vehicle Administration and the Maryland Department of the Environment that requires biennial emissions testing and equipment inspections for most motor vehicles of model year 1977 and newer registered in specified Maryland jurisdictions.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE)
stakeholders: Maryland vehicle owners in participating counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, and Washington) and Baltimore City, small businesses with vehicle fleets, and State agencies (MVA and MDE) responsible for program administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues will decrease by approximately 46500000 in FY 2027 and 67100000 in FY 2031 due to the loss of inspection and late fees. TTF expenditures are estimated to decrease by 14500000 in FY 2027 and 19300000 annually thereafter because of the elimination of vendor contracts and 21 administrative positions. The total net impact is a fiscal loss of 32000000 in FY 2027, increasing to 47800000 by FY 2031. Additional unquantified impacts include potential federal penalties for non-compliance with the Clean Air Act, costs for early contract termination, and one-time revenues from the sale of testing station property. There is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary agency responsible for administering the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) in collaboration with MDE. The bill repeals this program, impacting 10 MVA positions and the agency's operational functions, including fee collection and contract management.

MDOT is the parent department of the MVA. The bill results in a multi-million dollar revenue loss for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and impacts the department's bond coverage and net income test policy limits.

MDE is the primary agency responsible for the technical standards and joint administration of the VEIP. The repeal affects 11 MDE positions and eliminates the agency's role in setting emissions standards for the program.

DBM is responsible for state personnel and fiscal planning. The bill eliminates 21 state positions and causes a significant long-term decrease in both revenues and expenditures for the Transportation Trust Fund.
The Treasurer manages state funds and bond issuances. The fiscal note explicitly mentions that the loss of revenue from VEIP impacts MDOT's bond coverage and policy limits regarding debt service.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state contracts and property. The bill necessitates the termination of a major five-year VEIP service contract and the potential sale of state-owned testing facility real estate.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates environmental protection efforts. Repealing the VEIP is a major change to Maryland's air quality and emissions reduction strategy, impacting the state's broader environmental goals.

The OAG will likely provide legal counsel regarding the repeal, specifically concerning compliance with the federal Clean Air Act and potential penalties related to the State Implementation Plan (SIP).

The Comptroller oversees state financial integrity and revenues. The repeal removes a significant revenue stream and involves the termination of a large state contract, which the Comptroller reviews as a member of the Board of Public Works.
DGS manages state-owned facilities and real estate. The fiscal note mentions the potential sale of property and capital assets at testing stations currently owned by the state.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill may require the early termination of a multi-year vendor contract, it increases the likelihood of bid protests or contract disputes that would fall under the MSBCA's jurisdiction.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy shift and the associated budgetary changes resulting from the repeal of a major state regulatory program.

OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance and program performance audits. The closure of a major program involving property sales, contract terminations, and substantial revenue loss will be a subject of future audit focus.

DoIT oversees statewide IT strategies. The repeal of VEIP will require the decommissioning of digital infrastructure, notice systems, and data management platforms used by MVA and MDE for program compliance.

VEIP is part of Maryland's State Implementation Plan (SIP) for air quality. Repealing it impacts Maryland's standing and compliance with interstate environmental agreements and compacts related to ozone and air pollution.

The MTA is a modal administration under MDOT that relies on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF). The significant loss of VEIP revenue into the TTF affects the overall funding available for transit operations and capital projects.

The MAA is a modal administration under MDOT funded by the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF). The loss of multi-million dollar fee revenues into the TTF impacts the department's consolidated fiscal planning.

The MPA is a modal administration under MDOT. The fiscal note indicates that the revenue loss from VEIP repeal forces MDOT to adjust its six-year program, which affects all modal administrations relying on the TTF.
The SHA is an MDOT agency funded via the TTF. The significant revenue reduction in the TTF caused by this bill impacts the department's ability to fund highway construction and maintenance.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from utilizing certain personal identifying information or engaging in certain conduct in order to cause physical injury, serious emotional distress, or economic damages; prohibiting a person from using certain artificial intelligence or certain deepfake representations for certain purposes; providing penalties of 5 years of imprisonment and a fine of up to $10,000 or both where one victim is involved, and for two or more victims the term of imprisonment is up to 10 years and the fine is up to $15,000 or both; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Identity Fraud - Artificial Intelligence and Deepfake Representations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands the state's identity fraud laws to prohibit the use of personal identifying information, artificial intelligence, and deepfake representations to cause physical, emotional, or economic harm. It specifically criminalizes the use of deepfakes to impersonate or defraud others, establishes tiered criminal penalties based on the value and number of victims involved, and creates a civil cause of action for victims to seek injunctive or other appropriate relief.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, victims of identity fraud, law enforcement agencies, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note states that the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While the Office of the Public Defender indicated potential workload increases, the Department of Legislative Services concluded that any increased effort could be managed with existing budgeted resources. Specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to investigate and prosecute violations of the new identity fraud provisions involving artificial intelligence and deepfakes.
The bill grants the Department of State Police primary authority to initiate investigations and enforce these new identity fraud laws throughout the State without jurisdictional limitations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of new criminal offenses (both felonies and misdemeanors) related to AI and deepfake identity fraud will directly impact the workload of the Office of the Public Defender, as noted in the fiscal note.
The bill creates new criminal offenses and a new civil cause of action for victims of deepfake impersonation, requiring the Judicial Branch to handle these additional cases and legal proceedings.

The bill specifically grants investigative authority to the Maryland Transportation Authority Police, Maryland Port Administration Police, and Maryland Aviation Administration Police for these crimes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for correctional facilities, DPSCS will be impacted by the potential increase in the prison population due to the new felony and misdemeanor penalties established by the bill.

The bill incorporates the definition of 'Artificial Intelligence' from the State Finance and Procurement Article, which is under the policy purview of DoIT, and addresses emerging technology-based crimes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement; this bill's expansion of the identity fraud statute aligns with their role in advising on criminal justice policy.

Synopsis: Adding to the circumstances under which an individual who creates a trust for the benefit of the individual's spouse may not be considered the settlor of the trust with regard to the individual's interest in the trust.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Spousal Lifetime Access Trusts
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Judiciary; Withdrawn
bill_summary: This bill expands the legal protections for certain spousal trusts, specifically Spousal Lifetime Access Trusts (SLATs). It provides that an individual who creates an irrevocable trust for their spouse is not considered the settlor of that trust for creditor purposes if they later become a beneficiary through a power of appointment. This designation protects the trust's assets and income from being seized or attached by the original creator's creditors.
stakeholders: Trust settlors, spouses of settlors, beneficiaries of irrevocable trusts, and legal creditors.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. The bill clarifies estate and trust law regarding creditor access to trust assets, which primarily affects private legal interests. There are no explicitly stated financial mandates or revenue changes for state or local governments, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is relevant because the bill modifies the Estates and Trusts Article, which governs the legal interpretation of trusts and creditor rights—matters frequently adjudicated in the state's courts.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. Since the bill concerns the legal status of trust settlors and mentions the reimbursement of taxes on trust income or principal, it may have implications for the administration and collection of state income or inheritance taxes.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel on the interpretation of state laws. This bill makes substantive changes to the Estates and Trusts Article regarding the definition of a trust settlor and creditor protection, requiring legal oversight.

The Register of Wills is the primary state agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. Changes to the classification of trust settlors and spousal trusts directly impact estate administration and tax liability assessments under their jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow statewide a person to hunt deer on Sundays throughout the deer bow hunting season and to hunt turkey using a bow and arrow on Sundays throughout the turkey hunting season.
Title: Natural Resources - Bow Hunting - Sundays
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to allow bow hunting for deer and turkey on Sundays throughout their respective hunting seasons statewide in Maryland.
stakeholders: Bow hunters, small businesses (including outfitters and equipment retailers), farmers, and residents in areas with significant deer or turkey populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. However, it may have a meaningful economic impact on small businesses due to increased hunter expenditures and potential reductions in agricultural crop damage and deer-vehicle collisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Natural Resources is authorized by this bill to establish Sunday hunting for deer and turkey using a bow and arrow. The agency manages hunting seasons, enforces conservation laws through its Natural Resources Police, and oversees the regulations amended by this legislation.

The expansion of hunting opportunities is intended, in part, to manage deer populations which cause significant crop damage. The Department of Agriculture represents the interests of the farming community that would benefit from reduced agricultural losses.

The fiscal note indicates that a reduction in the deer population may lead to a decrease in deer-vehicle collisions. MDOT, specifically through the State Highway Administration, is responsible for highway safety and infrastructure maintenance affected by such incidents.

The fiscal note highlights a potential meaningful economic impact on small businesses related to hunting, such as lodging, food, and equipment providers. The Department of Commerce is responsible for supporting economic growth and the state's competitive position in these sectors.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and would be responsible for ensuring the new regulations comply with existing state and federal law, as well as defending the agency in any related litigation.
The Council addresses challenges in Maryland's 18 rural counties, where hunting is a significant cultural and economic activity and where agricultural damage from deer populations is most prevalent.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Natural Resources. The Governor is responsible for policy initiatives regarding environmental conservation and rural affairs mentioned in the bill's scope.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of a disposition under a certain provision of law if the disposition was included in a case that was disposed of by the court with a no finding designation or designated by the court as having been terminated without finding.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement - No Finding and Case Terminated Without Finding
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 466

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the expungement of criminal records to include charges for specific offenses when the court disposition is recorded as 'no finding' or the case is designated as 'terminated without finding.'
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records containing 'no finding' or 'terminated without finding' court designations, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $11,700 in fiscal 2027 for the Judiciary to update brochures, forms, and instructional videos. There may be an indeterminate operational impact on the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to a potential increase in expungement petitions. Local government finances and operations are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's changes within the Judiciary. It must update case management systems to accommodate 'no finding' and 'terminated without finding' designations and incurs a specific fiscal impact for revising expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional materials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) is responsible for processing and executing expungement orders for criminal records across the state. The bill's expansion of eligibility directly impacts the Department's operational workload for record removal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in criminal and expungement proceedings. Its attorneys and staff will be responsible for filing the expanded petitions for expungement authorized under this bill.

The Maryland State Police is a primary custodian of police records subject to expungement orders. The agency must comply with court orders to remove or restrict access to records for eligible dispositions.

The Motor Vehicle Administration maintains driving and vehicle records. Because the bill includes offenses from the Transportation Article as eligible for expungement, the MVA is a key custodian responsible for implementing expungement orders related to those records.

The Maryland State Archives serves as the central depository for permanent judicial and executive records. Expungement orders require the Archives to remove or restrict access to historical records related to the affected cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for criminal justice policy and advises the Governor on public safety strategies. The expansion of expungement eligibility is a significant policy shift within their purview.

As the parent agency for the Motor Vehicle Administration and other modal administrations, the Department of Transportation oversees the records and law enforcement activities impacted by the expungement of transportation-related offenses.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and will likely provide guidance on the legal interpretation of 'no finding' and 'terminated without finding' as used in the bill.

The bill includes offenses related to the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, such as possession with intent to distribute cannabis, as eligible for expungement. The Administration is relevant as the primary regulator for this industry.

The bill explicitly includes various offenses from the Natural Resources Article (related to hunting, boating, and speed limits) as eligible for expungement, impacting the records maintained by the Department and the Natural Resources Police.

The bill allows for the expungement of offenses related to business regulation and occupational licensing. As the agency overseeing these boards and commissions, the Department's background check and regulatory processes are impacted by the removal of these records.

The bill includes specific Election Law Article violations as eligible for expungement. The Board of Elections is the state's oversight body for the integrity of the electoral process and related records.

The State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes offenses related to election integrity and public ethics. Several offenses within the State Prosecutor's jurisdiction are listed as eligible for expungement under the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state agency expenditures and personnel. It is relevant due to the general fund expenditure noted in the fiscal analysis for implementing the bill's requirements.

The Governor is responsible for overseeing the executive branch agencies implementing the bill and for the final approval of the annual state budget, which includes the funds required for the Judiciary's updates.

Synopsis: Repealing and establishing the methodology used to calculate the weekly benefit amount; altering the taxable wage base used to determine employer contributions to the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund and the amount of earned wages subtracted from a weekly benefit amount; requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to determine and make available online the State annual average wage applicable to the rate of contribution; requiring, beginning in 2027, the maximum weekly benefit to be 40% of the state average weekly wage; etc.
Title: Unemployment Insurance Modernization Act of 2026
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The bill modernizes the Maryland unemployment insurance program by altering how weekly benefit amounts and employer taxable wage bases are calculated. It indexes the minimum and maximum weekly benefit amounts to the State average weekly wage and indexes the employer taxable wage base to the State average annual wage, phasing in these changes to increase both benefits for workers and contribution requirements for employers.
stakeholders: Unemployed individuals, Maryland employers (including small businesses and nonprofits), and State and local government agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to significantly increase revenues and expenditures for the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund (UITF). By calendar 2030, the Maryland Department of Labor estimates UITF expenditures will reach approximately $868,000,000 and revenues will reach $806,000,000. State and local government expenditures will increase significantly to reimburse the UITF for higher benefits paid to former employees, with State costs potentially exceeding $1,000,000 annually. Special fund revenues from administrative fees are projected to increase by about $7,800,000 in calendar 2027 due to the higher taxable wage base.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for administering the Unemployment Insurance program. The bill requires the Department to determine state average wages, set taxable wage bases, calculate benefit amounts, and adopt regulations to implement the phase-in of new maximum benefit levels.

As the central personnel and fiscal agency, DBM is impacted because the State, as an employer, must reimburse the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund for benefits paid to former employees. The bill's significant increase in benefit amounts will lead to higher State expenditures.

The Comptroller's tax collection and revenue estimation roles are impacted because unemployment insurance benefits are taxable income, while employer UI contributions are deductible. Changes to these amounts will affect state and local income tax revenues.

The bill contains a specific provision stating that compensation for individuals serving as election judges for local boards of elections may not be included when computing wages to be subtracted from a claimant's weekly benefit amount.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Department of Labor and will be responsible for advising on the significant regulatory changes and statutory interpretations required by this modernization act.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and appoints the Secretary of Labor, who is granted discretionary authority under the bill to determine the annual phase-in percentages for the maximum weekly benefit amount and the taxable wage base.

The Tax Court hears appeals from final decisions of state taxing authorities. Disputes regarding employer UI contribution rates or assessments resulting from the new taxable wage base methodology could be adjudicated here.

The Treasurer's Office is the chief financial agency responsible for managing state funds. Significant changes in the flow of revenues and expenditures within the nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund involve the Treasurer's custodial and management functions.

As the state's economic development agency, Commerce is impacted by major changes to employer tax structures. The bill's doubling of employer UI taxes and changes to the taxable wage base affect the state's business climate and competitive position.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning in the 2028-2029 school year, each public middle school and each public high school to begin instruction not earlier than 8 a.m. and 8:30 a.m., respectively, unless granted a waiver by the State Board of Education under certain circumstances; and requiring each county board of education and each public charter school to implement a certain public service campaign to raise awareness of sleep deprivation and later school start times.
Title: Public Middle, High, and Charter Schools - Start Time for Instruction
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill mandates that beginning in the 2028-2029 school year, Maryland public middle schools must start instruction no earlier than 8:00 a.m. and public high schools no earlier than 8:30 a.m. The State Board of Education may grant waivers for compelling reasons, though a lack of funding is explicitly excluded as a valid reason. Additionally, local school boards and charter schools must conduct a public information campaign during the 2027-2028 school year to educate the community on the health and academic impacts of sleep deprivation and the benefits of later start times.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Middle and high school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. At the local level, fiscal impacts vary significantly by jurisdiction; while some counties like Anne Arundel already comply and expect no impact, others face substantial costs primarily due to increased transportation needs. For example, Frederick County Public Schools estimates first-year costs exceeding $11,000,000 with annual recurring costs of $6,000,000 for additional buses, drivers, and maintenance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency overseeing public and charter schools, MSDE and the State Board of Education are responsible for granting waivers for school start times and assisting local boards with required public information campaigns regarding sleep deprivation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education and MSDE, particularly concerning the statutory requirements for school hours and the legal framework for granting or denying start-time waivers.
The shifting of instruction start times for middle and high schools impacts the deployment and coordination of school safety personnel and protocols, which are overseen by this agency.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives; this bill involves a significant change in statewide education policy and student health initiatives.

Synopsis: Requiring each county to adopt a charter by December 31, 2032, using a certain procedure; altering the method by which a county shall adopt a charter under certain circumstances; requiring the charter to provide for the election of members of the county council by the voters of councilmanic districts; limiting the applicability of certain constitutional provisions governing code home rule counties; and requiring the amendment proposed by the Act be submitted to the qualified voters of the State for approval or rejection.
Title: Constitutional Amendment - Form of County Government - Requirement to Adopt Charter Home Rule
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Chartered Counties -see also- AACo; BCo; CecilCo; etc.
Code Counties -see also- AllegCo; CarolineCo; ChsCo; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

Article.Title: XI-F - Home Rule for Code Counties

bill_summary: This constitutional amendment requires all Maryland counties and Baltimore City to adopt a charter home rule form of government by December 31, 2032. The bill mandates that each charter provide for the election of both a county executive and a county council, with council members elected from specific councilmanic districts. It effectively repeals the code home rule and commission forms of county government once the transition to charter home rule is complete.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and Boards of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Maryland voters, county government officials, and residents of the 12 Maryland counties currently operating under commission or code home rule forms of government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected by the constitutional amendment. However, local expenditures for the 12 counties currently using commission or code home rule are expected to increase significantly due to the costs of transitioning to a charter government. These costs include new salaries for county executives and councils, additional staff, and office space renovations. The Fiscal Note cites the example of Frederick County, where annual expenditures were approximately $725,000 higher after transitioning to a charter home rule form of government compared to its previous commission structure. Local revenues are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 190 proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the qualified voters of Maryland at the 2026 general election. The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for supervising and administering all statewide elections and managing the ballot process for such referendums.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel regarding constitutional amendments and ensures the legality of the procedures used by counties during their transition to charter home rule.

The Governor's Office oversees intergovernmental relations with local jurisdictions and has a constitutional mandate to receive election returns and proclaim the official adoption of ratified constitutional amendments.

The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records, including executive orders and laws. The office is responsible for recording constitutional amendments and their subsequent ratification status.

The Department of Planning provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments regarding land use and governance. Mandatory adoption of charter home rule significantly alters the legislative and planning authority of affected counties, requiring coordination with this department.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a merchant, in a certain transaction between the hours of 6 a.m. and 10 p.m., from prohibiting a person from making a cash payment to purchase an essential consumer good, requiring a person to purchase an essential consumer good by using a credit or debit card, or charging or collecting from a person a higher price than for an equivalent cashless transaction for making a cash payment for the purchase of an essential consumer good; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 714

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland retailers to accept cash for in-person purchases of essential items like food, water, hygiene products, medicine, and fuel if the total is under $300 and occurs between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Retailers cannot charge higher prices for cash transactions. The law, enforced by the Attorney General, includes specific exceptions for online sales, vending machines, and certain specialty stores, and allows merchants to provide cash-to-card conversion machines instead of accepting physical cash.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Division of Consumer Protection
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, retail merchants selling essential goods, and small businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact on state or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources. Small businesses may experience a meaningful operational impact if they are required to transition from electronic-only to cash-accepting transaction models.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General with enforcing the new cash payment requirements, including a mandated process of providing two opportunities to comply before assessing civil penalties.

The Governor oversaw the development of this policy initiative and signed the bill into law; the Governor's Office also oversees the executive branch departments responsible for consumer protection and economic regulation.

The bill designates 'fuel' as an essential consumer good subject to the cash payment mandate. The Comptroller is the primary regulator of the motor fuel industry in Maryland and ensures compliance among fuel merchants.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by new regulations on retail transactions that affect business operations and the state's commercial climate.

The bill defines 'essential consumer goods' to include health products, medicine, and medical supplies. The Department of Health regulates pharmacies and health care facilities that function as retail merchants and will be subject to these payment rules.

The Department of Labor regulates various retail industries and protects consumers and the public; it is relevant because the bill alters the legal requirements for businesses when conducting transactions with the public.

The bill establishes civil penalties for merchants who fail to comply with cash payment requirements. If merchants contest these fines or enforcement actions by the OAG, the Office of Administrative Hearings would provide the impartial adjudication process.

Synopsis: Exempting certain religious educational institutions accredited by accrediting bodies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education from the requirement to obtain a certificate of approval from the Maryland Higher Education Commission to operate in the State.
Title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Religious Educational Institutions - Certificate of Approval
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill exempts certain accredited religious educational institutions from the requirement to obtain a certificate of approval from the Maryland Higher Education Commission, provided they have been in continuous operation in Maryland since before January 1, 2013.
stakeholders: Accredited religious educational institutions and students pursuing religious vocations or purposes.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Higher Education Commission estimates that the bill will have no significant impact on its administrative operations, special fund revenues, or expenditures. Local governments are not affected, and there is no impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency mentioned in the bill, MHEC is responsible for issuing Certificates of Approval (COA) and regulating postsecondary institutions. The bill directly alters MHEC's regulatory requirements by exempting certain accredited religious institutions from the COA process.

This agency is the central regulatory and coordinating board for all postsecondary education in Maryland. It is directly responsible for implementing and overseeing the changes to the Certificate of Approval process for religious educational institutions as mandated by the bill.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel for MHEC. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation of the bill's exemptions and ensuring that the new regulations comply with state and federal law, including First Amendment considerations.

The MLDS Center links student data from partner agencies, including MHEC. Changes in which institutions are required to obtain approval or register with MHEC could affect the scope and consistency of student data collected and analyzed for state-wide reporting.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state and oversees MHEC's budget. While the fiscal note indicates a minimal impact, DBM is responsible for monitoring changes in the special fund revenues and expenditures related to institutional application and renewal fees.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. Since the bill modifies the regulatory authority of an executive commission (MHEC) and relates to educational policy, it falls under the administrative oversight of the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring a unit of State government to provide a certain debriefing of a contract award to certain persons on request; adding an exemption to the prohibition on an individual who assists in the drafting of specifications, an invitation for bids, or a request for proposals from submitting a bid or proposal or assisting in the submission of a bid or proposal; requiring a procurement contract to include a certain clause pertaining to certain contract modifications related to changes in State law; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Transparency and Procedures
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 396

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland state procurement laws by requiring government units to provide debriefings to unsuccessful bidders before contract approval. It also establishes new requirements for contract modifications related to changes in state law, alters the timeframes and procedures for filing contract claims and protests, and provides exemptions for individuals providing specific information during the solicitation process to avoid ethics violations.
responsible_party: Office of State Procurement within the Department of General Services
stakeholders: State agencies, procurement officers, and businesses or individuals bidding on or performing state government contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures are not expected to increase for the implementation of the bill as it can be handled with existing resources. However, changes to procurement ethics requirements may lead to an increase in bid protests, which could result in project delays and indeterminate cost overruns. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the administrative procedures, timelines, and final action definitions for procurement protests and contract claims, which are the primary matters adjudicated by this Board.

While independent, the Judiciary's procurement support agency is affected by changes to state procurement laws that govern inter-branch procedures and auditing standards.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Incarcerated Individual Apprenticeship Pilot Program within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS). In consultation with the Maryland Department of Labor, the program provides incarcerated individuals at the Baltimore City Correctional Center with the opportunity to serve as paid apprentices in state or local government agencies or with private entities. The program focuses on skilled trades to help participants develop marketable job skills and earn money prior to their release. The pilot program is established as a three-year initiative.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals at the Baltimore City Correctional Center, the Maryland Department of Labor, state and local government agencies, and private employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is projected to have a minimal fiscal impact on state and local governments. Expenditures may increase slightly for agencies that choose to employ apprentices, who must be paid at least the state minimum wage. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Maryland Department of Labor can implement the program within existing budgeted resources. There is no estimated impact on state revenues.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to conduct studies on the use of emerging technologies—such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and biometrics—to improve the safety and transparency of Maryland's gambling environment. It establishes the Workgroup on Gambling Prevention Technology to examine problem gambling on college campuses using geofencing technology and requires Maryland to join the National Council of Legislators from Gaming States.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission, Bowie State University, Morgan State University, Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling, Maryland college students, and gaming industry participants.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency can staff the workgroup and conduct the required studies with existing budgeted resources. Similarly, Bowie State University, Morgan State University, and the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling are expected to collaborate and participate in the workgroup using existing resources. There is no projected impact on state revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of gambling in Maryland, the agency is authorized by this bill to conduct studies on emerging technologies and is responsible for staffing and overseeing the newly established Workgroup on Gambling Prevention Technology.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Workgroup on Gambling Prevention Technology within the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to study best practices and report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

Morgan State University is explicitly named as a required collaborator for the Commission's studies on emerging gambling technology and as a formal partner in the Workgroup on Gambling Prevention Technology.

Bowie State University, a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, is specifically named as a mandatory collaborator for the technology studies and a partner in the workgroup established by the bill.

The Department of Health oversees behavioral health and the Problem Gambling Fund, which supports the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling, a named collaborator for the studies and workgroup mandated by the bill.
The Commission must submit reports on its findings and recommendations to the Governor, who also oversees the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency as part of the executive branch.

The bill requires studies on advanced technical areas including cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and digital identity verification, which fall under the strategic and advisory domain of DoIT.

The bill focuses on the impact of mobile sports wagering and problem gambling on college campuses, requiring coordination with higher education institutions and potentially impacting statewide postsecondary policy.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Commission and would likely be involved in reviewing any contracts or collaborative agreements made with private entities or institutions of higher education for the authorized studies.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of baby food to include infant cereal, thereby requiring it to meet existing state testing, labeling, and reporting standards for toxic elements like arsenic, cadmium, lead, and mercury. Manufacturers must make test results for baby food products publicly available on their websites without requiring consumers to provide purchase information, include QR codes on labels that link to these results, and maintain certificates of analysis for at least five years.
stakeholders: Baby food and infant cereal manufacturers, retailers, and consumers (specifically children under age 2 and their parents)
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Health can manage any increase in workload using existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on state or local revenues, and the bill is not expected to have a material financial effect on local governments. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for the implementation and enforcement of this bill. Its Center for Food Processing is tasked with licensing and inspecting food facilities to ensure compliance with food safety laws, including the testing and labeling requirements for baby food and infant cereal.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and is responsible for enforcing state laws related to consumer protection, which includes ensuring that manufacturers comply with statutory testing, reporting, and labeling requirements for products sold to consumers.

The Governor's Office for Children (GOC) is dedicated to the well-being of Maryland's children. This bill directly affects child health and safety by regulating toxic elements in food products specifically intended for infants and children under the age of two.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) is responsible for food quality assurance and promoting the viability of farming. As the bill adds 'infant cereal' (a grain-based agricultural product) to the regulatory framework, the MDA has a secondary interest in the impact on food processors and consumer confidence in agricultural food products.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor is responsible for the health-related policies implemented by the Department of Health and the safety standards established for vulnerable populations like infants.

bill_summary: This bill imposes an 11% excise tax on the gross receipts of federally licensed firearms dealers derived from the retail sale of firearms, firearm accessories, and ammunition in Maryland, including sales to residents by out-of-state dealers. The generated revenue is distributed to state funds and programs supporting violence intervention, trauma services, firearm violence prevention, and community supports.
stakeholders: Federally licensed firearms dealers, purchasers of firearms and ammunition, victims of homicide, law enforcement agencies (exempted), the Maryland Department of Health, the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, and the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, special fund revenues are projected to increase by 11,400,000 in FY 2028 (initially from large retailers) and rise to 26,500,000 by FY 2032 as the tax applies to all dealers. Special fund expenditures for the Comptroller to administer the tax are estimated at 2,100,000 in FY 2028, which includes one-time computer programming costs and personnel, stabilizing at approximately 600,000 annually by FY 2032.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Comptroller with administering the new firearm, firearm accessory, and ammunition excise tax, including collecting revenue, processing returns, and distributing funds to specific accounts and agencies.

The Maryland Department of Health is a primary beneficiary of the new tax revenue, receiving 26% for its Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention and 4% for the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office receives 20% of the tax revenue for the Survivors of Homicide Victims Grant Program and manages the Maryland Violence Intervention and Prevention Program Fund, which receives 26% of the distributed revenue.
The bill directs 20% of the excise tax revenue to the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, which is managed within the Department of Education.
As the agency responsible for adjudicating tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court would hear appeals regarding assessments and audits of the new excise tax.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and personnel management; it will oversee the fiscal impact of the new revenue streams and the creation of the six new positions required by the Comptroller for tax administration.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Comptroller for the drafting of new regulations and will represent the state in civil and criminal litigation related to tax enforcement and appeals.

As the state's chief financial agency, the Treasurer's Office is responsible for receiving and investing the state funds generated by this new excise tax before they are distributed to the designated special funds.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies implementing this tax and coordinates the policy initiatives related to community safety and violence prevention funded by the bill.
The OAH provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases involving state agencies, including potential administrative disputes regarding tax assessments by the Comptroller.

The MSP is the primary law enforcement agency for Maryland and regulates firearms; it may be involved in information sharing with the Comptroller regarding licensed firearm dealers to ensure tax compliance.

bill_summary: This bill requires law enforcement agencies to notify the State’s Attorney within 24 hours (or as soon as practicable) when a student is identified as a suspect in an investigation of a felony or a crime of violence. It authorizes the State’s Attorney to notify the local school superintendent of the investigation and mandates notification if a student is later determined not to be a suspect. Additionally, the bill expands annual reporting requirements on reportable offenses to include demographic data and educational outcomes for students identified as suspects in such investigations.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education, State Board of Education, local school superintendents, State's Attorneys, and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Students aged 5 to 21 enrolled in public and nonpublic schools, local school systems, law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates no impact on State revenues or expenditures, as the Maryland State Department of Education can adjust its reporting of reportable offenses with existing resources. Local notification requirements and procedures are not expected to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education to adopt regulations regarding the use and destruction of sensitive student information. Furthermore, MSDE must submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly detailing reportable offenses and student suspect data.

As an independent unit within MSDE responsible for school safety coordination and training, this agency is directly involved in the policy area of maintaining a safe and secure school environment through the management of reportable offense information.

The bill imposes a new mandate on law enforcement agencies to notify State's Attorneys within 24 hours when a student is identified as a suspect in a felony or crime of violence investigation. The Maryland State Police is the primary state-level law enforcement agency subject to these requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires school principals or county superintendents to invite a student's attorney to participate in conferences and manifestation determination reviews if the student is removed from their regular program due to being a suspect. The Office of the Public Defender represents many students in these proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including the management of funds and policies intended to reduce juvenile delinquency and improve interagency collaboration, which are central to the bill's objectives.

The bill involves the legal handling of reportable offenses by students and references the role of juvenile courts in authorizing the disclosure of confidential information. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support to the judicial branch involved in these determinations.
The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education to submit an annual report to the Governor regarding reportable offenses and student suspect identifications.
The OAG would likely provide legal counsel to the State Board of Education and MSDE regarding the constitutionality and drafting of regulations for handling confidential student suspect data.

bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to align with the national Uniform Simultaneous Death Act. It introduces a 120-hour survival requirement for individuals to be considered to have survived a decedent for inheritance, property distribution, and insurance purposes. Additionally, it establishes evidentiary procedures for determining death and provides liability protections for third-party payors who act in good faith when distributing assets.
stakeholders: Property co-owners, beneficiaries, estate executors, insurance companies, and trustees.
fiscal_impact_summary: No formal Fiscal Note is present in the provided text. The bill does not contain specific funding allocations or revenue mandates. It primarily affects the private distribution of assets. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. This bill directly alters the legal standards for inheritance and property devolution in cases of simultaneous death, which is central to the agency's core function.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish new evidentiary procedures and rules for determining survival in legal disputes. The Judicial Branch will be responsible for adjudicating these matters and managing property deposited with the court during disputes.

The bill defines 'governing instrument' to include insurance and annuity policies and 'payor' to include insurers. It establishes new rules for how insurance proceeds must be distributed when beneficiaries and the insured die nearly simultaneously.

The bill's definition of 'governing instrument' includes pensions and retirement benefit plans. As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System, this agency is a 'payor' that must comply with the 120-hour survival requirement for beneficiary payouts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency manages voluntary supplemental retirement plans which fall under the bill's definition of 'governing instrument.' It would be impacted as a payor in determining the proper distribution of assets to beneficiaries.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies on changes to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article and may be involved in litigation or interpretation regarding the Uniform Simultaneous Death Act.

As the central personnel agency managing state employee benefits, DBM is impacted by definitions involving the state as a 'payor' for various employee benefit plans and the legalities of asset distribution to survivors of state employees.

The Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues, including inheritance taxes. Changes to the rules of inheritance and property devolution could affect tax calculations and revenue collection procedures.

The bill explicitly references the Health - General Article for the definition of death and the procedures for death certificates. MDH's Vital Statistics Administration is responsible for the death certificates that will serve as prima facie evidence under this Act.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives; as this bill updates a uniform act and impacts multiple executive agencies (MDH, DBM, etc.), it requires administrative oversight.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to develop and maintain a real property flood risk disclosure form for residential real estate transactions. Starting July 1, 2027, sellers of residential properties with four or fewer units are required to provide this form to purchasers before a contract of sale is signed. The form includes information on whether the property is in a 100-year or 500-year floodplain, history of flood damage claims, and the availability of FEMA elevation certificates.
stakeholders: Purchasers and vendors of residential real property with four or fewer single-family units, and the Maryland Department of the Environment
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances, and the small business impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of the Environment (MDE) develop, publish, and maintain the real property flood risk disclosure statement form. MDE is the primary agency responsible for the administrative implementation of this law.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is responsible for enforcing disclosure laws in real estate transactions. Failure to provide the required flood risk disclosure could lead to consumer complaints and enforcement actions handled by this office.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Real Estate Commission, which regulates real estate licensees. Brokers and agents will be responsible for ensuring these new disclosure forms are completed and provided during residential property sales.

The bill creates new statutory requirements for contracts of sale under the Real Property Article. Disputes regarding the failure to disclose flood risks or inaccuracies in the disclosure form could lead to increased litigation within the state court system.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of the Environment and other implementing agencies. The Governor also plays a role in signing the legislation and coordinating the executive branch's response to flood management and climate resilience policies.

bill_summary: This bill provides a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for compensation received as tips or gratuities by individuals employed in food service facilities, hotels, and businesses licensed for on-sale alcoholic beverage consumption, as well as those providing taxicab or passenger-for-hire services.
stakeholders: Tipped employees in the food service, hospitality, and transportation sectors, including restaurant staff, bar employees, hotel workers, and taxi or rideshare drivers.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal fiscal note is present and indicates that State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues will decrease by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount annually beginning in fiscal 2027. The Comptroller’s Office can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Specific dollar estimates for the total revenue loss are unavailable due to data limitations regarding reported tips.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering state income tax laws and collecting revenues. This bill introduces a new subtraction modification that the Comptroller's Office will need to implement on tax forms and process for eligible taxpayers.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and developing the budget. The bill's anticipated decrease in general fund revenues directly impacts the fiscal planning and budget execution for which the department is responsible.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. This bill modifies tax policy and affects state revenue streams, which are central to the Governor's budgetary and policy priorities.

The bill targets the service, hospitality, and transportation sectors. As the state's economic development agency, Commerce has a direct interest in policies that affect the financial viability and labor market of these specific industries.

This agency promotes the hospitality and travel industries. Since the bill specifically benefits employees in food service and hotels—core components of the tourism economy—it is relevant to their mission of supporting these sectors.

The bill defines 'passenger-for-hire services' and 'taxicab services' by referencing the Public Utilities Article. The PSC is the independent agency that regulates these transportation services, making the bill's definitions relevant to their regulatory domain.

The Tax Court adjudicates disputes between taxpayers and the state regarding income tax assessments. This new subtraction modification may lead to administrative appeals regarding eligibility that the Court would be responsible for resolving.

The Treasurer manages and protects state funds. A significant reduction in state income tax revenue impacts the overall financial position and fund management duties overseen by the Treasurer's Office.

MDOT oversees the state's transportation network. The bill affects the compensation of workers in transportation sectors, such as taxicabs and passenger-for-hire services, that interact with the state's infrastructure and regulatory environment.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller. They may be required to provide legal interpretations of the new subtraction modification or defend the state in potential litigation.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Social Isolation and Loneliness Pilot Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health. The program is designed to provide grants of up to $20,000 to five eligible entities for operating costs related to programs that address social isolation and loneliness in vulnerable populations, specifically prioritizing youth, seniors, and rural residents. The department is required to evaluate the program and report its findings by December 1, 2029.
stakeholders: Vulnerable populations at risk of social isolation and loneliness, specifically youth, seniors, and rural populations, as well as organizations that serve these groups.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase between FY 2027 and FY 2030 to support the program and its administration. The bill mandates a $100,000 general fund appropriation in FY 2028 for the grant program. Total estimated general fund expenditures are $28,700 in FY 2027, $140,900 in FY 2028, $42,600 in FY 2029, and $22,200 in FY 2030. These costs account for both the grant funding and a part-time contractual policy analyst to manage the program. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Social Isolation and Loneliness Pilot Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health. The department is responsible for administering the program, awarding grants to eligible entities, conducting a program evaluation, and reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with the Department of Aging to prioritize senior populations when awarding grants under the new program.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with the Governor's Office for Children to prioritize youth populations when awarding grants under the new program.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with the Department of Housing and Community Development to prioritize rural populations when awarding grants under the new program.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific $100,000 appropriation for the program in the fiscal year 2028 budget. Additionally, the Maryland Department of Health must submit its final evaluation report to the Governor.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for implementing the mandated $100,000 appropriation and managing the contractual personnel costs identified in the fiscal note to support the program's administration.

Synopsis: Prohibiting employers from requiring, as a condition of employment, employees or prospective employees to enter into training repayment agreements; defining "training repayment agreement" as one that requires an employee to pay an employer or a third party, such as a training provider, a sum of money if the employee voluntarily or involuntarily leaves employment with the employer; and providing that an agreement that constitutes a training repayment agreement is null and void as being against the public policy of the State.
Title: Labor and Employment - Training Repayment Agreements - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 2:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits employers from requiring employees or prospective employees to enter into training repayment agreements—which require an individual to repay training costs if they leave their job—as a condition of employment. It declares such agreements null and void, allows the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to investigate complaints and assess civil penalties, and permits individuals to sue for economic damages and restitution.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Maryland employers, employees, and prospective employees
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $94,100 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a half-time wage and hour investigator and a contractual half-time Assistant Attorney General. Annual costs decrease to $53,700 in FY 2028 after the contractual position ends. Civil penalty provisions are not expected to materially increase general fund revenues. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commissioner of Labor and Industry, housed within this department, is the primary official responsible for investigating complaints, enforcing the prohibition of training repayment agreements, and assessing civil penalties.

The fiscal note specifically identifies the need for a contractual Assistant Attorney General to develop enforcement policies and procedures. Additionally, the office provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor regarding the implementation of the bill.
The bill establishes a private right of action, allowing employees or prospective employees to file civil lawsuits for economic damages and restitution in the state court system.
The bill stipulates that civil penalties assessed by the Commissioner are subject to the notice and hearing requirements of the Administrative Procedures Act, which are adjudicated by this agency.

As the central personnel agency for the state government, DBM would need to ensure that State of Maryland employment policies and contracts comply with the prohibition of training repayment agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a potentially meaningful impact on small businesses, which this office supports by monitoring procurement and economic opportunities affected by labor law changes.

The bill specifically excludes training repayment agreements entered into as part of a collective bargaining agreement. This agency oversees collective bargaining for the public sector and would be responsible for interpreting the bill's application to unionized public employees.

The board is responsible for statewide workforce development strategy; prohibitions on training repayment agreements impact how businesses and agencies manage employee training, retention, and workforce investment.

bill_summary: This bill establishes regulations to prevent waterborne diseases, specifically Legionnaires’ disease, by requiring public water suppliers to maintain minimum disinfectant residual levels and perform regular testing. It mandates that water suppliers notify customers of system disruptions and requires the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health to investigate Legionnaires' disease cases, maintain a public registry, and conduct a public awareness campaign. Additionally, owners of buildings meeting specific standards must implement water management programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH)
stakeholders: Public water suppliers, owners and operators of buildings meeting ASHRAE Standard 188-2018, Maryland residents using public water, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,919,600 in FY 2027 for MDE and MDH to hire staff, perform testing, and manage public outreach. Future annual costs are estimated to exceed $1,700,000. Local government expenditures will increase significantly for jurisdictions operating water systems; for instance, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) estimates costs of $50,000,000 in FY 2027 for infrastructure and equipment upgrades. Small businesses acting as water suppliers or owning covered buildings will also incur substantial compliance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory body for public water systems in Maryland, MDE is tasked with adopting regulations, establishing a public database for water distribution system disruptions, conducting investigations of residual disinfectant violations, and performing water system testing upon notice of Legionnaires' disease diagnoses.

MDH is a primary implementing agency responsible for conducting comprehensive investigations of Legionnaires' disease cases, testing fixtures at water exposure points, developing a public awareness campaign, and maintaining a registry of de-identified case data.

MES operates numerous water and wastewater systems for state and local government clients. The bill's requirements for minimum disinfectant residual levels and increased testing will have a significant operational and fiscal impact on the systems they manage.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance and operation of state-owned facilities, DGS must ensure that covered state buildings implement the water management programs required to control Legionella.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates large correctional facilities which likely meet the criteria for 'covered buildings' under the ASHRAE standards, requiring the implementation of new water management programs and potential infrastructure upgrades.

The PSC regulates for-profit water utilities. These utilities will incur costs to comply with the new disinfectant and testing standards, which may result in rate cases and oversight by the Commission to adjust consumer costs.

The University System manages numerous buildings and campuses that serve as both water suppliers and owners of 'covered buildings' (dorms, labs, etc.). The fiscal note identifies significant costs for USM to comply with the bill.
The Judiciary manages courthouses and facilities that must comply with the building water management program requirements. They are specifically identified in the fiscal note as an impacted entity.

DBM is the principal fiscal and personnel agency. It will be responsible for overseeing the significant general fund expenditure increases for MDE and MDH staff and the fiscal impact on other state agency facility budgets.
Local school systems, overseen by MSDE, are building owners and sometimes water suppliers. The bill requires schools to implement water management programs and may necessitate facility upgrades.
MDOT and its sub-administrations (MVA, SHA, MTA, etc.) operate facilities and terminals that will be subject to the bill's water management program requirements for covered buildings.
The IAC oversees funding for public school capital improvements. Compliance with new water safety standards may lead to requests for capital funding for school water system upgrades.
As an independent state university, Morgan State manages its own facilities and will be responsible for implementing water management programs for its covered buildings.
OAH may be required to adjudicate contested cases related to MDE's enforcement actions and civil penalties imposed on water suppliers for non-compliance with the new standards.

OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers. The significant costs for water utilities to comply with the bill will likely result in rate increases for consumers, necessitating advocacy from this office.
The college operates its own facilities and will be responsible for implementing water management programs for its covered buildings, as noted in the fiscal analysis.
The Governor receives the annual report required by the bill and oversees the executive agencies (MDE and MDH) responsible for the primary implementation of the new regulations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and MDH and would be involved in defending the new regulations and handling legal enforcement of penalties.
The Secretary of State may be involved if there are international implications or inter-state coordination regarding water quality standards, though their role is secondary.
