bill_summary: This bill establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to support rural communities in Maryland. Administered by the Rural Maryland Council, the program helps local entities build capacity for economic development and grant applications, while the fund provides grants of up to $50,000 for planning and community initiatives to those who complete the program.
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, State-recognized tribes, higher education institutions, regional planning agencies, and economic or workforce development organizations in 18 specified rural Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually starting in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund. Correspondingly, special fund revenues and expenditures increase as grants are awarded. Local governments in rural areas benefit from access to technical support and grants, though they are required to provide a 20% match for awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, both of which are to be administered by the Rural Maryland Council. This is the primary implementing agency for the bill's core provisions.
The Rural Maryland Council is administratively housed within the Department of Agriculture. As the parent agency, the Department will oversee the Council's expanded responsibilities and budget.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the new Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, a special nonlapsing fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State money.

The bill creates a new special fund requiring an estimated annual general fund expenditure of at least $100,000 for capitalization, necessitating coordination with DBM for budget planning and execution.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will provide legal counsel to the Rural Maryland Council regarding the establishment of the new program, fund regulations, and grant agreements.
The Council is required to submit an annual report on the grant program to the Governor. The Governor also oversees the executive branch and proposed the budget containing the fund's appropriations.

The bill focuses on rural economic development, which overlaps with the mission of the Department of Commerce. Furthermore, economic development organizations are identified as eligible applicants for the program.

Institutions of higher education are designated as eligible applicants for the Rural Readiness Program and associated grants, making the bill relevant to the Commission's oversight of these institutions.
As an institution of higher education in the State, Morgan State University is an eligible applicant for the Rural Readiness Program and the new capacity building grants.
Institutions within the University System of Maryland are eligible applicants for the program and funding established by the bill.
As an institution of higher education in the State, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible applicant for the program and grants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Board (MAERDAB) is responsible for reviewing and approving grant applications and recipients for the new fund.

Synopsis: Requiring an election judge to establish a voter's identity by requiring the voter to present a valid government-issued photo identification or a valid non-government-issued photo identification, and a current bill, statement, or check that states the voter's name and address as proof of identity; requiring a voter to vote a provisional ballot if the voter is unable to provide certain proof of identity; and prohibiting a person from knowingly and willfully voting or attempting to vote under a false form of identification.
Title: Elections - In-Person Voting - Proof of Identity
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill requires individuals voting in person to provide proof of identity, such as a government-issued photo ID or a combination of a non-government photo ID and a supporting document like a utility bill or bank statement. Voters unable to provide the required identification must vote using a provisional ballot. The bill also establishes criminal penalties for knowingly voting or attempting to vote with false identification.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, election judges, and local election officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $275,000 in FY 2028 and at least $250,000 annually from FY 2029 through 2031 for voter outreach, procedure redevelopment, and training. Additional illustrative costs for pollbooks and printers could increase State expenditures by approximately $532,000. Local government expenditures also increase to cover voter outreach, additional election judges, pollbook equipment, and the administration of an increased number of provisional ballots.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for supervising and administering elections in Maryland. The bill directly alters their core operational procedures by requiring election judges to verify voter identification and necessitates the development of new training and outreach materials.

This agency is responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process. The bill creates a new criminal provision prohibiting the use of false identification to vote, falling directly under this agency's mandate.

The bill requires voters to present valid government-issued photo identification. The MVA is the primary state agency responsible for issuing driver's licenses and state IDs, which will serve as the primary proof of identity for voters under this law.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and will likely be responsible for defending the new identification requirements against potential legal challenges related to voting rights.

The fiscal note indicates a need for additional pollbooks and software modifications. The Board of Public Works must approve significant state procurement contracts and expenditures related to these operational requirements.

DBM is responsible for the state's fiscal planning and budget execution. The bill has a significant fiscal impact, requiring at least $275,000 in additional general fund expenditures for outreach and equipment that DBM must oversee.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. The fiscal note highlights increased costs that will need to be reflected in future budget proposals to ensure the law is implemented effectively.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with disabilities. Changes to in-person voting identification requirements may impact the accessibility of the voting process, a key area of focus for the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor for voting under false identification. The OPD would be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with violating these new criminal provisions.
The AOC supports the judicial branch, which will handle the adjudication of the new misdemeanor offenses created by the bill regarding election-related identification fraud.
The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works, which would be required to approve the procurement of new election technology and materials necessitated by the bill.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, overseeing the state's procurement and contracts for equipment such as the additional pollbooks mentioned in the fiscal note.

The Secretary of State is the official custodian of state laws and executive records. While not the primary operator, the office manages the official recording and preservation of changes to the state's election laws.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the earning of diminution credits to reduce the term of confinement of an incarcerated individual who is serving a sentence for murder in the first degree in a State or local correctional facility.
Title: First Degree Murder - Diminution Credits - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits incarcerated individuals serving a sentence for first-degree murder from earning diminution credits to reduce their term of confinement in State or local correctional facilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals serving sentences for first-degree murder and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided, so specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill is expected to increase state and local expenditures by requiring individuals convicted of first-degree murder to serve longer sentences as they can no longer earn credits to reduce their time.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for overseeing state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation, DPSCS is the primary entity that manages terms of confinement and calculates diminution credits for incarcerated individuals.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for long-term fiscal planning and budget development. Prohibiting diminution credits will increase the average length of stay for individuals convicted of first-degree murder, significantly increasing state expenditures for correctional services over time.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to indigent defendants and is directly impacted by changes to the law that affect the sentencing, credit eligibility, and potential terms of confinement for their clients.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state, providing counsel to the General Assembly and executive agencies such as DPSCS on the implementation and legal defense of changes to sentencing and credit laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, including policies regarding sentencing and recidivism.

The AOC provides operational and legal support to the state's courts, which must be aware of and apply changes to the statutory framework governing terms of confinement for first-degree murder during the judicial process.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, enforces state laws, and proposes the annual state budget, which will be affected by the long-term increase in costs associated with longer prison stays.

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law relating to no-knock search warrants; providing that a search warrant may not authorize a law enforcement officer to enter a building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched without first giving notice of the officer's authority and purpose; and providing that an officer executing a search warrant, under certain circumstances, may not enter the building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched unless reasonable notice of the officer's authority and purpose is given to any individual inside.
Title: Criminal Procedure - No-Knock Search Warrants - Repeal
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill repeals the authority for circuit court and District Court judges to issue no-knock search warrants. It prohibits law enforcement officers from entering a building, apartment, or premises to execute a search warrant without first giving notice of their authority and purpose, and requires officers to wait at least 20 seconds for a response from occupants before attempting entry, unless exigent circumstances exist. Additionally, the bill removes requirements for law enforcement agencies to report specific data related to no-knock warrants to the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: Maryland residents and occupants of searched premises, state and local law enforcement agencies, SWAT teams, and the Maryland judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local finances. While no specific dollar estimates are provided for revenue or expenditures, the bill may necessitate operational changes within State and local law enforcement agencies to align with the new prohibitions on no-knock warrants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial process for issuing search warrants. Circuit and District Court judges, supported by the AOC, will no longer have the authority to issue no-knock warrants and must ensure warrant applications and issued orders comply with the new notice requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends reporting requirements for law enforcement agencies that submit data to GOCPP. The office is responsible for developing the reporting format and collecting data on search warrants, which will no longer include no-knock specific data under this bill.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is heavily involved in the execution of search warrants. The repeal of no-knock warrants will necessitate changes to their operational procedures, tactical training, and reporting.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for state agencies. They will be responsible for advising law enforcement agencies on the legal implications of the repeal and representing the state in challenges regarding the execution of search warrants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal of no-knock warrants significantly impacts criminal defense strategies. The OPD will likely utilize this law to challenge the admissibility of evidence obtained in violation of the new notice and 'knock and announce' requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees various investigative units and law enforcement personnel who must comply with search warrant procedures. The bill's changes to warrant execution directly affect their operational protocols.

MDOT oversees the MDTA Police, Maryland Transit Administration Police, and Maryland Aviation Administration (BWI) Police. These forces execute search warrants and will be required to adhere to the new prohibitions on no-knock entries.
The Maryland Natural Resources Police, housed within DNR, exercise statewide law enforcement authority and execute search warrants, making the bill's procedural changes relevant to their operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically amends the duties of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) regarding the development of standards for SWAT teams and the training of law enforcement officers in warrant service.
The Maryland Capitol Police, managed by DGS, are a state law enforcement agency that must comply with the bill's requirements for warrant execution and reporting.
USM member institutions employ campus police forces with the authority to execute search warrants. These officers must be trained on the no-knock repeal and updated notice requirements.
Morgan State University maintains its own police force which must comply with state laws regarding the execution of search warrants and the notice requirements established by this bill.
As an independent state agency with its own campus police, the college's law enforcement personnel are subject to the bill's changes to warrant service procedures.
The OSP investigates and prosecutes offenses related to official misconduct and the electoral process, which may involve the application for and execution of search warrants subject to this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing an immunity from liability for a person who discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior if the person acts in good faith; establishing a presumption of good faith unless it is shown by a preponderance of the evidence that the person acted with actual malice or intentionally or recklessly disclosed false information; providing for the award of attorney's fees and costs in certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Civil Actions - Immunity - Disclosure of Allegations of Sexually Assaultive Behavior (Stop Silencing Survivors Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.
bill_summary: The Stop Silencing Survivors Act establishes that a person who in good faith discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior is immune from civil liability for that disclosure. The bill creates a legal presumption that such disclosures are made in good faith unless a preponderance of evidence proves actual malice or the intentional/reckless disclosure of false information, and it requires courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to individuals who successfully defend against claims of bad faith.
stakeholders: Individuals reporting or disclosing sexual assault allegations, persons accused of sexually assaultive behavior, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. While it mandates the awarding of attorney's fees and costs in certain civil litigation, these represent transfers between private parties rather than State expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial proceedings by establishing a new immunity standard, a presumption of good faith in civil cases, and a requirement for courts to award attorney’s fees and costs in specific circumstances related to disclosures of sexually assaultive behavior.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles liability claims against the state. The establishment of civil immunity for certain disclosures could impact the defense and outcome of liability claims involving state employees or agencies.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to all state agencies and would be responsible for interpreting this immunity and representing state entities or employees who may invoke this immunity in civil litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD was a contributor to the fiscal note and has a vested interest in the legal definitions of sexually assaultive behavior and the intersection between civil disclosures and criminal law proceedings.

The Commission enforces anti-discrimination laws where sexually assaultive behavior often intersects with sexual harassment in employment and public accommodations. Immunity for those disclosing such behavior supports the reporting mechanisms central to the Commission's work.

Synopsis: Prohibiting recovery by a certain plaintiff from being barred in a certain civil action due to the plaintiff's negligence, except under certain circumstances; requiring any damages awarded under the Act to be diminished in proportion to the amount of negligence attributed to the plaintiff; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Civil Actions - Motor Vehicle Accidents Involving Vulnerable Individuals - Comparative Negligence
Status: In the House - Referred to interim study by Judiciary

bill_summary: This bill establishes a modified comparative negligence standard for civil lawsuits involving motor vehicle accidents where the plaintiff is a 'vulnerable individual' (such as a pedestrian, bicyclist, or person on a motorcycle). Under this standard, a plaintiff is not barred from recovering damages unless their own negligence was a proximate cause of the injury and was greater than the combined negligence of all defendants. Any damages awarded are reduced in proportion to the plaintiff's own degree of negligence.
stakeholders: Vulnerable individuals involved in motor vehicle accidents (pedestrians, cyclists, etc.), motor vehicle operators, the Maryland Transit Administration, and State and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may lead to a significant increase in State and local expenditures due to higher tort claim payments, settlements, and insurance premiums. Because the bill replaces the contributory negligence bar with a comparative negligence standard for vulnerable individuals, the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) may see increased payouts for claims previously barred. The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is particularly impacted as it does not have a statutory limit on liability. Additionally, the State Treasurer’s Office and the Office of the Attorney General may require additional personnel to handle increased claim volumes and litigation, with one estimate for a claims employee starting at $86,100 in fiscal 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which pays out tort claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. The bill is expected to significantly increase SITF expenditures and requires additional staffing for the agency's Insurance Division to process increased claims.

The MTA is specifically identified as being significantly impacted because its tort liability is not capped under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. As a major operator of motor vehicles (buses and trains) that interact with vulnerable individuals, it faces a high risk of increased claim payouts and litigation costs.

The judicial branch is responsible for adjudicating the civil actions affected by this bill. The shift from contributory negligence to a comparative negligence standard for a specific class of plaintiffs represents a fundamental change in how motor vehicle negligence cases are handled in Maryland courts.

The OAG provides legal representation for the State and its agencies in civil litigation. The bill is expected to increase the volume and complexity of tort cases, requiring additional legal and administrative personnel to defend the State's interests.

As the parent agency for modal administrations like the MTA and SHA, MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and safety policies. The change in liability standards for accidents involving vulnerable road users directly impacts MDOT's operational and fiscal planning.

The MIA regulates the state's insurance industry. A change from contributory to comparative negligence for a significant portion of motor vehicle accidents will necessitate regulatory oversight of how insurance companies adjust their policies, rate-setting, and claims handling.

As the insurer of last resort for Maryland drivers, MAIF is directly impacted by changes in liability rules. The shift to comparative negligence will likely increase the number of claims for which the fund must pay damages and affect its overall fiscal stability.

MSP operates a large fleet of patrol vehicles and frequently interacts with vulnerable road users and emergency responders on highways. The agency is subject to tort claims that would now be evaluated under the new comparative negligence standard.

SHA is responsible for the design and maintenance of the state's non-toll highways where vulnerable individuals (including pedestrians and workers) are present. The agency's highway safety initiatives and its own vehicle operations are directly relevant to the bill's focus.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency. It oversees the budget execution and premium assessments for state agencies that pay into the SITF, which are expected to rise as a result of the bill's impact on tort payouts.

MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains a police force. Its operations involve significant interaction with motor vehicles and vulnerable individuals on bridges and tunnels, exposing the agency to potential tort claims under the revised negligence standard.

MVA houses the Highway Safety Office and regulates the operation of motor vehicles. The bill's specific focus on motor vehicle accidents and the definitions of vulnerable individuals is highly relevant to the agency's safety mission and regulatory scope.

DGS manages the state's vehicle fleet and provides security through the Capitol Police. The change in liability standards increases the potential fiscal impact of accidents involving state-owned vehicles operated by various departments.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals using wheelchairs and electric personal assistive mobility devices, groups for whom this department advocates and coordinates services.

The Department of Aging represents older adults, who are frequently pedestrians and thus categorized as 'vulnerable individuals' under the bill. The agency has an interest in policy changes that affect the legal recovery rights of this demographic.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals lawfully operating farm tractors or farm equipment on highways, which falls under the regulatory and support scope of the Department of Agriculture.

The definition of 'vulnerable individual' includes persons providing emergency services on a highway. MDEM coordinates such personnel, and the bill provides enhanced legal protections for these individuals in the event of a motor vehicle accident.

Synopsis: Requiring the annual report of the Maryland Parole Commission to include certain information; altering a certain provision of law to require the Commission to provide certain documents to an incarcerated individual and the incarcerated individual's representative at a certain time; requiring the Commission to document, state on the record, provide to an incarcerated individual, and make available to the public certain information; applying the Act retroactively; etc.
Title: Correctional Services - Maryland Parole Commission and Erroneously Convicted Individuals - Improvements in Transparency and Equity
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 432

bill_summary: This bill increases transparency and equity in Maryland's parole system by requiring the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) to provide incarcerated individuals and their representatives with copies of all documents used in parole suitability determinations. It establishes that the MPC cannot permanently deny parole and entitles incarcerated individuals to subsequent hearings at specific intervals based on their sentence length. Additionally, the bill requires the MPC to record all parole hearings, provide recordings at no cost to the incarcerated person, and include race-disaggregated data in its annual reports. It also prohibits counties from participating as parties in administrative proceedings for compensation for erroneously convicted individuals.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, legal representatives of incarcerated individuals, crime victims, the Maryland Parole Commission, and erroneously convicted individuals seeking state compensation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least 346,800 in FY 2027 to hire four office secretaries and cover costs for audio recordings of hearings. Ongoing annual expenditures are estimated to reach 456,000 by FY 2031. There is also an indeterminate decrease in general fund revenue because the MPC will no longer collect the 30 dollar fee for audio recording requests. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is responsible for compensating individuals found eligible for compensation and benefits due to erroneous conviction, a process modified by the bill's changes to party designations in such proceedings.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is the body responsible for overseeing and approving the fiscal payouts for erroneously convicted individuals.

As the primary personnel and budget agency, DBM will be involved in the creation of the four new staff positions and the allocation of additional general funds required by the Maryland Parole Commission to implement the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission (MPC), which is the primary agency impacted by the bill, is administratively housed within DPSCS. The bill significantly alters MPC's hearing procedures, reporting requirements, and staffing needs.

The Maryland Parole Commission is required to submit an expanded annual report to the Governor containing detailed statistics disaggregated by race, and the Governor oversees the executive functions related to correctional services and parole.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and policy development, which includes the transparency and equity improvements in the parole process established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's provisions regarding increased transparency, access to documents, and the right to subsequent parole hearings directly impact the legal rights and representation of indigent individuals in the parole system.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which manages the fiscal aspects of compensation for erroneously convicted individuals.

Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) within the OAH are responsible for adjudicating petitions for eligibility for compensation and benefits for erroneously convicted individuals, a process affected by the bill's changes to eligible parties.
The OAG represents the State in proceedings regarding the wrongful conviction of individuals before an Administrative Law Judge, and the bill clarifies the parties involved in these proceedings.

Synopsis: Establishing the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth to support improved access to mental health care services for children and youth in the State; imposing a tax on certain annual revenues derived from certain digital social media services in the State; providing for the calculation and collection of the tax; requiring the Comptroller to distribute revenue from the tax in a certain manner; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a gross revenues tax on digital social media services provided by companies with global annual gross revenues of at least $500 million. The revenue collected from this tax, after deducting administrative costs, is distributed to the newly created Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth, which is dedicated to improving access to mental health services for children and youth in Maryland.
responsible_party: The Maryland Comptroller and the Secretary of Health
stakeholders: Digital social media service providers with significant global revenues and Maryland children and youth in need of mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are estimated to increase by more than $30,000,000 in FY 2029 and could exceed $75,000,000 by the fourth year of implementation. State special fund expenditures for the Comptroller’s Office are expected to increase by $1.8 million in FY 2029 for staffing and computer programming, with ongoing costs around $765,000 by FY 2031. Remaining funds are available for mental health services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the Digital Social Media Gross Revenues Tax, including the collection of revenues, processing returns, auditing taxpayers, and distributing funds to the administrative account and the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth.

The Secretary of Health is designated to administer the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth, which is established by the bill to improve access to mental health care services for children and youth in the State.

The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth separately and invest the money in the fund, with interest earnings credited back to the fund.
DBM will oversee the fiscal impact of the new special fund and the creation of approximately 8 to 12 new staff positions within the Comptroller's Office required to manage the new tax system.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies implementing this bill and is responsible for proposing the state budget, through which the new fund's expenditures must be authorized.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court will likely hear appeals related to the assessment and collection of the new Digital Social Media Gross Revenues Tax.

The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Comptroller and the Department of Health regarding the implementation of the new law and will be responsible for defending the tax against anticipated litigation.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties (misdemeanors and perjury) for failure to file returns or filing false returns, which may increase the caseload of the state's judicial system.
The BPW may be required to approve significant procurement contracts related to the $1 million IT system upgrades needed by the Comptroller to manage the new tax.
The imposition of a significant gross revenues tax on major digital social media companies may impact the state's business climate and the agency's efforts to retain or attract technology companies.
DoIT may be involved in the oversight or strategy of the $1 million IT system modifications the Comptroller needs to process the new tax returns.
The bill's purpose of improving mental health care access for children and youth aligns with this office's mission to promote child well-being and coordinate related policy initiatives.
The OAH may conduct administrative hearings for contested cases or regulatory enforcement actions related to the new digital social media tax.
OLA will be responsible for conducting periodic fiscal and performance audits of the Comptroller's tax collection and the Department of Health's management of the new fund.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain condominium unit owner to obtain a condominium unit owner insurance policy or a substantially similar property insurance policy for the unit; requiring a certain insurance policy to include certain provisions; and authorizing a council of unit owners to acquire an insurance policy on behalf of a unit owner who does not maintain a certain required insurance policy and charge the insurance premium as an assessment to the unit owner.

bill_summary: This bill requires owners of residential condominium units, excluding detached units, to maintain a specific insurance policy for their unit that includes coverage for the council of unit owners' property insurance deductible, personal property replacement, loss of use for at least 12 months, personal liability of at least $500,000, and loss assessment of at least $25,000. Unit owners must provide annual evidence of this insurance to the council of unit owners, which is authorized to purchase a policy on the owner's behalf and charge the premium as an assessment if the owner fails to maintain the required coverage.
stakeholders: Residential condominium unit owners and condominium councils of unit owners
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. No specific dollar estimates for State revenue or expenditures are provided as the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates specific types of insurance coverage and minimum limits (such as personal liability, loss of use, and loss assessment) for condominium unit owners. As the state's insurance regulator, the MIA is responsible for reviewing and approving the policy forms and ensuring insurance carriers comply with these new statutory requirements.

The Secretary of State is tasked with the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland. This bill directly amends the Maryland Condominium Act to establish mandatory insurance standards for residential units, falling within the agency's primary administrative purview.

The Office of the Attorney General, particularly its Consumer Protection Division, was identified as a source for the fiscal analysis. The bill affects the rights and financial obligations of condominium homeowners, and the OAG would be involved in providing legal counsel on the Act's implementation or handling consumer disputes related to the new mandates.

The bill establishes new mandatory costs for condominium owners to ensure property protection and personal liability. This intersects with the agency's mission to ensure safe and secure housing and its role in monitoring housing policy impacts on Maryland residents.

Synopsis: Establishing the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force to study and make recommendations regarding the use and regulation of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency in the State; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, the General Assembly, the Senate Finance Committee, and the House Economic Matters Committee by October 1, 2027.
Title: Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force - Establishment
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 548

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force to study and make recommendations regarding the use and regulation of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency in Maryland. The task force is required to analyze the benefits and risks of these technologies for state and local government and private businesses, as well as their impact on state revenue and energy consumption, with a report of findings due by October 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Financial services industry representatives, the Maryland Blockchain Association, state and local government agencies, higher education faculty, and the Office of Financial Regulation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures increase by $49,400 in FY 2027 and $53,500 in FY 2028 to cover the costs of one contractual administrative specialist to staff the task force. Travel reimbursements for task force members are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor to provide staff for the Task Force and includes the Secretary of Labor as a member. The fiscal note indicates specific special fund expenditures for this department to hire a contractual administrative specialist.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly establishes a new Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force, which is a temporary body tasked with conducting a study and providing recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Comptroller, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force. Additionally, the task force is required to assess the impact of the cryptocurrency industry on state revenues.
The State Treasurer, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force, reflecting the office's role as the state's chief financial agency.
The Secretary of Commerce, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force, as the study involves economic development and private business impacts in the State.

The Secretary of Information Technology, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force. The subject matter—blockchain and digital assets—falls directly within the department's strategy and infrastructure oversight.
The Securities Commissioner (part of the OAG's Securities Division) is a named member of the Task Force. The OAG also provides legal counsel to such task forces.

The Governor is responsible for appointing five members of the Task Force (representing industry, faculty, and the Blockchain Association) and will receive the final report on findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments will likely assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting the five specific members of the task force appointed by the Governor.
The Task Force is specifically required to assess the impact of the cryptocurrency industry on energy consumption in the State, which relates to the department's environmental protection mission.
DBM is the principal personnel agency and will be involved in the creation of the contractual position required for staffing the Task Force as outlined in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Providing that certain evidence obtained through the use of an unmanned aircraft is inadmissible in a criminal, civil, or administrative proceeding; prohibiting a unit of State government or a political subdivision of the State from deploying or operating an unmanned aircraft subject to certain exceptions; and prohibiting a unit of State government or a political subdivision of the State from using certain information acquired through the use of an unmanned aircraft.
Title: Public Safety - State and Local Governments - Use of Unmanned Aircraft
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland State and local government units from deploying or operating unmanned aircraft (drones) for surveillance, evidence collection, or other purposes, and from using information acquired from drones operated by other entities. Specific exceptions are provided for search warrants, arrest warrants, fresh pursuit, search and rescue operations, locating escaped prisoners, preventing imminent bodily harm, or countering high-risk terrorist threats. Any evidence obtained in violation of these provisions is inadmissible in criminal, civil, or administrative proceedings.
responsible_party: Maryland units of State government and political subdivisions of the State
stakeholders: State and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, public universities, and individuals involved in legal or administrative proceedings.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may result in a significant decrease in federal fund revenues, specifically a potential forfeiture of up to 1200000 in federal grant funds for the State Highway Administration if the remaining balance is not spent by the bill's effective date. State agencies, including the Department of State Police and Maryland Department of Transportation, will face significant operational impacts as the bill restricts drone use for investigations, crash reconstruction, and bridge assessments. Local governments are expected to face operational impacts, but their finances are not anticipated to be significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees all state agencies affected by this bill and is responsible for ensuring the enforcement of these new public safety regulations.
The Comptroller regulates the alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuel industries; the bill restricts the use of drones in regulatory investigations and inspections related to these fields.

The Treasurer's Office oversees state insurance protection and property management; the bill's restrictions on drone use for condition assessments of state assets may impact insurance risk assessments and property management.

The OAG will be responsible for advising state agencies on compliance with the new drone restrictions and litigating cases regarding the admissibility of drone-obtained evidence in criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture often utilizes aerial technology for environmental resource protection, soil conservation, and agricultural monitoring, all of which would be restricted by this bill.

DBM oversees the state budget and would be concerned with the fiscal impact of losing federal grant funding (such as the SMART grant) and the increased costs associated with finding drone alternatives.
The bill impacts the use of drones by local school systems and state education facilities for maintenance, site planning, and safety monitoring.
MDEM coordinates disaster response; while the bill contains a search and rescue exception, other drone uses for hazard mitigation and disaster recovery assessment would be significantly restricted.
MDE uses drones for environmental studies, monitoring water and air quality, and inspecting hazardous waste sites, which are impacted by the bill's restrictions.
DGS uses drones for facility maintenance, bridge inspections, and structural assessments of state-owned buildings, all of which would be prohibited under 'any other purpose'.
The Maryland Department of Health may use drones for environmental health inspections or monitoring regulatory compliance in various healthcare-related contexts.
DoIT coordinates state technology strategy; as drones are significant data-gathering tools, the department would be involved in managing the technical policy implications of this restriction.
DJS utilizes surveillance for facility security and youth supervision; the bill would restrict these capabilities except in cases of specific emergencies like escaped prisoners.
The Department of Labor enforces workplace safety and labor laws; drones are a primary tool for conducting safe and efficient inspections of industrial sites and regulated industries.
The DNR and Natural Resources Police rely on drones for wildlife monitoring, forestry management, and conservation law enforcement, which are significantly impacted by the surveillance ban.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS uses drones for facility security and perimeter surveillance; the bill limits these uses to specific exceptions such as locating escaped prisoners or preventing imminent harm.

MDOT faces a significant fiscal impact, including the potential loss of $1.2 million in federal grant funds, and an operational impact on bridge inspections, crash reconstruction, and highway safety planning.
The Maryland National Guard may use unmanned aircraft for state domestic missions; while some missions are exempt, routine surveillance or equipment testing by the state military would be affected.
MSP is a primary user of drone technology for crash scene mapping and fire marshal investigations (arson and explosives), both of which are hindered by this legislation.
The bill creates a new rule of evidence (Section 10-926) that makes drone-obtained evidence inadmissible, directly impacting court proceedings and the operations of the judicial branch.
The MCA utilizes drones for regulatory inspections and investigations of the cannabis industry; the bill would restrict these enforcement activities.
The MCSS monitors school safety; restrictions on drone use for surveillance or large-scale event monitoring at schools would impact their safety strategies.
MES uses drones for technical environmental services, such as monitoring landfills and wastewater facilities, which are impacted by the 'any other purpose' restriction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD will utilize the bill's evidence inadmissibility provisions to defend clients in criminal and juvenile proceedings where drone-obtained evidence is introduced.
The MSA uses drones for construction monitoring and facility inspections for sports venues and public schools, which would be restricted under the bill.
As an independent state agency, the university uses drones for research, security during major campus events, and facility management.
The OAH adjudicates administrative disputes; the bill's rule making drone evidence inadmissible will apply to the contested cases heard by Administrative Law Judges.
The PSC notes that the prohibition could impede the introduction of illustrative evidence in utility-related administrative proceedings.
USM institutions utilize drones for event safety, public safety monitoring during large gatherings, and research, all of which face new restrictions under the bill.
MHEC coordinates policies for state colleges and universities, which will need to adjust their institutional policies regarding the use of drones for safety and research.

Synopsis: Limiting the excess amount of tax credit certificates to $20,000,000, that the Department of Commerce may carry forward and issue in subsequent taxable years for a credit against the State income tax for certain costs related to certain theatrical productions in the State; prohibiting the Secretary from issuing tax credit certificates for credit amounts totaling more than $2,000,00 in the aggregate for a single theatrical production;  and extending the termination date of the credit to June 30, 2032.
Title: Income Tax - Theatrical Production Tax Credit - Alterations and Sunset Extension
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 18

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc

bill_summary: This bill extends the Maryland theatrical production tax credit for five years, through tax year 2031, with a final sunset date of June 30, 2032. Additionally, it imposes a $20,000,000 cap on the aggregate amount of unissued tax credits that the Maryland Department of Commerce may carry forward from prior fiscal years to be issued in subsequent taxable years.
stakeholders: Qualified theatrical production entities, including for-profit national touring or pre-Broadway live stage theatrical productions, and qualified theatrical production facilities located in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2032 based on recent program activity. There is no fiscal impact in FY 2027. If credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, revenues for the Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund will decrease, which would also result in a decrease in local highway user revenues. Expenditures are not otherwise affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the theatrical production tax credit, including issuing tax credit certificates and managing the new $20 million aggregate carry-forward limit.

The Comptroller's Office is responsible for processing the income tax credits and managing the resulting impacts on State tax revenues, including collections for the General Fund and other special funds.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and local highway user revenues, which are funded through tax collections managed in part by the Department of Transportation.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and managing the state's budget, which will be impacted by the projected revenue decrease through fiscal year 2032.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Commerce, and the Governor is responsible for proposing the annual state budget which will be affected by the revenue loss.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on a public school employer negotiating the maximum number of students assigned to a class.
Title: Education - Collective Bargaining - Certificated Employees - Class Size
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition on public school employers negotiating the maximum number of students assigned to a class during collective bargaining with certificated employees.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board and local boards of education
stakeholders: Certificated public school employees, local school systems, students, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State operations or finances. However, State general fund expenditures may increase for teacher retirement costs if local negotiations result in hiring more teachers. Local school system expenditures may increase for teacher salaries if class size limits are established, but these costs are constrained by the amount of funds a county government appropriates for its school system. Consequently, any additional spending might be redirected from other school system expenditures. The Public Employee Relations Board can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources, and the overall fiscal impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing collective bargaining, administering elections for exclusive representatives, and resolving impasse disputes for local public school system personnel, as specifically noted in the bill's fiscal note.

The Maryland State Department of Education provides leadership and oversight for the 24 local school systems whose collective bargaining processes and classroom environments are directly impacted by the removal of the class size negotiation prohibition.

The fiscal note indicates that if collective bargaining results in hiring additional teachers to meet class size requirements, the State's general fund expenditures for teacher retirement costs would increase; the SRA manages these pension and retirement benefits for teachers.

Reducing class sizes through collective bargaining may create a need for additional classroom space and facility expansion, which falls under the IAC's responsibility for planning and funding public school capital improvement projects.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the state budget and would be responsible for managing any resulting increases in state expenditures for teacher retirement costs or potential mediation expenses.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MSDE and PERB and may be required to provide legal interpretations of the change in collective bargaining statutes or represent the agencies in disputes.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from operating or towing a vehicle, subject to certain exceptions, without making reasonable efforts to remove from exposed vehicle surfaces accumulated snow and ice; and prohibiting a person from committing a violation of the Act that contributes to an accident resulting in property damage or the death of or serious bodily injury to another person.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Dangerous Accumulations of Snow and Ice - Removal From Exposed Vehicle Surfaces (Clear Before You Drive Act)
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 668

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Clear Before You Drive Act prohibits a person from operating or towing a vehicle without making reasonable efforts to remove accumulated snow and ice from exposed surfaces such as the hood, roof, and windows. The bill establishes specific fine structures for both noncommercial and commercial vehicles and allows for significantly higher penalties if the failure to remove snow or ice contributes to an accident resulting in property damage, injury, or death. Enforcement is primarily designated as a secondary action unless a related accident occurs.
responsible_party: Maryland State Police, local law enforcement agencies, and the District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Operators of noncommercial and commercial vehicles, law enforcement agencies, and the general motoring public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, there is a potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fines collected in the District Court. Fines for noncommercial vehicles range from $25 to $200 for standard violations and $200 to $1,000 if an accident occurs. Fines for commercial vehicles range from $75 to $1,000 for standard violations and $500 to $1,500 if an accident occurs. Enforcement is expected to be handled with existing resources, and there is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing motor vehicle and traffic laws on state highways. They will be directly responsible for the secondary enforcement of snow and ice removal requirements and issuing citations to violators.

As part of the Maryland Department of Transportation, the MVA manages driver licensing, vehicle registration, and the assessment of points on driving records. This bill amends the Transportation Article, and while it specifies fines, the MVA oversees the regulatory framework for vehicle operation and records related to such offenses.

MDOT is the parent agency for the MVA and the State Highway Administration. It is responsible for the overall safety and operation of the state's multi-modal transportation network, which is directly impacted by this new safety mandate for vehicles on state roads.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court of Maryland, which will be responsible for processing the new citations, collecting fine revenues, and adjudicating any contested cases resulting from the enforcement of this law.

The MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains its own police force. These officers will be responsible for enforcing the snow and ice removal requirements on Maryland's bridges, tunnels, and toll roads.

The State Highway Administration is responsible for maintaining state highways and ensuring traveler safety. Accumulated snow and ice falling from vehicles pose a significant hazard to the roadway safety and infrastructure managed by SHA.

The bill includes a specific exception for operators if compliance would cause them to violate workplace safety laws or regulations. The Maryland Department of Labor oversees workplace safety and labor laws, making them relevant to the interpretation of this exception.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the MDOT, State Police, and other state agencies regarding the implementation, enforcement, and legal interpretation of new statutory requirements within the Transportation Article.

The Comptroller's office is responsible for collecting state revenues. Fines collected from violations of this act will contribute to the state's general fund revenues, which the Comptroller monitors and manages.
DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The fiscal note indicates a potential increase in general fund revenues from the fines established by this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments (MSP, MDOT, etc.) tasked with implementing and enforcing this legislation. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Department of Juvenile Services from hiring or retaining an individual convicted of certain crimes.
Title: Department of Juvenile Services - Employees - Prohibited Convictions (Juvenile Offender Protection Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Juvenile Services from hiring or retaining any individual who has been convicted of certain serious crimes, such as murder, kidnapping, rape, and child abuse, unless the conviction has been reversed or vacated.
stakeholders: Current and prospective employees of the Department of Juvenile Services and the youth served by the Department.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The Department of Juvenile Services is already required to perform criminal background checks on all employees before they begin work.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary subject of the bill, the Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) is responsible for implementing the new hiring and retention prohibitions for individuals with certain criminal convictions to protect the youth in their care.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note specifies that DJS relies on the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which is housed within this department, to perform the background checks necessary to identify the prohibited convictions listed in the bill.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM oversees state employee policies and provides guidance to executive agencies regarding the implementation of statutory hiring and retention requirements.

The OAG provides legal counsel to DJS and would likely be involved in advising the department on the legal procedures for terminating existing employees under the 'retain' prohibition and representing the state in any resulting litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policies aimed at protecting youth and reducing juvenile delinquency, which aligns with the bill's 'Juvenile Offender Protection Act' goals.
The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; if current DJS employees are terminated (not retained) due to the bill's provisions, they may appeal those personnel actions to the OAH.

The Governor's Office has broad oversight over the executive branch and its departments, including the appointment of leadership for the Department of Juvenile Services and coordination of the administration's public safety priorities.

Synopsis: Repealing certain limitations on noneconomic damages in civil actions for personal injury or wrongful death; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Civil Actions - Noneconomic Damages - Personal Injury and Wrongful Death
Status: In the House - Referred to interim study by Judiciary

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory limitations, or caps, on noneconomic damages awarded in civil actions for personal injury or wrongful death. The bill does not affect caps on damages in medical malpractice cases and applies prospectively to causes of action arising on or after October 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Plaintiffs and defendants in personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits, the Maryland Transit Administration, insurance providers, and law firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund may increase significantly because the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is not covered by the Maryland Tort Claims Act's liability limits and would face higher damage awards. Local governments remain largely protected by the Local Government Tort Claims Act. The bill may also have an operational impact on the Judiciary and circuit courts due to potentially more complex or frequent litigation. Small businesses may see an increase in insurance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the Maryland Department of Transportation because its Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) unit is not covered by the liability limits of the Maryland Tort Claims Act. Repealing the noneconomic damages cap will likely lead to much higher settlement and award costs for MTA, potentially increasing Transportation Trust Fund expenditures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which the fiscal note identifies as being operationally impacted. Repealing damage caps is expected to increase the complexity and duration of personal injury and wrongful death litigation in circuit courts.

As the chief legal representative for the state, the Office of the Attorney General defends state agencies in civil litigation. The removal of noneconomic damage caps directly impacts the legal strategy, financial exposure, and workload of the office in personal injury and wrongful death cases.

As the state's insurer of last resort for drivers, the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is directly impacted by the removal of damage caps, which will likely increase the size of payouts for claims related to personal injury and wrongful death from vehicle accidents.

The State Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, which covers tort claims against most state agencies. While protected by the Maryland Tort Claims Act, the office oversees the state's fiscal liability and insurance protection, both of which are affected by shifts in damage award trends.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance market. The repeal of caps on noneconomic damages is expected to impact insurance premiums and market stability, requiring oversight and monitoring by the administration.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. Significant potential increases in state expenditures, such as those within the Transportation Trust Fund, fall under its budgetary oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals language in the Maryland Code that specifically references awards by the health claims arbitration panel, which is administered by this office. Additionally, the office was identified as a primary information source regarding the impact on injury claims.

Synopsis: Providing that during the trial of a criminal case in which a defendant is charged with an assault in the second degree, a certain statement is not excluded by the hearsay rule if the statement is offered against a party that has engaged in, directed, or conspired to commit wrongdoing that was intended to and did procure the unavailibility of the declarant of the statement, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Admission of Out-of-Court Statements - Assault in the Second Degree
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill expands an exception to the hearsay rule in criminal cases to include trials for second-degree assault. Under the bill, out-of-court statements from an unavailable declarant may be admitted into evidence if the defendant engaged in or conspired to commit wrongdoing intended to make the witness unavailable.
stakeholders: Defendants charged with second-degree assault, victims and witnesses of second-degree assault, Maryland State's Attorneys, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Specific dollar estimates for any minor administrative impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state's judicial branch. This bill directly alters the rules of evidence (hearsay exceptions) that must be applied by judges in criminal trials involving second-degree assault.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation for indigent defendants. Expanding the admissibility of out-of-court statements in second-degree assault cases directly impacts their defense strategies and the outcomes of their clients' cases.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Attorney General represents the state in criminal appeals. This change in evidentiary procedure will affect appellate litigation and the legal guidance provided to state prosecutorial entities.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal law violations, including second-degree assault. The bill affects the legal standard for using witness statements collected during their investigations when a witness is made unavailable by a defendant.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies. The bill represents a legislative policy change in criminal procedure that falls under their advisory and policy-development scope.

The Department of Juvenile Services manages youth in the justice system. Since second-degree assault is a common charge in juvenile proceedings, changes to the rules of evidence regarding such charges are relevant to their cases and the youth they supervise.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees correctional facilities and community supervision. While the bill is procedural, changes to evidence admissibility that could affect conviction rates for assault have a downstream impact on the population management of their facilities.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes specific criminal offenses. As an independent prosecutorial agency within the executive branch, they are relevant to any changes in the state's criminal procedure laws.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that impacts criminal justice procedures.

Synopsis: Altering a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for unreimbursed expenses paid or incurred by eligible teachers during a taxable year for the purchase of certain classroom supplies to include prekindergarten classroom teachers employed in publicly funded prekindergarten programs at eligible public providers or lead teachers or consulting teachers employed in a publicly funded prekindergarten program at an eligible private provider in the State; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Classroom Supplies Purchased by Teachers - Alteration
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 61

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility for a Maryland income tax subtraction modification for classroom supplies to include full-time prekindergarten teachers in publicly funded programs, including those at eligible public and private providers. The modification allows eligible teachers to subtract up to $250 of unreimbursed classroom supply expenses from their federal adjusted gross income for State tax purposes.
stakeholders: Full-time prekindergarten teachers in publicly funded programs in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $80,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Local income tax revenues are projected to decrease by about $50,000 annually starting in the same year. The Comptroller’s Office can implement the change using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's income tax laws and collecting revenue. This bill directly alters a tax subtraction modification, requiring the Comptroller to update tax forms, instructions, and processing systems to accommodate the expanded eligibility for prekindergarten teachers.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the public education system and the prekindergarten programs impacted by this bill. The bill's definition of an 'eligible teacher' relies on providers defined within the Education Article, which is administered by MSDE.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for fiscal planning and revenue estimation. The bill is projected to decrease state general fund revenues by $80,000 annually, requiring the agency to account for this fiscal impact in state budget planning.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. As the bill modifies state revenue and touches on education policy (a primary focus for the executive branch), the office has a high-level administrative interest in its fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Requiring the University System of Maryland to develop, in consultation with the State Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission, certain recommendations for a Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program and a teacher preparation pathway in a certain manner; establishing the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup; requiring, the Governor to include an appropriation of $125,000 in fiscal years 2028 and 2029, to support the Workgroup's recommendations; etc.
Title: Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup - Establishment
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup, led by the University System of Maryland. The workgroup is tasked with developing recommendations for a structured teacher preparation pathway for high school students in Southern Maryland, with a focus on increasing access for rural and underrepresented students and building a diverse teacher pipeline. The University System of Maryland must report its recommendations and an implementation plan by June 30, 2029.
stakeholders: High school students in Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties), historically underrepresented and rural students, and the Southern Maryland public school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a General Fund expenditure of $125,000 in each of fiscal years 2028 and 2029 (totaling $250,000) as an appropriation to the University System of Maryland (USM) to support the workgroup and the development of recommendations. USM higher education revenues and expenditures will increase by corresponding amounts. Local school systems can participate in the workgroup using existing resources. The bill terminates June 30, 2030, and does not fund the actual implementation of the program itself.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The University System of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for developing the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program recommendations, convening the associated workgroup, and receiving the mandated annual appropriation to support these efforts.

The State Department of Education is a mandated consultant for the program's development, its Superintendent is a member of the workgroup, and the agency is responsible for the program's long-term administration and implementation.
The Commission is a primary consulting body for the development of the teacher preparation pathway, and the Secretary of Higher Education is a mandated member of the program's workgroup.
The agency is tasked with consulting on the creation of the Southern Maryland teacher pathway and is represented on the workgroup established to develop implementation recommendations.
The President of Saint Mary's College of Maryland is specifically named in the bill as a required member of the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup, to study and propose a credit-bearing teacher preparation pathway.

The agency oversees the state's budget and personnel, and will be responsible for managing the mandated annual appropriation of $125,000 for fiscal years 2028 and 2029 to support the workgroup's activities.

The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing a representative to the program workgroup and will receive the final report and recommendations for the pathway's implementation and required legislative changes.

The office will assist the Governor in the administrative process of vetting and recommending a representative to be appointed to the newly created Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup.
The establishment of a new regional teacher pipeline and reporting on student outcomes aligns with the agency's mission to link and analyze student and workforce performance data.

The bill explicitly focuses on teacher shortages and educational access in rural areas such as Southern Maryland, which is core to the Council's mission of advocating for regional interests and economic development in rural counties.
