bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission on Historic, Cultural, and Civic Contributions in Education to evaluate and improve the inclusion of diverse histories and cultures in Maryland's K-12 education system. The commission is responsible for studying current curriculum standards, instructional materials, and school calendars to ensure they accurately reflect the contributions and experiences of diverse groups, including Indigenous, African American, LGBTQ+, and disabled communities. It requires recommendations to be made to the State Board of Education for curriculum updates and to the Maryland Higher Education Commission for teacher training improvements.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, K-12 educators, institutions of higher education, and members of diverse racial, ethnic, cultural, and social communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures will increase by $56,400 in fiscal year 2027 to cover the costs of a half-time education program specialist at the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to staff the commission. Projected costs increase annually, reaching $73,300 by fiscal year 2031. Local school systems may incur indeterminate costs related to future curriculum updates or professional development based on the commission's recommendations, although these are expected to align with existing curriculum review cycles.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. It is required to provide staffing for the new Commission, and the State Board of Education (within MSDE) must review the Commission's recommendations and update Pre-K through Grade 12 educational standards accordingly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to establish the Commission on Historic, Cultural, and Civic Contributions in Education, which fits the definition of an executive commission created to address specific government policy issues.

The Commission is mandated to make recommendations to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) regarding updates to teacher preparation programs to include instruction on the history of diverse people.
The Secretary of Disabilities is responsible for recommending a member to represent the state's disabled community on the Commission.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland is required to nominate/select a representative from a USM institution to serve on the Commission.

The bill requires a representative on the Commission from a Historically Black College or University (HBCU) that is a separate entity from the University System of Maryland; Morgan State University is the state's independent public HBCU.
The fiscal note indicates a general fund expenditure increase of $56,400 in FY 2027 to cover staffing and operational costs for the Commission, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget.

The Commission is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor annually, and the Governor may still have appointment roles or administrative oversight over the reporting process.
The bill (in its original form and through the involvement of the Commission on Indian Affairs) references cultural and ethnic commissions managed under GOCI for nominating members to the Commission.

As the legal representative for all state agencies, the OAG may be required to provide counsel to MSDE and the State Board regarding the implementation of new educational standards and the Commission's regulatory compliance.

Synopsis: Establishing the Foster Care Transition Grant Program in the Department of Human Services to provide for the economic security of individuals aging out of the out-of-home placement program; providing that, beginning in fiscal year 2028, an individual can become eligible for a foster care transition grant of $1,000 for 1 year under certain circumstances; providing that payments made under the Program may not be considered income or resources for purposes of determining eligibility for certain benefits; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Foster Care Transition Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Human Services to provide economic security for individuals aging out of foster care. Beginning in fiscal year 2028, the program provides eligible individuals with a $1,000 monthly grant for one year. To qualify, an individual must have been in an out-of-home placement on their 18th birthday and have turned 18 on or after October 1, 2026. The bill also mandates annual reporting on recipient demographics and outcomes.
stakeholders: Individuals aging out of the Maryland foster care system (out-of-home placement) who reach age 18 on or after October 1, 2026.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $479,500 in FY 2027 for contractual staff and one-time information technology costs. Expenditures peak at $4,077,900 in FY 2028 as grant payments begin and are estimated at approximately $3,170,000 annually for FY 2029 through FY 2031. The program and its associated costs terminate on September 30, 2031. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Foster Care Transition Grant Program within this department. DHS is responsible for implementing the program, determining eligibility, issuing the $1,000 monthly grants, and submitting annual outcome reports to the General Assembly.

The fiscal note explicitly states that DoIT will incur $378,000 in one-time programming costs in FY 2027 to update and maintain the Enrollment and Eligibility System (E&E) for managing the distribution of funds, plus annual maintenance costs thereafter.

The bill specifies that grants issued under the program may not be considered income for determining eligibility for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the significant general fund expenditure increases (estimated at over $3 million annually) required for the grants and contractual staff, and manage the associated budget execution.
The bill mandates that program grants are not considered income for State and federal financial aid and college support programs, which MHEC administers and coordinates.
The bill provides that the grants may not be considered income for purposes of the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), which the Comptroller's office manages and administers.

MHBE is responsible for determining eligibility for Medicaid and financial assistance; the bill's requirement to exclude the grant from income calculations directly impacts their eligibility determination processes.

The program directly aligns with GOC's mission to reduce child poverty and improve access to economic opportunities for vulnerable youth, specifically those transitioning out of the foster care system.

The team is specifically charged with identifying and piloting initiatives to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility; this grant program serves as a direct policy tool for these objectives.

The bill requires annual reporting on outcome measures such as employment and housing status; GOPI utilizes such data-driven metrics to oversee the implementation of the Governor's priorities and ensure government responsiveness.

OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like DHS and MDH. They may be required to review the bill's income exclusion provisions against federal law, a potential conflict noted in the fiscal note.
OLA will likely conduct fiscal compliance audits of the new program within DHS to ensure the appropriate distribution of millions in state general funds.
The center links student and workforce data; they may assist in analyzing the long-term effectiveness of the grant program on the employment and educational outcomes of foster care transition youth.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and DHS. The Governor is responsible for proposing the budget that will fund this multi-million dollar program.
As the provider of higher education for many transition-age youth, the system is impacted by how these grants are treated in financial aid calculations for its students.
MSU, as a public university, will be affected by changes in how state financial aid and college support programs are calculated for students receiving these transition grants.
As a public honors college, it is impacted by the bill's provisions regarding the exclusion of transition grants from financial aid eligibility assessments for its students.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Energy Administration to conduct a study on the potential for land-based wind energy generation in the State and the siting of land-based wind energy generating systems in the State; authorizing the Administration to use available funds in the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund to conduct the study; and requiring by December 1, 2026, the Administration to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly.
Title: Maryland Energy Administration - Study on Land-Based Wind Energy
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Energy Administration to conduct a study on land-based wind energy generation in Maryland. The study must evaluate the total potential for land-based wind energy, identify potential locations, and investigate mitigation strategies that allow wind energy systems to operate alongside military radar technologies. The Administration is authorized to use the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for this study and must report its findings to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland Energy Administration, land-based wind energy developers, military installations using radar technology, and Maryland state legislators
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill authorizes the Maryland Energy Administration to use existing money within the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to cover the costs of the study.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary agency responsible for conducting the study on land-based wind energy, assessing potential siting, and reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill specifically requires the study to investigate mitigation efforts for military radar technologies, such as ADAMS, which directly involves the military readiness and operations overseen by the Adjutant General.
The PSC is the regulatory body for utility-scale energy generation and siting in Maryland; the results of this study will directly impact the planning and regulation of future wind energy projects.
Land-based wind siting significantly impacts natural resources, wildlife habitats, and state-owned lands, which are managed and protected by DNR.
MDP is responsible for land use planning and providing technical assistance for infrastructure development, making them a key stakeholder in the siting and potential assessment of wind energy.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MEA, and is the recipient of the mandated report and recommendations.
The bill authorizes the use of funds from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) to conduct the study, requiring fiscal oversight by DBM regarding budget execution and personnel.
The assessment of wind energy potential has significant implications for economic development, job creation, and attracting green industry businesses to Maryland.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MEA and would likely assist in interpreting the statutory requirements for the study and any regulatory implications.
MDE is the lead agency for renewable energy goals and environmental protection, making the study's findings on sustainable energy generation highly relevant to their mission.

bill_summary: This emergency bill prohibits any person from operating an immigration detention facility in a building, structure, or facility that was not originally designed and constructed specifically for the purpose of housing or detaining individuals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals detained for federal civil immigration violations, private entities or persons operating detention facilities, and State and local government units.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing the state's correctional facilities and being governed by the Correctional Services Article, which this bill amends, DPSCS is directly impacted by changes to laws regulating detention facilities.

As the chief legal officer for the State, the OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to state agencies on the interpretation and enforcement of this new prohibition on immigration detention facility operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, directly advising the Governor on policies related to detention and law enforcement standards.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing state laws. This bill impacts executive policy regarding intergovernmental agreements and the use of facilities for detention.

DGS manages state-owned facilities, real estate leasing, and construction. They are relevant because the bill establishes specific requirements for the 'original design and construction' of buildings used for detention.

The Board approves significant state expenditures, including the acquisition, lease, and transfer of state property, which would be subject to the restrictions on facility use for immigration detention.

DJS operates secure residential and detention facilities. While focused on youth, shifts in the legal standards for detention facilities within the Correctional Services Article are relevant to their operational oversight.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP may be involved in the enforcement of state laws or coordination with local agencies regarding the legal operation of detention facilities.

MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws and monitors state contracts. Immigration detention facilities often involve civil rights considerations that fall under their monitoring and educational mandate.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent individuals in the justice system; changes to the regulation and location of detention facilities impact the rights and access of the populations they serve.
GOHS coordinates statewide disaster and safety strategies and acts as a liaison for federal security issues, which overlaps with the regulation of federal civil immigration detention facilities.
As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM oversees the budgets of the agencies implementing these detention facility standards, though the immediate fiscal impact is noted as minimal.
The bill references zoning variances and land use, which are areas where the Department of Planning provides data analysis and policy guidance to local governments.
The AOC provides support to the judiciary, which would adjudicate any legal disputes or appeals arising from the enforcement of this new detention facility regulation.
The OAH may be tasked with conducting hearings for contested cases involving state agency decisions related to the permitting or operation of these facilities.

Synopsis: Increasing the penalties for a violation of the prohibition against making certain threats against a State official, a local official, a deputy State's Attorney, an assistant State's Attorney, or an assistant Public Defender.
Title: Criminal Law - Threats Against State or Local Official - Penalties
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill reclassifies the crime of knowingly making a threat against a State official, local official, State's Attorney, or Public Defender from a misdemeanor to a felony. It also increases the maximum penalties for this offense from three years imprisonment and a $2,500 fine to 10 years imprisonment and a $5,000 fine.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: State and local officials (including the Governor, General Assembly members, and judges), State's Attorneys, Public Defenders, and individuals charged with making threats against these officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. Reclassifying the offense from a misdemeanor to a felony will likely shift cases from the District Court to the circuit courts and may lead to longer sentences for some offenders. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services reported minimal activity for this specific offense in fiscal 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor and Governor-elect are explicitly listed in the bill as State officials protected by increased criminal penalties for threats.
The Lieutenant Governor and Lieutenant Governor-elect are explicitly listed in the bill as State officials protected by increased criminal penalties for threats.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly includes assistant Public Defenders as protected parties under the reclassified felony prohibition against threats.
Judges and judicial appointees are protected State officials, and the bill's felony reclassification is expected to shift cases from the District Court to the circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reclassifies the offense to a felony and increases maximum imprisonment, which directly impacts correctional intakes and the supervision of probation cases.
The agency is responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses related to the integrity and safety of state officials.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the State Police are responsible for investigating criminal threats against high-ranking State officials.
Registers of Wills are constitutional officers and State officials specifically protected by the provisions of this bill.
The agency serves as the chief legal representative for the State and provides counsel to the Governor and other officials protected by the bill.
As a constitutional officer, the Comptroller is a protected State official under the bill's expanded penalty provisions.
As a constitutional officer, the State Treasurer is a protected State official under the bill's expanded penalty provisions.
As a constitutional officer, the Secretary of State is a protected State official under the bill's expanded penalty provisions.

bill_summary: This bill exempts psychiatric health care facilities and psychiatric or mental health services from the Certificate of Need (CON) requirement. It removes psychiatry and its subcategories from the definition of medical services that require review and approval by the Maryland Health Care Commission, thereby allowing for the establishment or expansion of these facilities and services without a CON.
stakeholders: Psychiatric health care facilities, mental health service providers, and patients requiring psychiatric or mental health services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances or small business finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission directly administers the Certificate of Need (CON) program and the State Health Plan, both of which are central to the regulatory changes proposed in this bill regarding psychiatric services.

The Department of Health is the parent agency for the Maryland Health Care Commission and is responsible for the state's behavioral health policy and the regulation of health facilities and providers.

The HSCRC regulates hospital rates and revenues; the establishment or expansion of psychiatric services at hospitals (exempted from CON requirements under this bill) would impact the commission's financial oversight and the state's all-payer model.
The Governor's Office coordinates major policy initiatives for the executive branch, including those related to healthcare access and the reduction of regulatory barriers for health services.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Department of Health regarding statutory changes and the enforcement of health regulations.

bill_summary: This bill requires certain health insurance carriers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for opportunistic salpingectomy for the purpose of ovarian cancer prevention. It prohibits these entities from imposing copayments, coinsurance, or deductible requirements on this coverage, with an exception for high-deductible health plans. Additionally, the bill mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a study on the coverage of non-opportunistic salpingectomy and report its findings by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, individuals seeking ovarian cancer prevention, state employees, and retirees
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program are estimated to increase by at least 25000 in fiscal 2027 and at least 50000 annually thereafter to provide coverage without cost sharing. The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal special fund revenue increase from filing fees in fiscal 2027. Local government expenditures may increase for jurisdictions that purchase fully insured health plans if premiums rise as a result of the mandate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing insurance laws. It will oversee compliance with the new coverage requirements for opportunistic salpingectomy and process the rate and form filings from carriers.

Section 3 of the bill specifically mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a mandated benefits study regarding salpingectomy for individuals not at high risk of ovarian cancer and report findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note indicates that the bill will increase expenditures for this program to provide the required coverage without cost-sharing.

As the administrator of Maryland's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange is responsible for monitoring health benefit mandates and their impact on plan offerings and federal cost-sharing standards.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees public health policy and the Medicaid program. While the mandate primarily affects private insurance, the department maintains a significant interest in cancer prevention strategies and health equity.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the primary implementing agencies (MIA, MHCC, and DBM) to ensure that new insurance regulations and mandated studies are conducted within legal and constitutional frameworks.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, coordinates policy initiatives, and is responsible for signing the bill into law.

bill_summary: The LEAD Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to mandate entrance-level and in-service police training regarding individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, and autism. This curriculum must include specific protocols for locating wandering or missing individuals, searching near bodies of water, sensory-aware approaches, reunification, documentation, and interagency coordination.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: Maryland police officers, individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, or autism, and local and state law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to conduct additional training to the extent that local police training schools do not already provide the specific training required by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is responsible for the training standards mentioned in the bill, is administratively housed within this department. The department is also listed as a source of information for the fiscal note.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police must implement the new entrance-level and in-service training requirements for its officers. The agency was also a consulted party for the fiscal note.

The department oversees developmental disabilities and behavioral health services, making them a primary subject matter expert for the curriculum development regarding autism and intellectual disabilities.

The bill's focus on intellectual and developmental disabilities directly aligns with this department's mission to coordinate and improve services for residents with disabilities and ensure inclusive practices.
The bill mandates training specifically regarding dementia and locating missing individuals, which is a core concern and focus area for the Department of Aging and its advocacy for older adults.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policies aimed at improving law enforcement interactions with vulnerable populations.

The agency oversees training for school safety personnel; since School Resource Officers (SROs) are police officers subject to MPTSC standards, this new curriculum will impact training for officers working in school environments with neurodiverse students.
The department operates the Natural Resources Police, whose officers must comply with the training standards set by the MPTSC. The agency was consulted in the fiscal analysis.
The department oversees several police forces, including the MDTA and MTA police, who are subject to these statewide police training requirements.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies and commissions involved in developing these training standards and ensures compliance with federal and state constitutional provisions.

bill_summary: This bill requires individuals with direct contact with children in child care facilities to undergo criminal history records checks and mandates the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to establish a centralized unit for managing these records by June 30, 2027. Additionally, it removes the limit on the number of Deputy State Superintendents of Schools, lowers the age requirement for probationary child care teachers from three to two years old, and requires MSDE to report on the background check process by October 2028.
stakeholders: Applicants for positions in child care facilities, child care center employees and volunteers, and child care facility operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is expected to implement the bill's requirements using existing resources with minimal fiscal impact. There is no impact on local government finances. Small businesses in the child care sector may experience a positive impact through expanded access to probationary staff.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is primarily relevant to MSDE as it is the lead agency responsible for establishing the centralized unit for child care background checks, modifying child care teacher qualifications, and reporting on the efficiency of the new process. It also removes the limit on the number of Deputy State Superintendents the department can appoint.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates the CJIS Central Repository, which is the primary source for the criminal history records checks required by the bill. The bill establishes a centralized unit to manage data provided by this repository and mandates interagency coordination.

As the principal personnel agency for the state, DBM is impacted by the bill's removal of the statutory cap on the number of Deputy State Superintendents within MSDE. DBM also oversees the budget for the new centralized unit.

DHS is responsible for child abuse and neglect clearances for child care facility employees. The bill's requirement for MSDE to review interagency coordination of background checks directly involves DHS's role in the vetting process.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MSDE, and is responsible for the appointment of high-level state officials. The bill modifies the leadership structure of MSDE and requires a report to the General Assembly via executive department channels.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to MSDE and will be needed to ensure the centralized unit complies with federal laws regarding background checks and maintains the confidentiality of sensitive criminal history data.

DoIT manages the state's data governance and cybersecurity. The creation of a centralized unit for the processing and management of digital criminal history information requires alignment with the state's IT and telecommunications strategy.

The bill specifically mandates a review to evaluate the efficiency and timeliness of background check processing. This aligns with GOPI's mission to use data-driven strategies to enhance the responsiveness of state government operations.
The Governor's Office for Children is focused on child well-being. This bill impacts the regulatory and safety standards for facilities that care for Maryland's children.

bill_summary: This bill allows a member, candidate for election to, or member-elect of the Maryland General Assembly to receive earned income from a State executive branch unit or a political subdivision of the State under certain conditions. To qualify for this exemption, the individual must have served at least one full elected term in the General Assembly and must meet the objective minimum education, licensure, and experience requirements for the position.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission and the Joint Committee on Legislative Ethics
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland General Assembly, candidates for election to the General Assembly, and members-elect of the General Assembly
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances. There are no specific revenue or expenditure estimates provided as the impact is expected to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Ethics Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering and enforcing the Maryland Public Ethics Law, which this bill directly amends regarding conflict of interest provisions and employment exemptions for General Assembly members and candidates.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Ethics Commission and the General Assembly, on the interpretation and implementation of statutory changes to public ethics laws.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM oversees the executive branch workforce. This bill affects the eligibility of General Assembly members to be employed by executive units, which falls under DBM's broader management of state personnel and employment policies.

The bill specifically applies to 'filed candidates for election to the General Assembly,' a group defined by their registration with the Board of Elections. While the board does not administer ethics laws, the bill governs the financial conduct of individuals within its regulatory scope.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. Since the bill creates exemptions allowing legislators to work for executive units, it impacts the administration of the executive departments under the Governor's authority.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Health to issue recommendations for certain immunizations, screenings, and preventive services based on certain evidence-based scientific and clinical guidance; requiring the Secretary, before adopting a recommendation for a certain preventive service, to hold a notice and comment period, obtain a certain analysis from the Maryland Health Care Commission, and cite the basis for the recommendation; altering the health insurance coverage requirements for certain immunizations, screenings, and services; etc.

bill_summary: The Vax Act requires the Maryland Secretary of Health to establish recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services for infants, children, and adults based on scientific consensus and clinical guidance. The bill authorizes pharmacists to administer vaccinations recommended by the Secretary to individuals aged 7 and older and mandates that health insurance carriers provide coverage for these services without cost-sharing. It also repeals outdated statutory language regarding the pertussis vaccine.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland residents (including infants, children, and adults), pharmacists, health insurance carriers, and licensed healthcare professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in FY 2027 due to $125 rate and form filing fees. Implementation costs for the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration are expected to be handled within existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health is the primary official charged with issuing and publishing recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services. The department also oversees the Board of Pharmacy, which regulates the pharmacists granted expanded authority to administer vaccinations under this bill.

The MIA is responsible for enforcing the bill's health insurance coverage requirements and cost-sharing prohibitions. The fiscal note also identifies a minimal increase in special fund revenues for MIA from rate and form filing fees associated with these changes.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Health to obtain an analysis from the MHCC regarding the social, medical, and financial impacts of any proposed preventive service recommendation that is not an immunization or already federally rated.

This is an Administration bill (the 'Vax Act') introduced at the request of the Governor. The Governor's Office is responsible for the policy initiative and coordinates the executive branch's health recommendations.

As the administrator of Maryland's health insurance marketplace, the MHBE must ensure that the private health plans offered through the exchange comply with the updated coverage requirements and cost-sharing prohibitions mandated by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Health to take into consideration guidance from the Maryland Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations when issuing recommendations.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health, the Insurance Administration, and the Health Care Commission as they implement and enforce the new regulatory frameworks for preventive services and insurance mandates.

DBM oversees the state's personnel and benefits policies; the bill's changes to health insurance mandates may affect the coverage and cost-sharing structures of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

Synopsis: Proposing an amendment to the Maryland Constitution to raise the mandatory retirement age of certain judges in the State from 70 to 73, under certain circumstances; and establishing a mandatory retirement age for judges of the Orphans' Court, subject to a certain exception.
Title: Judges - Mandatory Retirement Age
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to increase the mandatory retirement age for Maryland judges from 70 to 73. This change applies to justices of the Supreme Court of Maryland and judges of the Appellate Court, circuit courts, District Court, and Orphans' Courts. The bill includes transition provisions whereby judges currently in office as of November 3, 2026, generally remain subject to the age 70 retirement limit, while the new age 73 limit applies to those appointed or elected thereafter.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Maryland State judges, Maryland voters, and the State Retirement and Pension System
fiscal_impact_summary: If approved by voters, the amendment is projected to reduce State pension liabilities by $21,700,000 and reduce normal costs by $1,500,000. As a result, State general fund expenditures for pension contributions are expected to decrease by $4,300,000 beginning in FY 2029, with further decreases in subsequent years. There is no estimated impact on local finances or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The AOC provides operational, legal, and financial support to the Maryland Judicial Branch. The bill directly impacts the mandatory retirement age for judges in the Supreme Court, Appellate Court, Circuit Courts, and District Court, and the fiscal note indicates a potential impact on personnel expenditures related to judge sick leave managed by the AOC.

The SRA administers the Judges' Retirement System (JRS). The fiscal note highlights significant impacts on pension liabilities (decreasing by $21.7 million) and state pension contributions starting in FY 2029 due to the change in mandatory retirement age.
As a constitutional amendment, the bill must be submitted to the voters at the November 2026 general election. The SBE is responsible for administering this election and the ballot questions.

The Governor is responsible for appointing judges to fill vacancies in the appellate, circuit, and district courts, as well as the Orphans' Court. Additionally, the Governor must issue a proclamation upon the adoption of a constitutional amendment.

The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court. The bill establishes a new mandatory retirement age specifically for Judges of the Orphans' Court, which directly affects the administration of those courts.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for judicial vacancies. Altering the mandatory retirement age changes the frequency and timing of these vacancies.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state. The bill is projected to decrease state pension contributions (general funds) by millions of dollars annually beginning in FY 2029, impacting the state budget managed by DBM.

The Treasurer oversees state funds and pension investments, and holds a key position on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Judges' Retirement System affected by this bill.

The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records, including constitutional amendments and executive orders. They are involved in the official certification and recording process of the referendum results.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and its agencies, including the Judiciary and the Governor. They would provide legal counsel regarding the implementation and interpretation of this constitutional change.

bill_summary: This bill requires fixed base operators and aviation service companies to verify warrant information for detained individuals on flights they service. These entities must compile and submit monthly reports to the Maryland Aviation Administration (MAA) regarding these flights and refueling safety. Additionally, the MAA must develop health and legal forms for detained passengers, and aircraft refueling is prohibited while restrained individuals are on board unless they are moved to a climate-controlled enclosure with access to water and restrooms.
stakeholders: Detained passengers, fixed base operators (FBOs), aviation service companies, flight crews, local government airport operators, and the Maryland Aviation Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 for administrative costs related to form development and report collection. However, the Maryland Aviation Administration faces a potential loss of up to $300,000,000 in federal fund revenues if the bill is found to be in noncompliance with federal aviation laws and regulations. Local governments operating airports may also experience minimal administrative cost increases and speculative risks to federal funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Administration as the primary regulatory body responsible for developing medical information forms and receiving monthly compliance reports from aviation service companies and fixed base operators.
As the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration, the department oversees the modal administration's operations and the bill involves expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.

The agency will provide critical legal counsel to the Maryland Aviation Administration regarding the bill's intersection with federal laws like the Airline Deregulation Act and the interpretation of judicial versus administrative warrants.

The bill grants the Governor specific authority regarding extradition authorizations which serves as a condition for certain aviation contracts and grants, and the office oversees the implementing executive departments.
The bill's requirements involve the verification of judicial warrants, which are within the purview of the Maryland Judicial Branch supported by this office.

bill_summary: This bill modifies, repeals, or consolidates various mandated reports, boards, and commissions across several Maryland state agencies to improve administrative efficiency and remove obsolete or redundant requirements. It repeals specific entities such as the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board, the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, the Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission, and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care, while adjusting reporting deadlines and the composition of several other advisory bodies.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management and various state agencies
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies, board members, local boards of education, healthcare practitioners, and various industries including aerospace and renewable fuels.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill has no direct effect on state or local finances. It is largely procedural and intended to reduce administrative burdens on state departments, allowing staff to focus on other activities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts numerous boards and commissions whose members are appointed by the Governor. It also mentions the Governor's Office of Performance Improvement (GOPI) as a driver for the modernization efforts and requires various reports to be submitted to the Governor.
The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to report to the Comptroller on tax credit certificates issued for physician, nurse practitioner, and physician assistant preceptors.
The State Treasurer (or designee) is a member of the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, which is modified by the bill.
The Attorney General (or designee) is a member of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board, which is modified by the bill.

The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is a member of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities and the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, both of which are modified by the bill.
The bill repeals the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board and transfers its duties and certification processes for ethanol and biodiesel credits directly to the Department of Agriculture.

The bill was introduced by request of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). DBM is the principal agency for the government modernization initiative driving these revisions to mandated reports and boards.

The bill removes Commerce from several bodies (Customer Council, Green Purchasing Committee) while altering their role on the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board and the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is a member of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care and the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee, both modified by the bill.

The bill significantly alters MSDE's reporting requirements, repealing 'specialized intervention services' reports in favor of grade 3 literacy reports. It also removes MSDE from the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee.
The bill repeals the annual report for the Oil Contaminated Site Environmental Cleanup Fund and alters the composition of the Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Citizens Oversight Committee.
The Secretary of General Services chairs the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee and serves on the Customer Council, both of which are modified by this bill.

The bill makes extensive changes to MDH, including repealing reports on hepatitis C and the cancer registry, consolidating youth camp epinephrine reports, and altering its representation on multiple boards like the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.

The bill designates the Secretary of Housing and Community Development as the chair of the Interagency Council on Homelessness and mandates a new compensation policy for members with lived experience of homelessness.

The bill repeals the Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care, which were units or subtitles within DHS's purview. It also modifies prekindergarten enrollment reporting.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is a member of the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, which is modified by the bill.
The bill repeals an annual report required of the Department regarding voter registration efforts at one-stop career centers.
The bill repeals requirements for DNR to publish maintenance project lists over $25,000 and repeals the annual nutria eradication report.
The Department of Planning is a member of the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee, which has its membership composition altered by the bill.

The Commission has a representative on the Customer Council, whose membership is adjusted by removing the Department of Commerce representative.
The Secretary of State Police (or designee) is a member of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board and the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee, both modified by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly modifies the composition, duties, or existence of numerous executive boards and commissions, including the Life Sciences Advisory Board and the Interagency Council on Homelessness.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board, which is housed within GOCPP, and alters its representation on the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.
The fiscal note identifies GOPI and the Government Modernization Initiative (GMI) as the primary entities coordinating these efficiency-driven revisions to state reports and boards.
The bill modifies the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board, for which the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland appoints two members.
The Director of the Maryland Cannabis Administration is a designated member of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council, which is modified by the bill.
The bill requires MHCC to collaborate with the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities to analyze data for the Health Care Disparities Policy Report Card.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is a member of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board and was previously on the now-repealed multidisciplinary alternative response advisory council.

The Director of MEA was a member of the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board, which is repealed by the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Curbside Voting Pilot Program to test the viability of curbside voting in the State; establishing requirements governing curbside voting; and requiring the State Board to report to the General Assembly on the implementation of the Pilot Program by September 1, 2031.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Curbside Voting Pilot Program to test the viability of curbside voting in Maryland. The State Board of Elections will designate three counties of different sizes to implement the program, where voters can cast ballots from their vehicles at specific locations under the observation of election judges. The bill mandates accessibility standards, voter privacy protections, and requires a final report on the program's implementation to the General Assembly by September 2031.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Registered voters in designated pilot counties, the Maryland State Board of Elections, and local boards of elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $253,000 in FY 2028 for the initial implementation, rising to $273,000 by FY 2031. Local government expenditures in the three participating counties increase by approximately $174,000 in FY 2028 and $164,000 annually through FY 2031. Costs are driven by a new State Board of Elections staff position, voter outreach, additional election judges, and voting equipment like pollbooks and ballot marking devices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the State Board of Elections (SBE) to implement, administer, and adopt regulations for the Curbside Voting Pilot Program, including reporting on its implementation by 2031.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is relevant due to the bill's significant fiscal impact on the general fund (at least $253,000 in FY 2028) and the requirement for a new staff position at SBE to oversee the pilot.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and will likely be involved in reviewing the proposed regulations and ensuring the pilot program's compliance with state and federal voting laws and accessibility requirements.

The commission enforces anti-discrimination laws. Curbside voting is directly related to ensuring equitable access to the polls and protecting the voting rights of disenfranchised and protected classes.

The pilot program is designed to enhance voting accessibility, which is a core concern for the Department of Disabilities as they coordinate services and inclusive policies for residents with disabilities.

The bill requires SBE to certify that voting systems accommodate curbside voting and involves the deployment of pollbooks and ballot marking devices, areas overseen by DoIT's information technology and telecommunications strategy.

The Board oversees significant state contracts and expenditures. Procurement of new voting system software or hardware modifications required for the pilot program would likely require their approval.
As the chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees state expenditures and the fiscal integrity of the pilot program's implementation.
Curbside voting is highly relevant to older adults with mobility challenges, falling under the department's mandate to advocate for the rights and quality of life of older Marylanders.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and SBE, and will be responsible for proposing the state budget that includes the funds required for the pilot program.
The bill emphasizes location accessibility for historically disenfranchised communities, aligning with GOCI's mission to engage community affairs and connect residents with government resources.

GOPI utilizes performance metrics to oversee implementation of state priorities; they would likely monitor the data and results from the 5-year pilot program to assess government efficiency and responsiveness.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advocates for equal access to public services for the Deaf and hard of hearing community, who would be impacted by the accessibility standards of the curbside voting pilot.
The State Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, which must approve procurements related to the pilot program's specialized voting equipment.
OLA conducts fiscal and performance audits of state agencies; they would be responsible for auditing the SBE's management and expenditures associated with the pilot program.
As the central procurement authority, DGS may be involved in the purchase of signage, canopies, and other physical supplies required for the curbside voting locations.

The bill requires local boards to take into account accessibility by public transportation when designating curbside voting locations, which relates to MDOT's management of the state's transportation network.

bill_summary: This bill requires each electric company in Maryland to report geographic and demographic data annually to the Public Service Commission (PSC) regarding customers impacted by service outages and rate increases. The reports must cover outages lasting two hours or longer, scheduled maintenance outages, and any outages occurring during inclement weather, including service restoration times.
stakeholders: Maryland electric companies, municipal electric utilities (in Berlin, Easton, Hagerstown, Thurmont, and Williamsport), and electric service customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. It is assumed that both the Public Service Commission and the affected municipal electric utilities can manage the new reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires electric companies to report geographic and demographic data regarding service outages and rate increases to the Public Service Commission (PSC) each year. This information is directly related to the PSC's primary responsibility of regulating public utilities to ensure safe, reliable, and economical services.

The Office of the People's Counsel (OPC) is the primary advocate for Maryland's residential utility consumers. The geographic and demographic data required by this bill regarding rate increases and service outages is essential for the OPC's mission to represent consumer interests in proceedings before the Public Service Commission.

The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) advises the Governor and General Assembly on state energy policy. Data on service reliability and the impact of rate increases on different demographics and regions is highly relevant to the MEA's role in coordinating state-level energy planning and resource management.

The Department of Human Services (DHS) provides energy assistance to residents in economic need. Information on rate increases and service reliability, specifically when linked to demographic data, is relevant to DHS for identifying and assisting vulnerable populations who may be disproportionately affected by utility costs.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and the General Assembly. The OAG may be involved in the interpretation and enforcement of the new reporting requirements for electric companies.

The Maryland Department of Aging (MDoA) advocates for the quality of life for older adults. Geographic and demographic data on utility outages and rate increases is relevant to the department, as seniors are often more physically vulnerable during outages and financially impacted by rising utility costs.

The Maryland Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with disabilities. Data regarding service outages is critical as many individuals with disabilities rely on electricity for life-sustaining medical equipment and assistive technology.

The Governor's Office oversees executive agencies like the PSC and MEA and coordinates state policy. Data on utility reliability and affordability across Maryland informs the Governor's policy initiatives regarding infrastructure and economic equity.

bill_summary: The bill modifies the educational and experiential requirements for certified public accountant (CPA) licensure. It creates alternative pathways to licensure by allowing applicants to substitute additional practical work experience for certain academic credit hours, and it extends the maximum period during which an applicant can gain their required work experience from three years to six years.
stakeholders: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license applicants, licensed CPAs, the State Board of Public Accountancy, and accounting firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill's changes using existing resources. Special fund revenues may increase minimally if the alternative pathways result in more individuals seeking licensure. There is no fiscal impact on local governments. Small business accounting firms may experience a meaningful benefit from a larger pool of eligible license applicants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the most relevant agency as it oversees the State Board of Public Accountancy, which is responsible for licensing and regulating certified public accountants in Maryland. The bill directly alters the licensure requirements that the Board must enforce.

The Commission is responsible for establishing statewide policies and standards for colleges and universities. Since the bill modifies the specific educational pathways and credit-hour requirements for professional licensure, the Commission may need to coordinate with the Board regarding academic equivalencies and institutional accreditation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Public Accountancy. It will be responsible for advising the Board on the implementation of these new regulatory requirements and defending any legal challenges to the new licensing standards.

As the provider of accounting degrees across multiple institutions, the University System will be impacted by changes in licensure requirements, which may influence their curriculum design and how they advise students pursuing CPA certification.

As a state agency providing undergraduate and graduate accounting programs, the university will need to align its advising and potentially its curriculum with the new tiered educational and experiential pathways for CPA licensure.

As a public institution offering academic degrees, the college's accounting students will be affected by the changes in licensure qualifications, necessitating updates to their professional advising and program alignment.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including licensing boards. Changes to licensure qualifications can lead to disputes and appeals from applicants who are denied a license under the new criteria, which would be heard by Administrative Law Judges at the OAH.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Labor, and is responsible for signing the legislation into law and overseeing general policy coordination across state agencies.

responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of disabled veterans, local governments, and the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

Local property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $20,000,000 annually starting in FY 2027. The state revenue decrease may require an increase in the State property tax rate or a general fund appropriation to cover debt service on general obligation bonds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects the application process and eligibility requirements for property tax exemptions for the surviving spouses of disabled veterans, a key constituent group that the department is tasked with supporting and advocating for regarding state benefits.

The fiscal note indicates that the bill will significantly decrease revenue to the Annuity Bond Fund, which is managed by the Treasurer's Office to pay debt service on the state's general obligation bonds.

As the agency responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning, DBM is impacted by the projected decrease in state property tax revenues and the potential need for general fund appropriations to cover debt service shortfalls.

This board is the primary administrative body responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax exemptions and credits. It would adjudicate disputes arising from the implementation of the bill's new documentation requirements.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including real property tax assessments and exemptions, making it a critical entity for appeals related to this legislation.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues, including the state property taxes that will be reduced by this expansion of exemptions.

The Board of Public Works oversees state fiscal integrity and general obligation bond issuances; the bill's impact on the Annuity Bond Fund, which services these bonds, falls under their broader fiscal oversight.

The OAG would provide legal guidance to state agencies on the interpretation and implementation of the revised application requirements and the use of federal Dependency and Indemnity Compensation documentation.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies implementing this law and is responsible for the state budget, which may require adjustments due to the bill's fiscal impact on the Annuity Bond Fund.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from using their own sperm or ovum during assisted reproductive treatment without the recipient's written consent. Violators face felony charges, including up to 10 years in prison and a $5,000 fine, and are liable for civil damages to the recipient, their partner, or the resulting child.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Patients receiving assisted reproductive treatment, their spouses or domestic partners, children born from such treatments, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $8,400 in FY 2027 only for one-time programming costs for the Judiciary. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill has a direct fiscal impact on the Judiciary, including $8,400 for one-time programming costs. Additionally, the Administrative Office of the Courts must manage the new civil cause of action and the felony cases established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony punishable by up to 10 years in prison. DPSCS would be responsible for the incarceration and subsequent parole or probation supervision of individuals convicted under this statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for providing legal counsel to indigent defendants, the OPD will experience a potential increase in caseload to defend individuals charged with the new felony created by the bill.

As the chief legal officer of the state, the OAG provides counsel on the enforcement of new criminal laws and would represent the state in any appeals resulting from convictions under this new felony.
The bill regulates assisted reproductive treatments, which are healthcare services. MDH oversees the regulation of health care professionals and facilities that provide such treatments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office is relevant to the development and implementation of new felony statutes and sentencing policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office was identified as a source of information for the fiscal note and manages medical-related dispute resolutions, which may overlap with the civil causes of action involving medical providers.

bill_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to prioritize medical provider reports or physician referrals when making licensing decisions for individuals who self-report specific medical conditions. It authorizes the MVA to request additional documentation or testing and mandates an expedited learner's instructional permit process for individuals who were previously disqualified but have since medically improved. Additionally, the MVA is required to review its medical case review practices and report findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Driver's license applicants and holders who self-report a diagnosis of a medical condition, the Motor Vehicle Administration, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not anticipated to be materially affected, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the MVA is directly responsible for establishing the new licensing decision criteria, creating an expedited permit process for qualified individuals, and conducting the required examination and report on medical case review practices.

The MVA is a modal administration under MDOT. MDOT is responsible for the overall management of the state's transportation network and provides oversight for MVA's licensing policies and regulatory changes.

The bill centers on medical provider reports and physician referrals as the primary factor in licensing decisions. MDH regulates the healthcare professionals who provide these reports and oversees the Medical Advisory Board that assists the MVA with medical fitness determinations.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases involving the MVA, including driver's license suspensions and refusals. Changes to the decision-making criteria for licensees with medical conditions may impact the volume or nature of administrative hearings.

The bill impacts individuals with medical diagnoses that may constitute disabilities. The department is responsible for ensuring programs are inclusive and advancing accessible transportation for Marylanders with disabilities.

The bill identifies law enforcement requests for reexamination as a specific exception to the requirement that medical provider reports be the primary factor in licensing decisions, involving the MSP in the administrative process.

Medical self-reporting and the subsequent licensing review process are highly relevant to the older adult population, a core constituency for which the Department of Aging provides advocacy and support regarding quality of life and independence.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the MVA and MDOT and will likely be involved in reviewing the new regulations, the expedited process, and the confidentiality of medical records used in licensing decisions.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the implementation of the state budget and agency performance, though the fiscal impact is noted as being manageable within existing resources.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) to study the role of nuclear energy as a renewable energy resource to combat climate change in Maryland. The study includes evaluating the current state of nuclear energy, identifying benefits and potential for new initiatives, and locating sites for new generating stations. PPRP must report its findings and recommendations by September 30, 2027.
responsible_party: Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
stakeholders: The Governor, the General Assembly, the Department of Natural Resources, the nuclear energy industry, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general or special fund expenditures increase by $218,800 in FY 2027 and $11,600 in FY 2028 to complete the required study and report, specifically for hiring an independent consultant and a part-time contractual site assessor. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill and fiscal note explicitly task the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), which is an office within the Department of Natural Resources, with conducting the nuclear energy study and reporting the findings.

The study's focus on nuclear energy's role as a renewable resource and its potential in the state's energy portfolio directly aligns with MEA's mission to promote renewable energy and advise the Governor on energy policy.

The bill requires an assessment of adding nuclear energy to the state's Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS) and identifying sites for power plants, both of which are core regulatory responsibilities of the PSC.

The study aims to evaluate nuclear energy's role in combatting climate change and its environmental benefits, which falls under MDE's mandate to implement state laws regarding air quality and environmental restoration.
The report and recommendations must be submitted directly to the Governor, who oversees the state's energy policy and coordinates the initiatives proposed by the study.

The fiscal note identifies a need for additional general or special funds and contractual personnel for the Department of Natural Resources to complete the study, which impacts DBM's personnel and fiscal management duties.
The study is required to include recommendations for growing the nuclear energy industry in Maryland, which aligns with Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and attract new businesses.
The mandate to identify potential locations for nuclear generating stations involves land use planning and infrastructure development, which are primary functions of the Department of Planning.
The bill explores the potential for State-owned and operated nuclear energy generating stations, which would involve DGS's responsibilities for state real estate management and facility planning.
The OAG would provide necessary legal counsel regarding proposed changes to state energy laws, the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard, and the legal aspects of power plant siting.
As the state's green bank, the MCEC is relevant to any study seeking to advance the adoption of clean energy technologies and grow the clean energy industry in Maryland.

While the bill expands the redetermination process to an estimated 1,760 additional households, the Office of Home Energy Programs may adjust benefit levels to stay within available funding, which for fiscal 2027 includes $47,700,000 for the Electric Universal Service Program and $94,700,000 for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services is the primary implementing agency for the bill, as it houses the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is directly responsible for the redetermination process and the administration of the energy assistance programs mentioned.

The bill specifically reduces the age for special energy assistance redetermination from 65 to 60, aligning with federal definitions of 'older adults' and impacting the demographic served by this department.

The Maryland Energy Administration manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which provides significant funding for the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) affected by the bill's eligibility changes.

The Public Service Commission regulates the utilities that collect ratepayer surcharges used to fund energy assistance programs and oversees programs like the Utility Service Protection Program mentioned in the fiscal note.
The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal planning and execution of the state and federal funds (EUSP and MEAP) that support these energy assistance programs.
This is a departmental bill introduced at the request of the Department of Human Services, part of the Governor's executive branch oversight.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Human Services regarding the implementation of state and federal energy assistance regulations.
Energy assistance programs like MEAP include referrals to weatherization services, which are often administered or supported by the Department of Housing and Community Development.
