bill_summary: This bill requires Executive Branch units of the Maryland State government that issue permits for housing development projects to adopt streamlined permitting procedures, including concurrent filing, predictable sequencing, and expedited review. It mandates that the State Housing Ombudsman ensure consistency between these processes and authorizes State units to delegate permitting tasks to local government units by agreement.
responsible_party: Maryland Executive Branch units, Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), and the State Housing Ombudsman
stakeholders: Housing developers, contractors, subcontractors, State Executive Branch agencies, and local government units
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State agencies can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources because many of the mandates are already being carried out in response to Executive Order 01.01.2025.19. The bill is not expected to affect State revenues or materially impact local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that all units in the Executive Branch of State government responsible for housing permits adopt streamlined procedures, codifying the policy objectives and executive orders of the Governor's administration.
The OAG will be required to provide legal counsel to the various executive units as they develop new permitting procedures and enter into delegation agreements with local governments.
As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM oversees the resources and staffing within executive units that will need to implement and manage the mandated streamlined permitting frameworks.
Through its oversight of local health departments, the agency is involved in issuing critical permits for well and septic systems which are essential for many housing development projects to proceed.

This agency is the primary implementer of the bill, as it is responsible for designating the State Housing Ombudsman, ensuring permitting consistency across the state, and reporting on the program's development.
The agency's role in enforcing conservation laws and conducting reviews for forest conservation and critical areas is a mandatory part of the permitting process for many housing development projects.
MDOT and its various administrations are responsible for issuing access permits and infrastructure approvals necessary for residential development and utility connections.
MDE is a principal permitting authority for housing construction, overseeing essential approvals for water and sewer infrastructure as well as environmental quality permits.
As an executive unit, SHA is directly responsible for issuing the access and utility permits required for residential construction projects along state-maintained roads.

Synopsis: Altering the prohibition against taking and breaking open a letter; prohibiting the theft of mail under certain circumstances; prohibiting a person from possessing an arrow key under certain circumstances; and providing for concurrent jurisdiction in the District Court and circuit court to try a violation of the Act.
Title: Criminal Law - Mail and Package Theft (Porch Piracy Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: The bill establishes the 'Porch Piracy Act,' which creates specific criminal offenses and penalties for mail and package theft. It prohibits the unauthorized opening of mail, the theft of mail or packages (including the use of specialized 'arrow keys'), and the possession of arrow keys with intent to commit mail theft. The bill also grants concurrent jurisdiction to the District Court and circuit courts for felony violations.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals and entities involved in mail and package delivery, postal employees, and individuals accused of mail-related theft offenses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. While the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Office of the Public Defender identified potential impacts on incarceration expenditures and attorney workloads, these are expected to be manageable within existing resources, as many individuals targeted by the bill are likely already subject to prosecution under existing general theft statutes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the jurisdiction of the District Court and circuit courts (Sections 4-301 and 4-302 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article) and creates new criminal offenses that require processing and adjudication by the judicial system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for representing indigent defendants, the fiscal note explicitly states the bill will result in a workload increase and require additional effort for clients charged with the new felony mail theft offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies potential impacts on incarceration expenditures for the Division of Correction and probation case volumes for the Division of Parole and Probation resulting from the new mail theft penalties.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal violations of the law, which will include the new 'Porch Piracy' and 'arrow key' theft offenses established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies; the creation of new criminal penalties and the establishment of a state-level 'Porch Piracy Act' directly align with their policy development mission.

The OAG represents the state in all criminal appeals. The creation of new felony and misdemeanor mail theft classifications could lead to an increase in appellate litigation involving these new statutes.

Synopsis: Establishing that a commercial entity that distributes obscene material to minors on the Internet from certain websites is liable for certain damages; and prohibiting a commercial entity or third party that performs a certain age verification of an individual from retaining any identifying information of an individual under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: This bill requires commercial entities that host websites with a substantial portion of obscene material (more than one-third of total content) to implement reasonable age verification methods, such as government-issued identification, to ensure users are at least 18 years old. It prohibits the retention of any identifying information once the age verification process is complete and allows individuals to bring civil actions for damages if a minor accesses the material or if personal data is improperly retained.
stakeholders: Commercial entities distributing obscene material, minors, Maryland residents, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. However, it may have a meaningful fiscal impact on small businesses that must bear the costs of implementing age verification systems or face potential civil litigation and associated legal fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new civil cause of action within the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, allowing individuals to sue commercial entities for damages. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for managing the state's judicial system and will oversee the resulting litigation and court procedures.

As the chief legal representative for the State, the OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the constitutionality and enforcement of this new legislation, especially given potential First Amendment challenges common with age-verification laws.

The agency's mission is to promote the well-being of Maryland's children. This bill specifically aims to protect minors from accessing obscene material on the internet, aligning with the office's core focus on child safety and welfare.

The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and the executive branch. This bill represents a significant policy shift regarding internet regulation and child protection, which requires coordination with executive policy goals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. While the bill establishes a civil remedy, it references existing criminal definitions of obscenity and impacts broader public safety and youth protection policies.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of the Comptroller, by December 1, 2026, to study and report to the Governor and the General Assembly regarding certain matters related to an addition modification under the Maryland income tax for certain income exempt from federal tax by federal law or treaty but not State tax.
Title: Income Tax - Addition Modification for Federal Tax-Exempt Income - Study

bill_summary: This bill requires the Office of the Comptroller to study and report on Maryland residents who have foreign earned income that is exempt from federal income tax under Section 911 of the Internal Revenue Code. The report, which must be submitted to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026, must include the number of residents with such income, those whose income exceeds federal exclusion limits, and the countries where the income was earned.
stakeholders: Maryland residents with foreign earned income, the Office of the Comptroller, the Governor, and the Maryland General Assembly
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues are not materially affected. The Office of the Comptroller is expected to conduct the required study and report using existing budgeted resources. Although the original bill proposed tax modifications, the amended version focusing on a study does not have a significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically mandates the Office of the Comptroller to conduct the study and report its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly. As the state's principal tax collector, the agency is the primary implementer of the bill's requirements.

The bill requires the Comptroller to report the study's findings directly to the Governor. Additionally, the study concerns state tax policy and revenue, which are central to the Governor's executive responsibilities and annual budget proposal.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. A study regarding the taxation of foreign earned income provides data that directly impacts DBM's ability to project state revenues and develop future budgets.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and the Governor. The bill arises from legal ambiguities identified in the Cosgrove v. Comptroller court case, and the OAG would likely be consulted on the legal definitions and international treaty implications examined in the study.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Green and Renewable Energy Efficiency for Nonprofits (GREEN) Loan Program and a corresponding special fund within the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC). The program provides no-interest loans to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations for planning, purchasing, and installing qualifying energy systems (like renewable energy generation) and for energy efficiency improvements (such as HVAC replacement or window repairs). The bill also allows the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) to transfer money to this new fund and authorizes specific appropriations for fiscal years 2028 and 2029.
stakeholders: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Maryland, particularly those with annual budgets of $1,000,000 or less, and businesses providing energy efficiency or renewable energy installation services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a general fund expenditure of $140,000 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Clean Energy Center to establish the program. Special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) are estimated to increase by $5,000,000 in FY 2028 and by a potentially significant amount (up to $5,000,000 or more) in FY 2029 to capitalize the loan fund. The Green and Renewable Energy Efficiency for Nonprofits Loan Fund will receive these transfers, plus loan repayments and interest, to provide no-interest loans to nonprofits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Green and Renewable Energy Efficiency for Nonprofits (GREEN) Loan Program within the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) and tasks the agency with its administration, management, and the adoption of implementing regulations.

The bill alters the permissible uses of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is administered by the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), to provide funding for the newly established GREEN Loan Fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the GREEN Loan Fund separately and to invest and reinvest the money of the fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill specifically tasks the Comptroller with accounting for the GREEN Loan Fund and ensuring that interest earnings are properly credited to the fund.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the budget development and execution of the authorized general and special fund appropriations for the program, which include a projected $140,000 for startup costs and $5 million for the loan fund.

The bill defines 'qualifying energy systems' based on their ability to assist the state in meeting greenhouse gas reduction goals established in the Environment Article, which is overseen by MDE. The bill also references SEIF funding related to MDE's Air and Radiation Administration.
The Governor is authorized by the bill to include specific appropriations for the program in the annual budget bill and oversees the executive agencies responsible for the program's implementation.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to MCEC and MEA and would be responsible for providing legal advice regarding the establishment of the loan program, drafting regulations, and reviewing loan contracts.

bill_summary: This bill restores eligibility for State prescription drug coverage under the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program for Medicare-eligible retirees who began State service before July 1, 2011. It simultaneously discontinues prescription drug benefits for Medicare-eligible retirees who began service on or after that date and repeals several supplemental prescription drug reimbursement and assistance programs.
stakeholders: Medicare-eligible Maryland State retirees, their spouses, and dependent children, as well as current State employees hired before July 1, 2011.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (all funds) are estimated to increase by $299,400,000 in FY 2027, with annual increases projected through FY 2031 and beyond based on actuarial assumptions. According to the Fiscal Note, the bill increases total State other postemployment benefits (OPEB) liabilities by an estimated $10.2 billion over the next 30 years. There is no effect on State revenue or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal personnel agency and administrator of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is the primary agency responsible for implementing the benefit changes, managing the restored prescription drug coverage, and adjusting state agency budgets for the $299.4 million annual expenditure increase.

The bill directly impacts the benefits package for retirees who receive an allowance from the State Retirement and Pension System. The agency provides counseling and support services to the 420,000 members whose healthcare eligibility criteria are altered by this legislation.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to DBM and the Governor. The bill involves significant legal issues and contractual obligations regarding retiree benefits that have been the subject of extensive federal litigation (e.g., Fitch v. State of Maryland) mentioned in the bill's history.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. This bill creates a notable fiscal impact of nearly $300 million annually and over $10 billion in long-term liabilities that must be accounted for in future budget proposals.

As the state's chief financial officer responsible for paying state bills and employees, the Comptroller is directly involved in the execution of the state's financial obligations and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees fiscal integrity impacted by this bill.

The Treasurer manages state funds and anticipates monetary needs. The bill's significant impact on Other Postemployment Benefits (OPEB) liabilities (projected at $10.2 billion over 30 years) is a major factor in the state's long-term financial planning and credit management.

The Board of Public Works is charged with protecting the state's fiscal integrity. The magnitude of the fiscal impact on the state's personnel expenditures and long-term liabilities falls under their broad administrative oversight of state funds.

OLA is responsible for auditing executive agencies, including DBM, for compliance with state laws and financial accountability. It would be tasked with auditing the proper termination of old programs and the implementation of restored benefits specified in the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the earning of diminution credits to reduce the term of confinement of an incarcerated individual who is serving a sentence in a State or local correctional facility for murder in the first degree that occurred on or after October 1, 2026.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits individuals serving a sentence for first-degree murder for offenses committed on or after October 1, 2026, from earning diminution credits to reduce their term of confinement in State or local correctional facilities.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of first-degree murder, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and local correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances in the near term (the first five years). However, State general fund expenditures will increase in the long term, potentially significantly, as affected individuals serve longer sentences. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected as violent offenders are typically housed in State facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for managing state correctional facilities and the supervision of incarcerated individuals, DPSCS is directly responsible for calculating and administering diminution credits. The bill specifically amends statutes governing their operations and will result in significant long-term increases in incarceration costs for the department.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency and is responsible for long-term fiscal planning. The fiscal note indicates that the bill will significantly increase general fund expenditures over time due to longer terms of confinement, requiring DBM to manage these future budgetary impacts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and would represent the state in any legal challenges regarding the application of diminution credit prohibitions to incarcerated individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings, including those charged with first-degree murder. This legislation fundamentally changes the sentencing outcomes for their clients, impacting plea negotiations and legal advice.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies. This bill constitutes a major policy change regarding sentencing and recidivism strategies for violent crimes.

The judiciary is responsible for sentencing individuals for first-degree murder. While the calculation of credits is an executive function, the courts must be aware of the mandatory minimum terms resulting from the elimination of these credits.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget which will be impacted by the increased incarceration costs.

bill_summary: This bill transfers the authority to regulate crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors. It updates board operations by altering quorum requirements and the process for removing appointed members, mandates the hiring of an additional full-time inspector by fiscal 2028, and requires the board to establish a stakeholder workgroup to review relevant regulations.
responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
stakeholders: Crematory operators, reduction facility operators, licensed morticians, funeral directors, and consumers of death care services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by an estimated $101,200 in fiscal 2027 to support the hiring of an additional inspector, as required by the bill's mandate for the board to maintain at least two inspectors. These costs are projected to grow to $103,500 by fiscal 2031. Office of Cemetery Oversight special fund revenues decrease by approximately $6,000 biannually starting in fiscal 2027 due to the transfer of registration and permit authority. The Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors will see an indeterminate increase in special fund revenue from newly collected crematory and reduction facility fees. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily impacts the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which is a regulatory body situated within the Maryland Department of Health. The department will gain regulatory oversight and revenue from crematories and reduction facilities, and the bill mandates the creation of a new inspector position within this board.

The bill transfers regulatory authority and oversight of crematories and reduction facilities away from the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which is an agency within the Department of Labor. This results in a direct loss of jurisdiction and special fund revenue for the department.

The bill alters the Governor's statutory authority to remove appointed members of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, changing the criteria for removal to include repeated unexplained absences or just cause.

The bill explicitly requires the creation of a new Position Identification Number (PIN) for a full-time inspector starting in fiscal year 2028, which falls under DBM's responsibility for managing state personnel resources and the annual budget.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG provides counsel to the Board. Additionally, the bill specifically allows for the referral of consumer complaints to the OAG for binding arbitration.
The bill identifies the OAH as a potential venue for binding arbitration of consumer complaints and provides for contested case hearings for individuals aggrieved by Board decisions.

The bill involves the transfer of records and processes related to identifying unclaimed remains of veterans and their eligible dependents for proper disposition, which is a core interest of this department.
The Board is required to pay all collected fees and funds to the Comptroller for distribution into the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors Fund.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding civil liability protections for funeral establishments and establishes procedures for judicial review of Board decisions in circuit courts.

The bill establishes scientific and safety standards for 'natural organic reduction' (composting), including heavy metal and pathogen testing, which relates to the environmental protection standards overseen by MDE.

Because the bill modifies the composition and removal rules for the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, this office will be involved in the administrative process of vetting and managing these gubernatorial appointments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a police officer from intentionally violating the requirement that a police officer intervene to prevent or terminate the use of certain force by another police officer; prohibiting a police officer from intentionally violating the requirement to render certain first aid to a person injured as a result of police action and request certain assistance at a certain time; and classifying a violation of the Act by an officer as a misdemeanor and providing, on conviction, a term of imprisonment of up to 5 years.
Title: Maryland Use of Force Statute - Failure to Prevent Excessive Force or Render First Aid - Misdemeanor
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that a police officer's intentional failure to intervene to prevent another officer's use of excessive force, or intentional failure to render basic first aid and request medical assistance for a person injured by police action, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to five years in prison.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Judiciary
stakeholders: Maryland police officers, special police officers, law enforcement agencies, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While it creates a new misdemeanor punishable by up to five years of imprisonment, specific dollar estimates for increased expenditures or revenues are unavailable as the impact is expected to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary law enforcement agency for Maryland, its officers are directly governed by the Maryland Use of Force Statute and would be subject to the new misdemeanor penalties for failing to intervene or render first aid.
The agency operates the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are subject to the Use of Force Statute and the mandates regarding intervention and medical assistance.
MDOT oversees multiple law enforcement units, including the MDTA Police and the MTA Police, all of whom are subject to the bill's requirements and criminal penalties.
The agency manages the Maryland Capitol Police, who are classified as police officers and must comply with the intervention and first aid protocols established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees correctional facilities and parole and probation officers who are considered police officers under the definitions referenced in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this office is responsible for the policy development related to use of force and police conduct.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD would be responsible for providing legal defense to indigent individuals charged with the new misdemeanor or representing the rights of victims in related proceedings.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state law enforcement agencies and would represent the State in appeals of convictions under this new criminal statute.
The judicial branch will be responsible for adjudicating the new criminal cases resulting from the establishment of this misdemeanor.
The OSP investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of state officials and misconduct in office, which can include intentional violations of law enforcement statutes.
This agency coordinates training and certification for school safety personnel, who are subject to state use of force regulations in educational settings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that officers render basic first aid and request medical assistance; MIEMSS regulates the statewide emergency medical services network that interacts with these incidents.
The system's member institutions operate police departments that are subject to the requirements and criminal penalties of the Use of Force Statute.
As a public university with an independent police force, its officers are directly subject to the bill's requirements to intervene and provide medical care.
The Comptroller employs sworn enforcement officers for the regulation of alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuels, who are classified as police officers under the bill.
The college operates its own security and law enforcement personnel who must adhere to the Maryland Use of Force Statute.
The office oversees the executive branch and state law enforcement agencies, and the Governor proposes the policies and annual budget that support these agencies' training and operations.

Synopsis: Establishing a direct admission program at participating public senior higher education institutions for certain eligible high school students beginning in the 2028-2029 academic year; requiring the Maryland Higher Education Commission, the State Department of Education, and public senior higher education institutions to establish eligibility requirements for the program; and requiring the Commission with the Department to study and make recommendations to the General Assembly on the program by July 1, 2027.
Title: Higher Education - Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Direct Admission Program and Study
Status: In the Senate - Favorable Report by Education, Energy, and the Environment

bill_summary: This bill establishes a direct admission program at participating public four-year higher education institutions for Maryland high school students who meet college and career readiness standards and minimum GPA requirements. The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and the State Department of Education are responsible for setting eligibility criteria and managing the notification process. The bill also mandates a study by MHEC, due in 2027, to determine the operational and technical requirements for implementing the program by the 2028-2029 academic year.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Eligible Maryland high school students and public senior higher education institutions including the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a general fund expenditure increase of $100,000 in FY 2027 for a required implementation study. Additional implementation costs starting in FY 2028 are expected to be significant, potentially reaching millions of dollars, though exact figures are indeterminate until the study is completed. Because institutional participation is optional, any direct costs or revenue changes for universities will depend on their individual participation and subsequent student enrollment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering the direct admission program, managing the financial aid system integration, and leading the implementation study and report required by the bill.

The State Department of Education is a primary partner in the program, responsible for establishing eligibility requirements, providing student academic and College and Career Readiness (CCR) data, and collaborating on the required study.

As a public senior higher education institution defined in the bill, the University System of Maryland is required to participate in establishing program eligibility requirements and entering into a memorandum of understanding, and its constituent institutions may choose to participate in the program.

Morgan State University is explicitly named as a public senior higher education institution required to collaborate on eligibility requirements and the memorandum of understanding for the direct admission program.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly named as a public senior higher education institution required to collaborate on eligibility requirements and the memorandum of understanding for the direct admission program.
The department is impacted by the estimated $100,000 general fund expenditure for the study in FY 2027 and potential multimillion-dollar annual implementation costs starting in FY 2028.

The bill's requirement to study the integration of student academic data with financial aid and admission data aligns with the mission of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center, which links student and workforce data for policy analysis.

The bill requires a study of the technical mechanisms and system interoperability needed to integrate academic and financial data, which may involve the state's central IT agency, especially for projects with significant fiscal impact.

bill_summary: The Jack Cover Vernal Pool Wetlands Protection Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR), in coordination with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), to identify and maintain a list of vernal pools in the State. The bill mandates that DNR establish identification criteria, provide training to designated MDE staff, and publish the list on its website. MDE staff are required to notify DNR of potential vernal pool locations discovered while performing their standard regulatory duties regarding nontidal wetlands.
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Department of the Environment, the University of Maryland, environmental researchers, and native amphibian and invertebrate species that depend on vernal pool habitats.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. There is no anticipated effect on State revenues or local government finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Natural Resources to lead the creation and maintenance of the statewide list of vernal pools, establish identification criteria and procedures, and provide identification training to other state personnel.

The bill requires the Department of the Environment to coordinate with the Department of Natural Resources to create the vernal pool list, designate staff to receive specialized training, and notify the Department of Natural Resources of potential pools identified during nontidal wetland reviews.

The Office of the Attorney General will provide essential legal counsel to both the Department of Natural Resources and the Department of the Environment regarding the development of new identification criteria, the maintenance of the public list, and any associated regulatory implementation.

The bill specifically authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to consult with the University of Maryland (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) as a stakeholder group to provide scientific expertise for the identification of vernal pools.

As a major developer of state infrastructure and a significant landholder, the Department of Transportation is impacted by the formal identification and listing of vernal pools, which must be accounted for during the environmental review and permitting phases of transportation projects.

The Department of General Services manages state-owned land and facilities; the identification and public listing of vernal pools on state property is relevant to their site planning, maintenance protocols, and future construction activities.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments (DNR and MDE) tasked with implementing the act and coordinates the policy initiatives related to environmental protection and resource management.

Title: Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund - Uses - Cooperative Housing Corporations and Condominiums (Co-Op and Condo Energy Refund Equity Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: The bill expands the definition of 'residential distribution customer' to include members of cooperative housing corporations and condominium unit owners, ensuring they are eligible for electricity bill refunds or credits funded by the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund. It establishes a distribution mechanism where electric companies provide refunds to the governing bodies of these entities, who then pass them to individual residents. Additionally, it provides for a 'catch-up' refund in fiscal year 2027 for those who did not receive the initial credit in fiscal year 2026.
stakeholders: Members of cooperative housing corporations, condominium unit owners, electric companies, municipal electric utilities, and governing bodies of condominiums and housing cooperatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund increase by an indeterminate amount in fiscal year 2027 to provide catch-up refunds to eligible residents. The Fiscal Note provides an illustrative estimate of 5000000 based on the assumption that 2.5% of residential customers missed the initial refund. Local governments operating municipal electric utilities will be required to process these refunds without retaining overhead costs, and local revenues could be impacted if funds are redirected from other clean energy programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is the source of the funding for the energy refunds and credits mandated by this bill. The bill specifically alters the authorized uses of compliance fee revenue within the SEIF.

The bill explicitly states that the process for refunding or crediting energy compliance fees shall be directed and overseen by the Public Service Commission. Additionally, the Commission is responsible for awarding the grants to electric companies that facilitate these refunds.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility consumers. Since the bill directly impacts how energy refunds are distributed to a specific class of residential customers (condominium and cooperative housing members), this is highly relevant to their advocacy mission.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state budget execution. The bill involves the transfer of funds via budget amendment and the allocation of special fund expenditures from the SEIF, requiring DBM's oversight of the fiscal process.

The bill grants the Governor the authority to transfer funds from the SEIF to the Public Service Commission via budget amendment. The office also provides general executive oversight of the implementing agencies, MEA and PSC.

The Secretary of State's office is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums. As this bill establishes new financial rights and distribution procedures specifically for condominium unit owners and cooperative housing, it falls within the scope of their constituent oversight.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the MEA and the Public Service Commission. They would be responsible for advising these agencies on the implementation of the bill's new statutory requirements and definitions.

Synopsis: Exempting a lease of county property for a term of 5 years or less and with an annual rent of not greater than $750 made by Dorchester County from certain notice requirements.
Title: Dorchester County - County Property Leases - Notice Exemptions
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill exempts Dorchester County from the requirement to publish public notice in a newspaper before leasing county property, provided the lease term is five years or less and the annual rent is $750 or less.
stakeholders: Dorchester County government and individuals or businesses leasing county property
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Dorchester County expenditures for advertising public notices may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027, with an estimated savings of $200 per notice. The overall fiscal impact is expected to be minimal, and county revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As an agency dedicated to advocating for the interests of Maryland's 18 rural counties, the Rural Maryland Council is relevant because this bill directly addresses an administrative and financial burden (advertising costs and notice delays) specifically for Dorchester County, a rural jurisdiction.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides policy guidance and technical assistance to local governments regarding resource management. This bill modifies the statutory requirements for how Dorchester County manages and disposes of its property through leases.

The Governor's Office manages intergovernmental relations with local entities. This legislation affects local government autonomy and administrative procedures within Dorchester County, requiring executive branch awareness of the shift in local property disposition rules.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly. Because this bill proposes a specific county exemption to the Local Government Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, the OAG is involved in reviewing the legal sufficiency and constitutional implications of the measure.

Title: Community Eligibility Provision Expansion Program - Establishment

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) Expansion Program within the Maryland State Department of Education. The program provides supplemental state funding to eligible public and nonpublic schools that participate in the federal CEP child nutrition programs. The state is required to pay the difference between the federal paid reimbursement rate and the federal free reimbursement rate to help schools provide free meals to all students.
stakeholders: Students in high-poverty schools, local school systems, and participating nonpublic schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $10,000,000 beginning in fiscal year 2028. These funds will be used by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to provide grants to local school boards, after accounting for administrative costs including a part-time staff position and software enhancements. Local school systems will receive the majority of these funds, and increased participation in the federal CEP program may lead to a substantial increase in federal funding for school meals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and distributing funds for the Community Eligibility Provision Expansion Program, as well as reporting on its outcomes and student meal debt.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget development and personnel management. This bill mandates a $10 million annual appropriation and requires MSDE to hire additional staff, which directly impacts DBM's fiscal and personnel oversight duties.

The bill specifically mandates that the Governor include a $10 million appropriation in the annual budget bill starting in FY 2028 and aligns with the office's role in overseeing executive policy initiatives.
This agency focuses on reducing child poverty and improving access to education and health services; the expansion of free school meals directly supports its mission to combat youth food insecurity.

The Innovation Team is charged with piloting initiatives to address the Governor's priorities of reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility, which are central objectives of the CEP Expansion Program.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for paying state bills and distributing the $10 million in mandated program funds to school systems.
DHS administers SNAP and TANF programs, which provide the direct certification data necessary to determine a school's 'Identified Student Percentage' (ISP) for CEP eligibility.

GOPI oversees the implementation of the State Comprehensive Plan and aligns agency activities with performance metrics; this program requires specific outcome reporting that falls under their oversight of government responsiveness.
OLA is responsible for auditing executive branch agencies and will likely perform fiscal and performance audits on this new $10 million grant program at MSDE.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and other state agencies regarding the implementation, regulation, and enforcement of new state laws and programs.
The bill requires MSDE to consider geographic diversity in its funding prioritization, an area where the Council advocates for the interests and resource access of Maryland's rural counties.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) Enforcement Recovery Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support enforcement activities related to consumer protection, antitrust, and securities laws. The fund receives a portion of penalties obtained from civil enforcement actions, specifically allowing the OAG to deposit up to 25% of recoveries that exceed $100,000, subject to an annual aggregate cap.
stakeholders: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Maryland consumers, and entities subject to enforcement actions under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, antitrust laws, or the Maryland Securities Act.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a new special fund with an annual revenue cap of $7,500,000. Special fund revenues may increase starting in FY 2027 through the diversion of penalties that currently flow to the General Fund or the Consumer Protection Division Recoveries Fund. However, the Department of Legislative Services expects the overall impact to be minimal as actual recoveries meeting the bill's criteria may be limited, and interest earned on the fund is credited back to the General Fund. State expenditures are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Office of the Attorney General Enforcement Recovery Fund within the OAG to support its consumer protection, antitrust, and securities enforcement activities. The OAG is the primary agency responsible for administering the fund and managing its expenditures.
The Comptroller is explicitly tasked with accounting for the new special fund and is required to transfer any year-end balance exceeding $7.5 million to the General Fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State funds.

As the agency responsible for budget development and execution, DBM is impacted by the bill's 'non-supplanting' clause, which prevents the fund from being used to reduce general fund appropriations for the OAG.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the state budget. The bill imposes specific policy constraints on budget proposals by requiring that the new fund serves as supplemental funding and not as a replacement for standard appropriations.

Synopsis: Reserving jurisdiction with respect to certain federal land in the State under certain conditions; authorizing the Central Collection Unit of the Department of Budget and Management to collect a certain amount of delinquent federal funds; authorizing the Central Collection Unit, under a certain circumstance, to collect certain federal funds owed to the State, place liens on federal property in the State, and direct the Comptroller to withhold certain payments to the federal government; etc.
Title: State Finance - Delinquent Federal Funds (Federal Obligations Enforcement Act)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: The Federal Obligations Enforcement Act authorizes the Board of Public Works to determine if the federal government is delinquent in providing funds to the State due to noncompliance with court decisions regarding congressionally approved spending. Upon such a determination, the Central Collection Unit is authorized to collect the delinquent funds, place liens on federal property within Maryland, and direct the Comptroller to withhold state payments normally destined for the federal government.
responsible_party: The Board of Public Works, the Central Collection Unit of the Department of Budget and Management, and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies (including the Maryland Department of Transportation), the federal government, and Maryland residents who rely on federally funded programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by as much as $660,880 in FY 2027 for system programming at the Comptroller’s Office ($175,000) and staffing costs for the Office of the Attorney General ($485,827). There is a potential for significant but indeterminate decreases in both state expenditures (from withholding payments) and federal fund revenues (due to federal offsets or grant revocations). Specifically, the Maryland Department of Transportation notes that up to $1.5 billion in annual federal capital funding could be at risk if federal funds are withheld or grants are jeopardized.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary enforcement mechanism is handled by the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is a unit within the Department of Budget and Management. The CCU is tasked with collecting delinquent federal funds, placing liens on federal property, and directing the withholding of payments.

The Board of Public Works is given the statutory authority to determine, by a majority vote, whether the federal government is delinquent in its obligations to the State. This determination is the necessary trigger for the enforcement actions authorized by the bill.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Comptroller to withhold State payments to the federal government upon direction from the CCU. Additionally, the fiscal note identifies significant costs for the Comptroller's Office for vendor programming to enable manual intervention in these payments. The Comptroller also serves on the Board of Public Works.

The Attorney General is the legal advisor to the CCU. The fiscal note anticipates that the bill will lead to significant litigation with the federal government, requiring the OAG to hire additional assistant Attorneys General, paralegals, and administrative staff.

The Governor is a member of the Board of Public Works, which determines federal delinquency. Additionally, the bill updates the Governor's authority to enter into jurisdictional agreements with the United States regarding federal land in the State.

The fiscal note identifies a major fiscal risk to MDOT, noting that its capital program relies on $1.5 billion in federal funds which could be jeopardized by federal offsets or grant non-compliance if the State withholds payments to the federal government.
The State Treasurer serves as one of the three members of the Board of Public Works, which is responsible for the initial determination of federal delinquency under the bill.
The bill may result in an increase in cases heard and liens recorded in the circuit courts, which are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for retirement income by expanding the definition of eligible retirement plans to include Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs), Roth IRAs, and simplified employee pensions. It phases in an increase in the subtraction amount to 100% of eligible retirement income by tax year 2028 and removes the requirement to reduce the exclusion by Social Security or Railroad Retirement benefits.
stakeholders: Retired Maryland residents age 65 or older, individuals with total disabilities or disabled spouses, and retired forest, park, or wildlife rangers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are projected to decrease by $60,400,000 in FY 2027, $393,800,000 in FY 2028, and reach $784,800,000 by FY 2031. Local income tax revenues are also expected to decrease, with an estimated loss of $37,600,000 in FY 2027 and $245,200,000 in FY 2028. Implementation can be handled by the Comptroller's Office using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and enforcement. This bill directly alters the State income tax code regarding subtraction modifications for retirement income, and the fiscal note specifically mentions the Comptroller's ability to implement these changes.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill has a significant fiscal impact, reducing General Fund revenues by nearly $800 million annually by FY 2031, which directly affects the agency's core mission of developing and supervising the state budget.

The Governor proposes the annual state budget and oversees the executive branch. The massive revenue loss associated with this bill would require significant policy and budgetary adjustments within the Governor's proposed budget.
The bill provides substantial tax relief to Marylanders aged 65 and older, which is the primary demographic served by this department.
The bill provides tax relief for individuals who are totally disabled (or whose spouses are totally disabled), directly impacting the financial well-being of the department's target population.

The agency manages retirement benefits for over 420,000 members. The bill changes the tax treatment of the 'employee retirement system' and 'qualified retirement plan' income received by these retirees, significantly affecting their net take-home benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands tax exclusions for income from 401(k), 403(b), and 457(b) plans, all of which are administered by this agency for state employees and teachers.

MarylandSaves provides Roth IRAs to private-sector workers. This bill specifically adds Roth IRAs under section 408A of the Internal Revenue Code to the list of qualified retirement plans eligible for the subtraction modification, increasing the program's value proposition.

The Treasurer manages state funds and oversees the MarylandSaves program. The significant reduction in state revenues affects the funds the Treasurer manages, and the tax changes directly impact the retirement programs they oversee.
The bill contains specific provisions relating to retired forest rangers, park rangers, and wildlife rangers, which are professional categories employed and managed by DNR.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Tax Court may be required to adjudicate disputes regarding the expanded definitions and application of the new subtraction modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill amends a section of the Transportation Article that specifies the entities, including the courts, authorized to access confidential MVA digital records, affecting the broader judicial information ecosystem.

bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal prohibition against displaying or distributing obscene material to minors by adding drawings and illustrations to the definition of restricted items. It specifically prohibits public schools and school principals from openly displaying such obscene materials on school premises and includes the renting or borrowing of these items in the list of prohibited activities.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, local law enforcement agencies, and public school principals
stakeholders: Minors, public school administrators, and owners or managers of newsstands and other businesses frequented by minors
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Violations of the bill's provisions are classified as misdemeanors, which may result in fines ranging from $1,000 to $5,000 and potential imprisonment, though these are not expected to have a significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly expands criminal prohibitions regarding the display of obscene materials to specifically include public schools and school principals, directly impacting the governance and environment of Maryland's 24 local school systems overseen by MSDE.

As an independent unit within MSDE responsible for providing a comprehensive approach to school safety, this agency is relevant to the regulation of materials within school premises and the legal standards for school personnel.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to state agencies, including those managing education and law enforcement, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of updated criminal statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies a criminal statute and creates potential misdemeanor charges, necessitating legal representation from the OPD for indigent individuals charged under these provisions.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing the criminal laws and investigating potential violations of statutes related to the display of obscene material.
The judicial branch will be responsible for adjudicating misdemeanor cases resulting from the violations defined in the bill, requiring administrative and operational support.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of the modified statute carry penalties of up to three years of imprisonment, which has a direct impact on the correctional facilities and supervision services managed by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on criminal justice strategies and public safety policy, including the coordination of interagency efforts to address issues related to criminal law and minor safety.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing state laws and coordinating policy initiatives related to education and public safety.

The Public Service Commission is specifically referenced in the text of Section 11-203 of the Criminal Law Article regarding telephone company tariffs, although the bill does not alter that specific subsection.

bill_summary: This bill enhances privacy protections for Maryland residents by prohibiting data controllers from selling personal data to government units involved in civil immigration enforcement. It requires custodians of public records to take reasonable steps to ensure records are not accessed for immigration enforcement purposes without a warrant and extends these protections to law enforcement message switching systems. Additionally, it expands the definition of sensitive data and requires state and local government entities to update their data protection and disclosure procedures.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Motor Vehicle Administration, Department of State Police, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, data controllers and processors, state and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, and individuals or entities requesting public records.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary may increase significantly to implement new procedures for determining the intent of every data request. While most other state and local agencies are expected to manage the requirements within existing resources, some local governments may experience significant operational impacts due to the increased scrutiny required for public record requests. The bill has no direct impact on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies that the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts will experience a significant operational impact and increased general fund expenditures to implement new procedures for determining the purpose of data requests across all courthouse kiosks and records.

As a major collector of sensitive personal and financial data, the Comptroller is subject to the bill's expanded Public Information Act restrictions and the requirement to develop procedures to prevent the sale or redisclosure of sensitive data.

DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and personnel oversight; it will need to manage the budgetary impact of the bill, including potential staffing or programming costs for agencies like the Judiciary and DPSCS.

Mentioned in the fiscal note as being affected, MSDE will need to ensure its data management and public record disclosure policies comply with the bill's new sensitive data protections and immigration enforcement inquiries.

As an agency handling sensitive health and personal data, MDH is impacted by the bill's new restrictions on data disclosure for immigration enforcement and the requirement to develop privacy procedures in consultation with DoIT.
The bill explicitly requires every Maryland governmental entity to consult with DoIT to develop and publish procedures that prevent the sale and redisclosure of sensitive data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically names DPSCS to adopt regulations regarding message switching systems and reporting requirements for immigration-related data requests. It is a primary implementing agency for the public safety provisions.

The bill specifically tasks the Motor Vehicle Administration (a unit of MDOT) with adopting regulations to ensure compliance with data disclosure restrictions and mandates annual reporting on immigration enforcement data requests.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to adopt regulations to enforce data privacy compliance and to report annually on requests for personal information or facial recognition searches for immigration purposes.

The OAG oversees the Public Information Act Manual and website and will provide legal guidance to all state agencies on implementing the bill's new restrictions on data sharing and immigration enforcement inquiries.

Synopsis: Establishing a cause of action against a developer of a certain artificial intelligence system for defective design, failure to provide adequate instruction or warning, and breach of express warranty; establishing that a deployer of a certain artificial intelligence system may be sued in lieu of a developer under certain circumstances; authorizing the Attorney General to bring an action against a developer or a deployer for harm caused by a certain dangerous or defective product; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a cause of action for product liability regarding high-impact and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems. It allows individuals to sue AI developers or deployers for defective design, failure to provide adequate warnings or instructions, and breach of express warranty. The bill provides a rebuttable presumption that a system is not defective if the developer or deployer followed industry best practices, conducted rigorous testing, and mitigated risks to minors. Additionally, it empowers the Maryland Attorney General to bring enforcement actions, introduces a comparative fault standard (eliminating contributory negligence as a total bar to recovery), and allows for joint and several liability.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Developers of AI systems, deployers of AI systems (excluding small businesses with fewer than 20 employees or 10,000 users), and Maryland residents who suffer property damage, personal injury, or other harms from AI systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's fiscal impact is primarily on the State's general fund. Expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) are expected to increase to manage new litigation; the OAG estimated a cost of $276,569 in fiscal 2027, though the Department of Legislative Services notes that the actual impact depends on case volume. State general fund revenues may increase from civil penalties and the recovery of legal costs. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions against developers or deployers for harm caused by defective AI systems. The fiscal note indicates the agency will need additional staff and technologists to implement these enforcement powers.
The bill establishes a new cause of action for AI product liability, which will impact court operations and civil caseloads within the Maryland Judicial Branch.

As the state's IT strategy lead, DoIT will be responsible for overseeing the risk management policies that state agencies (acting as 'deployers') must implement to meet the bill's requirements for a rebuttable presumption against liability.

The bill allows governmental entities to be sued as developers or deployers of AI. The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, which provides the state's insurance protection and would handle claims or liabilities incurred by state agencies under this Act.
The bill defines 'high-impact' AI systems to include those used in medical devices and healthcare decisions, areas where the Department of Health provides regulation and oversight.
The bill targets AI systems used in vehicles and vehicle safety systems as 'high-impact' products, which falls under the regulatory scope of MDOT's modal administrations like the MVA and SHA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill identifies AI used in the criminal justice system as 'high-impact,' which directly involves the technologies deployed by DPSCS for supervision and administration of justice-involved individuals.
The bill includes AI used in the direct management or operation of critical infrastructure as 'high-impact.' The PSC regulates the utilities that comprise much of this infrastructure.
The bill specifically classifies AI systems used in making consequential decisions regarding insurance as 'high-impact,' impacting the industry regulated by the MIA.

The bill classifies AI systems used in employment and financial/credit decisions as 'high-impact.' The Department of Labor oversees workforce development, labor law enforcement, and the regulation of financial institutions.
The bill addresses AI used in education and includes specific requirements for mitigating risks to minors, which directly involves the oversight responsibilities of MSDE.
AI systems used in consequential education decisions are classified as 'high-impact' products, which is relevant to the commission's role in setting statewide policies for postsecondary institutions.
The bill identifies AI used for consequential decisions in housing as 'high-impact,' which relates to the department's mission of ensuring access to safe and affordable housing.
DBM is responsible for state personnel and fiscal planning; it will need to oversee the budget increases and staffing requirements (such as for the OAG) identified in the fiscal note.
The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and coordinates the executive branch's response to emerging technology risks and the enforcement priorities of the Attorney General.
As the state's economic development agency, Commerce is impacted by changes in product liability laws that affect the tech sector and the overall business climate in Maryland.

Synopsis: Increasing the salary of a judge of the Orphans' Court for Cecil County to be an amount determined by the County Council of Cecil County, but not less than $11,000; establishing that the Chief Judge shall receive certain additional compensation annually as determined by the County Council of Cecil County, but not less than $1,500; and specifying the annual allowance for travel expenses to be as determined by the County Council of Cecil County but not less than $1,500.

bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum annual salary for judges of the Orphans' Court for Cecil County to $11,000, with the exact amount to be determined by the County Council. It also requires the Chief Judge to receive at least $1,500 in additional compensation and sets a minimum annual travel allowance of $1,500 for all judges. These compensation changes take effect at the start of the next term of office following the bill's implementation.
stakeholders: Judges of the Orphans' Court for Cecil County
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on state finances. Cecil County expenditures will increase by at least $4,813 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $8,250 annually starting in fiscal 2028. These estimates represent the minimum mandated increases for judge salaries and allowances, which take effect when the next terms of office begin in December 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court in each jurisdiction. This bill specifically adjusts the compensation and travel allowances for the judges of the Cecil County Orphans' Court, directly affecting the administrative environment and the judicial officers supported by the Cecil County Register of Wills.

As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) provides operational and legal guidance to all state courts. While the salary increase is funded by Cecil County, the AOC oversees the broader judicial system in which the Orphans' Courts operate.

The Governor's Office is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the constitutional process of appointing individuals to judicial vacancies, including positions on the Orphans' Court should they become open.

stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and healthcare providers and patients in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect the Maryland Department of Health's operations or finances. MDH advises that it does not currently collect abortion data, but it can respond to CDC requests using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on local government or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit abortion data to the CDC upon request and evaluates the legality of such requests, making it the primary implementing agency.

The bill allows the Department to refuse data requests if they violate state or federal law. The OAG would be required to provide legal counsel regarding the intersection of federal requests and Maryland's existing reproductive health shield laws.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and coordinates policy regarding sensitive public health data and intergovernmental relations.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Algorithmic Addiction Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Department of Health to address the harmful effects of social media algorithms on children. The fund will be composed of revenue from civil penalties and settlements resulting from legal claims against technology and social media companies for algorithm-related harms. Proceeds will be used for addiction treatment, prevention services, digital literacy education, research, and youth mental health programs. The Secretary of Health is required to develop performance goals and report annually on the fund's use and effectiveness.
stakeholders: Maryland youth and children, technology and social media companies, local health departments, local school systems, and mental health service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a special fund to retain revenues from settlements or judgments against social media companies. Although the total potential revenue is indeterminate, the Maryland Department of Health will incur estimated general fund expenditures of at least $50,000 annually for contractual services and administration beginning in the year the fund is established, as the bill restricts the use of the fund for most administrative costs. Local governments and school systems may experience a positive fiscal impact through grants provided for algorithmic addiction prevention and treatment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Algorithmic Addiction Fund. The Secretary of Health must develop goals, objectives, and performance indicators; consult with stakeholders annually; establish a grant program for political subdivisions; and report expenditures and progress to the General Assembly.

The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for prosecuting the claims and securing the judgments or settlements that provide revenue for the fund. The bill also tasks the Attorney General with identifying the controlling versions of settlement agreements and notifying the Department of Legislative Services when the bill's contingencies are met.

The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Algorithmic Addiction Fund. The Comptroller's office will also be involved in managing the accrual of interest and the fiscal note indicates the office will be involved in accounting and holding the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Algorithmic Addiction Fund separately and to invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other State money.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will be responsible for overseeing the inclusion of the Algorithmic Addiction Fund in the state's annual budget and supervising the execution of its expenditures.

The bill authorizes the use of the fund for algorithmic addiction prevention services, specifically mentioning the organization of primary and secondary school education campaigns. This involves MSDE's oversight of public school policies and standards.

The bill's primary focus is addressing harm to children from social media and algorithms and providing youth mental health services, which aligns with this office's mission to promote the well-being of Maryland's children.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, which will now include the Algorithmic Addiction Fund. The Secretary of Health, who administers the fund, reports to the Governor.

The bill mandates the development of key performance indicators and objectives for the new fund. GOPI is responsible for utilizing data-driven strategies and performance metrics to oversee the implementation of state priorities and agency activities.

The bill requires the Secretary of Health to establish and administer a grant program for the distribution of funds to political subdivisions. The Grants Office provides technical assistance and resources for managing such grant programs.
While primarily a health and fiscal bill, the subject matter—algorithmic addiction and social media impacts—relates to the state's broader information technology and telecommunications strategy.
