The Secretary of State is the official custodian of the state's records, including executive orders and proclamations issued by the Governor.
The Maryland State Archives is responsible for preserving the permanent records of the executive branch, including the proclamations mandated by this bill.

This division within the Secretary of State's office coordinates international engagement and dialogue, which shares a thematic link with the bill's focus on international victims and regimes across over 40 nations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor and the General Assembly, ensuring the legal sufficiency of the proclamation and the renumbering of the General Provisions Article.
The Lieutenant Governor represents the state at ceremonial functions and may be involved in events associated with the commemorative day.

Synopsis: Providing for the valuation of a gift card for the purpose of determining value for crimes involving theft; prohibiting a person, with the intent to defraud another, from altering or tampering with a gift card or its packaging; and providing that a violation of the Act is a misdemeanor punishable by a term of imprisonment of up to 18 months or a fine not to exceed $500 or both.
Title: Criminal Law - Theft and Fraud Crimes - Valuation and Forgery of Gift Cards
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 457

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill makes it a crime to tamper with gift cards or their packaging to defraud others, creating a misdemeanor known as gift card forgery. It also establishes specific rules for determining the value of a gift card for theft prosecutions, setting the value as the greatest of the face value, a default of $100 if no value is listed, the value represented by the defendant, or the actual loss incurred.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Consumers, retail businesses, law enforcement agencies, and individuals involved in criminal proceedings related to gift card theft or fraud.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor of 'gift card forgery' and establishes specific valuation rules for gift cards in theft cases, directly impacting judicial proceedings, evidence assessment, and court administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency representing indigent defendants, the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for defending individuals charged with the new misdemeanor of gift card forgery and navigating the new statutory valuation rules in theft cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor with a penalty of up to 18 months in prison. This may lead to an increase in individuals under the supervision of the Division of Parole and Probation or housed in correctional facilities.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the new prohibitions against gift card tampering and fraud.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and enforces laws related to consumer protection; the bill's focus on gift card fraud and consumer product tampering falls within their area of concern for public safety and consumer rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and public safety policy, making the creation of new criminal penalties and theft valuation methods relevant to their mission.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives related to law enforcement and public safety, including the final approval of criminal law changes.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to develop a process to allow a homeowner to designate a family member or another representative of the homeowner to communicate and work with the Ombudsman on the homeowner's behalf; requiring the dwelling of a homeowner to be withheld from tax sale if the homeowner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship; increasing the maximum value of a dwelling that a homeowner may reside in and be eligible for the Homeowner Protection Program to $450,000; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protections - Revisions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 777

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: This bill expands protections for homeowners against tax sales by requiring local collectors to withhold properties from sale if the owner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship. It increases the eligibility threshold for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) by raising the maximum allowable dwelling value from $300,000 to $450,000, and it establishes a process for homeowners to designate representatives to work with the State Tax Sale Ombudsman on their behalf.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners facing tax sale, specifically those with terminal illnesses, medical hardships, or properties valued up to $450,000; local government tax collectors; and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may increase as expanded eligibility allows Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) funds to be more fully utilized, with potential for increased future revenues from homeowner repayments; however, total annual program funding remains $750,000. Local government revenues may see minimal delays or reductions starting in fiscal 2027 due to the new requirements for withholding properties from tax sale.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to define 'terminal illness' and 'medical hardship' by regulation. These definitions are central to determining eligibility for withholding properties from tax sale and priority enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program.

The bill impacts the Governor's oversight of executive branch agencies and programs. Additionally, the fiscal note mentions a statutory requirement for the Governor to annually appropriate $250,000 to the Homeowner Protection Fund, which the bill expands by increasing eligibility thresholds and priorities.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for managing the mandated annual appropriation to the Homeowner Protection Fund and overseeing the budget implications of expanding program eligibility and enrollment priorities.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the executive branch and would be responsible for providing legal review of the new regulations defining medical hardships and the procedural framework for homeowners to designate representatives to communicate with the Ombudsman.

The bill's protections for homeowners with terminal illnesses, medical hardships, or low income significantly impact older adults, who are primary constituents of the Department. The underlying law also specifically protects homeowners at least 65 years old from tax sales.

The bill includes priority enrollment for the Homeowner Protection Program for individuals receiving federal disability benefits and those facing medical hardships, aligning with the Department's mission to support Marylanders with disabilities and improve their access to secure housing.

The bill amends § 14-836 of the Tax - Property Article, which governs the judicial foreclosure of the right of redemption. It introduces a new procedural requirement for plaintiffs to send notice to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman in cases involving owner-occupied property, impacting court-supervised tax sale proceedings.

The Department's mission to prevent homelessness and ensure access to secure, affordable housing is directly supported by the bill's aim to divert vulnerable homeowners from the tax sale process and allow them to remain in their homes.

Synopsis: Altering the hours during which a holder of a Class B beer, wine, and liquor (golf course) license in Wicomico County may sell alcoholic beverages so as to begin at 7 a.m. rather than 10 a.m., Monday through Sunday.
Title: Wicomico County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B (Golf Course) License - Hours of Sale
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 820
bill_summary: This bill extends the permitted hours for the sale of alcoholic beverages by holders of a Class B beer, wine, and liquor (golf course) license in Wicomico County. It changes the starting time for sales from 10:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. every day of the week.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of public, for-profit 18-hole golf courses in Wicomico County and their patrons.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Locally, Wicomico County can handle any additional enforcement activities with existing resources, and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for the final review and signing of all legislation passed by the General Assembly. This bill was approved and signed into law by the Governor.

The Comptroller's office is identified in the agency summary as the entity that regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. This bill directly amends hours of sale for a specific class of alcoholic beverages license.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state government regarding the enforcement and interpretation of state laws, including those within the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education to develop and implement, not later than the 2026-2027 school year, a policy prohibiting the use of a personal electronic device by a student during school day hours; providing the policy may not prohibit a student from using a personal electronic device for any purpose related to an individualized program or 504 plan; providing that any disciplinary measures adopted as part of the policy may not include suspension or expulsion solely for violation of the policy; etc.
Title: County Boards of Education - Student Personal Electronic Device Use Policy - Establishment (Phones Away for the School Day Act)
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Ways and Means; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill, known as the 'Phones Away for the School Day Act,' requires each Maryland county board of education to develop and implement a policy by the 2026-2027 school year that prohibits students from using or carrying personal electronic devices during school hours. Students must store their devices in a manner determined by the board. Exceptions are provided for instructional devices, medical devices, and purposes documented in a student's Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 Plan. Schools are also required to provide designated telephones for students to contact parents or guardians if necessary.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and legal guardians, teachers, and local school board administrators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Local boards of education can likely develop and implement the required personal electronic device policies using existing resources. No impact on local revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the public education system by requiring county boards of education to implement specific student policies. As the oversight and leadership body for the state's 24 local school systems, MSDE is responsible for ensuring compliance and providing guidance on such educational policies. The fiscal note also confirms that MSDE and the State Board of Education previously convened a task force on this specific issue.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education responsible for coordinating school safety, MCSS is relevant because policies regarding the use and storage of electronic devices significantly impact school environment safety, emergency communication protocols, and the development of safe learning environments.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Department of Education and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality and constitutionality of the mandate on local boards and advising on potential liability issues related to the storage of student property.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of facial recognition technology by law enforcement to investigate the commission or attempted commission of certain crimes if the image used by facial recognition technology was captured in the interior of a dwelling.
Title: Law Enforcement - Use of Facial Recognition Technology - Images Captured in Dwelling Interior
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill authorizes law enforcement agencies to use facial recognition technology to investigate certain crimes, including arson, burglary, and trespass, provided the image being analyzed was captured by a camera located inside the interior of a dwelling.
stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, individuals suspected of crimes committed within dwellings, and residents or owners of dwellings.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. No specific revenue increases or expenditure mandates were identified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police is authorized to use FRT under this bill and is responsible for developing and publishing the model statewide FRT policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is mandated by law to develop and administer the required training program that all law enforcement officers and agents must complete annually before using facial recognition technology.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's expansion of authorized FRT use and its specific rules regarding evidence admissibility directly impact the defense of indigent clients in criminal and juvenile proceedings.
The bill explicitly identifies the MVA's driver's license and identification card photo database as a primary repository for comparison in law enforcement facial recognition searches.
The bill establishes new legal standards for the introduction and exclusion of FRT-generated evidence in criminal and juvenile court proceedings, which the Judiciary must implement.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on the interpretation and enforcement of FRT statutes and represents the state in related litigation regarding evidence admissibility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the coordinating body for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, including the use of advanced surveillance technologies.
The bill includes explicit protections against using FRT to discriminate based on protected classes such as race, religion, and sexual orientation, which aligns with the Commission's oversight role.
The bill's regulations regarding the admissibility of FRT evidence apply to juvenile court proceedings, which directly affects the justice-involved youth population managed by DJS.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies authorized to use this technology and is responsible for coordinating the policy initiatives that govern law enforcement procedures.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the theft of mail or packages; requiring the prosecutor of a violation of the Act to notify the victim or the victim's representative about each court proceeding, the right of the victim to submit a victim impact statement, any posttrial court proceeding, any appeal, and any sentence review related to the court proceedings; and providing that a person who violates the Act by depriving an owner of mail or a package is guilty of a felony and is subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years.
Title: Theft of Mail and Packages and Victim Notification
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill creates a new felony for the theft of mail or packages, punishable by up to five years in prison. It also requires prosecuting attorneys to provide victims or their representatives with notifications regarding court proceedings, the right to file victim impact statements, post-trial proceedings, appeals, and sentence reviews, regardless of whether a formal notification request was filed.
responsible_party: Maryland State's Attorneys' offices, the Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts), and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS).
stakeholders: Victims of mail or package theft, individuals charged with mail theft, State's Attorneys' offices, the Judiciary, and state and local correctional systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a minimal increase in state general fund expenditures for incarceration costs, which average 5838 dollars per month per person. There is a predicted minimal decrease in general fund revenues as cases shift from District Court to circuit courts. The Judiciary identifies a one-time programming expenditure of 1050 dollars. Local revenues and expenditures are anticipated to decrease minimally as cases and individuals move from local to state jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony for mail and package theft, which increases the likelihood of individuals being sentenced to state correctional facilities rather than local jails. Additionally, the department is specifically mentioned as an entity authorized to receive confidential victim information, and its Division of Parole and Probation is impacted by the new sentencing and supervision requirements.

The bill directly impacts court operations by requiring changes to victim notification protocols. The Administrative Office of the Courts manages the MDEC system used for these notifications and provides operational support to the clerks of the court who must execute the bill's procedural requirements.

The bill's victim notification requirements explicitly apply to juvenile intake officers and proceedings within the juvenile court system for acts that would be considered mail or package theft. The department is also authorized to receive confidential victim contact information for cases under its jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a new felony offense for theft of mail and packages will increase the severity of charges for indigent defendants represented by this agency, potentially requiring increased legal resources for trial and sentencing phases.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the newly created prohibition on mail and package theft, and is involved in the initial victim notification process required upon first contact.
The bill requires that in the event of an appeal, victim notification forms must be transmitted to the Attorney General, who represents the state in all criminal appeals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and manages funds for victim services. The bill's focus on criminalizing specific theft behaviors and expanding victim notification rights aligns with the agency's policy and funding oversight roles.

Synopsis: Altering the purposes for which the Secretary of Health may make grants from or agreements for the use of State and federal funds with respect to the provision of services for problem gamblers; and altering the purposes for which the Maryland Department of Health may utilize the Problem Gambling Fund to provide reimbursement to support peers providing behavioral health services to individuals with problem gambling issues who are receiving treatment or participating in certain prevention programs.
Title: Problem Gambling - Authorized Uses of Funds - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the authorized uses of the Problem Gambling Fund and other state and federal funds designated for gambling addiction services. It expands the fund's purposes to include reimbursing peer support specialists who provide behavioral health services to individuals with problem gambling issues. Conversely, it removes research and training from the list of authorized expenditures for problem gambling services.
stakeholders: Problem gamblers, behavioral health peer support specialists, and public or nonprofit organizations providing gambling treatment and prevention programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill primarily alters the purposes for which existing funds may be used, resulting in no net impact on state or local revenues or expenditures. It redirects expenditures from research and training toward peer support service reimbursement. The Maryland Department of Health can handle the administrative changes with existing resources. The fiscal 2027 budget includes 6100000 dollars in special fund expenditures from the Problem Gambling Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: While the Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementer, the Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for planning for the state's health system needs and increasing accountability. Changes to the funding and service network for problem gambling, a specific public health issue, align with their oversight of health system planning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Problem Gambling Fund is capitalized by annual fees paid by video lottery operation licensees, which this agency regulates. As the oversight body for the gaming industry that generates the fund's revenue, the agency is a key stakeholder in how those funds are redirected or utilized.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland State Treasurer invest and reinvest money in the Problem Gambling Fund, with interest and earnings accruing to the fund. This directly involves the Treasurer's core financial management responsibilities.

The bill specifies that expenditures from the Problem Gambling Fund must be made in accordance with the annual State budget or budget amendment procedures. As the agency responsible for supervising budget execution and estimating revenues, DBM oversees the fiscal process for these funds.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Secretary of Health, who is responsible for issuing the grants described. Additionally, the Governor proposes the annual state budget through which the fund's expenditures are approved.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for the Problem Gambling Fund and the establishment of the network of clinically appropriate services. The bill directly alters MDH's grant-making authority and expands the authorized uses of its funds to include peer support reimbursement.

Synopsis: Repealing the sentencing date limitation of October 1, 2021, for an individual convicted as an adult of an offense committed when the individual was a minor to file a motion to reduce the duration of the sentence.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Motion to Reduce Duration of Sentence - Repeal of Sentencing Date Limitation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for sentencing relief under the Juvenile Restoration Act by repealing the requirement that an individual convicted as an adult for an offense committed as a minor must have been sentenced before October 1, 2021. Under the bill, such individuals may file a motion to reduce their sentence duration regardless of their sentencing date, provided they have been imprisoned for at least 20 years.
stakeholders: Individuals convicted as adults for offenses committed as minors, crime victims and their representatives, State's Attorneys' offices, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is unlikely to have a state or local fiscal impact within the five-year period from fiscal 2027 to 2031. Because individuals must serve at least 20 years before becoming eligible to file a motion for sentence reduction, those sentenced after the original October 1, 2021 deadline would not be eligible to apply for relief until 2041 at the earliest.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the court to conduct hearings on motions to reduce sentences, and the Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for providing operational support and implementing policies for the Maryland Judicial Branch.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants; this bill expands eligibility for sentence reduction motions, which directly impacts the agency's caseload and duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees state correctional facilities and the supervision of incarcerated individuals; the bill's expansion of eligibility for sentence reductions directly affects the population of justice-involved individuals under their management.

As the primary legal representative for the State, the OAG represents Maryland in criminal appeals and provides legal counsel to state agencies, making it relevant to litigation or legal interpretations arising from sentencing motions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary body for coordinating public safety and criminal justice strategies. The bill pertains to sentencing policy for offenses committed by minors and involves victim impact considerations, which align with GOCPP's advisory and policy roles.
The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch; this bill represents a modification to criminal justice policy and the Juvenile Restoration Act.

Synopsis: Increasing, from 2 years to 3 years, the statute of limitations for the crime of theft of property or services with a value greater than $100 but less than $1,500.
Title: Criminal Law - Misdemeanor Theft - Statute of Limitations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill extends the statute of limitations for the prosecution of misdemeanor theft of property or services with a value of at least $100 but less than $1,500 from two years to three years. It maintains a two-year statute of limitations for theft of property or services valued at less than $100.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Individuals accused of misdemeanor theft involving property or services valued between $100 and $1,500; State and local law enforcement and prosecutors; and State and local correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2029 due to the extension of the statute of limitations, which may lead to more fines and incarcerations. Local per diem operating costs for detention facilities range from $140 to $350 per incarcerated individual. Specific aggregate dollar estimates are unavailable as the number of additional cases is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial process by extending the statute of limitations for specific misdemeanor theft charges, which affects the timing and filing of cases in the District and circuit courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational support for these court functions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants in criminal cases. Extending the statute of limitations for theft may lead to an increase in cases and workload for public defenders as more individuals are prosecuted for older offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation. The fiscal note indicates potential increases in expenditures for incarcerations (specifically in Baltimore City) and supervision for convictions resulting from the extended statute of limitations.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigate criminal theft. The bill provides a longer timeframe for the investigation and commencement of prosecution for these crimes.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and represents the state in criminal appeals. Changes to criminal laws and their statutes of limitations may affect their advisory and appellate duties.

The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues. The bill's fiscal note mentions a potential minimal increase in general fund revenue from fines imposed in the District Court for these theft cases.

Synopsis: Increasing to $40,000 over a 2-year period the amount of a certain subtraction modification under the State income tax for certain military retirement income received by an individual, regardless of age, during a taxable year for certain military service.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Military Retirement Income (Keep Our Heroes Home Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: The 'Keep Our Heroes Home Act' increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income. Starting in tax year 2026, the subtraction is increased to the first $25,000 of income, and for tax year 2027 and beyond, it is increased to the first $40,000, regardless of the recipient's age.
stakeholders: Military retirees residing in Maryland, including those from the armed forces, reserve components, the Public Health Service, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Coast and Geodetic Survey.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a decrease in State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues by expanding the income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income. While the bill text specifies individual subtraction limits of $25,000 and $40,000, specific aggregate fiscal impact figures from a formal Fiscal Note were not provided in the source text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing changes to the Maryland income tax code, including the administration and enforcement of the proposed increase to the military retirement income subtraction modification.

This bill directly benefits Maryland's veterans and military retirees by increasing tax relief. The department is the primary agency responsible for assisting veterans in securing benefits and advocating for their welfare.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and long-term fiscal planning. Because this bill increases a tax subtraction, it will result in a decrease in state income tax revenue, which DBM must account for in the state budget and fiscal projections.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget. This bill represents a significant policy change affecting state revenue and veterans' affairs, which are key executive priorities.

The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and anticipates the state's monetary needs. A change in income tax revenue affects the overall fiscal management and the state's financial position overseen by this agency.

As the Governor's senior military advisor, the Adjutant General is concerned with the welfare and retention of military personnel and retirees within the state, aligning with the bill's intent to 'Keep Our Heroes Home.'

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding income tax assessments and credits. It would be the final administrative body to hear appeals if disputes arise regarding an individual's eligibility for the increased subtraction modification.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of facial recognition technology by law enforcement to investigate the commission or attempted commission of certain crimes if the image used by facial recognition technology was captured by a camera affixed to the exterior of a dwelling by the owner or lawful tenant of the building.
Title: Law Enforcement – Use of Facial Recognition Technology – Images Captured by Camera Affixed to Dwelling Exterior
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the permitted use of facial recognition technology by law enforcement to include investigations into specific crimes—such as arson, burglary, and trespassing—provided the still or video image being analyzed was captured by a camera affixed to the exterior of a dwelling by its owner or lawful tenant.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, owners and tenants of residential dwellings with exterior cameras, and individuals investigated for property-related offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, MSP is directly authorized by the bill to use facial recognition technology in criminal investigations. Additionally, the fiscal note indicates MSP is responsible for adopting and publishing the model statewide policy regarding this technology.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for developing and administering the mandatory training program that all law enforcement officers must complete before using facial recognition technology. They also supervise correctional facilities where these investigations may originate.
The bill explicitly identifies the MVA's database of driver's license and identification card photos as the primary source for facial recognition comparisons used in criminal investigations.

The bill establishes specific rules and exclusions for the admissibility of facial recognition evidence in criminal and juvenile court proceedings, which directly impacts the operations of the judicial branch.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies implementing this technology (such as MSP and DPSCS) and oversees consumer protection and civil rights issues related to the use of biometric data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates statewide public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy, including the use of advanced technology like facial recognition for crime reduction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal and juvenile proceedings where FRT evidence may be introduced, and they are responsible for safeguarding constitutional protections against improper use of such technology.
As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the infrastructure and policies governing the databases used for facial recognition comparisons.
The bill specifically regulates the use of facial recognition results in juvenile court proceedings, which involves youth under the supervision or care of DJS.
DoIT manages the statewide network and cybersecurity strategy; they would likely be involved in ensuring the secure transmission and storage of biometric data used by law enforcement agencies.

The use of facial recognition technology is a significant civil rights issue; the Commission monitors for discriminatory practices and ensures technology is not used to target individuals based on protected classes.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for failure to pay the civil penalty issued as a result of a recorded image produced by a speed monitoring system.
Title: Speed Monitoring Systems - Citations - Failure to Pay
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill removes the requirement that a citation issued for a speed monitoring system violation must include a statement advising the recipient that failure to pay the civil penalty or contest liability is an admission of liability.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Registered motor vehicle owners and drivers who receive citations from speed monitoring systems
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill mandates administrative changes to the language required on speed camera citations, which may result in minor costs for state and local agencies to update citation templates, but no specific dollar estimates are available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the required content of citations for speed monitoring system violations, which are legal documents contested within the District Court system. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial functions associated with these proceedings.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency for the Motor Vehicle Administration and the State Highway Administration, both of which are central to the implementation and enforcement of speed monitoring systems and vehicle registration penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office is relevant to changes in law enforcement tools and the administration of traffic safety citations.

The Maryland State Police is a primary agency authorized to use speed monitoring systems, particularly in work zones. They are responsible for issuing citations that must comply with the specific content requirements altered by this bill.

The MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains its own police force, which may utilize speed monitoring systems in construction or work zones on its roadways, making the citation requirements relevant to their operations.

The bill explicitly mentions 'the Administration' (MVA) regarding its authority to refuse or suspend vehicle registrations for failure to pay speed monitoring citations. The MVA is responsible for the administrative consequences mentioned on the citations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding statutory compliance and the formatting of legal notices such as traffic citations to ensure they meet constitutional and legislative standards.

The State Highway Administration manages highway safety improvements and frequently coordinates the placement of speed monitoring systems in highway work zones. The bill affects the documentation generated by these safety programs.

Synopsis: Altering the compensation of an elected member and the president of the Montgomery County Board of Education to be based on the compensation of certain members of the General Assembly other than the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House that is in effect at the beginning of the elected member's term.
Title: Montgomery County Board of Education - Elected Members - Compensation MC 2-26
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill changes the compensation structure for the elected members and the president of the Montgomery County Board of Education. Rather than receiving a fixed annual salary, elected members will receive compensation equal to that of a member of the Maryland General Assembly, and the board president will receive the same amount plus an additional $10,000. These salary adjustments will take effect at the start of the next term of office for each board member.
stakeholders: Elected members of the Montgomery County Board of Education, the student board member, and Montgomery County taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on state finances. Locally, Montgomery County school expenditures are projected to increase by $77,317 in fiscal 2027, growing to $240,182 by fiscal 2030. These costs arise from tying board member salaries to the higher pay scales of General Assembly members and the resulting increases in student member compensation, which is capped based on regular member pay.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 local school systems, the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) monitors the governance and regulatory changes to local boards, including those affecting the Education Article.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. This bill specifically references constitutional limitations (Article III, Section 35) on salary changes during a term, which requires legal interpretation and review by the Attorney General's office.

The OLA is responsible for conducting performance and fiscal compliance audits of local school systems. Changes in board member compensation and expenditures are within the scope of their auditing duties for Montgomery County Public Schools.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs or vetoes legislation passed by the General Assembly. This bill involves structural changes to a state-authorized local board of education.

As the principal fiscal agency for the state, DBM monitors legislation with local fiscal impacts and oversees the state budget, which includes the General Assembly compensation benchmarks used in this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person with the intent to defraud another from creating, aiding in the creation of, or possessing a counterfeit lease of real property or rental agreement relating to real property.
Title: Criminal Law - Counterfeiting and Possession of Counterfeit Lease of Real Property - Penalty
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: House Bill 765 prohibits the creation, possession, or assistance in the creation of counterfeit leases or rental agreements for real property with the intent to defraud. Counterfeiting these documents is established as a felony, while possession of such counterfeit documents with fraudulent intent is a misdemeanor, both carrying potential prison sentences and fines.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Landlords, tenants, property owners, and the Maryland judicial and correctional systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures. General fund expenditures will increase minimally due to incarceration penalties; the average cost per incarcerated individual in State facilities is estimated at $5,838 per month. Local jurisdictions will also see minimal expenditure increases for detention in local facilities (ranging from $140 to $350 per day). General fund revenues will increase minimally through the collection of fines, which are capped at $1,000 per violation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new criminal offenses related to counterfeit leases, directly impacting the Office of the Public Defender's caseload for representing indigent defendants charged with these crimes, as noted in the fiscal note.

The Judiciary and the Administrative Office of the Courts are responsible for the adjudication of these new criminal offenses and the administrative handling of cases involving counterfeit instruments filed in circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is responsible for the incarceration of individuals convicted of the felony and misdemeanor offenses established by the bill, and the fiscal note explicitly discusses the impact on State incarceration expenditures.
The bill specifically identifies the filing of a counterfeit instrument with the Register of Wills as a basis for determining the venue where a prosecution may be commenced.

The legislation directly relates to the integrity of real property leases and rental agreements, which is central to the department's mission to ensure residents have access to secure housing and to protect the vitality of Maryland communities.
As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal violations, including the counterfeiting of documents and instruments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy, making the establishment of new criminal penalties for fraudulent leases relevant to its mission.
The OAG serves as the state's legal representative in criminal appeals and provides counsel to state agencies involved in the enforcement of the state's criminal laws.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies tasked with implementing this law and is responsible for signing the bill into law.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency and is responsible for the long-term fiscal planning related to the incarceration and personnel costs generated by the bill's implementation.

Synopsis: Establishing a Class C-PCL (premium cigar lounge) alcoholic beverages license for use in conjunction with a certain tobacco products retailer license; authorizing a local licensing board to issue the license; prohibiting a county clerk from issuing a certain tobacco products retailer license if the location is adjacent to a health care facility or a child care facility; exempting a holder of a certain tobacco products retailer license from the Clean Indoor Air Act; providing an annual license fee of $100; etc.
Title: Retail Tobacco Businesses and Establishment of a Premium Cigar Lounge Alcoholic Beverages License (Maryland Premium Cigar Lounge Act of 2026)

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Class C-PCL (premium cigar lounge) alcoholic beverages license for retail tobacco businesses, allowing patrons to consume their own alcohol on the premises under certain conditions. It provides an exemption from the Clean Indoor Air Act for these businesses provided they meet specific ventilation standards, revenue reporting requirements, and proximity restrictions regarding health and child care facilities.
stakeholders: Retail tobacco business owners (tobacconists), consumers of premium cigars and pipe tobacco, employees of cigar lounges, and local liquor licensing boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $152,300 in fiscal 2027, which includes $131,513 for the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to hire a field auditor and update licensing software, plus $20,744 for the Judiciary to modify the E-License system. Local revenues are expected to increase minimally through the $100 annual license fee collected for each of the approximately 46 authorized licenses statewide.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill prohibits the clerk of the circuit court from issuing a tobacconist license to businesses adjacent to health care or child care facilities. The fiscal note specifies that the Judiciary, through the Administrative Office of the Courts, must modify the E-License system used by these clerks to ensure compliance, requiring a specific general fund expenditure for programming.

The bill amends the Health – General Article regarding the Clean Indoor Air Act (CIAA), creating specific exemptions for certain retail tobacco businesses based on revenue percentages. MDH is the primary agency responsible for public health and the oversight of the CIAA framework.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector for the tobacco industry and regulates these industries. The fiscal note indicates the Comptroller audits licensed businesses, including retail tobacco businesses, to ensure compliance with statutory requirements in collaboration with regulatory commissions.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for overseeing the budget execution and personnel additions (such as the field auditors identified in the fiscal note) required to implement and enforce the new licensing and reporting requirements.

The bill prohibits tobacconist licenses from being issued for locations adjacent to licensed child care facilities. The Department of Education oversees early childhood development and child care licensing, making this a relevant safety and zoning constraint for the facilities under their jurisdiction.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions. They would be responsible for advising on the implementation of the new license class, the regulatory reports, and the legal implications of modified Clean Indoor Air Act exemptions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives. This bill introduces a new state-level license and reporting structure that aligns with executive policy regarding alcohol and tobacco regulation and public health.

Synopsis: Requiring a court to notify the United States Postmaster General of a certain conviction involving the theft, taking, or opening of mail or packages, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Law - Theft and Opening of Mail and Packages
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the knowing or willful theft of mail or packages from intended recipients, making the offense a felony punishable by up to five years in prison. It also requires the Maryland court system to notify the United States Postmaster General of convictions involving the theft or unauthorized opening of items delivered by the United States Postal Service and requires defendants to pay the associated administrative costs.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents and businesses receiving mail and packages, the United States Postal Service, private delivery service companies, and individuals convicted of mail or package theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Judiciary estimates a potential one-time expenditure of $256,700 in FY 2027 to develop an automated notification interface with the USPS, although costs could be lower if a manual system is used and offset by administrative fees paid by defendants. General fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may increase minimally as mail theft cases shift from local to state correctional facilities due to the new felony classification. State and local fine revenues may decrease minimally as cases shift from District Court to circuit courts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the court notify the United States Postmaster General of certain convictions and requires defendants to pay associated administrative costs. The fiscal note identifies a significant potential expenditure of approximately $256,700 for the Judiciary to develop an automated notification system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense for mail and package theft with a penalty of up to 5 years of imprisonment. This will likely increase the population in state correctional facilities and increase the workload for the Division of Parole and Probation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office will be responsible for defending indigent individuals charged with the new felony offense. The shift from misdemeanor general theft to a specialized felony offense may increase the resource intensity of defense cases.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal law violations and enforcing state statutes, including the new theft and mail-opening prohibitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office coordinates state public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement and victim services. New criminal statutes and changes to sentencing policy directly relate to their mission of reducing crime and recidivism.
If juveniles are involved in the theft of mail or packages, they would fall under the jurisdiction of the Department of Juvenile Services for supervision, assessment, and treatment.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in all criminal appeals. The creation of a new felony offense and the requirement for post-conviction notifications may lead to legal challenges or appeals requiring their representation.

The bill has potential significant fiscal impacts on the state budget, specifically for the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, which DBM would need to oversee during the budget development and execution process.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to the responsibilities of the Department of Human Services as representative payee and fiduciary for certain children committed to the custody of the Department; requiring the Department to use certain benefits in a manner that is in the best interest of the child including using the benefits for services for certain special needs; and requiring The Secretary to establish and maintain a foster youth savings program to conserve additional resources to assist youth in transitioning to independence.
Title: Department of Human Services - Benefits for Children in Custody - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) to screen children in its custody for eligibility for federal benefits such as Social Security and Veterans Affairs benefits. It mandates that DHS attempt to identify appropriate representative payees for these children and, beginning July 1, 2027, requires DHS to conserve all such federal benefits for the child's future use rather than using them to reimburse the State for the cost of the child's care. Additionally, the bill directs DHS to establish a foster youth savings program, subject to available funding, and provide transition and benefit information to foster youth starting at age 16.
stakeholders: Children in the care and custody of the Department of Human Services, foster youth, and the Department of Human Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, DHS general fund expenditures increase by $70,800 in FY 2027 for personnel and by $739,100 in FY 2028 for administrative and IT system updates. Federal fund revenues increase by an estimated $263,000 annually starting in FY 2028 due to administrative reimbursements. Special fund revenues available to DHS to cover care costs will decrease because approximately $557,735 in federal benefits previously used for reimbursement must now be conserved for the children.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the care and custody of foster children, DHS is the lead entity tasked with implementing the bill's requirements, including identifying representative payees, determining benefit eligibility, conserving federal benefits, and establishing the foster youth savings program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires DHS to consult and cooperate with the child's attorney throughout the process of identifying representative payees, appealing benefit denials, and providing annual accountings. OPD attorneys frequently provide legal representation for children in the foster care system.

The bill mandates judicial involvement by allowing beneficiaries who are at least 18 years old to request that the court authorize the use of benefits for unmet needs, requiring the court to make best-interest determinations.

The fiscal note indicates significant general fund expenditure increases and a reduction in special fund revenues (cost-of-care reimbursements), requiring DBM's oversight regarding budget development and fiscal planning for the department.

The fiscal note highlights that implementation will require one-time updates to the Child, Juvenile, and Adult Management System (CJAMS) to track federal benefits, which relates to the state's IT infrastructure and strategy.
The OAG provides legal counsel to DHS and may be involved in advising the agency on compliance with federal fiduciary standards and the regulatory changes required by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy initiatives; this bill impacts state-wide policy regarding child welfare and the management of federal aid for vulnerable youth.

Synopsis: Establishing a provisional social work license through which an individual issued a provisional social work license may receive a full license; and requiring the Board, beginning in 2027, to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the number of provisional licenses issued, the number of provisional license holders who obtained full licensure, and any recommendations for improving the program and the program's impact on the health care workforce.
Title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Provisional License to Practice Social Work - Established
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 227

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a provisional social work license for applicants who have completed the education and experience requirements for bachelor or master social work but have not yet passed the required examination. The license allows individuals to practice under the supervision of a board-approved social worker for a period of 12 to 24 months while they prepare for the exam.
responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Applicants for bachelor and master social work licenses and board-approved social work supervisors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund expenditures increase by $64,900 in FY 2027 to hire an administrator to manage the new licensing category. Expenditures are expected to increase annually thereafter, reaching $85,400 by FY 2031. Special fund revenues will increase by an indeterminate amount as the board is required by the bill to set provisional license fees at a level sufficient to cover these administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners (BSWE) is a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This department is directly responsible for overseeing the implementation of the new provisional licensing category, adopting necessary regulations, and managing the fiscal impact on the board's special funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners, which is the primary entity tasked with executing this bill's requirements, falls under this category of state entities authorized to address specific regulatory issues.

As the state's primary social service provider, DHS employs a significant number of social workers. Changes to the licensing pipeline, specifically the creation of a provisional license, directly impact their workforce recruitment and the legal practice status of their personnel.

Several USM institutions offer accredited bachelor's and master's programs in social work. This bill directly affects the transition from graduation to employment for their students and the requirements for supervised practice.

As a designated public urban research university with social work programs, Morgan State's graduates will be impacted by the creation of this provisional license as they enter the professional workforce.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and boards, including the Board of Social Work Examiners. They will likely be involved in reviewing the new regulations mandated by the bill and representing the board in any legal challenges.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. Licensing disputes or disciplinary actions related to the new provisional social work licenses would fall under their jurisdiction for independent review.

The bill addresses a healthcare workforce shortage by creating a path to provisional licensure. This aligns with the GWDB's mission to develop innovative workforce solutions and coordinate partnerships to improve economic mobility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs social workers within correctional facilities and for parole/probation services. This bill affects the hiring pipeline for social work positions within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD utilizes social workers for parental defense and other social services. Changes to social work licensing categories impact their staffing and the professional certification of their employees.

The bill explicitly mentions the Social Work Licensure Compact and clarifies that provisional license holders do not qualify for a multistate license under the compact, which is an interstate agreement Maryland joined.

DBM oversees state personnel and fiscal efficiency. While the board is special-funded, DBM is responsible for the overall personnel policies and budget supervision that may be affected by the need for new staff at BSWE.

As an emergency bill requiring the Governor's approval and involving the appointment of the board members who will implement it, the Governor's Office maintains executive oversight over the policy change.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim January 13 as Korean American Day; and requiring the proclamation to urge educational and cultural organizations to observe Korean American Day properly with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities.
Title: Korean American Day
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/17 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 13 as Korean American Day and urges educational and cultural organizations to observe the day with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities.
stakeholders: Korean Americans, educational organizations, cultural organizations, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no effect on State or local finances. Commemorating Korean American Day does not require any specific expenditure or generate revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 13 as Korean American Day.
The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records, including executive orders and proclamations issued by the Governor.

This office oversees ethnic and cultural commissions and serves as the primary unit for community engagement, making it highly relevant to the promotion and observation of a day dedicated to Korean American heritage.
The Lieutenant Governor represents the state at ceremonial functions and chairs advisory councils, often participating in the types of programs and ceremonies urged by the proclamation.

The bill requires the Governor to urge educational organizations to observe the day; as the oversight body for the state's public education system, this agency would be involved in responding to such a proclamation.

The bill requires the Governor to urge cultural organizations to observe the day; the Department of Commerce oversees the state's tourism, film, and arts programs, which align with these cultural observation goals.

Synopsis: Requiring each health occupations board to allow an applicant seeking license or certificate renewal to receive continuing education credits for completing a certain human trafficking awareness training program, conduct outreach to make individuals regulated by the board aware of human trafficking awareness training options, and adopt certain regulations related to continuing education credits for a certain human trafficking awareness training program by January 1, 2027; establishing requirements for the training program; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Human Trafficking Awareness Training
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 205

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland health occupations boards to grant continuing education credits to applicants for license or certificate renewal who complete an approved human trafficking awareness training program. The Maryland Department of Health must approve the training program, which must be provided free of charge and cover topics including indicators of human trafficking, trauma-informed care, and reporting protocols.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards
stakeholders: Licensed and certified health care practitioners, health occupations boards, and human trafficking survivors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Health and the health occupations boards can implement the training approval, outreach, and regulatory requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for approving the human trafficking awareness training program. Additionally, the bill mandates that each health occupations board, which are units under MDH, adopt regulations, conduct outreach, and allow continuing education credits for the training.

The bill explicitly names the University of Maryland SAFE Center for Human Trafficking Survivors as an example of a local university program that MDH must collaborate with to approve the training program. Institutions within the University System of Maryland will likely serve as key partners in developing or providing the curriculum.

As a public institution with health and social work programs, Morgan State University falls under the bill's definition of a 'local university' that may be consulted or collaborate with MDH in the approval and development of the training program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force (MHTTF) to approve the training program. The MHTTF is an advisory body within this category that coordinates statewide efforts to combat human trafficking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including human trafficking prevention, and often provides support or leadership for the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force mentioned in the bill.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees the public and private institutions of higher education (local universities) that are required to collaborate with MDH on the training program's approval.
The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the various health occupations boards as they draft and adopt the regulations required by the bill.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and its boards. The Governor also signed this bill into law and is responsible for overall executive policy regarding human trafficking.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health, rather than the Behavioral Health Administration and the Medical Care Programs Administration, to conduct a certain rate-setting study by June 30, 2028; establishing the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization in the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies for certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers; etc.
Title: Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization - Workgroup Establishment and Study
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 219

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a cost-driven rate-setting study for community-based behavioral health services by June 30, 2028. It also establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies for behavioral health clinics, outpatient centers, and independent providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Community behavioral health providers (including certified community behavioral health clinics and outpatient mental health centers), independent outpatient providers, direct care staff, and individuals receiving behavioral health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $392,000 in FY 2027 and $356,100 in FY 2028. Specifically, Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $181,700 in FY 2027 and $158,500 in FY 2028 for staff to conduct the rate study. Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $210,300 in FY 2027 and $197,600 in FY 2028 for contractual staff and services to support the workgroup. There is no impact on state revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily tasks the Department of Health (MDH) with conducting an independent cost-driven, rate-setting study for behavioral health services and implementing the recommendations of the new workgroup. It also requires MDH to designate a technical liaison to work with the Maryland Health Care Commission.

The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC). MHCC is responsible for staffing the workgroup, providing analytical support and technical assistance to MDH, and submitting interim and annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, which falls under this collective category of temporary bodies authorized by the General Assembly to address specific government policy issues.

The bill requires multiple reports to be submitted to the Governor regarding the progress of the rate-setting study and the impact of the payment system. As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies (MDH and MHCC) implementing this policy.

The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general and special fund expenditures for contractual staff and services. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and managing state personnel resources associated with these new positions.

As the primary legal representative for the state, the OAG would likely provide counsel to MDH and MHCC regarding the implementation of new reimbursement methodologies and the drafting of required regulations.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with disabilities, many of whom utilize community-based behavioral health services. Rate modernization impacts the availability and quality of services for this population.

Modernizing behavioral health reimbursement methodologies and provider rates can have significant implications for the broader insurance market and consumer protection, which are regulated by the MIA.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits and performance evaluations. They would be responsible for eventually auditing the expenditures and performance of MDH and MHCC in executing the requirements of this bill.

The bill specifically requires the workgroup to analyze geographic variations in the cost of providing outpatient behavioral health services, which directly impacts the economic viability of providers in Maryland's rural counties.

Synopsis: Requiring a motor vehicle to be at least 30 years old to be eligible for registration as a historic vehicle and at least 40 years old to be eligible for registration as a street rod vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Historic Motor Vehicles and Street Rod Vehicles - Minimum Age
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/27 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum age requirements for vehicles to be registered as historic or street rod motor vehicles. Specifically, it changes the eligibility for a Class L (historic) vehicle from a fixed 1999-or-earlier model year to a requirement that the vehicle be at least 30 years old. It also increases the minimum age for a Class N (street rod) vehicle from 25 years to at least 40 years old.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (specifically the Motor Vehicle Administration)
stakeholders: Owners of older motor vehicles (historic and street rods) and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues (including the Transportation Trust Fund) are estimated to increase annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 (starting with an estimated $300,000 in FY 2027) as fewer vehicles qualify for lower-cost historic registrations. However, revenues are projected to decrease beginning in FY 2030 (by approximately $109,000) and continue decreasing in subsequent years as the rolling age requirement allows more vehicles to qualify compared to the current static 1999 model year limit. Emergency medical services surcharge revenues will follow a similar pattern of initial increase followed by decrease. Local fiscal impact is expected to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and manages the state budget, which will reflect the revenue changes in the Transportation Trust Fund and Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors state revenue collection, including the registration fees and surcharges impacted by this bill.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and investments, including the Transportation Trust Fund, which is impacted by the bill's changes to registration revenue.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Motor Vehicle Administration and Department of Transportation regarding the implementation of the revised transportation statutes.
DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning; it monitors the fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund and local grants.
The bill impacts the Maryland Emergency Management System Operations Fund, which supports emergency response and is funded by registration surcharges affected by this bill.
The bill changes eligibility for historic and street rod vehicle status, which grants exemptions from state emission controls and inspections overseen by MDE.
