bill_summary: The bill establishes the framework for Maryland to appoint and oversee a delegation to a federal amendments convention called under Article V of the U.S. Constitution. It requires the General Assembly to appoint seven commissioners and a three-member advisory committee, providing for commissioner qualifications, oaths of office, compensation, and strict protocols for voting and media communication during a convention.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly and the Advisory Committee Oversight of Delegation to Amendments Convention
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland General Assembly, appointed convention commissioners, and the general public of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures would increase by at least $396,500 for commissioner salaries and expenses if a convention is convened, with additional potential costs for advisory committee staff. However, because it is unknown if or when a convention will be triggered by two-thirds of the states, a reliable total estimate is not feasible. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the creation of two specific bodies: a delegation of seven commissioners to represent Maryland at an Article V convention and a three-member advisory committee to oversee and monitor the delegation's activities.

The Attorney General is explicitly authorized under the bill to request a determination from the advisory committee on whether a commissioner has exceeded the scope of their authority and must be notified by the committee if a commissioner is removed for cause.

The bill requires that copies of each commissioner's written oath and credentials be filed with the Secretary of State, who serves as the principal custodian of official state records and commissions.

The bill specifies that commissioners are to receive compensation and expense allowances equivalent to members of the House of Delegates. As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for processing these payments and managing the associated payroll.

As the agency responsible for budget development and supervision, the Department of Budget and Management is impacted by the 'potentially significant' increase in general fund expenditures identified in the fiscal note to cover commissioner salaries and advisory committee staffing.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the theft of mail or packages delivered or left to be collected by the U.S. Postal Service or a delivery service company; requiring the Central Collection Unit to report certain overdue restitution to certain consumer reporting agencies; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a felony and is subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years.
Title: Criminal Law - Theft - Mail and Packages (Porch Piracy Act of 2026)

bill_summary: The Porch Piracy Act of 2026 prohibits the theft of mail or packages delivered by the U.S. Postal Service or private delivery services, establishing the crime as a felony with a maximum penalty of five years in prison. The bill mandates that courts order restitution or return of the property and requires the Central Collection Unit to report overdue restitution for these offenses to consumer reporting agencies.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and the Central Collection Unit
stakeholders: Maryland residents who receive packages, package delivery companies, consumer reporting agencies, and individuals convicted of package theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note identifies a minimal increase in State general fund expenditures as the offense moves from a misdemeanor under general theft laws to a felony under this bill, shifting some inmates from local to State facilities at an estimated cost of 5838 dollars per individual per month. General fund revenues and local finances are expected to see minimal decreases due to shifts in court jurisdictions and incarceration locations. No specific total dollar estimate is available beyond per-inmate cost data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense, which the fiscal note indicates will increase State expenditures as individuals are committed to State correctional facilities rather than local ones. Furthermore, the 'Division' (Division of Parole and Probation) within DPSCS is explicitly tasked with referring overdue restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Juvenile Services to refer overdue restitution accounts related to this new offense to the Central Collection Unit and coordinate with victims regarding settlements.

The bill mandates that the court order restoration or restitution as a condition of sentencing for the new felony. It also shifts jurisdiction for many mail theft cases from the District Court to the Circuit Court.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies that the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with this new felony offense, potentially increasing their workload.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is housed within DBM, is specifically required by the bill to report overdue restitution from these offenses to consumer reporting agencies. DBM is also cited as an information source in the fiscal note.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police will be responsible for enforcing this new criminal law and investigating reported thefts of mail and packages.

The bill references and reformats the existing mechanism where the Central Collection Unit certifies restitution obligors to the Comptroller for income tax refund interception, which will now include debts from the new felony.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reformats the provision allowing the Central Collection Unit to certify restitution obligors to the Agency for prize interception, which will apply to the new class of restitution established by the bill.
As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG may be involved in legal guidance regarding the implementation of the new felony statute and representing the state in subsequent appeals.

bill_summary: The Porch Piracy Act of 2026 creates a specific felony offense for stealing mail or packages delivered by the United States Postal Service or private delivery companies. For first and second offenses, the court must order restitution or the return of the property. For a third or subsequent conviction, the law mandates at least six months of imprisonment, a fine of up to $1,500, and permits the court to require substance use disorder treatment.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, delivery service companies such as USPS and private carriers, and individuals charged with package theft
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. While it establishes a felony for mail theft and sets a fine of up to $1,500 for repeat offenders, it is expected to primarily shift cases from District Court to circuit courts without significantly increasing overall costs or revenue. The behavior is largely covered under existing general theft statutes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense and mandates specific court-ordered restitution or restoration for first/second offenses, and potential imprisonment for third offenses, directly impacting court operations and sentencing procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency providing legal representation to indigent defendants, the creation of a new felony for 'porch piracy' will directly increase caseloads and require defense in criminal proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes mandatory minimum incarceration for repeat offenders and would involve the Division of Parole and Probation for supervising individuals and potentially monitoring court-ordered treatment.

The bill authorizes courts to order evaluation and treatment for substance use disorders as a condition of sentencing for repeat offenders, which falls under the regulatory and service oversight of the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy; the creation of a new category of felony theft aligns with their policy development and interagency collaboration mission.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws and investigating reports of theft, including the newly defined porch piracy offenses.
The OAG represents the state in criminal appeals and provides legal counsel to state agencies on the interpretation of new criminal laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

Synopsis: Authorizing certain members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive credit for certain military service if the member receives military service credit in another retirement system; and prohibiting an individual from receiving credit more than one time.

bill_summary: This bill allows members or vested former members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) who serve or served as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive up to five years of credit for military service, even if they already receive retirement benefits for that same service from another system (such as a military pension).
stakeholders: Helicopter pilots in State law enforcement aviation units who are members or former members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) and have prior military service.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is expected to have no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because it applies to a very limited number of individuals. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances, as the bill pertains specifically to State employees within the LEOPS system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) is responsible for the administration and management of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes LEOPS. The agency would be directly tasked with processing applications for military service credit, verifying eligibility, and adjusting retirement allowances for the helicopter pilots specified in the bill.

The Maryland State Police operates the state's primary Law Enforcement Aviation Command. The helicopter pilots employed in this unit are members of LEOPS and are the primary intended beneficiaries of the expanded eligibility for military service credit.

The Department of Natural Resources oversees the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are members of LEOPS. Any Natural Resources Police officers assigned as helicopter pilots in an aviation unit would be directly impacted by the bill's changes to military service credit eligibility.

As the central personnel agency for the state, the Department of Budget and Management oversees employee benefits and policies. It also monitors the fiscal impact of pension system changes on state contributions and liabilities.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Retirement Agency and the Maryland State Police. The office would be involved in interpreting the application of the bill and ensuring that the credit expansion complies with existing state and federal law.

Synopsis: Altering the exemption from the State transfer tax for instruments of writing that transfer improved residential real property to certain first-time home buyers.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill exempts first-time Maryland home buyers from the State transfer tax when purchasing improved residential real property to be used as a principal residence, replacing the existing reduced tax rate of 0.25%.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: First-time Maryland home buyers, sellers of residential real property, and local governments that receive land preservation funding.
fiscal_impact_summary: State transfer tax revenues are projected to decrease by approximately 20,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027. This revenue loss will result in a commensurate reduction in special fund expenditures for various land preservation and recreation programs, including Program Open Space, the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund, and the Rural Legacy Program. Local governments will also see a decrease in state funding for local land preservation efforts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency manages Program Open Space, the Rural Legacy Program, and the Heritage Conservation Fund, which collectively receive approximately 82% of State transfer tax revenues; the bill's projected $20 million revenue reduction will significantly decrease funding for these critical land preservation programs.

The agency oversees the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund, which receives a statutory allocation of 17.05% of State transfer tax revenues; the bill will result in a notable reduction in available funds for preserving the state's farmland.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Clerks of the Circuit Court, who are the primary entities responsible for recording deeds and collecting the State transfer tax; the bill changes the tax rate and the documentation requirements for first-time home buyer exemptions.

As the state's principal tax collector and chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for enforcing tax laws and overseeing the collection of state revenues, including the State transfer tax.

The agency's mission to promote homeownership for Maryland residents is directly supported by this bill, which provides a full State transfer tax exemption to lower the financial barrier for first-time home buyers.

The agency oversees the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority, which receives a portion of Program Open Space funds derived from transfer tax revenue; the bill's impact on total revenues will affect funding for heritage areas.

As the principal fiscal agency for the state, DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and budget execution; the bill's $20 million annual revenue loss requires long-term fiscal planning and adjustment of special fund expenditures.

The Governor's Office proposes the annual state budget and oversees the executive branch; the bill's significant impact on special fund revenues for land preservation and agricultural programs affects the Governor's fiscal and environmental policy priorities.

The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of state funds and manages the distribution of revenues; the agency is responsible for receiving and distributing transfer tax receipts to the various mandated special funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This quasi-public corporation facilitates rural land preservation and supports agricultural industries, which are programs funded in part by the transfer tax revenues that will be reduced under this bill.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates efforts to protect the Chesapeake Bay and preserve farmland; the reduction in transfer tax revenue directly impacts the fiscal resources available for the initiative's conservation goals.
The Council advocates for rural interests, including agriculture and natural resource stewardship, which are impacted by the fiscal reduction in land preservation funding resulting from this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, for a taxable year beginning after June 30, 2026, but before July 1, 2028, an increase of the assessed value of residential real property in Baltimore County except under certain circumstances; requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to retain an independent third party to study and make certain recommendations regarding the residential real property assessment practices and methodology of the Department; requiring the Department to report, on or before December 1, 2027, the results of the study; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a temporary moratorium on assessment increases for residential real property in Baltimore County for taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026, and before July 1, 2028. It prohibits increases in assessed value unless specific events occur, such as a change in zoning, property use, or improvements exceeding $100,000. Additionally, the bill requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to hire an independent third party to conduct a study on its assessment methodology and report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Residential property owners in Baltimore County, the Baltimore County government, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a decrease in property tax revenues for both the State and Baltimore County due to the moratorium on residential assessment increases. Furthermore, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation will incur expenditures to contract an independent third party for the required study and report. As the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates for these impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to report the findings and recommendations of its assessment practice study, as well as its implementation actions, directly to the Governor.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees the state's fiscal health and must approve the procurement contract for the mandated assessment study.
The Treasurer manages state funds and bond debt service, which are impacted by property tax revenues, and serves on the Board of Public Works to approve the procurement of the required study.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state executive agencies and would advise the Department of Assessments and Taxation on the implementation of the moratorium and the legal parameters of the mandated study.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and would manage the funding and fiscal impact related to hiring a third-party consultant for the assessment study.
DGS functions as the state's central procurement authority and would oversee the selection and contracting process for the independent third party required to conduct the study.
The Board of Public Works must oversee and approve the significant state expenditure and contract required to retain an independent third party for the residential real property assessment study.
GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies to enhance government efficiency and would likely oversee the implementation of the study's recommendations for improving assessment practices and methodology.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, the Tax Court will be directly affected by the outcome of the assessment methodology study and any legal challenges arising from the moratorium.

The board provides administrative review for property tax disputes; the moratorium on assessment increases in Baltimore County directly impacts the cases and valuations adjudicated by its local jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the theft of mail or packages delivered or left to be collected by the United States Postal Service or a delivery service; providing for the disposition of interest on unpaid restitution in certain cases involving the theft of mail or packages; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a felony and is subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years.

bill_summary: The Porch Piracy Act of 2026 prohibits the knowing or willful theft of mail or packages delivered by or left for collection by the United States Postal Service or a commercial delivery service. Violators are guilty of a felony and subject to up to five years of imprisonment. The bill requires the court to order the defendant to restore the stolen property or pay restitution, and it stipulates that interest accrued on overdue restitution payments be split equally between the victim and the court.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, delivery service companies, law enforcement, the state court system, and individuals convicted of theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures will increase minimally due to incarceration costs for the new felony offense, with the average cost per incarcerated individual estimated at $5,838 per month. State and local revenues are expected to decrease minimally as cases shift from misdemeanor theft (which includes fines) to the new felony mail theft charge (which does not include a specific fine). These revenue decreases may be partially offset by the court's receipt of 50% of the interest collected on overdue restitution payments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony theft offense, which shifts cases from the District Court to the Circuit Courts. It also explicitly requires that 50% of any interest accrued on overdue restitution for this specific crime be distributed to 'the court,' creating a direct fiscal and administrative impact on the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

The bill text specifically amends Section 11-616 of the Criminal Procedure Article, which directly governs how the Department of Juvenile Services handles and refers overdue restitution accounts for collection.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note explicitly identifies an impact on OPD, noting that the creation of a new felony offense for actions previously charged as misdemeanors will require increased legal effort and potential additional staffing to represent indigent defendants.

The bill's restitution enforcement mechanism involves certifying obligors to the Comptroller for income tax refund interception. The Comptroller also handles unclaimed money from judgments of restitution that are distributed to the State Victims of Crime Fund.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating criminal violations of the state's theft laws, including the newly created 'porch piracy' felony.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically utilizes the Agency's authority to intercept lottery and video lottery prize payouts to satisfy overdue restitution judgments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

Synopsis: Requiring that a carrier's internal grievance process provide for human review of grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring carriers to report certain information on grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring a carrier to provide a model review process under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Artificial Intelligence - Grievance Process and Reporting (AI Health Insurance Accountability Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to provide for a human review of any adverse decisions or grievances resulting from the use of artificial intelligence, algorithms, or software tools. It mandates quarterly reporting to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner regarding the use of such tools, including the number of decisions overturned and demographic data of the members involved. Furthermore, if AI-driven adverse decisions result in a high frequency of grievances, the carrier must perform a model review process. The bill establishes standards for AI use in utilization reviews, prohibiting determinations based solely on group datasets and ensuring that these tools do not replace healthcare providers or cause harm to enrollees.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health maintenance organizations (HMOs), nonprofit health service plans, dental plan organizations, pharmacy benefits managers, healthcare providers, and insured Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in state expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration to oversee the new reporting requirements and model review processes. Health insurance carriers will likely face increased administrative and operational costs due to the human review mandate and the complexity of the required quarterly reports. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulator responsible for overseeing the health insurance carriers subject to this bill. The Insurance Commissioner is tasked with receiving quarterly reports, compiling annual summaries, determining the percentage thresholds for model reviews of AI tools, and enforcing compliance through audits and examinations.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) co-regulates various aspects of health policy and HMOs. The bill specifically references the Secretary of Health's reporting requirements under the Health – General Article, and the regulations regarding adverse decisions directly impact the delivery of healthcare services overseen by MDH.

The bill requires carriers to report grievance data aggregated by whether the policy was purchased on the Health Benefit Exchange, which is the marketplace administered by this agency. Changes to AI-driven decision-making and human review processes will directly affect the plans offered through the Exchange.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for health system planning and improving access to care. The implementation of AI in utilization reviews and the potential for increased grievances or denials directly relate to the commission's mission of ensuring accountability and transparency in health services.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and is responsible for enforcing consumer protection laws. The use of AI in insurance determinations and the legal requirements for human review and non-discrimination are significant areas for legal oversight and consumer advocacy.

The bill explicitly prohibits AI tools from resulting in 'unfair discrimination' and requires reporting of grievance outcomes aggregated by race and gender. The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary agency for enforcing anti-discrimination laws and investigating complaints of bias.

The Governor's Office receives the mandatory annual summary reports compiled by the Insurance Commissioner regarding carrier activities, AI-driven adverse decisions, and grievance outcomes. The office also oversees the executive branch agencies implementing these regulations.

As the agency responsible for managing the State Employee Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM has a fiscal interest in the regulatory requirements and grievance processes of health insurance carriers that provide services to state employees and their families.

The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) oversees the state's strategic approach to technology, including AI governance and data standards. The regulatory framework for inspecting and auditing AI models used by private carriers aligns with DoIT's role in cybersecurity and information technology policy.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. If the Maryland Insurance Administration takes enforcement action against a carrier for non-compliance with the new AI grievance and reporting requirements, the carrier may appeal those decisions through the OAH.

The Health Services Cost Review Commission regulates hospital rates and quality outcomes. AI-driven adverse decisions and service denials by carriers can have a significant impact on hospital revenues, patient length-of-stay, and the financial stability of the state's all-payer system.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of recycling to exclude certain chemical conversion processes, pyrolysis, hydropyrolysis, methanolysis, gasification, enzymatic breakdown, or similar processes as determined by the Department of the Environment; and prohibiting a person from building in the State a facility that converts plastic to fuel or feedstock through a chemical conversion process.
Title: Recycling - Prohibition on the Chemical Conversion of Plastic
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of recycling to exclude specific chemical conversion processes, including pyrolysis, hydropyrolysis, methanolysis, gasification, and enzymatic breakdown. Additionally, it prohibits the construction of facilities in Maryland that convert plastic into fuel or feedstock using these chemical conversion processes.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, the plastic recycling industry, facility developers, and local governments responsible for solid waste management.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not affected. There is no immediate effect on local government finances or small businesses, although the bill restricts future options for plastic waste management and commercial activity in chemical conversion.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for enforcing recycling and solid waste laws. The bill specifically tasks MDE with determining which 'similar chemical conversion processes' are prohibited and authorizes the agency to adopt implementing regulations.

The Maryland Environmental Service (MES) provides operational environmental services, including solid waste and recycling management. As an agency that assists local governments with waste infrastructure, the prohibition on these chemical conversion facilities directly impacts their future project options and operational strategies.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for state agencies, including MDE. They would be responsible for providing counsel on the interpretation of the new prohibitions and defending MDE's regulatory determinations in court.

The bill prohibits the conversion of plastic to fuel through processes like gasification and pyrolysis. This affects the Maryland Energy Administration's oversight of alternative fuel sources and energy planning for the state.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by the prohibition on specific industrial facilities, which affects business attraction and retention in the recycling and chemical manufacturing sectors.

The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) provides financing and real estate development services for industrial projects. This bill limits the scope of recycling-related facilities that MEDCO can support or finance.

The Office of Administrative Hearings would adjudicate contested cases if MDE takes enforcement action against a person for building a prohibited facility or if MDE's regulatory determinations regarding 'similar processes' are challenged by a business.

The Department of Planning is involved in promoting sustainable growth and resource management. Prohibiting specific types of industrial waste processing facilities impacts land use planning and the state's long-term environmental visions.

TEDCO supports early-stage technology businesses. The prohibition of enzymatic breakdown and other chemical conversion processes for plastic recycling may affect potential investments or support for Maryland-based startups in the clean-tech and bio-tech space.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and MDE. The Governor also has final approval over the state's environmental policy priorities, which this bill directly addresses by altering the legal definition of recycling.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an employer from taking certain discriminatory employment actions against a fire and rescue public safety employee based on the employee's use of medical cannabis, subject to certain conditions; and requiring an employer to report an incident of a fire and rescue public safety employee reporting for work while impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis
Status: In the Senate - Favorable Report by Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits employers from discriminating against fire and rescue public safety employees—including firefighters, emergency medical technicians, cardiac rescue technicians, and paramedics—based on their possession of a medical cannabis certification or a positive test for cannabis. While protecting employees with valid certifications, the bill allows employers to maintain policies against on-duty use or impairment and requires reporting incidents of on-duty impairment to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
stakeholders: Fire and rescue public safety employees (firefighters, EMTs, paramedics) and their employers (State, county, and municipal governments).
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights increase by $67,800 in fiscal 2027 to hire a civil rights officer to handle an anticipated increase in discrimination complaints. Annual costs are projected to reach $89,400 by fiscal 2031. State and local governments may also face indeterminate cost increases related to potential litigation and the administrative updates of human resources policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws in employment. This bill creates a new protected status regarding medical cannabis use for specific public safety employees, and the fiscal note explicitly details a $67,800 expenditure increase for MCCR to handle the resulting increase in complaints.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that if a fire and rescue public safety employee reports to work while impaired by cannabis, the employer must report the incident to the State Emergency Medical Services Board, which is overseen and supported by MIEMSS.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and benefits. DBM noted fiscal and operational impacts regarding the State's role as an employer of fire and rescue personnel and the challenges of managing impairment policies.

The bill explicitly names the 'State Airport Authority' as an employer subject to these rules. The MAA owns and operates BWI and Martin State Airport, which employ fire and rescue personnel covered by the bill's protections.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration. The bill's specific inclusion of airport-based fire and rescue personnel makes MDOT a relevant employing agency.

The bill's protections are predicated on the 'written certification' and status as a 'qualifying patient' within the medical cannabis program, which is regulated and overseen by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

The Maryland State Police employs paramedics and emergency medical technicians, particularly within its Aviation Command. As a state agency employing individuals defined as fire and rescue public safety employees, MSP is impacted as an employer.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and will be responsible for advising them on the intersection of this state law and federal drug-free workplace requirements, as well as defending agencies in potential litigation mentioned in the fiscal note.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. Disputes regarding employment discrimination or professional reports to the EMS Board could result in hearings before an Administrative Law Judge.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies affected by this policy shift and is responsible for the final approval of the legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to authorize an eligible fund manager to receive, use, and retain a certain management fee; and authorizing the Department to set an annual cap on the cumulative amount of certain management fees an eligible fund manager may receive.
Title: Economic Development - Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Accounts - Management Fees (Small Business Increased Access to Capital Act)
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 391

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill allows the Maryland Department of Commerce to authorize fund managers of the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account to collect a management fee ranging from 1.5% to 3% of the total principal of each loan made. This fee is intended to cover administrative and lending-related expenses and is paid out of the account's existing funds.
stakeholders: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses; eligible fund managers including local economic development corporations and private investment firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect the total funding for the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA). However, it allows for the diversion of funds from lending to management fees. The fiscal note estimates that approximately 600,000 could be diverted as management fees annually based on an account funding level of 20,000,000. State expenditures for the Department of Commerce may increase for oversight, while local economic development entities serving as fund managers may see an increase in fee revenue, offset by a decrease in available loan capital.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA), authorizing eligible fund managers to receive management fees, and setting annual caps on those fees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors socioeconomic procurement programs and supports the exact demographic (small, minority, and women-owned businesses) targeted by the SMWOBA fund modified by this bill.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning, which includes the management and oversight of special funds like SMWOBA.
The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, overseeing the distribution of state revenues such as the video lottery proceeds that fund SMWOBA.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state's funds and acts as a custodian for state deposits; they have oversight interest in the fiscal integrity of the SMWOBA special fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Commerce and would likely be involved in drafting or reviewing the regulations and agreements related to the new management fee structures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The SMWOBA fund is primarily sourced from a percentage of gross video lottery terminal proceeds regulated and collected by this agency.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Commerce, and is responsible for the final approval of the annual state budget and policy initiatives like the SERVE Act that might interact with economic mobility.
OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies; they would eventually audit the Department of Commerce's adherence to the management fee limits established by this bill.
As a quasi-governmental entity with significant financial and investment experience, MEDCO could potentially serve as an 'eligible fund manager' authorized to receive the fees described in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to agricultural and rural businesses and could potentially qualify as an eligible fund manager under the criteria set by the Department of Commerce.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to adopt regulations related to the construction of a generating station that is co-located with a data center but is not interconnected with the electric transmission system or electric distribution system.
Title: Maryland Co-Location Energy Innovation and Reliability Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: The Maryland Co-Location Energy Innovation and Reliability Act requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to adopt regulations for generating stations that are co-located with data centers but not interconnected with the electric transmission or distribution system. These generating stations are to be treated as independent resources exempt from retail electric customer laws, state-mandated distribution fees, and Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS) obligations, provided they maintain backup power, cybersecurity safeguards, and submit annual performance reports.
stakeholders: Data center developers, power generation facility owners, the Public Service Commission, and Maryland electric utility ratepayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and related agencies can adopt the required regulations using existing budgeted resources. While the total fiscal impact is indeterminate, it could be significant; new construction of generating stations and data centers prompted by the bill would likely increase State and local tax revenues through economic activity. However, the specific effect on electricity rates and the potential conflict with the Next Generation Energy Act of 2025 make the long-term financial impact uncertain.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the PSC to adopt regulations for generating stations co-located with data centers and oversees the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) application process and annual reporting for these facilities.

As the advocate for residential utility consumers, the OPC is impacted by provisions that exempt off-grid generating stations from distribution fees and Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS) obligations, which may affect broader ratepayer costs.
DNR is a key participant in the CPCN process through its Power Plant Research Program, which evaluates the impact of new generating stations on the state's natural resources.
The MEA advises the Governor on energy policy and planning; the bill requires applicants to demonstrate that their off-grid generating stations contribute to the state's energy goals.
MDE is responsible for regulating environmental impacts and air quality permits for generating stations. The bill also requires reporting on the environmental impact of these stations to the PSC.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the PSC and would be involved in the development and legal review of the new regulations mandated by the bill.
The agency promotes economic development and business attraction; data center development is a major economic sector that is significantly impacted by energy reliability and regulatory costs.
The fiscal note indicates that the construction and operation of these facilities could have significant impacts on state and local revenues, which are collected and managed by the Comptroller.
The Governor's Office coordinates executive branch policy initiatives; this bill relates to broader state priorities regarding energy innovation, reliability, and economic infrastructure.

Synopsis: Updating certain provisions of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future that refer to "behavioral health" to be inclusive of "student well-being and human flourishing"; and amending the purposes, membership, and duties of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports to include the furtherance of student well-being and human flourishing.
Title: Education - Behavioral Health and Student Well-Being and Human Flourishing (Maryland Student Well-Being and Flourishing Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Student Well-Being and Flourishing Act updates the Blueprint for Maryland's Future to include 'student well-being and human flourishing' alongside behavioral health services. It defines well-being across eight dimensions (social, environmental, physical, emotional, spiritual, occupational, intellectual, and financial) and expands the mission and membership of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports to include promoting these dimensions through school-based services and extracurricular programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports and the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local school systems, and community-based behavioral health and support providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill specifies mandated annual appropriations for the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, including $70,000,000 in fiscal year 2026 and $100,000,000 in fiscal year 2027 and each year thereafter. This funding is intended to support holistic behavioral health and student well-being through grants to community partnerships and reimbursement for technical assistance. The bill text outlines these specific funding requirements as part of the implementation of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for Maryland's public education system, MSDE is responsible for implementing the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, which this bill amends. MSDE must coordinate per-pupil funding, require annual training for certificated school personnel on student well-being, and collaborate with other agencies to establish data-sharing processes and goals for student flourishing.

The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports, which are central to the bill's implementation, reside within the Department of Health. The bill also involves the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) for provider reimbursements and coordinates with local health departments.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Education to collaborate with the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to establish shared goals, data collection processes, and methods to leverage funding for student well-being and flourishing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill substantially amends the membership, duties, and reporting requirements of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports, which is an executive body tasked with developing the statewide framework for student behavioral health and well-being.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports, and this bill adds a new requirement for the Governor to appoint an individual with specific expertise in student well-being and human flourishing.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and execution. The bill mandates specific annual appropriations to the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, increasing to $100 million annually by fiscal year 2027.
The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, which is used for grants and reimbursements related to student well-being programs.
The bill requires a representative from local departments of social services, which are part of DHS, to serve on the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports.

The bill involves evaluation of reimbursement systems for commercial insurance participation and differences in commercial insurance payments for students, areas regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The bill identifies the National Center for School Mental Health at the University of Maryland, Baltimore (a USM institution) as a provider of technical assistance and permits the Fund to be used for reimbursements to the Center.

As the legal counsel for state agencies, the OAG would be involved in reviewing the new regulations and collaborative agreements required by the expansion of behavioral health definitions to include 'human flourishing.'
The bill's focus on the 'human flourishing' and well-being of students aligns with the GOC's mission to improve access to health services and support networks for Maryland's children.

Synopsis: Providing an addition modification under the Maryland income tax for the gain from the sale or exchange of certain small business stock excluded from federal gross income and a certain amount of fines, penalties, and trade or business expenses; providing certain modifications to the federal adjusted gross income of an individual or federal taxable income of a corporation for Maryland income tax purposes relating to certain deductions under the federal income tax for the depreciation of certain property; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Addition Modifications - Business Stock Gains, Fines, Penalties, and Bonus Depreciation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes Maryland income tax addition modifications for gains from the sale of qualified small business stock and for business-related fines, penalties, or restitution payments that exceed $50,000. It also repeals the current exemption for manufacturing entities regarding federal bonus depreciation and enhanced expensing allowances, effectively decoupling these businesses from certain federal tax benefits for state income tax purposes.
stakeholders: Maryland individual and corporate taxpayers, specifically manufacturing entities, investors in qualified small business stock, and businesses paying significant legal fines or restitution.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is estimated to increase total State revenues by $37.3 million in FY 2027, with $32.6 million specifically allocated to the general fund. Local government revenues are projected to increase by approximately $11.4 million. These revenue increases are driven by the removal of the manufacturing entity exemption for bonus depreciation and the new add-backs for small business stock gains. The Maryland Comptroller's Office will incur approximately $200,000 in one-time administrative expenses for implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing and administering the income tax addition modifications mandated by this bill, including one-time programming costs noted in the fiscal note.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes. The new tax addition modifications introduced by this bill are likely to result in appeals that the Court would need to adjudicate.
DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and long-term fiscal planning. This bill significantly impacts state revenues, increasing general fund revenues by over $30 million annually.
The bill has a direct fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), increasing its revenues by an estimated $3.9 million in FY 2027.
The bill increases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund (HEIF) by an estimated $0.8 million in FY 2027.

The bill removes tax conformity for bonus depreciation and expensing allowances specifically for manufacturing entities, which are a key part of the state's economic development and business retention strategy overseen by this agency.
The bill impacts the taxes of businesses in the agricultural sector, specifically those qualifying as small businesses or manufacturing entities.
The Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds. The bill increases overall state revenue across several funds (General Fund, TTF, HEIF) which the Treasurer oversees.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, and would represent the state in any legal challenges or appeals resulting from the new tax modifications.
The bill increases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund, which supports the institutions within the University System.
The bill increases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund, which provides financial support to the university.
The bill increases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund, which provides financial support to the college.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the tax treatment of gains from Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS), which is relevant to the small business community and policy efforts to encourage investment in such businesses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill introduces tax modifications related to the reporting of fines and penalties on IRS Form 1098-F, which overlaps with the office's interest in public safety and criminal justice policy.

Synopsis: Providing that the contents of a certain intercepted communication and evidence derived from the communication may be received in evidence in a certain proceeding under certain circumstances.
Title: Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance - Intercepted Communications - Admissibility of Evidence
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland District and Circuit courts to admit intercepted wire, oral, or electronic communications and derived evidence into criminal or civil proceedings under specific conditions, even if the interception violates Maryland's Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance Act. These conditions require the evidence to be a material fact, more probative than other procurable evidence, not conducted by Maryland law enforcement, and in the interest of justice, provided that advance notice is given to the adverse party.
stakeholders: Litigants in criminal and civil cases, legal counsel, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters evidentiary standards and court procedures for admitting intercepted communications in both criminal and civil trials within the Maryland District and Circuit Court systems.

As the state's chief legal representative in civil and criminal appeals and trial proceedings, the OAG will be directly impacted by changes to the rules of evidence and admissibility regarding intercepted communications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal and juvenile proceedings; changes to the admissibility of intercepted communications will significantly impact their defense strategies and the evidence used in their cases.

The OSP investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of state officials; the expanded admissibility of non-law enforcement intercepted communications may be utilized as evidence in their court proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy, the GOCPP is impacted by shifts in evidentiary rules that affect the prosecution and adjudication of crimes in Maryland.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the MSP is responsible for the overall enforcement and compliance standards of the State's Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance Act, which this bill significantly modifies.

Synopsis: Altering certain requirements of the career ladder for educators to increase the required percentage of working time a teacher on level one, two, or three of the career ladder must spend teaching in the classroom from 60% to 80%.
Title: Public Schools - Career Ladder - Teacher Classroom Teaching Time
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum amount of time that teachers on levels one, two, or three of the educator career ladder must spend teaching in the classroom from 60% to 80% of their total working time. The remaining 20% of their working time is reserved for other activities such as professional learning, tutoring students, and improving instruction.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education, local boards of education, and the Accountability and Implementation Board
stakeholders: Public school teachers on career ladder levels one, two, and three; local school systems; and public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State finances or State aid formulas. At the local level, school system personnel expenditures may decrease if the increased classroom time requirements reduce the necessity for additional educator hires. While Frederick County Public Schools projected a potential cost of approximately 16300000 dollars annually to hire additional support staff (Deans of Students and Instruction) due to the change, the Department of Legislative Services suggests that local school systems can likely manage the adjustment with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for the oversight of the public education system, including setting educational policies, certifying educators, and developing guidance for the implementation of the career ladder and teaching time requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), which is explicitly mentioned as the body responsible for reviewing pilot results and approving local school system career ladder plans that include classroom teaching time allocations.

The bill significantly alters the working time and conditions for public school teachers, which directly impacts collective bargaining agreements. The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is responsible for overseeing labor relations and resolving disputes for local public school system personnel.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including the implementation of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, of which the career ladder and teaching time requirements are central components.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education, MSDE, and other state agencies regarding the interpretation and implementation of education laws.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is involved in long-term fiscal planning and education revenue estimation related to the Blueprint's funding.

The bill may lead local school systems to hire fewer educators due to increased classroom teaching time. The Maryland State Retirement Agency manages the pension system for these teachers, and changes in the workforce size impact retirement funding and liabilities.

The Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center tracks student performance and workforce outcomes, including data on the educator workforce, which would be affected by changes to career ladder requirements.

Synopsis: Establishing the Aging Resilience Fund to be used to carry out the mission of the Department of Aging including personnel, partnership development, and any programs, services, or activities within the Department; requiring interest earnings of the Fund to be credited to the Fund; and requiring the Secretary to annually report by January 1 to certain committees of the General Assembly on the total amount in the Fund, the total number of deposits, including amounts and sources, and the amounts and purposes of the expenditures from the Fund.
Title: Department of Aging - Aging Resilience Fund - Establishment
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 15

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA). The fund is intended to support the department's mission by financing programs, services, and administrative activities, including personnel and partnership development. It is funded through investment earnings, departmental fees, and other contributions, and is designed to supplement rather than replace existing state appropriations.
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, their families, caregivers, and local area agencies on aging.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in an indeterminate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Aging anticipates that initial investments into the fund will be modest and expects to manage the fund using existing budgeted resources. Additionally, local area agencies on aging may see an increase in revenues and expenditures if funds become available for their programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund, which the Secretary of Aging is directly responsible for administering to support the department's mission, programs, and services.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Aging Resilience Fund separately and to invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Aging Resilience Fund, and the Comptroller is the state's principal officer for managing revenue and accounting for such funds.

The bill creates a new special, nonlapsing fund that interacts with the State budget and contains provisions restricting the Governor's authority to reduce appropriations to the fund, which falls under DBM's fiscal oversight.

The Secretary of Aging is a member of the Governor's Executive Council, and the bill limits the Governor's constitutional and statutory authority to reduce appropriations for this specific fund in the State budget.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Aging and will likely assist in the legal framework and regulatory implementation of the newly created special fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a certain covenant or agreement that ensures affordable pricing of the dwelling; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Building Homes Act
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 698

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to establish a property tax credit for dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a covenant or legally binding agreement of at least 20 years that ensures affordable pricing and income/equity restrictions. The credit amount may be up to the difference between the tax on the full assessed value of the dwelling and the tax on the portion of the value for which the homeowner is responsible on their first mortgage.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Homeowners of affordable dwellings, nonprofit housing organizations (such as Habitat for Humanity), and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the property tax credit is granted by local governments. The exact financial impact is indeterminate as the number of eligible dwellings and their specific selling prices cannot be reliably estimated. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary state entity responsible for affordable housing and homeownership. The bill creates a local tax credit for affordable dwellings subject to nonprofit mortgages and pricing covenants, which directly aligns with the department's core mission to ensure residents have access to safe and secure affordable housing.

The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill represents a key policy initiative regarding affordable housing and economic mobility and was signed into law by the Governor.

The PTAAB is the independent agency responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and the application of property tax credits. This bill creates a new credit that will be subject to their administrative review process for any disputes.

The Tax Court adjudicates appeals from the PTAAB. Any disputes regarding the calculation or eligibility of this new affordable housing property tax credit could reach this quasi-judicial body for final administrative review.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They provide guidance on the legal interpretation of the property covenants and Tax-Property Article changes introduced by this bill.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors all tax legislation and its impact on the state's broader fiscal health and revenue reporting, even when the taxes are local in nature.

DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning. While the fiscal impact is primary local, the agency monitors changes in local revenue capacities that can affect state budget allocations and fiscal coordination.

The team's mission includes enhancing economic mobility and reducing poverty. This bill provides an evidence-based tool for local governments to support affordable homeownership through nonprofit partnerships, aligning with the team's policy incubation goals.

The office focuses on reducing child poverty and improving economic opportunities for families. Stable and affordable housing is a fundamental component of reducing family poverty and promoting child well-being.

The AOC was identified as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis and oversees the judicial branch, which handles the recording of the mortgages and covenants required to qualify for the tax credit.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration and the Secretary of the Environment to establish an application process and requirements to certify facilities to conduct tests or inspections under the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program; and establishing a certificate for certain facilities to conduct tests or inspections under the Program.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program - Modifications
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) by requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration and the Department of the Environment to certify private facilities to conduct emissions tests and inspections. It transitions the program from a centralized, contractor-run system to a decentralized system of certified private inspection facilities, allowing these facilities to charge fees to cover the cost of testing.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration and the Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Maryland motor vehicle owners in designated emissions inspection areas and private businesses seeking certification as emissions inspection facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances until fiscal 2036. Beginning in fiscal 2036, Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are projected to decrease by tens of millions of dollars annually as inspection fees shift from the State to private facilities. For context, VEIP generated approximately $32,000,000 in fiscal 2025 and is projected to generate $67,100,000 by fiscal 2031. TTF expenditures may increase due to the need for additional personnel to oversee and monitor the new private testing facilities. No direct local government impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT is responsible for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF). The fiscal note indicates that TTF revenues will likely decrease by tens of millions of dollars annually due to the shift from state-collected fees to private facility charges.

MVA is the primary implementing agency specifically named in the bill. It is charged with establishing the application process and requirements for certifying private facilities, issuing certificates, and adopting new regulations for the decentralized Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program.

The Secretary of the Environment is a co-lead with MVA in establishing certification requirements and regulations for emissions testing. The agency oversees environmental laws related to air quality, making the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program a core part of its mission.

DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning. The bill's projected decrease in TTF revenues by tens of millions of dollars and the potential need for additional monitoring personnel directly impact the state's budget and long-term fiscal planning.

OAG provides legal counsel to MVA and MDE. They will be involved in drafting the complex new regulatory framework for certifying private emissions facilities and defending the agencies in potential litigation or enforcement actions.

OAH adjudicates administrative disputes for state agencies. The bill creates a new certification process; if MVA or MDE denies, suspends, or revokes a facility's certificate, those legal challenges would likely be heard by an OAH Administrative Law Judge.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is relevant to significant changes in state revenue streams. The transition of VEIP fees from state-collected revenue to private facility fees affects the state's financial reporting and oversight.

The bill facilitates a transition to a decentralized model that allows private businesses to become certified emissions inspection facilities, creating a potential economic opportunity for small business repair shops across Maryland.

Synopsis: Requiring a teacher preparation program to include certain training in English language learner-related teacher competencies and include English language learner-related teacher competencies in other courses throughout the curriculum; and requiring a teacher preparation program to include a certain course in teaching English language learners beginning in the 2028-2029 academic year.
Title: Education - Teacher Preparation Programs - English Language Learner Teacher Competency Requirements
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill requires teacher preparation programs to include training in English language learner (ELL) teacher competencies and to integrate these competencies throughout the curriculum. Additionally, starting in the 2028-2029 academic year, these programs must require at least one three-credit course specifically focused on teaching English language learners.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), and the State Board and the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board
stakeholders: Higher education institutions with teacher preparation programs, faculty, prospective teachers, English language learner (ELL) students and their families, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local public higher education institutions may incur operational and fiscal impacts related to curriculum revisions and the development of a required three-credit course on teaching English language learners. While most institutions are expected to absorb these costs within existing resources, some smaller institutions might face higher expenses for faculty or course development. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission can absorb administrative duties within existing resources. Specific dollar estimates were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing teacher preparation programs, providing technical assistance, developing feedback systems, and setting recruitment goals. The State Board within the department is also tasked with adopting regulations to implement the bill.

The commission is the state's regulatory board for colleges and universities. It is specifically required to consult with the Department of Education to establish teacher recruitment and retention goals and oversees the approval of the institutions that must implement the new curriculum.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for higher education institutions, this agency oversees the policies and financial standards for the public and private colleges that must implement the mandated English language learner curriculum.

The University System of Maryland governs several public four-year institutions (such as Towson, Salisbury, and UMES) that operate approved teacher preparation programs. These institutions are directly impacted by the requirement to redesign curricula and add a new three-credit course.

As a public university with an approved teacher preparation program, Morgan State is directly impacted by the bill's requirements to incorporate new competencies and a standalone course into its educational curriculum.
As a public honors college that offers a Master of Arts in Teaching and teacher preparation, St. Mary's is directly impacted by the requirement to update its curriculum and instructional components.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board to adopt regulations in consultation with other bodies to carry out the act's provisions.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is relevant because the bill may result in operational and fiscal impacts for state-funded higher education institutions, potentially requiring faculty adjustments or curriculum mapping expenses.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission and would likely be involved in the development and legal review of the regulations required by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementation (MSDE and MHEC) and appoints the members of the boards tasked with adopting the new regulations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Medical Assistance Program from applying a prior authorization requirement in certain circumstances to and from applying a step therapy or fail-first protocol for a prescription drug used to treat an adult enrollee's diagnosis of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, major depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, or a medication-induced movement disorder associated with the treatment of serious mental illness.
