stakeholders: Electronic device manufacturers, electronic device retailers, Maryland households, small businesses (10 or fewer employees), public sector agencies, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by at least $67,800 in FY 2027 for MDE to hire staff for oversight and enforcement, while special fund revenues increase by at least $146,000 through manufacturer registration fees. Future fee revenue is expected to be adjusted by MDE to cover administrative costs. Local governments are expected to benefit from the bill through financial compensation for collection efforts and free electronics recycling for local agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary implementing and regulatory agency for the Electronic Device Producer Responsibility Program. It is responsible for reviewing plans, managing registrations and fees, staffing the Advisory Council, and enforcing compliance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Electronic Device Producer Responsibility Advisory Council, a new body within the executive branch tasked with advising the Department of the Environment on the program's implementation and administration.

The Maryland Environmental Service is explicitly designated for a seat on the new Advisory Council and currently manages electronic waste collection sites on behalf of several counties, meaning its operations may be indirectly impacted by the new producer responsibility system.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the personnel and budget oversight regarding the new natural resources planner and environmental compliance specialist positions identified in the fiscal note as necessary for the program.

The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities and handles the procurement and disposal of state property, including electronic devices, making it a relevant 'covered entity' and an information source for the fiscal note.

As the state's lead IT agency, DoIT is impacted by the management of electronic waste and is considered a 'covered entity' under the bill, which entitles it to free electronic device recycling services.
The State Treasurer's Office is responsible for holding, investing, and distributing the funds within the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive the manufacturer registration and review fees.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to MDE, oversees enforcement actions, and handles legal matters related to the bill's provisions on state antitrust law exemptions and trade secret protections.
The Comptroller's Office is responsible for accounting for the revenues and expenditures of the State Recycling Trust Fund, which receives fees and penalties under this program.

As a large state educational entity and 'covered entity' under the bill, the University System of Maryland is impacted by changes to electronic device disposal and was a primary information source for the fiscal note.
Morgan State University is a 'covered entity' that will be able to utilize the new recycling program free of charge and was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

The bill references composting standards established by the Secretary of Agriculture and excludes agricultural equipment from the definition of covered electronic devices; the agency also houses the Rural Maryland Council.
The Maryland Department of Health is a 'covered entity' that generates electronic waste and was an information source for the fiscal impact analysis.

The Department of Transportation is a 'covered entity' under the bill; additionally, the bill's definitions exclude electronic components used in motor vehicles, which is relevant to MDOT's oversight.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Secretary of the Environment, who is responsible for the program's administration and the appointment of many Advisory Council members.

The Rural Maryland Council is relevant due to the bill's specific requirements for rural county representation on the Advisory Council and the mandate to ensure collection site convenience for rural residents.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the governing body of a county or municipality from enacting a local law or ordinance prohibiting the offering of certain residential property as a short-term rental by an operator solely because the operator is a lessee or sublessee of the property; authorizing the governing body of a county or municipality to enact a local law or ordinance prohibiting the operator of a short-term rental who is a lessee or sublessee of the property from operating more than one short-term rental within the county or municipality; etc.
Title: Real Property - Short-Term Rentals
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: The bill prohibits local governments from enacting laws that ban short-term rentals solely because the operator is a lessee or sublessee. It permits local jurisdictions to limit these operators to one short-term rental property and specifies that property owners may still prohibit or restrict their tenants from using properties as short-term rentals.
responsible_party: Local governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities
stakeholders: Short-term rental operators (specifically lessees and sublessees), residential property owners, and local government authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new legal standards for short-term rental operations and limits local government authority over real property, which may lead to litigation or administrative appeals that the Maryland Judicial Branch must adjudicate.

As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the collection of sales and use taxes and other revenues. Short-term rentals are taxable lodging activities, and the bill affects the legal framework for who can operate them, impacting the potential tax base.

The Department of Commerce oversees tourism in Maryland. Short-term rentals are a critical component of the state's tourism infrastructure and accommodations market, which are vital to the agency's economic development goals.

DHCD is responsible for ensuring access to safe, affordable housing and supporting community revitalization. The regulation of short-term rentals directly impacts housing availability, affordability, and the residential rental market.

Short-term rentals are a significant land-use and sustainable growth issue. The agency's role in promoting sustainable development and providing policy guidance to local governments makes the regulation of these properties relevant to its work.
The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill involves state preemption of local laws and impacts broader economic and housing policy priorities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. This bill involves the interpretation of real property law and the preemption of local ordinances, which may requires legal guidance or defense of the state's authority.

Synopsis: Establishing the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Maryland Department of Labor; requiring that investment earnings be credited to the General Fund of the State; requiring the Secretary of Labor to annually calculate costs; authorizing the Department to set fees; requiring providers of travel services to file with the Department proof of professional liability and errors and omissions liability insurance in the amount of at least $1,000,000; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Travel Services - Special Fund, Fees, and Surety Requirement (Don't You Worry (Wurie) Act)
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 611

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

bill_summary: This bill requires sellers of travel services and independent travel agents to register annually with the Maryland Department of Labor and provide proof of professional liability and errors and omissions insurance of at least $1,000,000. It establishes the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund to cover the costs of administering and enforcing these requirements, initially funded by a $300 annual filing fee.
stakeholders: Sellers of travel services, independent travel agents, and consumers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, special fund revenues will increase by at least $99,000 annually starting in FY 2027 from registration fees. State expenditures are projected at $106,500 in FY 2027 for staffing and one-time start-up costs, requiring a $5,500 general fund contribution to cover a first-year revenue gap. Fees may be increased annually by up to 12.5% to ensure the special fund covers administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to pay all fees collected from travel service registrations to the Comptroller, who is then responsible for distributing those fees into the newly created Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund.

As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the oversight of the new executive director position and the fiscal management of the special and general fund expenditures required to implement the new regulatory framework.

The Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency. It is responsible for establishing the new registration fund, setting and collecting fees, enforcing insurance requirements for sellers of travel, and adopting necessary regulations.

The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and investments. The bill specifies that investment earnings from the new Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund must be credited to the General Fund, which the Treasurer oversees.

The Department of Labor is tasked with enforcing the new subtitle. Contested cases resulting from enforcement actions, such as registration denials or penalties, would likely be adjudicated by Administrative Law Judges within the OAH.
The bill and fiscal note explicitly state that the new Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits to ensure fiscal accountability.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor. It will likely be involved in drafting the required regulations and providing legal support for the enforcement of the new insurance requirements.

Synopsis: Prohibiting behavioral health care providers from using artificial intelligence to provide behavioral health care to a patient; authorizing a behavioral health care provider to use a system that employs artificial intelligence in performing administrative support tasks under certain circumstances; and requiring a behavioral health care provider to obtain certain informed consent from patients if the provider uses a certain system that employs artificial intelligence under certain circumstances.
Title: Health Occupations - Behavioral Health Care Providers - Use of Artificial Intelligence
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: House Bill 995 prohibits behavioral health care providers from using artificial intelligence (AI) to perform clinical functions such as assessment, diagnosis, treatment, or therapeutic communication. Providers are permitted to use AI for administrative support tasks, such as scheduling and billing, provided they ensure data security, enter into confidentiality agreements with AI vendors, provide notice to patients, and independently verify AI-generated output. Additionally, providers must obtain informed consent if an AI system could materially affect clinical decision-making or patient-facing services.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and health occupation boards
stakeholders: Licensed behavioral health care providers, patients receiving behavioral health services, and health occupation licensing boards
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can monitor compliance with the bill using existing budgeted resources. While violations are subject to disciplinary action, including potential civil penalties, such revenues are not expected to materially affect State special funds. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for the health occupation boards that license and certify behavioral health care providers. MDH will be responsible for monitoring compliance and the respective boards will handle disciplinary actions for violations of the AI restrictions.

The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) is the principal agency for the state's AI strategy and cybersecurity. The bill references definitions of AI used in procurement and the fiscal note highlights DoIT's role in governing AI policy and assessing high-risk AI systems.

The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases involving state agencies. It would be responsible for adjudicating appeals from health occupation boards regarding disciplinary actions taken against providers for violating the bill's AI provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office administers mandatory arbitration for medical malpractice claims. If the use of AI by a behavioral health care provider leads to professional negligence or damages, the claim would likely pass through this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the health occupation boards and the Department of Health. It also oversees consumer protection, which may be relevant given the bill's informed consent and patient notification requirements.

As a regulatory agency within MDH focused on health system planning, informed decision-making, and accountability, this commission is relevant to the integration of new technologies like AI into the healthcare landscape.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates state policy initiatives. The fiscal note highlights the Governor's role in establishing the AI Subcabinet and overall AI governance strategy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Governor's AI Subcabinet, which is explicitly mentioned in the fiscal note as being responsible for adopting policies regarding high-risk AI and overseeing state AI strategies.

The fiscal note appendix mentions the establishment of an AI Evidence Clinic Pilot Program within the AOC to provide expertise on electronic evidence that may have been altered by AI, which could include behavioral health records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees correctional facilities where behavioral health care is provided to incarcerated individuals. Staff or contracted providers at these facilities must comply with the bill's AI restrictions.
The department provides behavioral health care to youth within the juvenile justice system. Providers operating under DJS authority would be subject to the bill's limitations on AI use.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public school systems where behavioral health services are provided. The fiscal note also mentions MSDE's own internal initiatives regarding AI use in schools.

The bill's provisions regarding administrative support tasks include billing insurers. The MIA regulates the insurance market and would be interested in how AI restrictions and informed consent impact healthcare liability and claims processing.

This team tests and pilots novel initiatives for the Governor's priorities. Since the bill regulates a frontier technology in the critical area of health services, the team may be involved in analyzing the impact on service delivery.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to notify a person who files a charter document if the Department does not accept the document; requiring the Department to accept a corrected charter document under a certain circumstance; authorizing certain governing bodies of certain corporations to take certain actions without a meeting of the governing body subject to certain conditions;  repealing the authority of certain persons to maintain a suit in a State court; etc.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Revisions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 313

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's laws for corporations and partnerships. It requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to notify filers of rejected documents and allows a 30-day window for corrections to retain the original filing date. It permits open-end investment companies to take board actions with majority written consent rather than unanimous consent. The bill also simplifies corporate actions taken under federal bankruptcy orders by removing stockholder approval requirements, repeals criminal penalties for officers of unregistered foreign corporations, and establishes default rules for the adoption and amendment of partnership agreements.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, open-end investment companies, foreign corporations, partnerships, and limited partnerships
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no anticipated material effect on state revenues and no impact on local government finances. The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor fine of up to $1,000 for officers of unregistered foreign corporations while maintaining a $200 corporate penalty.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), which is the primary agency tasked with implementing the document notification and rejection protocols established by the bill.
As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller relies on accurate corporate and partnership registration data from SDAT to enforce tax laws and manage revenue collection.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including SDAT, and would be responsible for interpreting the new statutory requirements regarding charter documents and corporate governance changes.
DBM oversees the budget and personnel of SDAT; while the fiscal note suggests SDAT can implement the bill with existing resources, DBM monitors the execution of these administrative changes.

As the state's economic development agency, Commerce is impacted by changes to corporate law that affect the business climate, specifically governance revisions for investment companies and the ease of business formation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note specifically identifies a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, as the bill provides greater certainty in the formation and resubmission of business entity charter documents.

The bill impacts the judicial branch by altering the standing of foreign corporations to maintain suits in state courts and by providing procedures for state entities to carry out federal bankruptcy court orders.
The MIA regulates insurance companies, many of which are organized as corporations or investment-related entities that may be affected by the revised governance and filing provisions.

The Archives is the central depository for permanent government records, including corporate charter documents filed with the state; changes to filing and acceptance dates affect these historical records.

The Tax Court hears appeals from final decisions of SDAT; while often related to assessments, changes to the legal status and registration requirements of business entities provide critical context for their review.

OLA is responsible for auditing SDAT's fiscal and compliance operations, including ensuring the agency follows the new statutory mandates for notifying filers of rejections and correctly backdating resubmitted documents.

The Secretary of State serves as a custodian of state records and manages various business-related registrations; revisions to the treatment of foreign corporations and partnership agreements overlap with their administrative functions.

Synopsis: Modifying the method by which the Commissioner of Labor and Industry determines a prevailing wage rate; and requiring the Commissioner to vacate a certain prevailing wage rate under certain circumstances.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - Prevailing Wage Rate - Calculation
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Government, Labor, and Elections; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Commissioner of Labor and Industry from surveying or using wage data of employees directly employed by investor-owned gas, electric, or combined utility companies when determining prevailing wage rates. Additionally, it requires the Commissioner to vacate and recalculate a prevailing wage rate if a petition for review shows that prohibited wage data was used in the calculation.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Construction workers, investor-owned utility companies, contractors, subcontractors, and state and local government agencies managing public works projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. Any potential adjustments to prevailing wage rates are expected to be negligible and will not significantly affect the costs of public works projects. The Maryland Department of Labor is expected to implement the bill using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, who is part of the Department of Labor, with modifying the method for calculating prevailing wage rates and handling petitions to vacate and recalculate those rates.
As the state's primary agency for construction and procurement, DGS manages public works projects that are subject to the prevailing wage laws affected by this bill.
MDOT oversees extensive highway and transit construction projects (through SHA and MTA) that are major users of prevailing wage classifications affected by this legislation.
The IAC oversees public school construction projects, which represent a significant portion of the projects subject to the state's prevailing wage requirements.

The bill relies on definitions for investor-owned gas and electric companies from the Public Utilities Article, which the PSC administers, and the bill affects how wages for projects involving utility infrastructure are determined.
The Maryland Stadium Authority manages its own prevailing wage program for sports and school construction projects, often using wage rates determined by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry.

Although technically exempt from state prevailing wage law, USM often voluntarily complies with prevailing wage requirements for large construction contracts, making the calculation changes relevant to their project costs.
Similar to USM, Morgan State University is exempt but typically follows prevailing wage requirements for its capital construction projects.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and would be involved in defending or interpreting the new wage calculation methodology and the petition review process.
The Board of Public Works approves the significant state procurement and construction contracts that are subject to the prevailing wage rates modified by this bill.
As a public honors college with independent status, it is mentioned in the fiscal note as an entity associated with prevailing wage law compliance for its construction projects.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class 7 micro-brewery license to the holder of a Class B-D-7 license in the 46th alcoholic beverages district, subject to a certain limitation; requiring the Board to establish a standard template for certain memoranda of understanding by January 1, 2027; authorizing certain holders of certain Class D licenses in the 46th alcoholic beverages district to apply for a 7-day sales privilege under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Baltimore City – Alcoholic Beverages – 46th Alcoholic Beverages District
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 844

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill modifies alcoholic beverage laws in Baltimore City, primarily in the 46th district. It authorizes Class 7 micro-brewery licenses for certain Class B-D-7 holders, permits license transfers between districts, and allows Class D holders to apply for a 7-day sales privilege for a $15,000 fee. It also requires the creation of standard memoranda of understanding (MOU) templates for license applicants and neighborhood associations, and extends the expiration of specific licenses for renewal or transfer.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City's 46th district, local neighborhood associations, non-profit entities, and the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. It establishes a one-time $15,000 fee for certain Class D license holders applying for a 7-day sales privilege, with revenue dedicated to the Board for MOU enforcement. Other provisions regarding license transfers and expiration extensions have minimal fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation. Additionally, the Governor appoints the members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, which is the primary entity tasked with implementing the bill's provisions.

The Comptroller's Office is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting related state revenues. This bill modifies licensing structures and establishes conditions for the consumption of donated alcohol (specifically mentioning tax remittance), which falls under the Comptroller's broader regulatory and fiscal oversight.

The OAG serves as the primary legal counsel for state agencies, including local boards of license commissioners. The bill requires the Board to establish standard templates for legal documents (MOUs) and adopt new regulatory penalties, which would involve legal review and advisory support from the OAG.

Synopsis: Authorizing the holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to manufacture, rectify, or bottle more than one brand of alcoholic beverage; and authorizing the holder to manufacture or rectify up to 31,000 gallons of product of an entity other than the holder.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 9 Limited Distillery License - Alteration
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 860

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing -see also- Breweries; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows the holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to manufacture, rectify, or bottle more than one brand of alcoholic beverage and authorizes the holder to produce up to 31,000 gallons of product per year for another brand or entity.
stakeholders: Class 9 limited distillery license holders and small distillery businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. Small businesses holding Class 9 limited distillery licenses may see a meaningful increase in revenue from contract distilling and the ability to maintain multiple brands.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's summary explicitly states that the agency is responsible for regulating the alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuel industries and collecting state revenues. This bill directly alters the Class 9 limited distillery license, which falls under the agency's primary regulatory and revenue oversight duties as described in the summary.

The bill is identified as having a meaningful impact on small business distilleries by expanding their capacity to manufacture multiple brands and providing opportunities for contract distilling. This aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission to stimulate economic growth, attract and expand businesses, and support Maryland's competitive economic position.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards. The agency would be responsible for advising the regulatory bodies on the implementation of these statutory changes to the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and ensuring the new production and branding limits are legally sound.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning July 1, 2026, the school mapping data produced with funding from the School Mapping Data Program to contain site- specific labeling for bodies of water in the 1-mile radius surrounding the school grounds.
Title: Public Schools - School Mapping Data - Radius of School Grounds
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/07 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Water -see also- Coastal Bays; Riv,Str,Lks; Wastewater; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires that all school mapping data produced with funding from the School Mapping Data Program include site-specific labeling for bodies of water located within a one-mile radius of the school grounds.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) and the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC)
stakeholders: Local school systems, public school students and staff, and local, State, and federal public safety agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's fiscal impact is indeterminate. While the labeling requirement can likely be incorporated into future school maps using existing resources from the School Mapping Data Program (which received a $3,000,000 appropriation in the fiscal 2026 budget), state general fund expenditures and local school system expenditures could increase significantly if the bill is interpreted to require the updating of existing school maps.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) administers the School Mapping Data Program, which is directly modified by this bill to include specific labeling requirements for bodies of water.

The IAC is responsible for developing the mapping standards that schools must follow to comply with the School Mapping Data Program and will need to update these standards to reflect the new requirements.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees the state's public education system and the schools impacted by these mapping requirements.
The fiscal note indicates that the Department of Information Technology works with the IAC to make data available for the creation of these school maps.
The bill has a potential fiscal impact on state general fund expenditures if additional grant funding is required to update existing maps, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing the program and is responsible for the final approval of the legislation and related budget appropriations.

Synopsis: Requiring a police officer who is on duty at a polling place to obey the authority of the State Administrator, the Deputy State Administrator, or a local election director; providing that, in a polling place, certain individuals have the authority to keep the peace and order the arrest of certain persons; requiring a local election director, while serving in a polling place, to protect certain rights of challengers and watchers; etc.
Title: Election Law - Authority at Polling Places, Early Voting Centers, and Counting Centers - Revisions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 467

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants the State Administrator of Elections, the Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors authority at polling places to maintain peace and order arrests, similar to the existing authority of election judges. It also updates regulations for the designation and conduct of accredited challengers, watchers, and canvass observers, expanding their authorized presence to early voting centers and prohibiting them from handling voting equipment.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections, Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors
stakeholders: Election officials, candidates, political parties, political committees, police officers, and registered voters serving as challengers, watchers, or observers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no effect on State finances and is not expected to directly affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for supervising and administering elections. This bill directly expands the authority of the State Administrator and Deputy State Administrator at polling places and modifies the regulation of challengers, watchers, and observers, which are core functions of the agency.

The bill explicitly requires police officers on duty at polling places to obey the orders of the State Administrator, the Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors, and provides specific legal protections for arrests made under their authority.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and election laws. The bill identifies specific actions that constitute a breach of peace or election law at polling places and grants election officials the authority to order arrests for such offenses.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and state officials. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the interpretation and implementation of the expanded authorities granted to election administrators.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the State Board of Elections. The bill alters the statutory authority of the State Administrator, a significant executive leadership position.

The bill establishes that police officers making arrests under the order of the State Administrator or local election directors are legally protected as if they were acting under a valid warrant, which impacts the legal framework for arrests that eventually enter the judicial system.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging a resident to certain housing or before receiving certain confirmations; altering the information required to be included in a certain notice or new notice; requiring that a certain notice or new notice be provided to certain residents at least a certain period of time before an involuntary discharge or transfer; establishing time requirements that apply to the discharge or transfer of a resident if a new notice of involuntary discharge or transfer is provided; etc.
Title: Nursing Facilities - Involuntary Discharge or Transfer
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 24

NarrowSubjects.Name: Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Nursing Homes -see also- AsstLiving; ContinCare; LTCare
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: This bill prohibits nursing facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging residents to temporary housing such as hotels or shelters and requires that the receiving facility confirms acceptance before a move occurs. It also updates the requirements for involuntary discharge notices to include specific contact information for advocacy organizations and establishes clear timelines for providing new notices and developing post-discharge care plans.
stakeholders: Nursing facility residents, their families and representatives, nursing facility operators, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, Maryland Legal Aid, and Disability Rights Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements can be handled with the Maryland Department of Health's existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances. The financial impact on small business nursing facilities is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary regulatory agency for nursing facilities. The bill requires the Department to prepare and provide standardized notice forms, receive copies of involuntary discharge notices, and adopt regulations to implement the safe, secure, and sustainable environment standards for post-discharge plans.

The Maryland Department of Aging oversees the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program. The bill requires that this program be included in the standardized notice provided to residents and that the Ombudsman receive a copy of every written notice of involuntary transfer or discharge.

The bill details the hearing process for residents appealing an involuntary discharge or transfer, which is conducted by Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) within the Office of Administrative Hearings. The bill specifically establishes notice requirements and timelines that are triggered by ALJ orders.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Department of Aging. They would likely be involved in drafting the required regulations and representing the agencies in matters related to the enforcement of nursing facility discharge standards.

The bill requires discharge notices to include contact information for Disability Rights Maryland for residents with intellectual or developmental disabilities or mental disorders. As the principal agency coordinating services for this population, the department is relevant to the policy goals of ensuring safe transitions for disabled residents.

Synopsis: Requiring the Anne Arundel County Board of Education and the State Board of Elections, in consultation with the State Department of Education, to establish a pilot program in the county schools to prepare students for a career as an election official.
Title: Anne Arundel County Public Schools - Election Official Career and Technical Education Pilot Program
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Ways and Means; Withdrawn

Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Anne Arundel County Board of Education and the State Board of Elections, in consultation with the Maryland State Department of Education, to establish a career and technical education pilot program in Anne Arundel County Public Schools designed to prepare students for careers as election officials.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Students in Anne Arundel County Public Schools and election administration agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Elections to establish and develop the career pilot program in partnership with the local school board to prepare students for careers as election officials.

The bill mandates that the pilot program be developed in consultation with the Department of Education, which oversees state educational standards, policies, and Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency; it would be responsible for overseeing the budget execution and any potential resource allocations required by the State Board of Elections or MSDE for this pilot.
As the body responsible for Maryland's workforce system strategy, this career-focused pilot program aligns with the board's mission to develop innovative workforce solutions and talent pipelines.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments tasked with the pilot and is responsible for proposing the state budget that would provide the necessary funding.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from manufacturing, selling, delivering, holding, or offering for sale in the State food that contains any ingredient or additive that is prohibited for use in food under regulations adopted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or any other federal law or regulation.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the manufacture, sale, or distribution of food containing certain additives, specifically brominated vegetable oil, potassium bromate, propylparaben, and Red 3, along with any other substances prohibited by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or federal law. It establishes criminal and civil penalties for violations.
stakeholders: Food manufacturers, distributors, retailers, consumers, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely handle enforcement with existing resources. Penalty revenue is not expected to be material. Local government expenditures may increase starting in fiscal 2028 if local health departments require additional staff to inspect food products in licensed food establishments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for food safety, licensing food processing plants, and enforcing the Maryland Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, which this bill directly amends. Its Center for Food Processing handles the relevant inspections and regulatory oversight.

OAG serves as the legal representative for MDH and the state, providing counsel on the implementation of these regulations and representing the state in civil and criminal enforcement actions or appeals related to violations.
The bill establishes criminal and civil penalties for violations, which will be adjudicated within the Maryland court system managed by the AOC.

MDA oversees food quality assurance and regulatory activities for the state's agricultural and seafood industries; the broad definition of food in the bill may impact products under their general oversight.

MFCA manages regional food distribution and wholesale facilities; since the bill prohibits 'holding' or 'delivering' food with specified ingredients, the businesses operating within MFCA facilities must ensure compliance.
MSDE manages school nutrition and food programs for the public education system, which must comply with state laws regarding food ingredients and safety standards.

As the agency responsible for supporting and attracting businesses, the Department of Commerce is relevant due to the impact of the ingredient prohibition on Maryland's food manufacturing and processing sector.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and budget execution; they would oversee any fiscal impacts or staffing changes required for MDH or local health departments to enforce the new food standards.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementation and coordinates the broader policy initiatives related to public health and consumer safety addressed by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Human Services, by May 1, 2028, to develop a certain form for the submission of a written report concerning suspected child abuse or neglect for cases in which the victim is currently at least 18 years old; requiring the Department to consult with certain individuals, entities, and the State's Attorney in the process of developing the form; requiring the form to include certain information including, if known, information on whether the accused individual currently has access to children; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Human Services (DHS) to develop a standardized form for mandatory reporters to use when reporting suspected child abuse or neglect in cases where the victim is now an adult. The form, which must be developed by May 1, 2028, must include information such as whether the survivor wants an investigation and if the alleged abuser currently has access to children, and it must be accompanied by a document explaining how the reported information will be used.
stakeholders: Adult survivors of child abuse and neglect, mandatory reporters (including health practitioners, police officers, educators, and human service workers), local departments of social services, law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Human Services can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for child welfare and social services, the Department of Human Services is explicitly mandated by the bill to develop the new survivor reporting form, consult with stakeholders, and make the form available to mandatory reporters.

The bill affects educators and schools, who are designated as mandatory reporters under the Family Law Article and will be required to utilize the newly developed form when reporting suspected abuse or neglect involving adult survivors.

Health practitioners and public health agencies are mandatory reporters under the bill; the Department of Health regulates these professionals and will be involved in ensuring they have access to and utilize the new reporting form.

Police officers are mandatory reporters under the statute, and the bill specifically requires the Department of Human Services to consult with law enforcement agencies during the development of the new reporting form.
The bill specifically mentions juvenile detention centers as institutions whose staff members are mandatory reporters required to follow the new reporting protocols for adult survivors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note clarifies that human service workers, who are mandatory reporters, include parole and probation officers managed by this department.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will likely provide legal counsel to the Department of Human Services regarding the form's development and its compliance with the Family Law Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety and victim services policy; the bill's focus on survivor reporting reform aligns with its mission to support victim services and develop criminal justice strategies.

bill_summary: This bill allows the Talbot County Board of Education to implement a school scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days and reduces the total number of school days below 180, provided the required 1,080 school hours are maintained. The bill also mandates that the board provide hourly employees with opportunities to make up any wages lost because of the shortened schedule.
stakeholders: Public school students, teachers, and hourly employees in Talbot County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Talbot County Board of Education to offer hourly school employees opportunities to make up lost wages resulting from a reduced number of school days. Specific dollar estimates for the state or local fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal fiscal note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's public education system, MSDE (and the State Board of Education) is directly responsible for enforcing the school attendance requirements modified by this bill. The bill specifically requires the Talbot County Board of Education to report its scheduling operations to the State Board of Education.

The bill includes a specific labor mandate requiring the county board to offer hourly employees an opportunity to make up wages lost due to scheduling changes. The PERB has jurisdiction over labor relations and disputes involving local public school system personnel.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education and the Department of Education regarding the implementation of changes to the Education Article of the Maryland Code.

Synopsis: Regulating commercial financing transactions, including by establishing requirements related to certain disclosures, calculations of annual percentage rates, terms of repayments, and other related items, and the extension of specific offers.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Small Business Truth in Lending Act, which regulates commercial financing transactions in Maryland. It requires providers of sales-based financing, factoring, and other commercial credit products to provide recipients with specific disclosures, including the annual percentage rate (APR), total finance charges, and repayment terms. The bill excludes certain entities such as banks, credit unions, and transactions exceeding $2,500,000, while authorizing the Maryland Commissioner of Financial Regulation to enforce compliance through civil penalties and investigative powers.
responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Small businesses seeking commercial financing and commercial financing providers operating within the state of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally due to civil penalty provisions of up to $2,000 per violation and $10,000 per willful violation. The Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) within the Maryland Department of Labor expects to handle implementation and enforcement with existing resources. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), which is a unit of the Maryland Department of Labor, is the primary agency responsible for implementing and enforcing the bill. The Commissioner of Financial Regulation must adopt regulations, monitor APR disclosures, investigate complaints, and impose civil penalties.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by changes to the lending environment for small businesses. The bill regulates commercial financing, which is a critical resource for the businesses the department seeks to attract and retain.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors socioeconomic procurement and connects small businesses to economic opportunities. The Small Business Truth in Lending Act directly affects the transparency and terms of financial products offered to the small, minority, and women-owned businesses that this office serves.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the Department of Labor. They will be involved in drafting or reviewing the required regulations and representing the state in any legal challenges or high-level enforcement actions resulting from the bill.

The bill's enforcement provisions may lead to increased caseloads for the judicial system, including applications for subpoena enforcement in circuit courts and judicial review of administrative penalty orders.

DBM is responsible for state personnel and budget execution. While implementation may begin with existing resources, DBM would oversee any future requests for additional staff or IT funding needed by the Department of Labor to handle the increased regulatory workload.

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill represents a significant regulatory policy change affecting the state's business climate, requiring alignment with the administration's economic priorities.

Synopsis: Authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to delay or deny a disbursement from the account of a certain individual or the account on which a certain individual is a beneficiary; requiring a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to provide certain financial records to certain entities; authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to contact certain individuals; and providing certain fiduciary institutions immunity from certain liability.

bill_summary: The Vulnerable Adult Banking Protection Act authorizes fiduciary institutions to delay or deny disbursements from the accounts of seniors (aged 65+) and vulnerable adults if financial exploitation is reasonably suspected. The bill requires institutions to notify local Adult Protective Services, law enforcement, or the State's Attorney within four business days of a disbursement request and provides for the sharing of relevant financial records. It also grants fiduciary institutions immunity from civil or administrative liability for actions taken in good faith and exercising reasonable care under these provisions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services (local Adult Protective Services agencies) and the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.
stakeholders: Seniors aged 65 and older, vulnerable adults, fiduciary institutions (including national and state banks, credit unions, and savings and loan associations), and local law enforcement and social service agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local social service agencies and law enforcement agencies are expected to manage the notification and investigation requirements within existing resources. No impact on state or local revenues is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires fiduciary institutions to notify the Adult Protective Services (APS) program in local departments of social services, which are overseen by the Department of Human Services. DHS is responsible for delivering services to vulnerable adults requiring protection from abuse and neglect.

The bill governs 'fiduciary institutions,' including those subject to the supervision of the Commissioner of the Office of Financial Regulation within the Department of Labor. The department regulates the financial institutions that are authorized to delay or deny disbursements under this act.

The bill requires fiduciary institutions to notify law enforcement agencies when they suspect financial exploitation. As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police would receive and potentially investigate these reports.

The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction to issue orders that terminate or extend the delay of disbursements. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support to the state's courts that will handle these requests.

The bill specifically targets 'eligible adults,' defined as individuals at least 65 years old. The Department of Aging is the cabinet-level agency dedicated to protecting the rights and improving the quality of life for older adults in Maryland.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the state agencies involved in implementing this bill and enforces consumer protection laws, which are relevant to the prevention of financial exploitation.

The bill applies to 'vulnerable adults' who lack the physical or mental capacity to provide for their daily needs, a population that often includes individuals with disabilities served by this department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates Maryland's public safety strategies and manages funds for victim services. The bill's focus on reporting and preventing the financial exploitation of seniors aligns with the office's mission to reduce crime and assist victims.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a clerk of the circuit court from recording an instrument that effects a change of ownership of real property from the United States to another person unless the instrument is accompanied by a Certificate of Compliance; requiring the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to review certain changes of ownership of real property and issue a Certificate of Compliance following a determination of legal compliance; etc.

bill_summary: The Land Transfer Accountability Act requires a Certificate of Compliance from the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation before a clerk of the circuit court can record a property transfer from the U.S. government to a private party. The bill also increases the State transfer tax rate from 0.5% to 2% for these specific transactions and directs the resulting revenue to Program Open Space.
responsible_party: The Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Parties involved in real property transfers from the United States government, the Office of the Attorney General, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Administrative Office of the Courts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the State transfer tax rate from 0.5% to 2% for property formerly held by the U.S. government, with the revenue from this increase dedicated to Program Open Space. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation are required to establish fees for the review and issuance of Certificates of Compliance to cover administrative costs, with those fees deposited into the General Fund. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the source text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Attorney General to review real property instruments for compliance with state and federal laws and, in collaboration with the Department of Assessments and Taxation, issue certificates of compliance.

The bill mandates that the Administrative Office of the Courts work with circuit court clerks to establish uniform statewide procedures for receiving and recording the newly required certificates of compliance.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues and is specifically directed by the bill to credit transfer tax revenue from the new 2% rate to Program Open Space.

The bill establishes a 2% transfer tax rate for certain property transfers, with the resulting revenue directed to Program Open Space, a program governed by the Natural Resources Article and managed by the Department of Natural Resources.

As the chief financial agency, the Treasurer's Office manages state funds and oversees the issuance of bonds that are secured by the State transfer tax revenue mentioned in the bill's distribution section.
The bill requires fees for certificates to be deposited into the General Fund, which DBM manages, and the agency oversees the personnel and fiscal resources required for the implementing departments.
The bill references the distribution of transfer tax revenue to the Agricultural Land Preservation Fund, which supports the department's mission of rural land preservation.
The Tax Court would have jurisdiction over appeals regarding the assessment or calculation of the new 2% transfer tax established by the bill.
The new transfer tax is based on property values determined at the date of finality; disputes regarding these valuations, which form the basis of the tax, are heard by this board.
The Board of Public Works oversees the fiscal integrity of the state and approves bond issuances, including those supported by the transfer tax revenue streams modified by this bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to adopt regulations for the review, certification, and decertification of election-supporting technology, such as electronic pollbooks and risk-limiting audit tools, and to conduct annual evaluations of such technology starting in 2027.
stakeholders: State Board of Elections, local boards of elections, and election-supporting technology vendors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $506,300 in fiscal 2027, primarily for consultants and a new technology writer/reviewer position to develop regulations and frameworks. Ongoing annual expenditures are estimated to range from $95,400 to $109,000 through fiscal 2031. The bill is not expected to affect State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill's requirements, which include adopting regulations for certifying and decertifying election-supporting technology and conducting annual evaluations of such technology.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact requiring increased general fund expenditures for a new permanent staff position and the hiring of consultants, which requires budget and personnel oversight by DBM.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG will likely be involved in drafting and reviewing the required regulations for certification and decertification processes to ensure legal sufficiency.
Since the bill focuses on the certification of technology and software, DoIT may provide technical guidance or alignment with statewide IT security and strategy standards.
The OAH may be relevant if the decertification of election-supporting technology leads to contested cases or administrative disputes between the State Board of Elections and technology vendors.

The workgroup's focus on public school students directly aligns with the department's oversight of the state's public education system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes a new temporary body (a Workgroup) to conduct studies and make policy recommendations, which falls under this collective entity.
The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing two executive branch members to the workgroup and is one of the primary recipients of the final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department is responsible for vetting and recommending candidates for the Governor's appointments to state task forces and commissions.
The Attorney General is required to appoint an advisory member to the workgroup, likely to provide legal counsel on statutory and regulatory policy recommendations.
The bill entitles workgroup members to travel reimbursement as provided in the state budget, which is overseen by the Department of Budget and Management as the state's principal fiscal agency.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to establish multidisciplinary local suicide fatality review teams. These teams are tasked with reviewing suicide deaths to identify systemic risk factors, improving coordination among prevention and crisis response entities, and developing recommendations to prevent future suicides. The bill also establishes protocols for membership, data confidentiality, and immunity from liability for team members.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and local health departments
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local health officers, law enforcement, behavioral health professionals, social service agencies, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) may increase by approximately $163,289 starting in fiscal 2027 for a data analyst and program administrator, though the Department of Legislative Services suggests these costs might be absorbed within existing resources. Local health department expenditures are estimated to increase by $30,000 to $50,000 for each jurisdiction that chooses to establish a team. Penalty provisions for confidentiality violations are not expected to materially affect finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary state agency for health policy and oversees local health departments and behavioral health authorities, both of which are mandated members of the local review teams. Additionally, the department is authorized to adopt regulations to carry out the subtitle.

The bill requires local departments of social services, which are part of DHS, to be represented on the suicide fatality review teams. The agency also coordinates child fatality review teams mentioned in the bill.
The bill requires local superintendents of schools to be represented on the local review teams, and the Department of Education oversees these local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local teams to coordinate with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, which is a state-level committee tasked with identifying suicide trends and prevention strategies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Emergency medical services providers are designated members of the local suicide fatality review teams. MIEMSS is the state agency responsible for overseeing and regulating the EMS network.
State law enforcement officers are listed as potential members of the multidisciplinary local teams. The Maryland State Police is the primary state-level law enforcement agency.
The bill contains significant legal provisions regarding confidentiality, Open Meetings Act exemptions, and immunity from liability, requiring legal counsel and interpretation from the OAG.

The bill establishes rules regarding the use of records as evidence, subpoenas, and discovery in judicial proceedings, as well as providing immunity from liability for team members, which impacts the court system.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for assessing the fiscal impact of the bill on state agencies, including the Maryland Department of Health's potential need for additional resources.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved in these review teams and coordinates the policy initiatives related to public health and suicide prevention.

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires the Prince George’s County Board of Education and the County Superintendent to provide full-time salaries and benefits to all individuals employed as one-to-one student aides beginning in the 2027-2028 school year. It mandates quarterly reporting on special education services, requires annual professional development for special education staff, and directs the Maryland State Department of Education to hire a third-party auditor to conduct a comprehensive performance and financial audit of the county's special education department for fiscal years 2021 through 2025.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of Education, Prince George’s County Superintendent, and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Students with special needs in Prince George's County Public Schools, one-to-one student aides, and special education employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a significant new spending mandate for Prince George's County by requiring full-time salaries and benefits for one-to-one student aides. The Maryland State Department of Education will incur costs to contract with a third-party auditor for a multi-year audit. Specific dollar estimates for these expenditures are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department is responsible for hiring a third-party auditor to evaluate Prince George's County Public Schools, receiving and publishing quarterly special education updates, and certifying compliance. Additionally, the State Superintendent of Schools is authorized to withhold funds from the local school system for non-compliance with the act's record production requirements.

The bill requires a comprehensive audit of special education due process filings and resolution timelines; the OAH is the independent agency responsible for adjudicating these contested cases, which includes special education disputes, via its Administrative Law Judges.

The bill mandates that one-to-one student aides in Prince George's County receive full-time salary and benefits equivalent to other employees, which directly impacts the administration of collective bargaining and labor relations for public school personnel overseen by this board.

The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for coordinating and improving the delivery of services to residents with disabilities; the bill's focus on the delivery of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and the provision of one-to-one aides for students with disabilities is a core policy focus for this agency.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts; the requirement for the Department of Education to hire a third-party auditor to conduct a performance and financial audit would involve a contract that likely requires the Board's approval.

The OLA conducts performance and fiscal compliance audits of local school systems; the scope of the third-party audit mandated by this bill regarding special education services, financial data, and staffing within Prince George's County Public Schools is highly relevant to OLA's statutory oversight role.

The audit required by the bill includes analysis of student outcomes such as graduation rates, chronic absenteeism, and discipline; the MLDS Center is the state's repository for linking and analyzing the student performance data necessary for these longitudinal evaluations.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and the State Superintendent; they would likely be involved in drafting the audit contract and providing legal guidance on the enforcement mechanisms and fund withholding provisions of the bill.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state; it would oversee the budget execution related to the Department of Education's new oversight duties and the fiscal implications of withholding state funds from the local school system.

This office utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to enhance the responsiveness of state government; the bill's requirements for transparency dashboards, objective performance thresholds, and a corrective action plan based on audit metrics align with GOPI's mission.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Education; this bill represents a significant policy initiative concerning educational accountability and equity, and involves the appointment of various reporting requirements within the executive branch.

The office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and improving access to education and health services; this bill's aim to ensure accountability and service delivery for students with special needs directly impacts the children and families supported by this agency.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a specific definition for 'danger to the life or safety of the individual or of others' in the context of involuntary admissions and emergency evaluations for mental disorders. The definition includes a substantial risk of serious bodily harm, an inability to provide for basic needs such as food or medical care, or a substantial deterioration in judgment or reasoning, regardless of whether the risk is imminent, based on recent and relevant conduct.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Individuals with mental disorders, peace officers, healthcare professionals, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $414,000 in FY 2027 for the Office of the Public Defender (OPD) to hire three attorneys and support staff to manage an estimated increase of 1,000 involuntary admission cases. These expenditures are projected to reach $553,900 by FY 2031. The Judiciary may also face an indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures due to a higher volume of emergency evaluation petitions. No significant fiscal impact is expected for Maryland Department of Health hospital facilities. Local jurisdictions may see impacts on police activities and circuit court caseloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary executive agency responsible for overseeing behavioral health services and the mental health laws amended by this bill. It is responsible for receiving and evaluating individuals for involuntary admission to state facilities and setting regulatory policy for these clinical interventions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in involuntary admission proceedings. The fiscal note indicates this bill will increase their caseload by an estimated 1,000 cases per year, requiring a significant increase in general fund expenditures to hire additional attorneys and support staff.

The Judiciary, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, processes petitions for emergency evaluations. The bill's expanded definition of 'danger' is expected to increase the volume of these petitions in both District and Circuit courts, impacting judicial and clerical workloads.

The Maryland State Police serve as peace officers who have the authority to petition for emergency evaluations. The change in the legal definition of 'danger' directly affects the standards by which state troopers assess and intervene with individuals suffering from mental disorders.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Judiciary regarding the enforcement of state laws. They will be responsible for providing guidance on the new legal threshold for involuntary admissions and representing state interests in related litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services frequently manages individuals with mental health needs within the justice system. Revisions to the criteria for involuntary admission affect the coordination of care and legal standards for justice-involved individuals requiring psychiatric intervention.

The bill explicitly applies the new definition of 'danger' to the involuntary admission of individuals to Veterans’ Administration hospitals, making this directly relevant to the department's role in assisting veterans with health benefits and advocacy.

As the principal agency for coordinating services for Marylanders with disabilities, including mental health conditions, this department is impacted by changes to legal standards that affect the rights and treatment of its target population.

The Department of Human Services manages protective services for vulnerable adults. The bill's inclusion of a person's inability to provide for basic needs (food, clothing, shelter) as a criterion for 'danger' intersects with the department's mission to assist those at risk of self-neglect due to mental impairment.

The Department of Aging advocates for older adults, who are a demographic frequently subject to emergency evaluations and involuntary admissions related to cognitive and mental health disorders. The revised standards will affect the legal protections and treatment pathways for this population.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises on public safety and criminal justice strategies. While a specific provision regarding criminal justice involvement was removed during amendments, the bill remains a significant public safety policy regarding the detention and treatment of potentially dangerous individuals.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive departments impacted by this bill, proposes the state budget that must account for the bill's fiscal impact on the Public Defender and the Judiciary, and is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

Title: Developmental Disabilities Services - Expedited Eligibility Determinations for Recently Relocated Individuals (Ralph's Act)
