bill_summary: This bill requires public and nonpublic primary and secondary schools to adopt written policies and procedures to protect the privacy of student records. Additionally, nonpublic prekindergarten programs and nonpublic primary and secondary schools must annually report incidents of alleged discrimination to the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which is then required to compile this data and submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Public and nonpublic primary and secondary schools, nonpublic prekindergarten programs, students, and parents or guardians.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. Private schools may incur some additional administrative costs to meet reporting and privacy policy requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing Maryland's public education system and nonpublic schools, the Department is responsible for receiving annual discrimination reports from nonpublic entities and submitting a compiled statewide report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Governor's Office is the recipient of the annual report from the Department of Education regarding discrimination incidents in schools and provides overall executive oversight of the implementing agencies.

The Department operates schools within its secure residential facilities for youth; as a public primary or secondary school provider, it must adopt the mandated written student privacy policies and procedures.

As a state-operated public school, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly impacted by the requirement to adopt and maintain written policies and procedures regarding the privacy and release of student records.

The bill's focus on reporting incidents of alleged discrimination based on protected classes like race, religion, and disability aligns with the Commission's core mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Student Data Privacy Council, which is tasked with reviewing best practices and making recommendations regarding student data privacy laws in Maryland.
The bill's focus on protecting student privacy and monitoring discrimination in schools directly impacts the well-being of Maryland's children, which is the primary mission of this office.

The agency serves as the central repository for student and workforce data; changes to student record privacy policies and data collection standards are relevant to its data governance and privacy mission.
The Office is responsible for auditing state agencies and local school systems to ensure compliance with laws and regulations, which would include the new student privacy policy requirements.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and other state-operated schools regarding compliance with the new privacy and reporting mandates.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Chamber of Commerce Grant Program in the Department of Social and Economic Mobility to provide grants for membership subsidies for underrepresented individuals and inter-chamber events; specifying certain application requirements for the Program; requiring Program applicants to meet certain eligibility requirements; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $100,000 for the Program.
Title: Department of Social and Economic Mobility - Maryland Chamber of Commerce Grant Program - Established (Business Networks Access Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Chamber of Commerce Grant Program within the Department of Social and Economic Mobility to provide grants to chambers of commerce for membership subsidies for underrepresented individuals and for hosting joint inter-chamber events.
responsible_party: Department of Social and Economic Mobility
stakeholders: Maryland chambers of commerce and underrepresented individuals seeking business networking opportunities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a $100,000 annual General Fund appropriation for the Maryland Chamber of Commerce Grant Program. The Department of Social and Economic Mobility will incur administrative costs to manage the application and disbursement process, while local chambers will receive grant funding to subsidize memberships and host events. A formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, so these estimates are based on the mandated appropriation included in the bill text.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds the new grant program to Section 9–4109 of the State Government Article, which falls under the statutory subtitle governing this department, making it the primary administrative home for the program.
The bill contains a mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $100,000 for the program in the state budget bill.
As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising execution, DBM must include the mandatory appropriation and oversee the fiscal management of the grant program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program provides membership subsidies for underrepresented individuals in business chambers, directly aligning with this office's mission to support minority and small business owners and promote economic inclusion.
The team is specifically charged with identifying and piloting initiatives to enhance economic mobility, which is the primary focus of the 'Business Networks Access Act'.
This office leads statewide efforts to enhance economic mobility and reduce poverty, mirroring the stated purpose of the program and its facilitating department.
As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce works closely with chambers of commerce and business networks to attract and retain businesses.
The Comptroller, as the state's chief financial officer, is responsible for the disbursement of state funds and would handle the payments for the awarded grants.

Synopsis: Requiring a child care providers in registered family child care homes and registered large family child care homes and licensees and staff of a child care center to complete training on the detection and reporting of child abuse at certain intervals.
Title: Child Care - Child Abuse and Neglect - Training Requirements
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/07 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires child care providers in registered family child care homes and staff at licensed child care centers to complete mandatory training on the detection and reporting of child abuse. The training must be completed within 90 days of registration or starting employment and must be repeated annually thereafter.
stakeholders: Child care providers, licensees, and staff of child care centers and registered family child care homes, as well as children receiving care in these facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates there is likely no state or local fiscal impact because all child care staff and providers in Maryland are already required to complete child abuse and neglect training through the Maryland State Department of Education's Basic Health and Safety training program. MSDE intends to use existing protocols and training to satisfy the bill's requirements, resulting in minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Education Article to require the State Board (MSDE) to adopt regulations for child care providers and centers regarding mandatory child abuse detection and reporting training. MSDE's Division of Early Childhood Development is responsible for the licensing and oversight of these entities.

DHS is the primary state agency responsible for child protection and investigating abuse and neglect. Additionally, the fiscal note mentions that DHS provides the free online training course for mandatory reporters that child care providers would likely use to fulfill the bill's requirements.

The bill establishes requirements that, if violated, can lead to the suspension or revocation of a child care provider's license. The OAH adjudicates contested cases and appeals involving state agency decisions, such as license revocations issued by MSDE.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Department of Education and the Department of Human Services, and would be involved in the drafting and legal review of the new regulations and any subsequent enforcement actions or litigation.

This office coordinates policy initiatives for the well-being of Maryland's children and families. Policies aimed at improving the detection and reporting of child abuse align directly with its core mission to protect vulnerable children.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary body for public safety strategy and victim services funding, this office has a policy interest in the effective detection and reporting of criminal acts such as child abuse.

Synopsis: Allowing a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain overtime compensation; and applying the Act to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025, but before January 1, 2029.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification - Overtime Compensation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes a temporary Maryland income tax subtraction modification for qualified overtime compensation received by taxpayers, aligning State law with the federal deduction created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 for tax years 2026 through 2028.
stakeholders: Maryland residents earning qualified overtime compensation and meeting specific income thresholds.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is estimated to reduce State general fund revenues by $85,200,000 in FY 2027, $88,600,000 in FY 2028, and $92,100,000 in FY 2029. Local income tax revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $51,900,000 in FY 2027, $54,000,000 in FY 2028, and $56,100,000 in FY 2029. Additionally, the Comptroller’s Office will incur a one-time general fund expenditure of $50,000 to $100,000 in FY 2027 for system programming.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and administration; the bill requires the agency to update tax systems, forms, and audit procedures to accommodate the new subtraction modification, with a specified fiscal expenditure for programming.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the state's General Fund, reducing revenues by approximately $85 million to $92 million annually, which directly affects the agency's responsibility for revenue estimation and state budget development.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which will be impacted by the significant revenue reduction resulting from the bill.
As the agency for administrative review of tax disputes, the Tax Court may see increased appeals regarding the qualification and calculation of overtime compensation for the subtraction modification.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding tax law implementation and represents the state in litigation or appeals related to the new tax subtraction.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and cash flow, which will be affected by the reduction in income tax revenue deposits into the General Fund.
The office is responsible for auditing the Comptroller’s implementation and fiscal compliance regarding the new subtraction modification.
The bill's focus on providing tax relief for overtime compensation aligns with the team's mission to identify strategies for enhancing economic mobility for Maryland families.

Synopsis: Requiring the Independent Investigations Division of the Office of the Attorney General to investigate the death of a person that occurs in connection with an interaction with federal law enforcement or federal immigration enforcement; requiring the Division to submit a certain report to the Governor and the General Assembly after conducting the investigation; and requiring the Attorney General to prosecute a certain case under certain circumstances.
Title: Office of the Attorney General - Independent Investigations Division - Federal Law Enforcement or Immigration Enforcement
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Judiciary; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires the Independent Investigations Division (IID) of the Office of the Attorney General to investigate any death or serious physical injury occurring during an interaction with federal law enforcement or federal immigration enforcement. The IID must report its findings to the Governor and General Assembly, and the Attorney General is required to prosecute the case if the investigation provides sufficient grounds to charge a federal officer with a crime.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Independent Investigations Division)
stakeholders: Federal law enforcement officers, federal immigration enforcement officers, and individuals in Maryland involved in incidents with these federal agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) estimates an annual expenditure of approximately $1,000,000 for additional personnel (three assistant Attorneys General, two investigators, and one paralegal) to handle the expanded jurisdiction. However, the Department of Legislative Services (DLS) anticipates that the OAG can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, noting that the need for permanent additional staff is speculative and can be addressed through the annual budget process if necessary. Local finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the responsibilities of the Independent Investigations Division within the Office of the Attorney General to include investigating and potentially prosecuting deaths or serious physical injuries involving federal law enforcement or immigration enforcement.
The bill requires the Independent Investigations Division to submit its findings to the Governor and involves the administration of a new investigative mandate within the executive branch.
The judicial branch, supported by the AOC, would be responsible for adjudicating any criminal cases prosecuted by the Attorney General under the new authority granted by this bill.

The Independent Investigations Division utilizes personnel detailed from the Maryland State Police to conduct its investigations; expanding the division's scope will likely increase the operational demand for MSP officers.

As the agency responsible for state personnel and fiscal oversight, DBM would manage the potential budgetary implications and staffing requests (estimated at $1 million by OAG) identified in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to conduct a study and make recommendations on the potential scope, structure and implementation of Commission oversight of broadband service and voice over Internet protocol service; and requiring the Commission to report by December 31, 2026, its findings and recommendations to the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment, the House Environment and Transportation Committee, and the General Assembly.
Title: Public Service Commission - Broadband and Voice Over Internet Protocol Service - Study
Status: In the Senate - Special Order until 4/10 (Senator Salling) Adopted

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC) to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding the potential scope, structure, and implementation of PSC oversight of broadband and Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services in the state. The study will evaluate federal preemption, potential regulatory frameworks for service reliability and emergency preparedness, implementation costs, and necessary legislative changes. The PSC must report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 31, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland broadband and Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service providers and their customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the Public Service Commission can complete the required study using existing budgeted resources. The bill does not affect State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically mandates the Public Service Commission to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding the potential scope, structure, and implementation of Commission oversight of broadband and VoIP services.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Commission. Oversight of broadband and VoIP directly impacts utility rates, service quality, and consumer advocacy within their jurisdiction.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division currently handles complaints regarding VoIP services, and the agency provides legal counsel to state commissions and enforces consumer protection laws related to telecommunications.

The department houses the Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB), which is responsible for broadband deployment and planning. The bill's focus on broadband oversight overlaps with the OSB's mission to ensure reliable and affordable connectivity.
DoIT is the principal agency for the state's information technology and telecommunications strategy and was consulted as an information source for the fiscal analysis of the bill.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that, before a certain date each year, a dog owner or keeper must apply for a license from a certain county employee; and repealing a requirement that a certain county employee issue a tag to a dog owner or keeper.
Title: Caroline County - Regulation of Animals - Dogs
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals specific state statutory requirements for dog licensing in Caroline County, such as the requirement to apply annually to the county tax collector and specific tag design mandates. Instead, it grants the Caroline County Commissioners the authority to adopt their own rules and regulations regarding the issuance of dog licenses, record-keeping, and animal control enforcement.
stakeholders: Dog owners and kennel operators in Caroline County, Caroline County animal control officers, and the Caroline County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local fiscal impact is expected to be minimal, as the bill maintains the authority of the Caroline County Commissioners to set licensing regulations and fees. The county is expected to retain its current fee structure, where registration and vaccine certification fees (typically $3.00 or $10.00) are paid to the Caroline County Humane Society.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing legislation into law and overseeing the executive branch's interaction with local government regulations.
The Office of the Attorney General reviews all legislation for legal sufficiency and provides counsel regarding the delegation of state authority to local jurisdictions.
The Department of Agriculture oversees animal health across the state and is broadly concerned with the regulation and protection of animals in rural communities.
The Department of Health oversees public health and rabies control programs, for which dog licensing is a primary enforcement and tracking mechanism.
The Department of Natural Resources regulates hunting and the use of dogs in hunting, which are specifically mentioned in the licensing requirements of this bill.
The Rural Maryland Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's rural counties, including Caroline County, and supports local governance autonomy.

Synopsis: Requiring, on or before January 1 each year, each county board of education to provide certain information to the parent or legal guardian of a student who attends a failing school; requiring that a failing school continue to be designated as a failing school until certain conditions are met; requiring that a student who is attending a failing school be provided the opportunity to attend an alternative school; establishing the Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today Program; etc.
Title: Education – Primary and Secondary Schools – Alternative School Options (Right to Learn Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Hate Crimes

bill_summary: The Right to Learn Act requires Maryland county boards of education to notify parents if their child attends a 'failing school' (one with a one-star rating for three consecutive years) and provides those students with the opportunity to transfer to an alternative school, including other public schools, nonpublic schools, or boarding schools. The bill establishes the Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Program in statute to provide 'Right to Learn' scholarships for students who choose nonpublic schools. It also mandates that local school systems pay for students to attend military boarding schools if they are determined to be violent or are subject to continuous disciplinary action.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Students in underperforming schools, students facing continuous disciplinary action, parents and legal guardians, local school systems, nonpublic schools, and military boarding schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal 2027, state general fund expenditures will increase minimally for administration, including an estimated $190,000 annual cost for scholarship application system contracts. Starting in fiscal 2028, per-pupil state and local education aid will decrease as students transfer to nonpublic schools and are removed from public school enrollment counts. The Fiscal Note estimates that local school systems will lose approximately $22,100 per student in funding for each student receiving a Right to Learn scholarship, though the overall fiscal impact is expected to be minimal due to the limited number of currently eligible schools. The bill also codifies the BOOST program, which has recently been funded at $9,000,000 annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch, proposing the state budget, and coordinating policy initiatives. This bill introduces a significant educational policy change (the Right to Learn Act) and affects the annual budget through education aid formulas.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the distribution of state revenues and education aid. The bill involves the remittance of per-pupil funds from local boards to the Department of Education, which impacts state financial administration.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Education. They would likely be involved in drafting and reviewing the regulations required by the bill for the BOOST and Right to Learn programs.

The Department of Budget and Management is the principal fiscal agency responsible for budget development and execution. The fiscal note indicates the bill will have an impact on general fund and Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund expenditures.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency. The bill tasks MSDE with administering the BOOST Program and Right to Learn scholarships, adopting necessary regulations, and managing the state accountability (star rating) system.

The Governor's Office for Children focuses on well-being and reducing child poverty. The bill's focus on providing scholarship options for students in failing schools (often in underinvested communities) aligns with this office's mission.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and procurement. Given the potential impact on education aid distribution and state scholarship funds, the Board maintains a general oversight role.

The bill facilitates students moving from public to nonpublic or military schools. Significant shifts in enrollment counts, as noted in the fiscal analysis, impact long-term facility planning and the assessment of school construction needs.

The Maryland State Innovation Team is charged with piloting novel initiatives to reduce child poverty and enhance mobility. The educational options provided by the Right to Learn Act are directly relevant to their work on evidence-based strategies for underinvested communities.

Synopsis: Requiring that money in the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund be allocated in certain amounts in fiscal years 2028 through 2032 to certain programs that reduce the impact of climate change.
Title: Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund - Mandated Uses - Climate Change Programs
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m. (Environment and Transportation)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires that the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) prioritize and allocate at least $365,000,000 annually from fiscal year 2028 through 2032 to specific programs aimed at reducing the impact of climate change. These allocations support various initiatives including incentives for electric appliance and heat pump installations, solar energy deployment, electric vehicle infrastructure, zero-emission school buses, energy efficiency in state buildings, and workforce development within the clean energy sector.
stakeholders: Maryland residents (specifically low- and moderate-income households), county boards of education, clean energy businesses and workers, and State agencies including the Departments of Environment, Education, Labor, and General Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a prioritised annual mandate of at least $365,000,000 from the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) for fiscal years 2028 through 2032. This funding is distributed across multiple agencies and initiatives: $234,000,000 to the Maryland Energy Administration for appliances, solar, and vehicles; $13,000,000 to the Department of the Environment; $45,000,000 to the State Department of Education for school facilities and electric buses; $1,000,000 to the Department of Labor for workforce development; $5,000,000 to the Department of General Services; $50,000,000 to the Maryland Clean Energy Center; and $2,000,000 to the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute. The bill also adjusts the percentage allocation of proceeds from the sale of carbon allowances within the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary administrator of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), the MEA is responsible for implementing the new $365 million annual mandate, which includes over $234 million directly allocated for MEA-run incentives and clean energy programs.
The bill mandates an annual allocation of $50 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to the Maryland Clean Energy Center to support its clean energy mission and programs.
The bill explicitly allocates $13 million annually from the SEIF to MDE for clean energy technology support, marketing, and climate change programs.
The agency is mandated to receive $45 million annually to assist school boards in reducing carbon emissions from facilities and to acquire and implement electric school buses.
The bill mandates a $5 million annual allocation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to the Department of General Services for energy efficiency initiatives.
The bill allocates $1 million annually to the Department of Labor for an industry-led, regional competitive workforce development grant program related to clean energy.
The PSC oversees utility compliance fees that fund the SEIF and is responsible for directing and overseeing the energy relief refunds and credits to residential customers.

DHS administers energy assistance programs, including the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), which are primarily funded by the SEIF; the bill significantly alters the funding allocation priority and percentages for these programs.
The Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Strategic Energy Investment Fund separately and manage its investment and distribution.
The Comptroller is responsible for the accounting and fiscal oversight of the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
The Maryland Energy Innovation Institute, which is housed within the University of Maryland (part of the USM), is mandated to receive a $2 million annual allocation from the fund.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures and contracts, which includes the large grants and capital projects funded by the new SEIF mandates.
DBM is responsible for the budgetary oversight and implementation of the mandated fund allocations within the annual state budget and through budget amendments.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the multiple executive agencies, including the MEA and MDE, that are tasked with implementing the expanded SEIF programs.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing these mandates and directs the state's broader climate change and energy policy strategies.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Department of Health from issuing or renewing a certificate or accepting alternative accreditation for a youth camp if any structures that are or will be used to house a camper are located in a flood hazard area.
Title: Youth Camps - Structures in Flood Hazard Areas - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from issuing or renewing certifications or accepting alternative accreditation for youth camps if any structures used to house campers are located within a flood hazard area, defined as an area with a 1% annual chance of flooding.
stakeholders: Youth camp operators, campers and their families, and the Maryland Department of Health
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. Potential fiscal impacts include a decrease in certification fee revenue for the Maryland Department of Health if existing camps are unable to qualify for renewal and significant compliance or relocation costs for private and public youth camp operators with housing facilities in flood hazard areas.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from issuing or renewing certificates or accepting alternative accreditation for youth camps if any structures used to house campers are located in a flood hazard area, making MDH the primary implementing and enforcing agency.

The bill defines 'flood hazard area' and '100-year flood event' based on existing provisions within the Environment Article, and this department is responsible for mapping and regulating such areas in the state.

As an agency that adjudicates contested cases for state departments, the OAH would likely handle appeals from youth camp operators whose certificates are denied or not renewed due to the new flood hazard area restrictions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Department of the Environment regarding the interpretation, implementation, and enforcement of health and environmental regulations mandated by this bill.

MDEM coordinates the state's hazard mitigation and preparedness efforts for floods; the bill's intent to remove youth from high-risk flood zones aligns with the department's mission to reduce disaster risk.
The Department of Natural Resources manages state parks and public lands that frequently host youth camps, and it enforces conservation laws related to Maryland's waterways and flood-prone areas.
The Department of Planning provides data analysis and policy guidance on land use and sustainable development, including the management of infrastructure within flood-prone regions.
DBM oversees state personnel and budget execution; it would be responsible for assessing the fiscal impact of MDH's increased regulatory and monitoring requirements under this mandate.
This office coordinates policies to promote the well-being and safety of Maryland's children, a mission that includes ensuring safe environments for youth at recreational camps.

This multi-agency initiative promotes sustainable development and environmental protection, including the preservation of flood-prone lands and the implementation of state planning visions relevant to this bill.

Synopsis: Clarifying that it is the intent of the General Assembly regarding the development and offering of structural racism training that applicants for the renewal of a health occupations license are required to take be developed and offered at no cost to the State using funding from certain external sources.
Title: Health Occupations - Structural Racism Training - Funding Sources
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill clarifies the intent of the General Assembly that mandatory structural racism training for health occupation license renewals be developed and offered at no cost to the State. It specifies that funding for such training should come from external sources, such as grants provided to the Maryland Nurses Association from the American Nurses Association.
stakeholders: Licensed and certified health care professionals, Maryland health occupations boards, and the Maryland Nurses Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is clarifying in nature and stipulates that required structural racism training be funded through external sources rather than State expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency impacted as it oversees the health occupations boards and the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, which are responsible for identifying and approving the structural racism training programs referenced in the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and its health occupations boards, and would be responsible for advising on the statutory implementation of the training requirements and the interpretation of the 'at no cost to the state' provision.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning; the bill's clarification that training be offered at no cost to the State aligns with their oversight of state expenditures.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinate policy initiatives. The Governor would be responsible for signing this bill and ensuring that the Department of Health follows the legislative intent regarding the use of external funding sources for these programs.

Synopsis: Authorizing a public high school to allow certain homeschool students to participate in athletic activities sponsored by the school under certain circumstances; authorizing certain homeschool students to participate in an athletic activity sponsored by certain public high schools, subject to certain requirements; and requiring that certain liability insurance cover certain homeschool students under certain circumstances.
Title: Homeschool Students in Maryland - Right to Play
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill authorizes public high schools in Maryland to allow homeschool students to participate in interscholastic athletic activities sponsored by the school, provided the activities occur outside school hours and do not grant academic credit. Homeschool students must meet specific residential criteria, comply with the same health and conduct rules as enrolled students, and provide their own transportation. Public high schools must give priority to enrolled students if roster space is limited.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Homeschool students, public high school students, parents of homeschoolers, local school systems, and the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA)
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education can manage regulatory requirements using existing resources. Because the bill is permissive rather than mandatory, it does not affect local school finances, and it is assumed that the total number of students participating in interscholastic athletics will not expand significantly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency impacted as the bill amends the Education Article and involves interscholastic athletics and home instruction programs, both of which are governed by MSDE regulations (COMAR). The agency will likely need to develop new regulations and provide guidance to local school systems and the MPSSAA.

The bill contains specific mandates regarding liability insurance coverage for homeschool students and authorizes schools to require proof of insurance or payment of premiums. As the state's insurance regulator, the MIA is a key stakeholder and was consulted for the fiscal note.

The bill explicitly states that homeschool students participating in school sports are subject to the same codes of conduct and safety rules as enrolled students. MCSS is responsible for coordinating school safety standards and training across the state.

The bill requires homeschool students to meet the same immunization and health requirements as enrolled students, which falls under the public health oversight and regulatory standards of the Maryland Department of Health.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state's insurance protection and was consulted regarding the fiscal impact of extending liability coverage to homeschool participants.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal requirements and ensuring that the implementation of the 'Right to Play' does not conflict with existing state or federal laws.

The bill aligns with the GOC's mission to improve access to services and opportunities for Maryland's children, specifically by opening public school athletic programs to students in home instruction.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the release of a defendant pending sentencing or exhaustion of appellate review after conviction of a specified crime resulting in the death of a victim under the age of 14 years.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Postconviction Release - Crimes Resulting in Death of Young Victim
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Hate Crimes

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a court from releasing a defendant after they have been convicted, but before sentencing or the conclusion of appellate reviews, if the conviction was for a crime of violence or child neglect that resulted in the death of a victim under the age of 14.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and Maryland trial courts
stakeholders: Defendants convicted of crimes of violence or child neglect resulting in the death of a victim under 14; Maryland Judiciary; law enforcement and correctional facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations, as stated in the Fiscal and Policy Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures and judicial discretion regarding the release of defendants following a conviction. As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is responsible for implementing the operational and procedural changes required by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: By prohibiting postconviction release for specific categories of defendants, the bill will result in these individuals remaining in custody at state or local facilities during sentencing and the duration of their appeals. This directly impacts the management and population of facilities overseen by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal representation to indigent defendants. This bill directly affects the post-conviction rights and status of their clients, specifically their ability to seek release pending sentencing or the exhaustion of appellate review.

The OAG represents the state in all criminal appeals. The bill's restrictions on release specifically extend through the 'exhaustion of any appellate review,' a phase of the criminal justice process where the OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the State.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy in Maryland. This bill represents a significant policy shift regarding the handling of violent offenders and the protection of young victims, falling within the office's advisory and policy development scope.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program is required to disclose prescription monitoring data to a federal law enforcement agency to prohibit the disclosure if the Protected Health Care Commission determines that the data is sensitive health services information that has been determined by the Secretary of Health to be legally protected health care.
Title: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program - Data Disclosure to Federal Law Enforcement - Limitation
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This emergency bill limits the circumstances under which the Maryland Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) must disclose data to federal law enforcement agencies. Specifically, the PDMP is prohibited from disclosing monitoring data to a federal agency, even with a subpoena for a bona fide investigation, if the data involves sensitive health services that the Protected Health Care Commission and the Secretary of Health have determined to be legally protected health care.
stakeholders: Patients receiving sensitive health services (such as reproductive or gender-affirming care), federal law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to complete one-time programming updates to the PDMP database to support compliance. There is no fiscal impact on local governments or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) and provides staff for the Protected Health Care Commission (PHCC). The Secretary of Health is responsible for making final determinations on what constitutes legally protected health care and oversees the PDMP's data disclosure policies. The agency also incurs a fiscal impact for necessary database updates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill centers on the recommendations of the Protected Health Care Commission (PHCC), which is established to identify sensitive health services. This collective entity encompasses such commissions tasked with providing expertise and recommendations to executive departments.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission, or their designee, is a statutory member of the Protected Health Care Commission, which is responsible for identifying sensitive health services and making recommendations to the Secretary of Health.

The Attorney General, or their designee, is a statutory member of the Protected Health Care Commission. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General is an authorized recipient of PDMP data for investigation purposes under existing law, which this bill modifies in context.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is an authorized recipient of PDMP data via subpoena. While the bill specifically restricts federal law enforcement access, the overall management and availability of prescription monitoring data is highly relevant to their investigative functions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and cabinet-level departments like the Department of Health. The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Protected Health Care Commission and coordinating policy initiatives related to health data privacy and law enforcement.

Synopsis: Requiring a school to provide notice to the parent, guardian, or caretaker of a child if a mandated reporter reports certain suspected abuse or neglect that occurs at a school or school-sponsored activity, unless the parent, guardian, or caretaker is the subject of the report; and requiring the notice to be provided not later than 24 hours after the report is made.

bill_summary: This bill requires schools to notify a parent, guardian, or caretaker within 24 hours when a mandated reporter makes a report of suspected child abuse or neglect occurring at school or a school-sponsored activity. This notification is not required if the parent, guardian, or caretaker is the subject of the report.
responsible_party: Maryland public schools and local school systems
stakeholders: Parents, guardians, and caretakers of students; students; and mandated reporters within the school system
fiscal_impact_summary: The provided text does not contain a formal Fiscal Note or specify state or local revenue and expenditure figures. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable, though schools may incur administrative costs to implement the required 24-hour notification process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Education Article requiring schools and school-sponsored activities to provide parental notification within 24 hours of a report of suspected abuse or neglect. As the oversight body for Maryland's public education system, MSDE will be responsible for policy implementation and ensuring compliance across local school systems.

The bill directly amends Section 1-202 of the Human Services Article regarding the disclosure of reports or records concerning child abuse or neglect. DHS is the primary agency responsible for managing these records and administering the state's child protective services and mandated reporting frameworks.

As an independent unit within MSDE focused on safety training and resources, the Center would likely be involved in developing protocols and training for school staff on how to safely and legally handle these parental notifications.

As a state-operated school agency, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly subject to the requirements of the Education Article and would need to implement these parental notification procedures for its students.

The OAG would provide legal guidance to MSDE and DHS regarding the confidentiality of child abuse records and the intersection of this new notification requirement with existing state and federal privacy laws.

The GOC coordinates policies aimed at the well-being of Maryland's children. This legislation relates to child safety and the rights of parents and guardians within the state's educational and social service frameworks.

bill_summary: House Bill 1047 requires individuals to register as limited X-ray machine operators with the Maryland Board of Physicians to perform specific X-ray procedures. It establishes educational and clinical training requirements, examination standards, and disciplinary procedures for these registrants. The bill also specifies conditions under which physician assistants may perform X-ray duties and recodifies existing laws regarding the delegation of duties to cardiovascular invasive specialists and supervised medical graduates.
stakeholders: Limited X-ray machine operators, physician assistants, physicians, radiographers, supervised medical graduates, and healthcare facilities including hospitals and physician offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Board of Physicians can implement the registration and oversight requirements using existing resources. While the bill authorizes the collection of registration and renewal fees and allows for civil penalties (up to $5,000 for hospitals/offices and $1,000 for individuals), these are not expected to have a material impact on State revenues. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts the Maryland Department of Health as it expands the regulatory authority of the State Board of Physicians, which is housed within the department. It requires the department's Secretary to make final decisions on joint regulations if boards cannot agree and oversees the new registration and disciplinary framework for limited X-ray machine operators.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Board of Physicians. The bill specifically mandates that the OAG file certified docket entries with the Board in cases of criminal convictions to trigger mandatory registration suspensions or revocations.

The bill establishes a disciplinary process for limited X-ray machine operators that includes the right to a hearing. The OAH is the agency responsible for conducting these administrative hearings for contested cases involving regulatory enforcement by the Board of Physicians.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its agencies, including the Department of Health. The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the administration of the boards that implement these regulations.

The bill establishes registration and renewal fees as well as civil penalties. The fiscal note indicates that these fines are paid into the State's general fund, which the Comptroller's office manages as the state's principal tax and revenue collector.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget execution for the Board of Physicians. While the fiscal note suggests MBP can handle the bill's requirements within existing resources, DBM maintains oversight of the personnel and budgetary shifts related to the new registration program.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in selecting and vetting members for the State Board of Physicians, which is the primary body tasked with adopting regulations and adjudicating the new registration categories created by the bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires chain restaurants with 20 or more locations to display warning icons and specific health-related disclosure text on menus and menu boards for items containing high sodium (1,150 milligrams or more) or high added sugars (25 grams or more). It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the icons, provide compliance guidance on its website, and report to the General Assembly by 2032 on the impact of these requirements on consumer behavior and menu reformulation.
stakeholders: Chain restaurants with 20 or more locations, Maryland consumers, and local health department inspectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are not expected to be affected, although the bill establishes misdemeanor fines for violations (up to $500 for a first offense and $1,000 for subsequent offenses). There is a potential meaningful fiscal impact on small business franchisees who must comply with the new labeling and menu requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is mandated to adopt regulations for sodium and sugar warning icons, establish size and text requirements, publish guidance on its website, and submit a report to the General Assembly by 2032 evaluating the impact of the requirements on consumer behavior and food reformulation.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for the state and would provide counsel to the Department of Health during the regulatory process. Additionally, the bill includes provisions for civil penalties and injunctions, which the OAG would be responsible for pursuing in the District Court to ensure compliance with the new public health standards.

The bill establishes new criminal misdemeanor penalties and civil penalties for violations of the menu labeling requirements. These cases would be adjudicated within the state's court system, and the Administrative Office of the Courts would oversee the operational and financial aspects of processing these filings and collecting fines.

As the state's primary economic development and business advocacy agency, the Department of Commerce is relevant due to the bill's regulatory impact on chain restaurants and franchisees. The requirements for menu redesign and nutritional disclosure impose operational changes on a significant sector of Maryland's business community.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill includes a technical amendment to Section 13-517 of the Education Article, which governs the Automated External Defibrillator (AED) program managed by MIEMSS. The amendment ensures that restaurants subject to the new nutritional labeling requirements are correctly categorized in relation to MIEMSS facility definitions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments, including MDH, that are tasked with implementing the bill. The reporting requirement to the General Assembly on the effectiveness of the warning icons will inform future executive policy decisions regarding public health and nutrition.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the voting requirements for credit union mergers by allowing the board of a surviving credit union to approve a merger without a mandatory vote from its members. Under the bill, while a vote by the members of the surviving credit union becomes optional, the members of the merging credit union (the entity being absorbed) must still provide an affirmative majority vote to approve the merger.
responsible_party: Commissioner of the Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Maryland credit unions, their boards of directors, and credit union members.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, is the primary regulator for state-chartered financial institutions. This bill directly amends procedures for credit union mergers and consolidations, specifically regarding membership voting requirements and the oversight authority of the Commissioner.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, assisting in the interpretation and enforcement of the Financial Institutions Article as modified by this bill.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Labor and is responsible for signing this legislation into law.

MSDE may use or reference existing educational materials from these organizations if they are age-appropriate, evidence-based, medically accurate, and consistent with the Maryland Revised Uniform Anatomical Gift Act.
stakeholders: Maryland State Department of Education, county boards of education, organ procurement organizations, the qualified nonprofit entity operating the state donor registry, and students in Maryland public schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no material effect on State operations or finances. The Maryland State Department of Education advises that any consultation or curriculum adjustment required by the bill can be absorbed within existing resources. There is no anticipated effect on local school system expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency named in the bill, MSDE is responsible for consulting with the donor registry and procurement organizations when developing, updating, or approving educational materials and curriculum guidance regarding organ, eye, and tissue donation for use by local school systems.

The bill deals with organ, eye, and tissue donation, which is a public health and medical topic. MDH is responsible for protecting and improving the health of Marylanders and ensuring health policy is evidence-based and medically accurate.

The MVA is the primary agency that handles the driver's licenses through which Maryland residents typically join the donor registry mentioned in the bill. Educational curriculum in schools regarding the registry directly supports the systems managed by the MVA.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and other state agencies. The bill requires educational materials to be consistent with the Maryland Revised Uniform Anatomical Gift Act, which may require legal review or interpretation from the OAG.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Meds-to-Beds Program, which requires all Maryland hospitals to have a licensed pharmacist deliver discharge medications to patients at their bedside before they leave the facility to reduce readmissions. It also authorizes health care facilities to use automated and remote drug dispensing systems, allows pharmacies to outsource specific prescription processing tasks to other pharmacies, and expands the legal definition of telehealth to include these automated dispensing systems for insurance reimbursement purposes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, patients, pharmacies, nursing and long-term care facilities, and health insurance providers
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill results in a minimal special fund revenue increase of $125 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Insurance Administration from rate and form filing fees. Implementation and regulation by the Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy are expected to be managed with existing resources. There is no impact on local government finances and no meaningful impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Meds-to-Beds Program within the Executive Branch's Department of Health and requires the Governor's administration to oversee the implementation of this new public health initiative.

As the agency responsible for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is impacted by changes to the definition of telehealth and insurance coverage requirements for dispensing systems.

MDH is the primary agency responsible for establishing the Meds-to-Beds Program, adopting regulations for the program, and overseeing the State Board of Pharmacy, which will regulate the new drug dispensing systems and outsourcing protocols.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy in developing the new regulatory framework and enforcing compliance with the health and insurance articles amended by the bill.
The bill authorizes the use of automated drug dispensing systems in nursing facilities, which are a primary focus of the Department of Aging's advocacy and long-term care programs.

The MIA is responsible for regulating the insurance market and must process rate and form filings related to the expanded definition of telehealth and mandatory coverage for remote drug dispensing systems.
The bill specifically preserves the HSCRC's authority to set hospital rates and facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth services, which now include the new dispensing systems.
The change in telehealth definitions and insurance coverage mandates affects health plans offered through the state's insurance marketplace administered by the Exchange.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and hospital regulation, which is impacted by the mandatory hospital participation in the Meds-to-Beds Program and the introduction of new dispensing technologies.

The bill explicitly requires pharmacies located outside the facilities they serve to obtain a controlled substances registration from OCSA before stocking controlled substances in the new dispensing systems.

The University of Maryland Medical System is a primary site for existing Meds-to-Beds programs, and the UM School of Pharmacy provided the research and reporting that informed the bill's telepharmacy recommendations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition and size of the Maryland School for the Deaf's Board of Trustees, which is the agency's governing body. The school will also experience a minimal fiscal impact due to decreased meal costs for fewer board members.
The Governor is the appointing authority for the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf and is responsible for prioritizing the appointment of deaf members as mandated by the bill.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for the Board of Trustees and will be responsible for managing the transitions and specific membership requirements defined in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for the welfare of deaf residents and ensures state programs are inclusive; the bill's focus on increasing deaf representation on the governing board of the state's school for the deaf is highly relevant to its mission.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from intentionally causing physical injury to another if the person knows or has reason to know that the other is an official, an umpire, a referee, or a judge officiating at a sporting event; authorizing a police officer to arrest a person without a warrant if the police officer has probable cause to believe that the person has committed a certain assault; and establishing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor of assault in the second degree and is subject to certain penalties.

bill_summary: This bill classifies the intentional causing of physical injury to a sports official—including referees, umpires, and judges—while they are officiating a sporting event as a misdemeanor second-degree assault. Additionally, it authorizes police officers to perform warrantless arrests if they have probable cause to believe such an assault has occurred.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Sports officials (referees, umpires, judges), law enforcement officers, and individuals participating in or attending sporting events.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. The penalties for the newly defined misdemeanor second-degree assault against a sports official include imprisonment for up to 10 years and a fine of up to $2,500, which is consistent with existing penalties for general misdemeanor second-degree assault.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, MSP is directly responsible for enforcing criminal laws and exercising the new warrantless arrest authority provided in the bill for assaults on sports officials.
The bill creates a specific classification of second-degree assault that must be adjudicated through the state court system, requiring updated judicial procedures and tracking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is responsible for representing indigent defendants charged under this new specific criminal provision and managing the legal impact of the expanded warrantless arrest authority.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on the enforcement of criminal laws and represents the state in appeals related to new criminal statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates statewide public safety strategies and policy development related to criminal justice and victim services.
The department oversees public school athletics through the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA), which employs and manages the sports officials protected by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the supervision and rehabilitation of individuals convicted of misdemeanor second-degree assault and sentenced to incarceration or probation.
DJS would be responsible for the assessment and supervision of youth who are involved in the juvenile justice system for assaulting sports officials at youth or school events.
The Natural Resources Police, a unit within DNR, possess law enforcement authority and would be empowered to make warrantless arrests under the bill's provisions on state lands.
MDOT's law enforcement units, such as the MDTA Police, would be authorized to use the expanded warrantless arrest powers for crimes occurring on transportation-related property.
The MSA manages major sports and entertainment facilities where sports officials work and where the incidents addressed by the bill are likely to occur.

bill_summary: This bill increases the statute of limitations from two years to three years for the prosecution of criminal offenses under the Maryland Public Ethics Law, as well as criminal malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance in office by State, local, or bicounty public officers. This extension also applies to attempts and conspiracies to commit these offenses.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, State Ethics Commission, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Public officers of the State, State agencies, political subdivisions, and bicounty or multicounty agencies; law enforcement and legal professionals; and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. No specific revenue or expenditure changes are identified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding the statute of limitations for specific misdemeanors, directly impacting judicial proceedings and the administration of cases within the court system.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies. Criminal malfeasance or ethics violations by state officers significantly intersect with the department's oversight of public servant conduct and personnel management.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for ensuring state laws are enforced. This bill affects the legal accountability of officers within the executive departments managed by the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender would be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with the misdemeanors identified in the bill, such as ethics violations or malfeasance in office, over an extended timeframe.

The OLA identifies financial mismanagement, fraud, and misconduct through its audits of state agencies and its fraud hotline. Its findings often serve as the basis for investigations into criminal malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to all state agencies and represents the state in criminal appeals. It has a significant interest in the statutes governing the prosecution of public officials.

The OSP is the primary agency tasked with investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses related to the integrity of state officials, including ethics laws and misconduct in office (malfeasance, misfeasance, and nonfeasance). This bill directly extends their window for bringing such charges.

The State Ethics Commission administers and enforces the Maryland Public Ethics Law. Since the bill specifically extends the statute of limitations for criminal violations of that law, it is highly relevant to the commission's regulatory and investigative work.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to screen all newborns for Gaucher disease. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a statewide system for Gaucher disease screening, perform the laboratory tests in its public health laboratory, manage results, and oversee the Newborn Screening Program Fund.

The bill specifies that the Secretary of Health shall pay all collected fees to the Comptroller, who is then responsible for distributing those fees to the Newborn Screening Program Fund.

The OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies. It would be tasked with auditing the Maryland Department of Health's management and expenditure of the Newborn Screening Program Fund, which will be impacted by the new testing mandate.

bill_summary: The Artificial Intelligence Ready Schools Act requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to provide artificial intelligence (AI) guidance through an online platform, develop evaluative rubrics for AI tools, and provide professional development for school leaders and educators. It mandates that each local school system adopt an AI policy, designate a noninstructional staff member as an AI coordinator, and procure AI tools in accordance with state standards. bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to develop a tracking and reporting system for petitions for emergency evaluations (mental health crises) of students in public and nonpublic schools. Schools and local boards of education must collect and report data including student demographics, the initiating employee, the reason for the petition, the use of handcuffs, and clinical outcomes. The bill also establishes a workgroup to study school-based mental health crisis responses and requires MSDE to submit annual reports to the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Primary and secondary students, public and nonpublic schools, local boards of education, school-based mental health professionals, and law enforcement officers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $58,900 in FY 2027 to hire a half-time administrator to manage the data collection and support the workgroup, with costs projected to reach $76,900 by FY 2031. Local school systems may incur additional administrative costs to comply with tracking and reporting requirements, particularly those with a high volume of petitions or those that do not currently track such data. While Section 2 regarding the workgroup sunsets on December 31, 2027, the tracking and reporting requirements are ongoing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary implementing agency, responsible for developing the tracking and reporting system, verifying data, staffing the required workgroup, and submitting annual reports to the General Assembly.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is specifically named as one of the educational institutions required to implement the tracking system and report petition data directly to the Department of Education.

The petitions for emergency evaluation are governed by the Health - General Article, and the bill tracks clinical outcomes such as facility admission. Additionally, the workgroup must include hospital and psychiatric providers regulated by or associated with this department.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education focused on school safety coordination and mental health crisis response, this agency is directly involved in the policy and training objectives of the bill's reporting requirements and workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the creation of a temporary workgroup composed of various stakeholders to study student petitions for emergency evaluation and recommend policy improvements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency oversees the statewide emergency medical services network, which is often responsible for the prehospital care and transport of students undergoing an emergency evaluation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office coordinates policies and welfare for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents, including students at the Maryland School for the Deaf, which is a primary reporting entity under the bill.
The judiciary is involved in the legal approval of petitions for emergency evaluation, and the agency is listed as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
The bill requires general fund expenditures for additional personnel at the Department of Education to manage data collection and reporting.
The bill specifically requires the tracking system to collect data on whether a student has an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 plan and the nature of their disabilities.
Youth involved in the juvenile justice system are a relevant demographic for school-based emergency evaluations, and the agency was consulted for the fiscal note.
The agency's focus on child well-being and access to health services aligns with the bill's goal of studying and improving mental health crisis responses for students.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and juvenile delinquency reduction, which intersects with the bill's focus on law enforcement involvement and the use of restraints during petitions.
The commission plans for state health system needs and tracks the quality and cost of health services, including the psychiatric services and facility admissions mentioned in the bill.
This agency serves as the repository for student and workforce data and would be interested in the student-level health crisis data collected under the new system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents individuals in involuntary commitment proceedings, which can be the legal outcome of a petition for emergency evaluation.
Law enforcement officers are often tasked with executing petitions for emergency evaluation and are required to be represented in the workgroup established by the bill.
The agency would provide legal counsel regarding State and federal privacy laws (such as FERPA and HIPAA) as schools and the Department navigate data sharing requirements.
