fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Judiciary can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judicial Branch, as it requires judges to order restitution, evaluate specific financial and custody criteria to determine amounts, and manage the scheduling of periodic payments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency provides legal representation to indigent defendants who would be facing these mandatory restitution orders as part of their sentencing for homicide by motor vehicle or vessel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees the incarceration of individuals convicted of these crimes and is responsible for supervising the Division of Parole and Probation, which typically monitors the collection and payment of court-ordered restitution.

The bill explicitly requires courts to consider whether a child is in the custody of the Department of Human Services when determining the amount of restitution and evaluating the financial needs of the child.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for criminal justice strategies and victim services in Maryland, this office is relevant to the implementation of policies that provide financial support and restitution to victims of crime.
The OAG represents the state in criminal appeals and provides legal counsel to state agencies involved in the implementation of the Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure articles.
The State Police is the primary agency investigating motor vehicle and vessel homicides involving impairment or alcohol, which are the predicate offenses for the restitution mandated by the bill.
The bill addresses the well-being and economic security of children who have lost a parent, aligning with the office's mission to reduce child poverty and improve support networks for families.

The bill concerns fatalities caused by motor vehicles and vessels, which fall under the broad purview of MDOT's highway and maritime safety interests, though the agency does not directly manage restitution.
The MVA manages driver records and licensing related to the underlying convictions (homicide by motor vehicle while impaired) mentioned in the bill.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget execution and personnel needs for the departments (like DHS or DPSCS) that may be impacted by the administrative requirements of the bill.

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch departments responsible for implementing the bill's provisions regarding child welfare and correctional supervision.

Synopsis: Requiring, to make a claim under a warranty for certain agricultural equipment, a consumer to provide written notice to certain parties to report a nonconformity, defect, or condition occurring in certain agricultural equipment; requiring certain parties to correct the nonconformity, defect, or condition in a certain manner; and requiring certain parties to provide a consumer with the opportunity to replace agricultural equipment or receive a refund under certain circumstances.
Title: Consumer Protection - Agricultural Equipment Warranties
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 307

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Agricultural Equipment Warranty Enforcement Act, which requires consumers of self-propelled farming equipment to report defects in writing to manufacturers or dealers. It mandates that nonconformities be corrected within 30 days and provides consumers the right to a replacement or refund if the equipment remains defective after multiple repair attempts or is out of service for a cumulative total of 30 days during a season of use. Violations are designated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Consumers (including farmers) purchasing new agricultural equipment, as well as manufacturers, factory branches, and authorized dealers of such equipment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can implement the bill using existing resources. While no specific appropriation is provided, violations are subject to existing civil and criminal penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and courts may award up to $5,000 in damages to consumers if a manufacturer is found to have acted in bad faith.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines violations of the Agricultural Equipment Warranty Enforcement Act as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the Office of the Attorney General is primary responsible for enforcing.

The bill focuses exclusively on 'agricultural equipment' used in the business of farming. This is directly relevant to the Department's mission to support the economic viability of the farming sector and provide consumer confidence in agricultural services.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action for consumers to enforce warranty claims and allows for courts to award damages for bad faith, which impacts the operations of the Maryland Judicial Branch.

The bill applies to self-propelled vehicles and specifically mentions the refund of license and registration fees, which are administered and collected by the MVA. The bill also references definitions within the Transportation Article.

As an agency that adjudicates contested cases involving state regulatory enforcement, OAH may be involved in administrative hearings arising from consumer protection enforcement actions under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

Agricultural equipment is a critical asset for the economies of Maryland's rural counties. The Council advocates for interests that improve the quality of life and economic development for farmers and rural residents.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (such as MDA and OAG) that will be involved in implementing or enforcing this policy, and the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors legislation for potential impacts on state resources and manages the fiscal planning related to agency personnel and administrative costs.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on Blueprint Fiscal Sustainability and Student Achievement to study and make recommendations on the successful and sustainable implementation of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future; and requiring the Commission to provide an interim report on or before December 31, 2026, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2027.
Title: Commission on Blueprint Fiscal Sustainability and Student Achievement - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/12 at 1:00 p.m. (Ways and Means)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission on Blueprint Fiscal Sustainability and Student Achievement to evaluate the implementation and financial sustainability of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future education reform. The commission is charged with studying school funding formulas, the educator career ladder, and the efficiency of various student achievement models. It must submit an interim report by December 31, 2026, and a final report by December 1, 2027.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents, teachers, local school boards, and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. The bill text indicates that the Maryland State Department of Education and the Accountability and Implementation Board must provide staff support for the commission. Additionally, commission members are entitled to reimbursement for travel expenses as provided in the state budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Education is mandated to provide staffing for the Commission and the State Superintendent of Schools is a designated member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes a new temporary commission to study and make recommendations on the fiscal sustainability and implementation of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
The Chair of the Interagency Commission on School Construction is a designated member of the commission, reflecting the Blueprint's impact on school facilities.
The Secretary of Higher Education is a designated member of the commission, as the Blueprint includes significant components related to postsecondary education and teacher preparation.
The Secretary of Labor is a member of the commission, representing the agency's role in the workforce and career-readiness aspects of the Blueprint.
The Governor jointly designates the chair of the commission and the body is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor.
The Chair of the Governor's Workforce Development Board is responsible for appointing a member of a local workforce development board to the commission.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is significantly impacted by a commission dedicated to the fiscal sustainability of the state's largest educational investment.
The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for state agencies and commissions and may be called upon for legal counsel during the commission's study process.

Synopsis: Requiring the Interagency Commission on School Construction, when calculating a school's Gross Area Baseline, to allocate square footage to accommodate certain aquatic facilities; requiring each local school system to develop a certain facilities plan before the start of a certain school year; and requiring the Interagency Commission to collaborate with each school system on developing a certain facilities plan.
Title: School Construction - Gross Area Baseline Calculation - Aquatic Facilities
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 1:35 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) to include square footage for aquatic facilities intended for athletic education and competition when calculating a school's Gross Area Baseline. It also mandates that each local school system develop a facilities plan in collaboration with the IAC to identify options for student access to aquatic facilities before the 2026-2027 school year.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local school systems, and the Interagency Commission on School Construction
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not change the overall level of State support for school construction but may shift the allocation of funds, potentially reducing the number of other projects funded. Local school systems may face meaningful increases in maintenance costs for new aquatic facilities and operational costs for providing student access to existing pools. Specific dollar estimates for these impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the IAC to update its Gross Area Baseline calculations to include square footage for aquatic facilities and requires the commission to collaborate with local school systems to develop facilities plans for aquatic access.

As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of the state's 24 local school systems, MSDE is relevant because the bill requires local school systems to develop facilities plans identifying options for student access to aquatic facilities.

The Board of Public Works approves significant state expenditures, including capital projects and school construction contracts, which will be affected by the increased project sizes and funding shifts resulting from the new Gross Area Baseline requirements.

MSA is responsible for the design and construction of public schools through the Built to Learn Act; schools built under this program must adhere to the IAC's baseline standards, which the bill seeks to expand.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller reviews and approves school construction projects and funding allocations that will be impacted by the changes in baseline square footage calculations.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees and approves the capital project expenditures for school construction affected by this legislation.
The Governor chairs the Board of Public Works and oversees the executive branch agencies, including the IAC, responsible for implementing the school construction funding shifts.

DBM oversees the state's capital budget; while the bill may not change the total amount of funding, it shifts the allocation of those funds toward aquatic facilities, impacting long-term fiscal planning for school infrastructure.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the IAC and the Department of Education regarding the implementation of new regulatory standards and facilities planning requirements.

Synopsis: Suspending the imposition of the State transfer tax from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.
Title: State Transfer Tax - Temporary Suspension
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill suspends the imposition of the Maryland State transfer tax on instruments of writing, such as property deeds, recorded or filed between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2029. The state transfer tax, typically 0.5% of the property's consideration, is a primary funding source for land preservation and conservation programs.
responsible_party: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation and the clerks of the circuit courts
stakeholders: Property buyers and sellers, first-time homebuyers, the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (Program Open Space), the Maryland Department of Agriculture (Agricultural Land Preservation Fund), and local governments receiving land preservation grants.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a substantial decrease in State revenue and spending. Total State revenues are estimated to decrease by $245.4 million in fiscal 2027, $263.6 million in fiscal 2028, and $277.6 million in fiscal 2029. These reductions include a $25 million annual decrease in general fund revenue and significant decreases in special fund revenue. Consequently, special fund expenditures for land preservation programs (such as Program Open Space and the Rural Legacy Program) will decrease by $220.4 million in fiscal 2027, $238.6 million in fiscal 2028, and $252.6 million in fiscal 2029. Local government funding for land preservation will also decrease by commensurate amounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary beneficiary of the State transfer tax, receiving the vast majority of its revenue to fund Program Open Space, the Rural Legacy Program, and the Heritage Conservation Fund. The suspension of this tax would cause a significant decrease in special fund expenditures for land preservation and acquisition.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture receives 17.05% of the State transfer tax revenue for the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund (MALPF). A suspension of the tax would result in a substantial loss of funding for its agricultural land preservation activities.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the collection and enforcement of state taxes. The bill's suspension of a major revenue stream directly impacts the agency's revenue management and auditing functions.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for developing the state's budget and estimating revenues. The projected loss of over $245 million annually in special and general fund revenues requires significant adjustments to long-term fiscal planning and budget execution.

Instruments of writing subject to the transfer tax are recorded with the clerks of the circuit courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational support for these clerks, who would be responsible for implementing the temporary suspension of tax collection at the point of recording.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. The bill's suspension of transfer tax revenues would significantly impact the Governor's ability to fund environmental and agricultural policy initiatives through the budget process.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures, including land acquisitions and capital projects funded by transfer tax revenues (such as those for Program Open Space). A suspension of these funds would reduce the volume of projects requiring Board approval.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is tasked with supporting the sustainability of agriculture and resource-based industries, often partnering with other agencies to facilitate rural land preservation funded by the transfer tax.
The Maryland Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and land use preservation, which are policy areas heavily supported by the programs funded through the State transfer tax.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates efforts to protect the Chesapeake Bay and preserve farmland, goals that are primarily funded by the transfer tax revenues allocated to the Department of Natural Resources and the Department of Agriculture.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works and is responsible for managing state funds. The loss of hundreds of millions in tax revenue impacts the overall management of state cash deposits and investments.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements for consumer reporting agencies that use algorithmic systems to assemble or evaluate consumer credit information on consumers for the purpose of furnishing consumer reports to third parties; and requiring the Commissioner of Financial Regulation of the Maryland Department of Labor to establish certain assessment thresholds for algorithms, mandate regular training for human reviewers, and implement a certain whistleblower protection program.
Title: Consumer Protection - Consumer Reporting Agencies - Use of Algorithmic Systems
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes comprehensive regulations for consumer reporting agencies that use algorithmic systems to process consumer credit information. It mandates that agencies provide plain-language explanations for evaluations, maintain a public registry of algorithms, and adhere to strict accuracy standards, including an error rate of less than 0.5% and data input accuracy of 99.9%. Agencies must conduct quarterly third-party bias audits, provide human review for automated decisions, and offer non-algorithmic options for consumers. Additionally, the Commissioner of Financial Regulation is required to oversee these standards, provide reviewer training, and implement whistleblower protections for agency employees.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation of the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Consumer reporting agencies, Maryland consumers, and employees of consumer reporting agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the bill text. The legislation creates new regulatory and oversight duties for the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, including the establishment of assessment thresholds, the implementation of a whistleblower protection program, and the mandate for regular reviewer training. These activities are expected to increase state expenditures for administrative oversight and enforcement, although specific dollar estimates are currently unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Department of Labor with establishing assessment thresholds for algorithms, mandating training for reviewers, implementing a whistleblower protection program, and adopting regulations.

As the primary legal representative for the state and enforcer of consumer protection laws, the OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and potentially litigating enforcement actions under the Commercial Law Article.

The bill addresses algorithmic discrimination and harmful bias based on protected characteristics, which falls directly within the mission of the Commission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and promote civil rights compliance.
Regulatory decisions or penalties imposed by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation on consumer reporting agencies would likely be subject to adjudication by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

The bill involves technical oversight of algorithmic systems, data governance, and AI-generated content detection. DoIT, as the lead agency for state IT strategy, may provide technical guidance on these standards.
The bill establishes significant regulatory requirements and audit costs for consumer reporting agencies, which are businesses operating within the state's economic landscape.

Consumer reports are frequently used to determine eligibility for housing; improvements in report accuracy and reductions in bias would impact the Department's mission to ensure access to secure housing.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM would oversee the fiscal impact and potential staffing needs of the Department of Labor to implement the assessment thresholds and whistleblower program.

Synopsis: Authorizing the suspension or revocation of a shellfish aquaculture harvester permit or shellfish aquaculture harvester registration card for certain violations; prohibiting a person whose permit or registration card has been suspended or revoked in accordance with the Act from engaging or working in any aquaculture activity during the suspension or revocation; authorizing a certain leaseholder and the Department of Natural Resources to complete a process to remove gear or transfer a shellfish aquaculture lease; etc.
Title: Shellfish Aquaculture - Penalties - Suspension or Revocation of Permit or Registration Card
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 304

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to suspend or revoke shellfish aquaculture harvester permits or registration cards for specific offenses, including illegal harvesting from closed or unauthorized areas and failing to meet health-related delivery requirements. It establishes a formal hearing process for such actions and permits sole leaseholders whose credentials are revoked to follow a specific timeline to remove gear or transfer their lease to another party.
stakeholders: Shellfish aquaculture harvester permit holders, registration card holders, and shellfish aquaculture leaseholders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 to cover the costs of administrative hearings, which are estimated at 3,500 dollars per hearing. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly provides for judicial review of the Department of Natural Resources' final decisions regarding the suspension or revocation of permits, which involves the state's judicial system managed by the AOC.
The bill codifies a violation of the Maryland Department of Health's Vibrio Parahaemolyticus Control Plan as specific grounds for the suspension or revocation of a shellfish aquaculture permit.

As the primary agency for managing shellfish aquaculture, DNR is responsible for issuing permits, holding administrative hearings, enforcing suspensions and revocations, and managing the lease transfer process established by the bill.

The bill requires hearings to be conducted in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act for any permit suspension or revocation; the fiscal note identifies that OAH will conduct these hearings at a specific cost per case.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and the Department of Health and would represent the state in any judicial reviews of the administrative decisions made under this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring qualified providers to inform patients of certain information and obtain signed, written informed consent before performing a procedure to terminate a pregnancy.
Title: Public Health - Abortion - Informed Consent
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/19 at 2:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires qualified healthcare providers to inform patients of the nature of an abortion procedure and specific potential risks—including depression, infection, hemorrhage, breast cancer, danger to subsequent pregnancies, infertility, and regret—and to obtain signed, written informed consent prior to performing the procedure.
stakeholders: Patients seeking abortion services and qualified health care providers authorized to perform abortions in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact. Small business qualified providers whose practices include performing abortions may experience a meaningful impact to ensure compliance with the bill's informed consent and record-keeping requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article and sets specific medical practice requirements for 'qualified providers'. The Maryland Department of Health oversees public health services and regulates health care professionals and facilities, making it the primary agency responsible for the policy area addressed by the bill.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel to the Department of Health and the various health occupation boards. It would be responsible for defending the state in any legal challenges to the informed consent requirements and advising boards on enforcement of these new regulations.

If a qualified provider's license is challenged for failure to comply with these statutory informed consent requirements, the resulting contested case would likely be heard by an Administrative Law Judge within this office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office administers medical malpractice claims. Because the bill mandates specific disclosures to ensure informed consent, a provider's failure to follow these procedures could form the basis for medical malpractice litigation, which is initially processed through this office.

The University System of Maryland operates academic medical centers and student health services that employ 'qualified providers'. These providers would be required to comply with the new informed consent and record-keeping protocols.

The MHCC is responsible for planning for the state's health system needs and improving the quality and accountability of health services. This bill introduces new regulatory standards for clinical practice that fall within the scope of their system-wide health policy oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS provides medical services to justice-involved individuals. If procedures to terminate a pregnancy are performed within state correctional facilities or through their medical contractors, those providers would be subject to these informed consent requirements.

The MIA monitors the financial stability of professional liability insurers. This bill adds specific statutory duties for medical providers, which may impact the risk profiles and claims handled by medical malpractice insurance carriers regulated by this agency.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and coordinates policy initiatives. This bill introduces a significant shift in public health policy regarding reproductive services that would require executive coordination.

As a state-operated institution with student health services, Morgan State University's health providers would need to comply with the bill's informed consent requirements if they perform or facilitate such procedures.
As an independent state unit providing student health services, the college would need to ensure its health providers follow the bill's protocols for informed consent and medical record maintenance.

Synopsis: Requiring a medical examiner in receipt of notice that a deceased individual was Muslim to release the body of the deceased within 48 hours after the completion of the autopsy.
Title: Medical Examiner - Release of Body - Requirements for Muslims
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill requires a medical examiner to release the body of a deceased Muslim individual within 48 hours after the completion of an autopsy, provided the medical examiner receives notice of the individual's faith through specific documentation, such as a will, notice from next of kin, or confirmation from an imam or mosque.
responsible_party: Medical Examiners and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Muslim residents of Maryland, their families and next of kin, imams, mosques, and state or local medical examiners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the provided text does not include the formal Fiscal Note. The bill mandates a 48-hour timeline for the release of bodies of deceased Muslim individuals following an autopsy, which is expected to have a minimal fiscal or administrative impact on state or local government operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (OCME), which is the agency directly responsible for performing autopsies and releasing deceased individuals. This bill mandates specific timeframes for the OCME to release the bodies of deceased Muslims.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Health. It would be responsible for advising the medical examiner on the legal sufficiency of the various forms of notice described in the bill and ensuring compliance with religious freedom laws.

The GOCI manages faith-based commissions and coordinates between the state government and religious communities. It may be involved in establishing standards or communication protocols between the medical examiner and imams or mosques as specified in the bill.

The Register of Wills is the state entity responsible for the safekeeping and probate of wills. Since a will is a primary document used to notify the medical examiner of the deceased's religious status, this agency may be involved in verifying such documents.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and its units, including the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, ensuring that statutory mandates regarding the treatment of deceased residents are implemented.

Synopsis: Authorizing the people to petition to a vote a proposal to add to, amend, and repeal the public general laws or the Maryland Constitution under certain circumstances and establishing the Initiative process; and requiring that the amendment be submitted to the qualified voters of the State at the next general election in November 2026 for adoption or rejection.
Title: Election Law - Initiative Process
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to establish an initiative process in Maryland, allowing voters to petition for the addition, repeal, or amendment of public general laws or the State Constitution. To qualify for a ballot, a petition must be signed by at least 10% of the number of voters who cast ballots in the most recent gubernatorial election, with no more than 50% of signers residing in any single county or Baltimore City. Once certified by the Secretary of State, proposals are submitted to voters at a general election; laws require a simple majority to pass, while constitutional changes require a two-thirds majority.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State, Office of the Attorney General, and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Registered voters of Maryland, the Maryland General Assembly, the Secretary of State, and State and local boards of elections
fiscal_impact_summary: If voters approve the constitutional amendment in November 2026, State and local expenditures will increase to manage petition processing, signature verification, and ballot production. While total costs depend on the number and complexity of initiatives, the Department of Legislative Services provides an illustrative estimate that additional ballot cards could increase costs by $240,000 (split equally between the State and local governments). Local boards of elections would also incur indeterminate personnel costs to verify approximately 201,000 signatures per petition within the required 20-day window.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires that the Governor determine the number of votes cast for and against an initiative proposal and issue a proclamation declaring successful proposals effective. The Governor also has the authority, with legal advice, to resolve irreconcilable conflicts between competing successful initiatives.

As the primary agency for election administration, the State Board of Elections is responsible for assisting petition sponsors, coordinating signature verification with local boards, and managing the significant ballot printing and mailing costs associated with statewide initiative questions.

The bill mandates that the Attorney General approve the accuracy of any summary included in an initiative petition. Additionally, the Attorney General provides legal advice to the Governor regarding whether successful initiative proposals are in irreconcilable conflict.

The Secretary of State is the primary administrative entity for the initiative process, responsible for receiving the text of proposals, accepting the filing of petitions, and certifying proposals for a vote once signature requirements are met.

Synopsis: Stating the authority to construct, permit, and operate in the State an energy generating system that produces energy from natural gas; authorizing investor-owned electric companies and electricity suppliers in the State to construct, acquire, or lease, and operate, their own generating facilities and construct, acquire, or lease, and operate, certain transmission facilities; authorizing certain investor-owned electric companies to recover certain investments and costs in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Energy Generation and Transmission
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Renewable Energy Sources -see also- Geotherm; Solar; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the construction and operation of natural gas power plants in Maryland. It permits investor-owned electric companies and electricity suppliers to build, own, or lease their own generation and transmission facilities. The legislation establishes a process for utility companies to recover their investments and costs through customer electricity rates or surcharges, provided certain conditions are met, such as obtaining a favorable credit rating assessment for large-scale projects. It also expresses legislative support for nuclear energy and calls for faster grid connection processes for new thermal power sources.
stakeholders: Investor-owned electric companies, electricity suppliers, residential and commercial utility customers, and PJM Interconnection, LLC.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill allows investor-owned electric companies to recover 'all prudently incurred' generation and transmission costs, including capital, operation, and fuel costs, through electricity rates or nonbypassable surcharges. This creates a mechanism for significant infrastructure investment funded by ratepayers. While the bill text does not provide specific dollar estimates for state revenues or expenditures, it establishes a regulatory framework for utility-led energy generation that would be overseen by the Public Service Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body for public utilities in Maryland. This bill directly amends the Public Utilities Article, granting the PSC new authorities and responsibilities regarding the permitting, construction, and operation of natural gas and nuclear generating facilities, as well as overseeing cost recovery through electric rates and nonbypassable surcharges.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the statutory advocate for residential utility consumers. Since the bill allows investor-owned utilities to recover generation and transmission costs through rates and surcharges, the OPC would be heavily involved in representing consumer interests in the resulting PSC proceedings.

The MEA is the state's lead agency for energy policy and planning. The bill's significant shifts in energy generation policy—specifically the explicit authorization of natural gas facilities and support for nuclear energy—directly impact the MEA's mission to coordinate energy planning and advise the Governor and General Assembly.

The MDE is responsible for enforcing state and federal environmental laws. The construction and operation of new natural gas or nuclear power plants authorized by this bill would require significant environmental permitting for air emissions, water use, and potential hazardous waste management.

The DNR, through its Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), conducts the scientific and environmental reviews of power plant applications for Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN). The bill's promotion of new thermal and nuclear generation would increase the DNR's workload in reviewing these projects.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and other state agencies. The new regulatory frameworks for cost recovery, credit rating assessments, and utility-owned generation proposed in the bill would require significant legal oversight and potential representation in litigation.

The bill establishes significant new state policies regarding energy independence and specific support for nuclear and natural gas power. As the office responsible for overseeing policy initiatives and the executive branch, this impacts the Governor's energy and environmental agenda.

The MCEC's mission is to advance clean energy and energy efficiency. While natural gas is a fossil fuel, the bill explicitly categorizes nuclear energy as 'clean energy' and supports its development, which aligns with the financing and promotional role of the MCEC.

The Department of Planning coordinates land use and resource management. The construction of major new generation and transmission infrastructure involves significant land use planning and impacts on state development visions.

Large-scale energy infrastructure projects, such as the natural gas and nuclear facilities promoted in this bill, are significant drivers of economic development and capital investment in the state, which falls under the purview of the Department of Commerce.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a candidate for certain State offices and a person acting on behalf of a candidate for certain State offices from participating in certain campaign finance activities during a regular session of the General Assembly.
Title: Election Law - Campaign Finance Activities - Candidates for State Office
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands existing prohibitions on campaign finance activities during a regular session of the Maryland General Assembly to include candidates for the offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Comptroller, State Treasurer, and member of the General Assembly. Prohibited activities include receiving, soliciting, or depositing contributions and conducting fundraising events.
stakeholders: Candidates for State office, campaign finance entities, and individuals acting on behalf of candidates.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may result in an indeterminate increase in State revenue to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund from civil penalties collected for violations of the fundraising prohibition. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for supervising elections and managing campaign finance compliance. This bill expands the existing session-fundraising ban to include all candidates for specified State offices, an area of law administered and enforced by the Board.

The Governor is specifically listed as an individual subject to the bill's expanded campaign finance prohibitions. As the executive head of the state, changes to the Governor's ability to conduct fundraising during the legislative session directly impact the office's principal.
The Lieutenant Governor is explicitly named in the legislation as an official subject to the restricted campaign finance activities during the General Assembly's regular session.

The Comptroller is one of the five constitutional officers directly impacted by the bill's prohibition on receiving, soliciting, or depositing campaign contributions while the legislature is in session.

The State Treasurer is explicitly listed as an individual subject to the bill's fundraising restrictions. The agency's principal would be directly regulated by the new candidate-specific prohibitions.

The Attorney General is a subject of the legislation. Furthermore, as the chief legal officer for the state, the agency provides counsel on the interpretation and enforcement of the Election Law article amended by this bill.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting offenses related to the integrity of state officials and the electoral process, specifically including the enforcement of state election laws and session-fundraising bans.

The Office of Administrative Hearings provides an impartial forum for contested cases involving state agencies; it would be the venue for any appeals of civil penalties issued for violations of these campaign finance restrictions.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person charged with murder or manslaughter in any degree or a crime under Title 3, Subtitle 2 of the Criminal Law Article to assert the defense that the person acted in self-defense and need not prove that the person believed danger was imminent or immediate if the victim had previously committed a certain act against the person.
Title: Criminal Law - Self-Defense - Prior Acts by Victim
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the requirements for asserting a self-defense claim in criminal cases involving murder, manslaughter, or assault. It allows a defendant to claim self-defense without proving they believed danger was imminent or immediate if the victim had previously committed an assault or sexually assaultive behavior against them.
stakeholders: Criminal defendants who were previously victimized by their alleged victims, the Maryland court system, State's Attorneys, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text, and the bill does not contain explicit financial implications such as fee changes or appropriations. Therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the legal standards for self-defense in criminal cases, which directly affects judicial proceedings, jury instructions, and the adjudication of violent crimes within the Maryland court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill significantly impacts the defense strategies available to indigent clients charged with murder, manslaughter, or assault, as it expands the statutory defense of self-defense based on prior acts by the victim.

The OAG represents the state in criminal appeals and provides legal counsel to state agencies; changes to the elements of self-defense will likely lead to extensive appellate litigation and require updated legal guidance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy; this bill represents a significant change to the Maryland criminal code and self-defense jurisprudence.
DJS oversees youth charged with violent offenses, including assault and manslaughter; the modified self-defense standard would apply to youth in the juvenile justice system.

As the primary law enforcement agency investigating violent crimes, the change in the self-defense standard may impact evidence collection and investigation protocols concerning prior relationships between suspects and victims.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Changes to criminal defense statutes can affect trial outcomes, potentially influencing conviction rates and the resulting population and management of correctional facilities.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives; this bill involves a major policy shift in criminal law that requires executive branch coordination and review.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Administrator of Elections to provide certain additional notice to voters using certain methods if there is an occurrence of federal judicial action regarding the timely receipt of absentee ballots with federal contests that preempts certain State law and regulations.
Title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - Notice of Timely Receipt
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Administrator of Elections to provide additional notice to Maryland voters if federal judicial action changes the requirements for the timely receipt of absentee ballots for federal contests. The notice must inform voters of the requirements for both federal and state/local contests and encourage them to mail their ballots at least one week before election day or use an official ballot drop box. The Administrator must use multiple communication methods, including written instructions with ballots, social media campaigns, and mass media communications.
stakeholders: Maryland voters using absentee ballots
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates an indeterminate increase in State expenditures for the State Board of Elections to conduct mass media and social media campaigns and to provide updated written notice with ballots. This spending is contingent upon an occurrence of federal judicial action that preempts state regulations. No specific dollar estimates are provided in the bill text, and a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the source.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Administrator of Elections, who leads the Maryland State Board of Elections, to provide additional voter notices and manage media campaigns in response to federal judicial actions that preempt state absentee ballot regulations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state agencies and would be responsible for determining if a federal judicial action triggers the notice requirements by preempting current state regulations.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures; it would likely be required to review and approve any emergency procurement contracts for the mandated mass media and social media campaigns.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the state's fiscal planning and budget execution, which would be affected by the costs associated with the required mass media and social media communications.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates state policy initiatives, including the emergency responses to federal legal changes that impact state election procedures.

Synopsis: Authorizing a law enforcement agency to impound a motor vehicle for which three or more citations from an automated traffic enforcement system have been issued if the citations are unpaid and overdue by at least 30 days.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Automated Traffic Enforcement Systems - Impoundment
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes law enforcement agencies to impound a motor vehicle if it has three or more unpaid and overdue civil citations issued by automated traffic enforcement systems, such as speed monitoring, red-light cameras, or school bus cameras. Impoundment is permitted only as a secondary action during a traffic stop for a different suspected violation or if the vehicle is already parked.
stakeholders: Owners of motor vehicles with multiple unpaid automated traffic citations, law enforcement agencies, and Maryland local and state governments operating traffic enforcement systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Financial implications include the potential increase in state and local revenue from the collection of delinquent traffic fines and possible administrative costs for law enforcement agencies related to vehicle impoundment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's primary law enforcement agency, the State Police are responsible for enforcing traffic laws on state highways and would be directly authorized to impound vehicles under this bill's criteria.
MDOT is the umbrella agency for the MVA, SHA, MTA, MDTA, and MAA, all of which are involved in traffic enforcement, vehicle registration, and the management of automated enforcement systems.
The MVA manages vehicle titling and registration. Effective implementation would require MVA records to identify vehicles with three or more unpaid and overdue citations for impoundment.
MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains a police force that utilizes automated enforcement systems and would have the authority to impound vehicles.
The bill explicitly references bus lane monitoring systems, which the MTA operates. The MTA Police would be authorized to impound vehicles violating these and other traffic laws.
SHA manages the state's non-toll highways and is responsible for many of the automated monitoring systems mentioned in the bill, such as work zone speed control systems.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on the implementation of new enforcement authorities and would represent the state in any constitutional challenges to the impoundment law.
The judicial branch handles the adjudication of civil citations. Changes in enforcement mechanisms for unpaid citations may impact court caseloads and administrative processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy, which includes new tools for traffic law enforcement.
MCSS oversees school bus monitoring cameras, which are included in the definition of automated traffic enforcement systems subject to this bill.
OAH may be tasked with hearing administrative appeals from vehicle owners regarding the legality of vehicle impoundments performed by state agencies.
DBM oversees the fiscal impact on state law enforcement agencies that must integrate these impoundment procedures into their operations, including potential staffing and technology costs.
MSDE oversees the local school systems that implement school bus monitoring cameras, one of the enforcement systems used to trigger impoundment.
DGS manages the Maryland Capitol Police, who have law enforcement authority and may be involved in impounding vehicles on or around state property.
DoIT may be involved in the data integration required between the MVA, law enforcement agencies, and the courts to track and flag vehicles with multiple unpaid citations.
DNR's Natural Resources Police enforce laws on public lands and state parks, where they could encounter and impound vehicles with outstanding citations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD provides legal representation to indigent individuals, who may require defense or advocacy regarding the secondary detention actions leading to vehicle impoundment.
Member institutions within the USM have their own campus police departments that would be authorized to use this impoundment authority.
Morgan State University maintains its own police force with law enforcement authority to impound vehicles on and near its campus.
The college maintains its own law enforcement presence that would be authorized to exercise the impoundment powers granted by this bill.
The MAA operates its own police force at BWI and Martin State airports, where they may identify and impound vehicles with excessive unpaid citations.
MPA manages port police who enforce traffic and safety laws at maritime terminals and would have authority to impound vehicles under this bill.
MCCR may monitor the implementation of impoundment policies for potential disparate impact on protected classes.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including major changes to law enforcement and traffic safety protocols.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct certain prevalence studies concerning problem and pathological mobile gambling, with an initial study to be completed on or before July 1, 2031; requiring the Secretary of Health, on or before November 1 each year, beginning in 2027, to submit a report to the General Assembly on how the funds in the Problem Gambling Fund have been expended on treatment and prevention programs; and altering the distribution of certain fantasy competition and sports wagering proceeds.
Title: Gaming - Problem Gambling - Prevalence Study and Fund Revenue
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct prevalence studies on mobile gambling, with an initial study due by July 1, 2031, and subsequent updates every five years. It increases revenue for the Problem Gambling Fund by redirecting 1% of proceeds from fantasy competitions and sports wagering, which reduces the share previously retained by gaming operators. Additionally, the bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit annual reports on the expenditure of these funds for gambling treatment and prevention programs starting in 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Individuals affected by problem gambling, fantasy competition operators, sports wagering facility and mobile licensees, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill redirects 1% of proceeds from fantasy competitions and sports wagering to the Problem Gambling Fund, increasing state funding for gambling treatment programs while decreasing revenues for gaming operators and potentially the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund. The Maryland Department of Health will incur costs for conducting the mandated mobile gambling prevalence studies every five years. Specific dollar estimates were not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Health to conduct prevalence studies on mobile gambling, manage grants for problem gambling services, and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding the Problem Gambling Fund's expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency, acting as the Commission, is responsible for collecting proceeds from fantasy competitions and sports wagering and distributing a new 1% share of these revenues to the Problem Gambling Fund as mandated by the bill.

The Comptroller is designated as the official with control over sports wagering proceeds and receives accountings from the Commission regarding all revenue generated under the sports wagering and fantasy competition subtitles.

The bill reduces the percentage of gambling proceeds distributed to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund (which supports the state's education system) by diverting 1% of those funds to the Problem Gambling Fund.

As the state's chief financial agency responsible for the management and protection of state funds, the Treasurer's Office would oversee the distribution and investment of the modified gambling revenue streams.

As the principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for supervising budget execution and would be involved in the long-term fiscal planning necessitated by the reallocation of gambling revenues.

Synopsis: Allowing a credit against the State income tax for qualified employers who provide certain paid organ donation leave to eligible employees; allowing a qualified employer to carry over any excess credit to certain taxable years; and applying the Act to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Credit for Paid Organ Donation Leave
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows qualified employers to claim a State income tax credit for providing paid organ donation leave to eligible employees. The credit equals 100% of the wages paid to an employee during the first 12 weeks of organ donation leave, provided the leave is in addition to other leave benefits and the employer pays 100% of the employee's regular wages during the period.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Comptroller
stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees who donate organs for transplantation
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a decrease in State income tax revenue due to the creation of the tax credit for paid organ donation leave. While the bill text outlines the mechanics of the credit, including a three-year carry-forward provision, specific dollar estimates of the revenue loss are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly defines 'Department' as the Maryland Department of Health. It tasks the agency with receiving applications, verifying eligibility for organ donation leave, issuing tax credit certificates to qualified employers, and reporting to the Comptroller.

As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for administering the income tax credit, receiving reports from the Department of Health, and jointly adopting regulations to implement the program.

The bill references Title 8.3 of the Labor and Employment Article regarding paid leave benefits, and the new tax credit directly impacts workplace leave policies which the Department of Labor regulates.
The bill creates a new income tax credit which will have a fiscal impact on state revenues. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Comptroller during the drafting of regulations and the implementation of this new tax credit program.
The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Health, which is the primary implementing agency for the new credit.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees general fiscal matters and state contracts that could be affected by tax revenue changes.
The OAH may be required to adjudicate disputes if the Department of Health denies a tax credit certificate application to an employer.

Synopsis: Requiring an owner or operator of a large-scale data center to submit a disclosure report to certain State and local agencies and elected officials under certain circumstances; specifying the contents of the disclosure report; requiring the Department of the Environment to publish the disclosure report on its website within 30 days of receiving the report; requiring, by June 30, 2027, each local jurisdiction with a population of at least 10,000 residents to adopt by local law a large-scale data center plan; etc.
Title: Data Center Planning and Transparency Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.
