bill_summary: This bill designates "The Heart of Maryland," written by Jayla Elise from Dorchester County for the Maryland 250 Project, as the official State song of Maryland.
stakeholders: Residents of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no effect on State or local finances. Designating a State song does not require any specific financial allocations or generate revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for government records and is responsible for maintaining the official list of State symbols and the Maryland Manual, both of which must be updated to reflect the new State song.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The song was written for the Maryland 250 Project, which is managed by the Maryland 250 Commission, a body authorized via Executive Order and classified under this agency umbrella.
The Governor oversaw the creation of the Maryland 250 Commission via Executive Order 01.01.2023.10 and is responsible for the official adoption and symbolic use of state emblems.
As the custodian of official records and laws, the Secretary of State manages the registration of the Great Seal and other official state designations.

Maryland Public Television (MPT) frequently produces and broadcasts educational and cultural content regarding Maryland's history and heritage, which would naturally include the performance and dissemination of a new official State song.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and executive agencies regarding the statutory changes required to renumber sections of the General Provisions Article.

Synopsis: Providing an exemption from the sales and use tax for certain construction material or warehousing equipment that is purchased for use in the Mount Aetna Technology Park in Washington County; requiring the buyer to maintain for at least 3 years after the date of sale a record of the amount of tax that was not paid as a result of the exemption; and requiring on or before December 31, 2027, that the Comptroller submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly on the aggregate amount of tax not paid due to the exemption.
Title: Washington County - Sales and Use Tax Exemption - Target Redevelopment Area
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 731

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill provides a 10-year State sales and use tax exemption for construction materials and warehousing equipment purchased for use in the Mount Aetna Technology Park, a designated target redevelopment area in Washington County. It requires buyers to maintain records and report the amount of tax not paid to the Comptroller, who must then report aggregate data to the Governor and General Assembly.
stakeholders: Property owners, developers, and businesses located within the Mount Aetna Technology Park in Washington County; construction contractors; and warehousing operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues will decrease by an indeterminate amount from fiscal 2027 through 2036. The exact fiscal impact depends on the volume and value of construction materials and warehousing equipment purchased for the redevelopment area. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the sales and use tax exemption. The bill requires the Comptroller to issue evidence of eligibility to buyers and to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding the aggregate amount of tax not paid due to the exemption.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is relevant because the bill provides a targeted tax incentive designed to attract business and stimulate redevelopment within the Mount Aetna Technology Park in Washington County.

The bill will result in an indeterminate decrease in State general fund and special fund revenues from fiscal 2027 through 2036, which directly impacts the department's responsibilities for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and receives the annual report from the Comptroller regarding the fiscal impact of the tax exemption. The Governor also approved the legislation.

The bill defines the target redevelopment area based on specific zoning districts (office, research, and industry), which falls under the department's focus on sustainable growth, land use planning, and community revitalization.

MEDCO's mission is to assist in the retention, expansion, and attraction of business and industry. This bill provides a specific financial incentive (tax exemption) to support the development of a technology park, aligning with MEDCO's focus on economic prosperity.

bill_summary: This bill extends eligibility for Maryland job creation and property tax credits and exemptions to members, veterans, and surviving spouses of the U.S. Space Force. It establishes a uniform definition of active military, naval, air, or space service to ensure Space Force members receive the same tax incentives as other branches of the armed forces.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, Department of Commerce, and State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Members, veterans, and surviving spouses of the U.S. Space Force, and Maryland businesses hiring qualified veterans.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is assumed to have no material effect on State or local finances. While it expands eligibility for existing tax incentive programs, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit (capped at 4,000,000 dollars annually), the overall fiscal impact is expected to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly amends the principal statute governing the department (State Government Section 9-901) to include the Space Force in the definition of active military service and veterans. The department is the primary agency responsible for advocating for and assisting veterans and their families in securing state benefits, including the tax incentives modified by this bill.
The bill applies Space Force service to the Job Creation Tax Credit, which is administered by the Department of Commerce as the state's primary economic development and financial assistance agency.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for processing income tax incentives like the Job Creation Tax Credit and ensuring compliance with the updated definitions for military-related tax benefits.

This agency adjudicates disputes regarding property tax exemptions and credits. The bill modifies eligibility criteria for several property tax benefits for disabled veterans and surviving spouses, which falls under the board's appellate jurisdiction.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, including those involving property tax credits and exemptions or decisions made by the Comptroller regarding tax incentives.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department and the Governor's senior military advisor, the Adjutant General is responsible for the oversight and classification of state military personnel, which is directly impacted by the bill's expansion of military service definitions to include the Space Force.
The bill updates definitions for uniformed services and active military duty, which applies to the personnel and mission readiness standards managed by the Maryland National Guard.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and signs the legislation into law; the bill aligns with executive policy priorities regarding military and veteran affairs.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors tax incentives and their impact on state revenue and budget execution.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies involved in implementing these tax changes, including the Comptroller, Commerce, and the Department of Veterans and Military Families.

Synopsis: Establishing an exception to the prohibition against operating or riding on a motorcycle without certain protective headgear for an individual at least 21 years old who has been licensed to operate a motorcycle for at least 2 years or has completed a certain motorcycle safety course and for the individual's passenger.
Title: Motorcycles - Protective Headgear Requirement - Exception (In Remembrance of Gary "Pappy" Boward)
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 1/28 at 11:00 a.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill creates an exception to the requirement that motorcycle operators and passengers wear protective headgear. The exception applies to individuals who are at least 21 years old and have either been licensed to operate a motorcycle for at least two years or have completed an approved motorcycle rider safety course. The exemption also extends to passengers riding with an operator who meets these criteria.
stakeholders: Motorcycle operators and passengers at least 21 years of age, law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues from traffic citations are expected to decrease minimally beginning in FY 2027. While a specific dollar estimate is unavailable, for context, 218 citations for helmet violations were issued in FY 2025 with a prepayment penalty of $110. The bill may also result in a negligible increase in Medicaid expenditures due to potential increases in serious head injuries resulting from reduced helmet use.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts traffic citation volume and the adjudication of motorcycle-related violations. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support for the judicial branch, which handles the resulting fine revenue and case processing mentioned in the fiscal note.

The fiscal note identifies a potential increase in Medicaid expenditures if the lack of protective headgear leads to more serious head injuries for crash-involved motorcyclists who are covered by the state's Medicaid program.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and highway safety initiatives, both of which are directly impacted by changes to motorcycle helmet requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees the state's trauma centers and EMS network. The bill's impact on head injuries from motorcycle crashes directly affects the trauma system's operational data and patient care workload, as evidenced by the trauma center data provided in the fiscal note.

Maryland State Police is the primary agency responsible for enforcing traffic safety and motor vehicle laws on state highways. This bill changes the enforcement criteria for motorcycle helmet requirements.

The bill assigns specific responsibilities to the MVA Administrator, including approving motorcycle rider safety courses, establishing headgear standards, and maintaining lists of approved protective equipment.

bill_summary: This bill requires Prince George’s Community College to perform a comprehensive feasibility study and program design assessment for establishing aerospace and aviation systems technology workforce training programs. The study will examine workforce demand, industry needs, curriculum requirements, facility and equipment costs, and potential partnerships, with a final report due by December 1, 2027.
stakeholders: Prince George’s Community College students and faculty, private sector aerospace and aviation employers, the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Prince George’s County Economic Development Corporation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in fiscal 2027 (as included in the budget passed by the General Assembly) and $100,000 in fiscal 2028 (mandated by this bill). Prince George’s Community College revenues and expenditures will increase by the same amounts to conduct the feasibility study and assessment. Other state agencies can consult using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill contains a mandated appropriation for fiscal year 2028, requiring the Governor to include $100,000 in the annual budget bill for the Prince George's Community College feasibility study.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for budget development and will oversee the $100,000 mandated appropriation for the study in the fiscal year 2028 budget.

The bill explicitly requires Prince George's Community College to consult with the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission, which is housed within the Department of Commerce, to conduct the workforce demand analysis and study.
MSDE is listed as an information source in the fiscal note. The program design assessment includes evaluating pathways from high school to college and careers in aerospace technology.
The bill explicitly requires Prince George's Community College to consult with the Maryland Department of Labor regarding workforce development, labor markets, and apprenticeship opportunities.
The bill requires consultation with state workforce development entities to align the proposed programs with regional labor market needs.

The commission is the state's central regulatory body for postsecondary education. The fiscal note identifies it as a consulting entity for the study, and any resulting degree or certificate programs would require commission approval.

As the state's central regulatory board for higher education, the agency is responsible for overseeing community college programs and is identified in the fiscal note as a consulting body for the feasibility study.

Synopsis: Requiring a grant from the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund to provide opportunities to participate in certain water-dependent activities for eligible companions of individuals with disabilities or service-disabled veterans; and defining "eligible companion" as an accompanying family member or direct support professional of an individual with disabilities or of a service-disabled veteran participating in sailing, boating, kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding, or surfing activities.
Title: Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund - Eligible Companions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 654
bill_summary: This bill expands the scope of the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund to include 'eligible companions'—family members or direct support professionals—of individuals with disabilities or service-disabled veterans. This allows grants from the fund to be used to provide water-dependent recreational opportunities, such as sailing and kayaking, to these companions when accompanying the primary participants.
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities, service-disabled veterans, their family members, direct support professionals, and nonprofit organizations providing water-dependent recreational activities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct state or local fiscal impact as the changes are considered technical in nature. While the bill expands the population eligible to participate in activities funded by the Individuals with Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, it does not increase the maximum grant amount of $40,000 per fiscal year per grantee. According to the Maryland Department of Disabilities, the fund has not yet received an appropriation, and grants are allocated as lump sums rather than on a per-person basis.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Disabilities is the primary agency responsible for administering the Individuals With Disabilities and Service–Disabled Veterans Boating Fund and overseeing the grant process established by this bill.

This bill directly concerns opportunities for service-disabled veterans and their companions to participate in water-dependent activities, aligning with the department's mission to support and advocate for veterans' benefits.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Individuals With Disabilities and Service–Disabled Veterans Boating Fund separately from other state funds.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Individuals With Disabilities and Service–Disabled Veterans Boating Fund.
As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM is involved because the fund consists of money appropriated in the state budget.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signed the bill into law; the primary implementing agency (MDOD) is a cabinet-level department under the Governor's direction.

Synopsis: Authorizing a police officer who is denied a certain right to apply to the circuit court at a certain time for an order that directs the law enforcement agency to show cause why the right should not be granted.
Title: Police Discipline - Order to Show Cause
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/31 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Police Conduct -see also- Ethics; Law Enforcement

bill_summary: This bill authorizes a police officer who is denied a right related to police accountability and discipline to apply to a circuit court for an order requiring their law enforcement agency to show cause why the right should not be granted. This legal remedy is available when the denial of the right is not eligible to be addressed through a trial board proceeding.
responsible_party: Maryland Circuit Courts and Law Enforcement Agencies
stakeholders: Police officers, State and local law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland Circuit Court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material impact on State or local government operations or finances. The Fiscal Note indicates that applications for show-cause hearings in the circuit courts are expected to be few in number.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new legal remedy by authorizing police officers to apply to the circuit court for an order to show cause. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which will be responsible for handling these new filings and proceedings.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is a major employer of police officers whose disciplinary procedures are governed by the statutes this bill amends. It would be the primary respondent in show cause applications filed by its officers.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for state agencies. It would be responsible for representing statewide and bi-county law enforcement agencies in circuit court when an officer applies for a show cause order.
The department operates the Natural Resources Police, a major state law enforcement body. Its officers are subject to the disciplinary and accountability laws addressed in this bill.
MDOT oversees the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) Police and other modal security units. Its officers are entitled to the procedural rights and remedies provided in this bill.
The MDTA maintains its own nationally accredited police force. As an independent state agency with sworn police officers, it is directly impacted by changes to police disciplinary court procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs various sworn officers and investigators within its intelligence and internal affairs units who are subject to the statewide police accountability and discipline process.
DGS manages the Maryland Capitol Police. The bill affects the procedural rights of these officers during disciplinary matters and the agency's legal obligations in circuit court.
The Comptroller's office includes a field enforcement division with sworn officers who fall under the state's police accountability framework and would be eligible for the bill's judicial remedies.
Member institutions of the University System of Maryland maintain campus police departments. These officers are state employees subject to the disciplinary statutes modified by this bill.
As a state agency with its own police department, Morgan State is an employer of police officers who would be entitled to use the bill's show cause application process.
The college maintains its own police force and is recognized as a state agency whose officers are subject to the police discipline laws referenced in the bill.
The department employs various investigators and sworn personnel who may be categorized as police officers under the Public Safety Article, making the agency subject to these court proceedings.

Synopsis: Repealing the Maryland estate tax; and applying the Act to decedents dying after June 30, 2026.
Title: Maryland Estate Tax - Repeal
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 1/21 at 10:00 a.m.
bill_summary: This bill repeals the Maryland estate tax for the estates of individuals who die on or after July 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Estates and beneficiaries of individuals dying on or after July 1, 2026; the Maryland Comptroller's Office.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $44,000,000 in FY 2027 and $182,500,000 in FY 2028, with annual revenue losses projected to reach $193,800,000 by FY 2031. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller’s Office may decrease minimally due to reduced administrative and auditing requirements. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering, collecting, and auditing the Maryland estate tax. The bill's repeal of this tax directly removes one of the agency's core revenue collection functions and, according to the fiscal note, will lead to a decrease in administrative expenditures and the redirection of auditing staff.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The repeal of the estate tax represents a significant loss of general fund revenue (estimated at over $190 million annually by FY 2031), which directly impacts the agency's core mission of developing and managing the state budget.

The Register of Wills is responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. The Maryland estate tax is closely linked to inheritance taxes through statutory credits, and the Register of Wills is a primary information source for estate-related tax data. The repeal simplifies the tax landscape for the estates they manage.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the annual state budget and coordinating major policy initiatives. A repeal of a major tax with a significant revenue impact requires executive-level policy direction and necessitates adjustments to the Governor's long-term fiscal strategies and budget proposals.

The State Treasurer's Office manages the state's cash flow, deposits, and investments. Significant reductions in general fund revenue from the estate tax repeal affect the Treasurer's anticipation of the state's monetary needs and the management of state funds.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes involving state taxes, including the estate tax. Repealing the tax will eventually eliminate the court's caseload related to estate tax appeals, representing a shift in its judicial workload.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the transition, handling any lingering litigation from previous tax years, and ensuring the repeal is implemented in accordance with state law.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts fiscal compliance audits of the Comptroller's Office. The repeal of the estate tax will remove this specific revenue stream from the scope of their future audits of the state's tax collection processes.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of military service to 'uniformed services'—including the U.S. Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration—across various Maryland laws. Key changes include extending trout stamp fee exemptions for residents on leave, broadening eligibility for local government employment hiring credits, and expanding expedited landlord repossession remedies for active service members. Additionally, it updates the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to include fees from specific non-combat-related uniformed services medals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services (including the U.S. Public Health Service and NOAA), veterans, active duty service members, and their families.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources are estimated to decrease by up to $4,400 annually as more individuals qualify for trout stamp exemptions. Other provisions, including those related to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund and local government hiring, are not expected to have a material financial impact on state or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal agency for veterans and military families, this bill directly impacts their operations by expanding the definitions of eligible service members for benefits and altering the composition of the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund.
The bill explicitly modifies the exemptions for trout stamps to include all uniformed services, and the fiscal note indicates a specific decrease in special fund revenues for this department.
The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding military protection orders and modifies procedures for tenant holding over actions in the District Court.
The bill alters the definition of 'federal facility' in the Transportation Article and relates to fees from special registration plates that fund veteran-related initiatives.
The MVA is responsible for the issuance of the special registration plates mentioned in the bill, the fees from which contribute to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund.
The bill modifies the criteria under which veterans may apply to the State Board to obtain a high school diploma by expanding the definition of qualifying service.
The bill updates the definition of 'military protection order' within the Family Law Article, which relates to the department's mandate to assist residents facing abuse and neglect.
The bill specifically includes the Maryland National Guard in the updated statutory definitions for military protection orders.
As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General oversees the forces specifically named in the bill's updated definitions of military protection orders.

As the state's chief financial officer and revenue collector, the Comptroller is involved in the collection of fees for the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund and the oversight of licensing revenues like trout stamps.
The Treasurer manages and protects state funds, including the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund whose composition is altered by this bill.
The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to the various state agencies implementing the bill's expanded definitions of 'uniformed services' across multiple legal articles.
The Governor oversees the executive branch departments affected by these policy changes and is responsible for the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund within the Executive Department.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors the fiscal impacts described in the bill, such as the revenue changes for the Department of Natural Resources.

Synopsis: Providing for the designation of the Carroll Creek, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, and Herring Run watersheds as interjurisdictional flood hazard watersheds for certain planning purposes.
Title: Environment - Interjurisdictional Watersheds - Flood Management
Status: In the House - Hearing 4/02 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: The bill designates specific watersheds—Carroll Creek, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, Herring Run, and the Patapsco River (including their headwaters and tributaries)—as interjurisdictional flood hazard watersheds. This designation requires that flood management plans for these areas be developed in coordination with the Maryland Department of the Environment and reviewed as a unified plan across the involved local jurisdictions.
stakeholders: Local governments in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick City, Frederick County, Howard County, Carroll County, and Anne Arundel County; property owners and developers within the designated watersheds.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) indicates that the bill will have no material fiscal impact, as the designations largely align with existing state stormwater regulations. However, the Department of Legislative Services notes that if the codification is interpreted to require new watershed studies or updated flood management plans, local jurisdictions could incur significant costs, estimated between $250,000 and $400,000 per plan.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including designating interjurisdictional flood hazard watersheds and reviewing/approving flood management plans and grant requests.
The bill explicitly requires local subdivisions to prepare flood management plans in cooperation with the Department of Planning and other appropriate State agencies.
The bill explicitly requires local subdivisions to prepare flood management plans in cooperation with the Department of Agriculture and other appropriate State agencies.

According to the fiscal note, grant funds requested under the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program for watershed studies and capital projects are subject to the review and approval of the Board of Public Works.
As the principal state agency for emergency preparedness and response, MDEM has a direct interest in flood management planning and is listed as an information source for the fiscal analysis.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies tasked with implementing the bill and is responsible for proposing the state budget, which includes the funding for the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program.
DBM oversees the state's budget and may be involved in the allocation of funds for the grant program and the fiscal impact assessment of required watershed studies and planning.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and other state agencies regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state environmental laws and regulations modified by this bill.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for reviewing and approving the expenditure of state funds related to flood management grants and projects.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer is responsible for reviewing and approving the expenditure of state funds and bond proceeds related to flood management grants.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland political subdivisions and State agencies from charging parking fees to motor vehicles displaying disabled veteran special registration plates at on-street parking meters and State-owned or controlled parking lots.
responsible_party: Maryland State agencies and political subdivisions
stakeholders: Veterans with disabled veteran special registration plates and State and local government entities managing parking facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund revenues will decrease from lost parking fees at MDOT facilities, and expenditures will increase for MDOT to modify automated parking systems or increase staffing. Local government revenues from parking meters are expected to decline minimally. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the number of qualifying vehicles cannot be projected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency overseeing the Transportation Article being amended and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which the fiscal note indicates will see a decrease in revenue and an increase in expenditures for system modifications.
The MVA is the specific unit within MDOT responsible for issuing the disabled veteran special registration plates that trigger the parking fee exemption established by the bill.

MAA operates BWI Marshall Airport and Martin State Airport. The fiscal note explicitly identifies BWI as a site that will lose parking revenue and require costly upgrades to automated parking systems to recognize the new plate exemptions.

MTA operates transit-related parking facilities, including the BWI Marshall Amtrak/MARC station specifically mentioned in the fiscal note as having significant operational and fiscal impacts from the bill.
MPA operates the Cruise Maryland Terminal, which is identified in the fiscal note as a facility that will lose parking revenue due to the mandate for free parking for certain veterans.
DGS manages and maintains state-owned facilities and parking lots for various executive branch agencies, all of which would be prohibited from charging fees to vehicles with the specified plates.

The department is responsible for advocating for veterans' benefits; this bill creates a direct financial benefit for disabled veterans by exempting them from parking fees at state and local facilities.
The USM institutions are state entities that manage extensive parking operations and collect significant revenue from parking fees, which would be reduced by the mandated exemptions.
As a state university with its own parking facilities, Morgan State would be prohibited from charging parking fees to eligible veterans, impacting its revenue streams.
As an independent state college, its parking facilities are subject to the bill's prohibition on charging fees to vehicles with disabled veteran special registration plates.
The Authority manages major state-owned facilities like the Camden Yards Sports Complex, which have significant fee-based parking lots impacted by this bill.
DNR manages state parks and public lands that often charge parking or entry fees; the fiscal note identifies DNR as a source of information regarding the bill's impacts.
MDH operates numerous state facilities and hospitals with public parking lots that would no longer be permitted to charge fees to veterans with the specified plates.
MSP is responsible for traffic and motor vehicle law enforcement and will need to update its procedures to recognize these special plates as exempt from parking citations in state and local lots.
DBM oversees state revenue estimates and fiscal planning; it will be impacted by the reduction in revenue for the Transportation Trust Fund and other agency parking funds.
The department coordinates policies for residents with disabilities; the bill specifically concerns registration plates for service-connected disabled veterans.

Synopsis: Requiring a unit to structure procurement procedures to meet certain federal procurement standards; establishing certain overall percentage goals of the unit's total dollar value of procurement contracts to be made directly or indirectly with historically underutilized business zone businesses in certain years; requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to adopt regulations establishing a certification process and a percentage price preference; and establishing penalties for certain violations.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a procurement preference program for historically underutilized business zone (HUBzone) businesses in Maryland. It requires State agencies to meet specified percentage goals for contracts awarded directly or indirectly to HUBzone businesses, starting at 1% in 2026 and increasing to 3% by 2029. Additionally, it tasks the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs with creating a certification process and price preferences for these businesses while establishing penalties for fraudulent participation.
responsible_party: The Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (within the Department of Social and Economic Mobility)
stakeholders: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBzone) businesses, Maryland State agencies, and State procurement contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, general fund expenditures increase by $85,600 in FY 2027 for the Department of Social and Economic Mobility to hire a Compliance Manager to administer the HUBzone program, with costs rising to $114,800 by FY 2031. Additional costs for other State agencies to manage procurement staff and monitoring are likely but indeterminate. The price preference program may also result in higher State contract prices due to reduced competition, though the exact impact is not yet feasible to estimate. Penalty provisions are not expected to significantly impact State revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks this office with adopting regulations for the certification of HUBzone businesses, establishing price preferences, tracking participation, and reporting annually to the Legislative Policy Committee.

As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is responsible for implementing the procurement goals and preferences established by the bill and was a primary contributor to the feasibility study cited in the fiscal note.

The bill requires state units to report alleged violations to the Board, which then must report them to the Office of the Attorney General. The Board also oversees significant state contracts impacted by these new preference goals.

The bill requires the OAG to receive violation reports from the Board of Public Works and determine whether to bring civil actions. The OAG also provides legal counsel on the regulations and procurement standards required by the bill.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state. The fiscal note identifies a need for general fund expenditures to support the implementation and staffing of the HUBzone program.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller will be responsible for overseeing the reported violations and the fiscal impact of higher contract prices resulting from the new preferences.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer's office participates in the oversight and approval of contracts and the reporting of violations mandated by the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch units required to implement these procurement procedures and is the parent organization for the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs.

The bill applies to state units, and the fiscal note explicitly lists the Administrative Office of the Courts as an affected entity that provided information regarding the bill's impact on judicial operations.

As a major state entity with significant procurement activity, the University System of Maryland is impacted by changes to procurement preferences and was consulted as an information source in the fiscal note.
As an independent state agency with its own procurement authority, Morgan State University is impacted by the bill's requirements and was identified as an information source in the fiscal analysis.
As a public honors college with independent state agency status, it must adhere to state procurement mandates and was listed as an information source for the bill's fiscal impact.
The OLA is responsible for auditing state agencies for fiscal compliance. This bill adds new regulatory requirements and goals that will become part of future compliance audits for state units.
The bill's focus on historically underutilized business zones aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and support small business development in Maryland.

Synopsis: Authorizing a member of the Health Services Cost Review Commission to continue to serve for a period not to exceed 6 months after the expiration of the member's term of office, rather than until a successor is appointed and qualifies; and repealing the authority of a member of the Commission who was appointed after a term began to serve until a successor is appointed and qualifies.

bill_summary: The bill limits the amount of time a member of the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) may continue to serve after their official term expires to a maximum of eight months. It also repeals the provision that allowed members appointed mid-term to serve until a successor is qualified, restricting their service to the remainder of the specific term.
stakeholders: Members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission, the Governor's office, and the Maryland Department of Health
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, the changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary subject of the bill, the Health Services Cost Review Commission is directly affected by changes to its governing statutes regarding member terms and holdover limits.

The Governor is the appointing authority for all seven members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission; the bill modifies the Governor's ability to allow members to serve past the expiration of their terms.

The Office of Appointments facilitates the recruitment and vetting of candidates for state boards and commissions; this bill creates a strict 8-month deadline for finding successors, which directly impacts their workflow and timeline for these specific positions.

The Health Services Cost Review Commission is an independent agency located within the Maryland Department of Health, and any changes to the commission's structure or leadership terms are relevant to the department's broader organizational landscape.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state commissions and the Governor regarding statutory compliance and the legal status of board members during transition periods.

bill_summary: This bill requires businesses holding cigarette or other tobacco product licenses to obtain a separate license if they want to manufacture, distribute, or sell electronic smoking devices (ESDs). It removes the previous authorization that allowed these businesses to handle ESDs under their existing tobacco licenses. Additionally, the bill exempts tobacco license holders from paying the additional fee for an ESD retailer or vape shop vendor license if they already hold specific cigarette or tobacco product licenses.
stakeholders: Cigarette and other tobacco product (OTP) manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers; electronic smoking device (ESD) manufacturers and retailers; and vape shop vendors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to increase by up to 25,100 annually starting in fiscal 2027 from additional ESD license fees collected by the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission. Existing cigarette and tobacco licensees must obtain these separate ESD licenses once their current licenses expire (starting May 2027). Local circuit court clerks will experience minimal operational impact for license processing, with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: According to the provided summary, the Comptroller is responsible for regulating the tobacco industry. This bill directly pertains to the licensure requirements and regulations for tobacco products and electronic smoking devices, making the Comptroller the primary regulatory agency involved.

The fiscal note identifies that the clerks of the circuit courts, who are supported operationally and financially by the Administrative Office of the Courts, are responsible for issuing retail licenses and will experience an operational impact due to the new licensure requirements.

The fiscal note specifies that a significant portion of the license fees collected ($275 per retail license) is distributed to the Department of Health for the enforcement of laws prohibiting the sale of tobacco or electronic smoking devices to minors.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the state and its agencies. It would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the new licensure framework and representing the state in any enforcement actions or legal disputes arising from the bill.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for monitoring revenue changes and fiscal planning. The bill is projected to increase general fund revenues by approximately $25,100 annually from new license fees.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementing the new licensure rules, and the Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and proposing the annual budget which will include the projected revenue increases.

Synopsis: Altering, for a certain licensing requirement, the definition of "money transmitter" under the Maryland Money Transmission Act to exclude a certain person designated as an agent of a payor for the purpose of the agent's provision of payroll processing services under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: The bill modifies the Maryland Money Transmission Act to exclude certain payroll processing agents from the definition of a money transmitter. For the exclusion to apply, the agent must provide services under a written agreement with the payor, the payor must identify the agent as such to employees and other payees, and the payor's legal obligation to the payee must remain if the agent fails to remit the funds.
stakeholders: Payroll processing companies, employers, and employees
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, state special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor are expected to decrease by $6,000 annually starting in fiscal year 2027. This revenue loss results from three companies that currently operate as payroll processors no longer needing to pay the $2,000 annual money transmitter licensing fee. There is no anticipated effect on state expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, specifically the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) within the department, is the primary regulator for the Maryland Money Transmission Act. The bill directly alters the scope of their licensing authority and will result in a decrease in special fund revenue from licensing fees.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Office of Financial Regulation regarding the interpretation and enforcement of the Maryland Money Transmission Act. They would also be involved in any legal challenges or clarifications regarding the new agent designation requirements.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. They will track the $6,000 annual reduction in special fund revenues for the Department of Labor resulting from this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Labor, and is responsible for the execution of state laws such as the Maryland Money Transmission Act.

bill_summary: The Building Affordably in My Back Yard Act requires business entities that own and rent residential property to file contact information for an authorized representative with the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). Additionally, the bill authorizes local jurisdictions to establish administrative processes to review and approve housing development projects if a shortage of affordable housing is determined to exist.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
stakeholders: Business entities owning residential rental property, local government officials, residential housing developers, and individuals seeking affordable housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $74,100 in FY 2027 for DHCD to hire a communications assistant to manage the new entity registry, with costs projected to reach $98,500 by FY 2031. Local government expenditures may increase if jurisdictions choose to implement the authorized administrative review processes for housing applications. There is no impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is tasked with receiving and organizing contact information certifications from business entities that own residential rental property and must provide this information to local governments upon request. The agency also defines the parameters for affordable housing projects cited in the bill's regulatory framework.

As the agency responsible for promoting sustainable growth and land use planning, the Department of Planning is relevant because the bill amends the Land Use Article and impacts local development review processes, which the department monitors and supports through data analysis and policy guidance.

The fiscal note indicates that the bill will require additional general fund expenditures to hire new personnel at DHCD to manage the entity certification process. DBM oversees state agency budgeting and personnel management.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like DHCD and will be responsible for advising on the legal requirements of the new certification process, including documents affirmed or acknowledged under oath.

The bill aligns with executive priorities and previous executive orders regarding the affordable housing crisis and housing production targets. The Governor's Office coordinates the policy initiatives that this legislation addresses.

Synopsis: Altering the amounts of certain capital grants calculated based on highway user revenues that are required to be appropriated to Baltimore City, counties, and municipalities in fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter; etc.
Title: Transportation - Highway User Revenues Capital Grants - Calculation
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the amount of capital grants distributed from the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account to Baltimore City, Maryland counties, and municipalities. Specifically, it raises the percentage of revenues allocated to counties starting in fiscal 2027 and prevents scheduled decreases in allocations to Baltimore City and municipalities that were set to occur in fiscal 2028, effectively making higher funding levels permanent.
stakeholders: Baltimore City, Maryland counties, Maryland municipalities, and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not change overall Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures but redirects significant funding from the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to local governments. According to the fiscal note, MDOT will be required to redirect an estimated $227,600,000 in FY 2027, $324,000,000 in FY 2028, $332,300,000 in FY 2029, $341,600,000 in FY 2030, and $351,200,000 in FY 2031 from its capital program to local jurisdictions. Consequently, local government revenues will increase by these same amounts annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary manager of the Transportation Trust Fund and the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, MDOT is directly responsible for distributing Highway User Revenues. The bill significantly reduces MDOT's retained share of these revenues, necessitating a redirection of an estimated $1.6 billion from MDOT's internal capital program to local governments over the five-year forecast period.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and execution. This bill mandates a change in the statutory formula for capital grant appropriations from the Transportation Trust Fund, requiring DBM to ensure that the annual state budget reflects these increased mandatory distributions to local jurisdictions.

The Governor's Office proposes the annual state budget and oversees the executive branch. This bill alters the long-term fiscal planning and capital project prioritization within the executive branch by mandating higher revenue transfers to Baltimore City, counties, and municipalities.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector for the revenues that feed the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, including motor fuel taxes and vehicle titling taxes. The bill impacts the distribution of the revenues collected by this agency.

The Treasurer's Office manages the state's financial assets and is responsible for the custody and distribution of state funds, including those within the Transportation Trust Fund and its subsidiary accounts mentioned in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly and willfully causing another individual to ingest an abortion-inducing drug if they know or believe the person is pregnant and act without consent, or through fraud, coercion, force, or threat of force. A violation is a felony punishable by up to 25 years in prison.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Pregnant individuals and persons who attempt to induce an abortion in another without their consent.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to incarceration costs. It is not expected to materially affect local finances or the operations of the Judiciary or the Office of the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary, through the Administrative Office of the Courts, is responsible for adjudicating criminal cases. This bill creates a new felony, directly impacting the court system's workload and processing of trials and sentencing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for defending indigent individuals charged with crimes. The creation of a new felony for causing the ingestion of abortion-inducing drugs will directly increase their caseload and litigation requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a felony with a prison sentence of up to 25 years. This has a direct fiscal impact on the department's correctional facilities and budget due to potential increases in the inmate population and duration of stay.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal violations of state law, including the felony offenses established by this bill.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in all criminal appeals. The creation of a new felony for drug-induced abortion coercion will require legal review and potential representation in the appellate courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates statewide public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy. A new felony regarding drug-induced coercion falls under their oversight of criminal justice and victim services strategy.

The Department of Health oversees public health and reproductive health services. While the bill is criminal in nature, the subject matter involves medicinal preparations and health policy related to abortion and reproductive rights.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is relevant due to the potential increase in general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services resulting from the bill's incarceration penalty.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an insurer, with respect to private passenger motor vehicle insurance, from increasing a premium, adding a surcharge, or removing, altering, or refusing to consider a discount based on accidents or losses caused by a collision with a free-roaming wild animal and for which the insured was not at fault for the loss.

Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits private passenger motor vehicle insurers from increasing premiums, adding surcharges, or altering discounts based on an accident or loss caused by a collision with a free-roaming wild animal, provided the insured was not at fault for the loss.
stakeholders: Private passenger motor vehicle insurance policyholders and insurance companies operating in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) will increase minimally in fiscal 2027 due to rate and form filing fees. There may be an indeterminate impact on general fund revenues from premium taxes if insurers adjust overall rates in response to the prohibition, though this cannot be reliably estimated. The Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) and local governments are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing the Maryland insurance market, enforcing the Insurance Article, and reviewing and approving the rates and forms that insurers must file to comply with the bill's prohibitions.

As a state-created independent agency that provides private passenger motor vehicle insurance, MAIF is directly subject to the bill's requirements and prohibitions regarding premium adjustments for collisions with wild animals.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and represents the agency in any legal challenges or enforcement actions resulting from these new regulatory requirements.

DNR is the state agency responsible for managing wildlife and was consulted as an information source regarding collisions with free-roaming wild animals, the subject matter of the insurance claims addressed in the bill.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. The bill may impact general fund revenues derived from the 2% premium tax if insurance premiums are adjusted in response to the bill's prohibitions.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Judiciary Case Search from displaying or referring to records related to alleged violations of the Maryland Vehicle Law or any other traffic law, ordinance, or regulation committed by a minor.
stakeholders: Minors with alleged traffic violations, the public users of the Maryland Judiciary Case Search system, and the Maryland Judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $83,100 in fiscal 2027 for one-time computer programming changes to remove both historical and new references to traffic violations by minors from the Judiciary Case Search system. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for overseen the executive branch and has the final authority to sign the bill into law or veto it.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and may be required to provide legal counsel regarding the implementation and interpretation of privacy requirements for court records.
The bill specifically concerns legal violations by minors; DJS is the primary agency responsible for the treatment and supervision of youth involved in the justice system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages criminal records and public safety data; changes to the visibility of traffic violations in judicial searches intersect with the broader criminal record ecosystem they navigate.
MDOT oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and the enforcement of the Maryland Vehicle Law, which is the primary subject of the records being restricted.
The AOC is the primary implementing agency as it operates the Maryland Judiciary Case Search. It will incur a direct fiscal impact of approximately $83,100 for mandatory system programming changes.

As the agency responsible for vehicle titling, registration, and driver licensing, the MVA's regulatory area (Maryland Vehicle Law violations) is directly impacted by how these records are displayed to the public.

Synopsis: Establishing a certain immunity from liability for a person who donates a pet item or dispenses a donated pet item; and authorizing the State Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial feed and establish procedures for handling donated commercial feed.

bill_summary: This bill establishes immunity from civil liability for persons who, in good faith, donate or dispense pet supplies (including commercial feed) to nonprofit organizations or government units, provided the action does not involve gross negligence or willful misconduct. It also authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial feed for wholesomeness and to establish procedures for handling such donations.
stakeholders: Donors of pet supplies, nonprofit organizations, state and local government agencies, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $84,600 in fiscal 2027, which accounts for the cost of hiring one agricultural inspector to perform inspections and the purchase of a vehicle. Annual expenditures for subsequent years are estimated to range from approximately $69,700 to $80,000. The bill is not expected to affect state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial pet feed for wholesomeness and to establish procedures for its handling. The fiscal note indicates a direct fiscal impact for the department, including a general fund expenditure of approximately $84,600 for the hiring of an agricultural inspector.

The bill establishes a new immunity from liability within the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for the operational and legal support of the judicial branch, which will adjudicate civil disputes involving these new liability standards.

The bill requires a general fund expenditure for a new personnel position (Agricultural Inspector) at the Department of Agriculture. DBM is the principal agency for budget development, execution, and personnel management, making it responsible for the fiscal oversight of this expansion.

The Office of the Attorney General will provide legal counsel to the Department of Agriculture for the drafting of new handling procedures and inspection protocols. They also serve as the state's representative in civil litigation, which may involve interpreting the immunity provisions granted to state units.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law to require a law enforcement agency to require the use of body-worn cameras, subject to a certain policy, by each sworn law enforcement officer, regardless of rank, employed by the law enforcement agency while the officer is in uniform, in public, and conducting law enforcement-related duties.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement Agencies - Use of Body-Worn Cameras

bill_summary: This bill expands the requirement for body-worn cameras (BWCs) to all sworn law enforcement officers in Maryland, regardless of rank, while they are in uniform, in public, and performing law enforcement-related duties. stakeholders: Sworn law enforcement officers, Maryland law enforcement agencies, and the general public.

Synopsis: Requiring an insurer that issues or delivers private passenger motor vehicle insurance policies in the State to disclose the use of a program that measures the operation of an insured vehicle and to establish a process by which a policyholder may correct or appeal data the policyholder believes to be erroneous; prohibiting insurers with respect to certain private passenger motor vehicle insurance policies from initiating a premium increase in increments of less than 6 months; etc.

bill_summary: This bill regulates how private passenger motor vehicle insurers use programs that measure vehicle operation, such as telematics. It requires insurers to disclose the use of such programs, establish an appeal process for policyholders to correct erroneous data, and prohibits the use of this data to cancel, refuse to renew, or refuse to underwrite a policy. Additionally, it prevents insurers from increasing premiums in increments of less than six months for policies using these programs and requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to set limits on the types and amount of data collected.
stakeholders: Private passenger motor vehicle insurance companies and policyholders in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can adopt the required regulations and oversee the new requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect state or local finances, nor is it anticipated to significantly impact general fund revenues from the insurance premium tax. The Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is unaffected as it does not currently use vehicle operation measurement programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary agency responsible for the implementation and enforcement of this bill, including adopting new regulations to limit data collection, specifying disclosure methods, and potentially requiring governance plans for insurers.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would be involved in the drafting of mandatory regulations and the enforcement of statutory prohibitions.
OAH adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions, which may arise if the Maryland Insurance Administration takes action against insurers for non-compliance with the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Maryland Insurance Administration, and the bill requires the Governor's approval and appointment of officials who lead these regulatory efforts.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "eligible project"; requiring an appropriation of a certain amount to the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program if the Governor appropriates less than $80,000,000 to the Community College Construction Grant Program in each fiscal year; increasing the number of grants, from 8 to 16, the Maryland Higher Education Commission may make in each fiscal year; etc.

bill_summary: The bill expands the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program by removing project cost limits and increasing the number of grants that can be awarded each year from 8 to 16. It also sets a new funding requirement: if the state's main community college construction fund receives less than $80 million in a fiscal year, the state must provide enough funding to the renewal program to make up the difference. Additionally, it removes the rule that prevents colleges from receiving grants in consecutive years and requires funds to be distributed equally among eligible colleges.
stakeholders: Maryland community colleges and Baltimore City Community College
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a state funding mandate for the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program. If the annual appropriation for the Community College Construction Grant Program is less than $80,000,000, the Governor must appropriate the difference to the Facilities Renewal Grant Program. This ensures a baseline funding level when construction appropriations are below the $80,000,000 threshold. The bill also doubles the number of possible grants from 8 to 16 and removes the $1,000,000 project cost cap and the $500,000 individual grant limit. Specific state expenditure increases are indeterminate as they depend on future annual budget cycles, but the $80,000,000 figure serves as the primary fiscal benchmark.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program, determining grant awards in consultation with colleges, and adopting necessary regulations.
